### D813. The window's layout and wording details
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-17** · Built: as D808.
- Decision: order: the asker, the account line, the email sharing line; then the headline (`h2`), the red banners
  and the red lines (moved up after the security review), the amount figure where D765 shows one, the summary's lines
  (at most four grouped lines, D814), the network and fee rows, the amber lines, the request's own facts (the NEAR leaving the account, a NEP-413 recipient, the message), the page's notes
  (test-app note or mainnet demo banner, the out-of-policy reason), the details, the buttons. The request's kind ("EVM
  transaction", "NEAR transaction, fee paid by a relayer") moves into the details as their first heading. A relayed
  NEAR action's fee line says "paid for you by a relayer", not "Journear pays": the popup can't know which relayer
  will send it (a partner can relay it itself). A fee-bump's payer is a summary line ("Your account pays the network
  fee for a transaction from …", or "The network fee is paid by …, not your account"), replacing the old amber
  line; an operation on another account says so in its own step.
- After the second security review: the page builds a request's or consent's screen off the page before showing it;
  if building fails it shows "Journear can't read this request, so it can't be approved." with no Approve (or the
  consent's refusal with no Allow), never the previous screen, and only then is the new request the one on show.
  Reject and Approve answer only the request they were drawn for.
- After the third security review: a Stellar address is the user's when it is the user's account or that account in
  muxed form (M…, `stellarBaseAccount`): every comparison with the user's address uses that (the sources counted in
  "XLM leaving your account", the transaction and operation sources, recipients, claimants, a Soroban `from`), worded
  "your account (muxed id N)". The vault signs a transaction with a muxed source after the user approves it (the
  policy matcher treats it as another source, so it is never signed automatically); it debits the base account.
  EVM addresses are compared case-insensitively; NEAR account ids are lowercase by the protocol and the user's is the
  implicit one the decoder checks, so neither needs more. Deliberately neutral steps (listed only up to five): a
  sequence bump, a data entry (its small reserve aside), inflation (a no-op), keeping or restoring contract data (paid
  by the network fee), ending a sponsorship begun in the same transaction (its begin is listed), an issuer's
  trust-line authorization of someone else's holding, a cancelled offer, a setOptions that changes no signer or
  threshold; NEAR account creation. The overflow note (`watchOverflowing`) measures again when the details
  open or close, since a box in closed details measures zero. A message's bytes are also in its details, as hex.
- Address impact: none.
- Amended 2026-11-19 by D886: within the request's own facts a message comes before the blue note about networks
  (headline, a NEP-413 recipient, "The message" and the message, then the note); for a test app's message or raw
  signing that note carries the test-app advice and the page's own test-app note is left out.

### D814. Multi-step requests: one box per colour, at most four grouped lines, amounts shown conservatively
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-17** (after seeing the 100-action screen: "this looks crazy
  with so many rows, this will definitely confuse the user"); the details below decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** ·
  Built on `feat/approval-plain-summary`: `packages/core/src/decode/summary.ts` (`groupSteps`, `stellarStep`,
  `nearAction`'s steps, `displayUnits`, `nearDisplay`, `shortId`, the warnings' `short` forms),
  `packages/web/src/auth/render-approval.ts` (`riskBox`, `RiskItem`, `accountControlShorts`, the NEAR bullet forms),
  `auth/css/approval.css`; tests `packages/core/test/approval-summary.test.ts` ("D814"), web and e2e · Amends D809
  and D813.
- One box per colour. Every red item of a request is in one red box (announced, `role=alert`): the most serious in
  full, then each other red item as one short bullet ("Adds a full-access key (ed25519:cGfH…izuN)", "Calls a contract
  on your own account", "Lets 0x3333…3333 spend all of your tokens of contract 0x1111…1111"), an identical bullet
  said once with its count. Ranks: account control (the banner, then each control line) > raw or unreadable > no-limit
  spend, collection operator, Permit2 look-alike > own-contract call or burn > left-out steps that move value > the
  rest. No red item is dropped. Amber items likewise share one amber box. A key, address or account id in a bullet is
  cut recognisably (a prefixed key keeps its prefix and 4 + 4 characters, anything else its first 6 and last 4); the
  whole value is in the lead (when it leads) or in the details. The info notes, the test-app note and the mainnet demo
  banner stay as they are (the demo banner keeps its own box: its balance line updates in place).
- What it does: at most four lines, steps grouped by everything a line says about them except an amount that is
  summed: never two recipients, assets, contracts or methods in one group. Each group says its count and its exact or
  bounded total ("Send NEAR to your account, 99 times (less than 0.000001 NEAR in total)", "Send 6 XLM to G… in 3
  payments", "Use c.testnet (a), 2 times (attaching 1 NEAR in total)"); groups whose line has a per-step amount
  repeat it ("3 times: offer to sell 5 XLM for at least …"). Order: control changes, value to others (the chain's coin
  first, then the largest total), approvals and grants, contract calls, other value (trust lines, sponsorship,
  claims, stake), moves to the user's own account, the rest. A group to someone else is always above any group to
  the user's own account. With more than four groups the fourth line is "…and N other steps: see the details." and
  the box gets a bullet: red when a left-out group moves or grants value or changes control, amber otherwise. The
  largest amount to others is never left out (when control groups fill the lines, the last of them gives way: control
  changes are always in the red box anyway); approvals and control changes always have their bullet even when not in a
  line. Amended after an automated review: room for the largest amount to others comes from the lowest-priority
  visible group that isn't a control change or a grant (the rest, then moves to the user's own account, then calls);
  only when every visible line is a control change does the last of them give way. Every left-out control change,
  grant and value to someone else then gets its own red bullet naming its key, spender or recipient ("Not in the
  lines above: …"), besides the collective "steps not listed" one. Step lines name what tells two steps apart (a
  signer change names the signer, an approval its spender), and Stellar steps group only when their operations are
  identical. A single-step request reads as before.
- Amended after the review of 5ef13452: a control change's key, signer or address is never cut. A NEAR key change
  names the whole key in its line and headline ("add the full-access key ed25519:… to your account", "remove the key
  …"), a global contract change names the contract, and every control bullet and every "Not in the lines above"
  bullet carries the whole value (long values wrap, as code text). A spender in a bullet is its whole address, after
  its verified name or marked "(unverified)". No bullet is cut any more; identical bullets merge only when their full
  texts match. Value to others carries its native-coin amount for the ranking (path payments, account creation,
  claimable balances, offers selling the coin), so a 1,000,000 XLM path payment outranks a 1 XLM payment group. A
  buy offer's received amount rounds down and its cost up; a clawback or a token transfer reaching the user rounds
  down. A left-out approval of 0 reads as taking a permission back.
- Amended by the Tech Lead (2026-11-17, after seeing the 100-action screen show the same key twice): a control bullet
  is dropped when its step's own line is in view, as that line names the same key, signer or address in full. The
  match is on the step (its operation or action), not on similar text: the summary reports which steps its visible
  lines show (`shownSteps`: the headline of a single-step request, or every step of a visible group), and the page
  drops only the control bullets of those steps. The box's lead (the banner) always stays, and the box may then hold
  only its lead. Bullets for steps not in the lines ("Not in the lines above", the steps-not-listed bullet) always
  stay, as do bullets that say more than the line: the removal of the user's own Journear Passport key (the line
  names the key, not whose it is), a burn or an own-contract call, and every spend or grant warning (its amount is in
  the bullet, not the line). So every control change is named in full at least once above the fold, and the key of
  the 100-action case exactly once (tested as a property in the web tests).
- Amounts (all chains, in the summary, its totals and the amount figure): exact up to six decimals; below 0.000001
  "less than 0.000001" (received: "a tiny amount (less than 0.000001)"); otherwise "about N" with six decimals, rounded
  up for amounts that leave the user and down for amounts the user receives. A non-zero amount is never shown as 0.
  The exact figure is in the details. The totals ("NEAR leaving your account", "XLM leaving your account") follow it,
  and per-step amounts appear only in the group lines.
- Amended 2026-11-17 (branch `feat/evm-sponsored-approval`, the leftover Low of PR 65's review), decided while
  building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18**: a Stellar `setOptions` that sets the account's own key's weight to 0 keeps its bullet "Sets your
  own Journear Passport key’s weight to 0: you lose control of the account" even when its step's line is in view, as
  NEAR's removal of the user's own key does: the line ("set your own key’s weight to 0") doesn't say the user loses
  control (`render-approval.ts` `accountControlItems`' `keep`; test `render-approval-sponsored.test.ts`). Any other
  weight drops its bullet as before. After PR 72's review: every signing-threshold change keeps its bullet too, "Changes
  the signing thresholds: wrong values can lock you out of the account", since whether new thresholds lock the user out
  depends on the account's current signers and weights, which the request doesn't carry.
- Why: the Tech Lead's audience; a long numbered list or a stack of red boxes hides the one fact that matters.
- Address impact: none.


## EVM gas sponsorship (D831–D852), 2026-11-17

The parallel EVM gas sponsorship builds to the shared spec of 2026-11-17, in number order: D833 and D846 from
`feat/evm-sponsor-core` (the signing core, merged into `next` at d39d1d69), D832, D840, D847, D848 and D836's addendum
from `feat/evm-sponsor-api` (the API handlers; from `next` @ d14607a6, `next` @ d95b5ff5 merged in; not merged, not
deployed), D849 from `feat/evm-deploy-scripts` (the deploy and key scripts, merged into `next` at d95b5ff5), D834–D836 from `feat/evm-sponsor-manifest`
(the manifest block, its generation and the API's config parser; from `next` @ 7243d2af, `next` merged in; not
deployed), D841 and D845 from `feat/evm-delegate-contract` (the delegate contract, MIT, in `contracts/evm-delegate`;
from `next` @ 7243d2af, `next` merged in; not deployed), D831, D839 and D850 from `feat/evm-sponsored-approval` (the
approval kind, its decoder, summary and window; from `next` @ e4ee9762; not merged, not deployed), D851 from `feat/evm-relayer-simple` (the relayer object, from `next` @ c6b434f4; not merged, not deployed), superseding D837 (PR 70's first relayer, never merged). Decided by the user 2026-11-17: non-Web3 users who don't know what gas is; EVM first, Base Sepolia (84532)
only for now; a self-hosted relayer with an EIP-7702 delegate behind an API gate (no third-party bundler or
paymaster); Journear absorbs the fees within daily budgets, 0.02 test ETH a day overall and 0.01 per app; the user's
address never changes; testnet only; free tiers; a staff-only allowlist in the manifest.
Current state of the delegate: `contracts/evm-delegate/README.md`, `docs/security.md` "The EVM delegate contract",
`docs/operations.md` "CI and git", `LICENSING.md`.

### D831. One approval for the one-time setup and the first batch; the window's words
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-17** (one approval, the wording, never "upgrade" or "smart
  account"), **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (the setup note keeps its wording) · Built on `feat/evm-sponsored-approval`, not merged, not deployed: `packages/core/src/decode/summary.ts`
  (`SPONSORED_FEE`, `accountSetupNote`), `packages/web/src/auth/render-approval.ts` (`sponsoredDetails`, `validUntil`);
  tests `packages/core/test/evm-sponsored-approval.test.ts`, `packages/web/test/auth/render-approval-sponsored.test.ts`,
  `apps/e2e/tests/approval-summary.spec.ts`.
- Decision: a sponsored action is one approval; the account's one-time setup (its EIP-7702 authorization) rides with
  the first batch. The headline is the calls' own summary. The fee row reads "Network fee: none. Journear pays it for
  you." Only when the approval also signs the authorization, an amber note: "One-time setup: this also turns on free
  network fees for your account on {chain name}. Your address stays the same and you still approve every action." The
  words "upgrade" and "smart account" never appear in user-visible text (tested); EIP-7702 is named only in the folded
  details: "Account setup (EIP-7702): account helper 0x… ✓ Journear Passport account helper v1, chain N, account nonce
  N" (later: "Account helper (EIP-7702): 0x… ✓ … (no setup in this approval)"), "Paid by: Journear’s relayer 0x…",
  "Valid until: HH:MM" (with the date when it isn't today, and the raw value). "Turn it off" in Passport Home is
  phase 2, before mainnet.
- Address impact: none (EIP-7702 keeps the account's address).

### D832. The vault prepares and submits sponsored actions; the signatures never go to the partner page
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: the vault submits decided by the user 2026-11-17 (the shared spec); the API's enforcement
  decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** · Built (API side; the vault's is WP3): `apps/api/src/origins.ts` (`HANA_CALLERS`,
  `PARTNER_ENDPOINTS`), `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor.ts`, `sponsor-status.ts`; tests `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts`
  ("the gate"), `test/origins.test.ts`.
- Decision: `POST /v1/evm/sponsor/prepare` and `POST /v1/evm/sponsor/send` are callable only from the vault
  (`VAULT_ORIGIN` with an `x-hana-parent-origin` in force for the app), never from a partner page: the Execute signature
  and the EIP-7702 authorization exist only in the vault and the API. `GET /v1/evm/sponsor/status` (no signature, no
  chain read) is the partner page's and the vault's. All three are behind the app gate kind `evm-sponsor`.
- Why: a partner page holding a user's authorization could submit it elsewhere or race the vault; keeping both
  signatures inside Journear's origin means the page only ever sees the result (the hash). The Origin header is still
  forgeable by a script, so this is not what bounds a spender: the account's signature, the allowlist and the limits
  are (D847).
- Rejected: prepare from the partner page (the SDK has nothing to do with its answer; it would open chain reads to any
  page holding the key).
- Address impact: none.

### D833. The generic signing paths never make a delegate signature: typed data in the delegate's domain and type-4 transactions are refused there
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: the approach (Journear's own relayer, an EIP-7702 delegate, the user approves every action)
  decided by the user 2026-11-17; this rule decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-17 · Built:
  `packages/core/src/evm-sponsor/guard.ts` (`isSponsorDomain`), `packages/core/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts`. **Enforced in
  the vault from branch `feat/evm-sponsored-approval`** (after PR 72's independent review, 2026-11-17; not merged,
  not deployed): `packages/web/src/vault/signing.ts` refuses typed data in a pinned delegate's domain before any popup
  or policy (4100, reason `sponsor_domain_reserved`, `SPONSOR_DOMAIN_RULE`), on the normalized object, and checks the
  very object it hashes again when signing; the popup's decoder refuses it too (`decode/request.ts`, `unsupported`, no
  Approve), so the auto-approve matcher, which decodes the same way, can never match it (`decode_failed`, tested with a
  policy-listed pair). Exact name only: a padded or look-alike name is another EIP-712 domain whose digest the delegate
  never accepts, so it is ordinary typed data (the generic red line). Tests `packages/web/test/vault/sponsor-domain.test.ts`
  (key order, hex and string chain IDs, another version or primary type, the name alone, look-alikes, unrelated typed
  data still signs, type 4 refused at the port and by the SDK's `normalizeTxInput`), `packages/core/test/evm-sponsored-approval.test.ts`.
- Decision: a signature the delegate accepts (an `Execute` or an EIP-7702 authorization) is made only through the
  sponsored-action approval and its signers (`signExecute`, `signAuthorization`, D846). The generic paths refuse
  what could make one: `eth_signTypedData_v4` refuses typed data whose domain `name` is a pinned delegate's
  (`isSponsorDomain`: exact name, any version, chain, `verifyingContract` or `salt`; the contract hashes its name as a
  constant, so another name can't make a signature it accepts), and `eth_signTransaction` keeps taking only type 0 and
  type 2 (`parseEvmTxRequest` refuses `type` `0x4` and an `authorizationList` field; the popup's decoder refuses
  EIP-7702 as `unsupported`), so an authorization can't ride in a generic transaction.
- Why: an Execute signed on the generic path would let any page that may ask for typed data run calls as the user's
  account outside the sponsored approval, its allowlist and its limits; an authorization to any other contract would
  hand the account to that contract.
- Not covered by this rule: raw signing (`hana_signRaw`) signs any 32-byte digest, so it could sign an Execute digest
  or an authorization hash. It stays as it is: off unless the app turns it on, refused outright for test apps, and a
  popup with the raw warning every time for live apps (never auto-approved). `personal_sign` can't collide: its
  EIP-191 prefix (0x19 0x45) differs from EIP-712's (0x19 0x01) and the authorization's magic (0x05).
- Address impact: none.

### D834. The manifest's `evm.sponsor` block, checked against core's pinned delegate table, generated as `EVM_SPONSOR` and the vault's chain table
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: the block, testnet only, Base Sepolia first and a pinned delegate decided by the user
  2026-11-17; the rest decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-17 · Built: `packages/env/src/evm-sponsor.ts` (schema, rules,
  `evmSponsorDelegateProblems`, `evmSponsorPageChains`), `src/schema.ts` (`evm`), `src/evm-sponsor.test.ts`,
  `src/evm-sponsor.fixture.ts`, `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-config.ts`, `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor-config.test.ts`,
  `apps/api/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts` (`evmSponsorVars`, `evmRelayKeysLine`), `scripts/test/gen-evm-sponsor.test.ts`,
  `apps/api/src/env.ts`, `packages/web/scripts/gen-envs.ts`, `src/hana-env.ts` (`evmSponsor`), `test/gen-envs.test.ts`,
  `.gitleaks.toml`, `scripts/secret-scan-selftest.mjs`, `envs/README.md`, `docs/operations.md`.
- Decision: an optional `evm: { sponsor }` block beside `near` (fields and bounds in `envs/README.md`). Absent = off
  everywhere. The schema's rules are one pure function, `evmSponsorProblems`, which also names a non-testnet network
  (the manifest's enum allows only testnet today). Chains must be in core's `TEST_EVM_CHAINS`: `packages/env` keeps the
  ID list itself (it doesn't depend on core) and a test in `packages/web` checks it equals core's; 31337 and 1337 only
  in `local*` envs; `opStack` true exactly on the OP Stack test chains (84532, 11155420).
- Addresses are EIP-55 checksummed (the form `checksumEvmAddress` in core writes and explorers show): an all-lowercase
  or mistyped one is refused, so a typo is caught at `gen` (`@noble/hashes` 1.8.0, already in the workspace, added to
  `packages/env` and `apps/api` for keccak). Selectors are lowercase.
- Pinned delegate: `evmSponsorDelegateProblems(sponsor, pinned, envName)` takes the table as a parameter (shape of
  core's `SPONSOR_DELEGATES`; `address` compared case-insensitively, and `placeholder`) so `packages/env` needs no
  dependency on core. The generators run it: the API's `gen` (`evmSponsorVars`) and the page build (`gen-envs`
  `sponsorProblems`) refuse a block when no table is passed, a chain has no pinned entry, a delegate differs, or the
  entry is a placeholder (`placeholder: true`, a test stand-in; core's 31337 entry was one until D846's amendment made it
  the delegate's deterministic deployment, so the rule is now tested with a fixture table) outside a `local*` env. Wired (after
  `next` @ d39d1d69 brought core's module): `gen-envs` `main` defaults `sponsorDelegates` to `SPONSOR_DELEGATES`; the
  API's `gen` loads it in its command line (`cli`, a dynamic import: `apps/api/vitest.config.ts` imports
  `gen-wrangler.ts` under Node's own type stripping, which core's sources don't support), while `main` and
  `wranglerConfig` still take it as a parameter. Core has no Base Sepolia entry yet, so a non-local env with the block
  is refused until the delegate is deployed and pinned.
- `EVM_SPONSOR` (API var): the block as JSON, its fields in a fixed order and nothing else (`evmSponsorVar`). `gen` also
  runs the API's parser on it and refuses a var the Worker would refuse. The Worker parses it again at run time
  (`parseEvmSponsorConfig(raw, { network, envName, pinnedDelegates })`, same bounds and rules but the provider check on
  `rpcFallback`, which needs the public suffix list) into wei and gas as bigints; the config is immutable all the way
  down (plain frozen objects with no prototype, frozen arrays; no Map; `sponsorChain` and `sponsoredTarget` look
  things up). Anything absent, malformed, out of bounds or off testnet is `{ status: 'unconfigured', reason: 'absent' |
  'invalid', problem }`, never a partial config. Self-contained (no Worker-only types, no core root import), so `gen`
  runs it in Node; tests keep its bounds and chain lists equal to the schema's.
- Run-time delegate check: `pinnedDelegates` is core's pinned table. With the block present, no table, a delegate that
  differs, a chain with no entry or a placeholder entry outside a `local*` env is `invalid`. The sponsorship handlers
  (WP5a) must pass `SPONSOR_DELEGATES` from `@hana-id/core/evm-sponsor` (which typechecks in the Worker); tested with a
  fixture table and with core's own.
- Shared rules (after the independent review, 2026-11-17): amounts are converted by exact decimal arithmetic on
  `String(v)` (exponent forms included) into a BigInt of the smallest unit, refusing more decimals than it allows
  (`sponsorDecimalUnits`; a float conversion refused valid values such as 33.999997859 gwei); loopback hosts
  (`isSponsorLoopbackHost`: `localhost`, `*.localhost`, 127/8, `[::1]`, IPv4-mapped 127/8, each with a trailing dot)
  and the RPC URL rule (`sponsorRpcUrlProblem`: https DNS names, no IP literal, no loopback or `.local` host outside
  `local*` envs, no credentials, path, query or fragment: no API keys in manifest URLs, a keyed RPC goes in a secret)
  are one block of code copied word for word into both packages (they can't share code), with a test comparing the
  text and differential tests comparing the answers. `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` keys are refused
  anywhere in the block, explicitly, by both (zod's records drop a `__proto__` key silently); `null` for an optional
  field is refused by both.
- `EVM_RELAY_KEYS` (API secret): a JSON array of exactly one `0x` + 64 lowercase hex secp256k1 key, because every
  signed batch names one relayer (`relayerAddress`). `.secrets/<env>/evm-relay-keys.json` (0600);
  `gen --dev-vars` writes it only when the key's address is `relayerAddress`, refuses the file for an env without the
  block, and never shows the key. The secret-scan rules catch the file and a pasted `EVM_RELAY_KEYS=` line (self-test
  cases added).
- Vault build: `HanaEnv.evmSponsor = { "<chainId>": { delegate, relayer } }`, only after the same delegate check (D855 adds the chain's public `rpc` and `rpcFallback`).
- Not in this package: routes, the relayer, the vault's signing, `env-secrets` and deploy steps for the new secret
  (later packages).
- Rejected: importing core into `packages/env` (a new dependency edge for one list); a check at schema time with a
  table the schema can't see; all-lowercase addresses (no typo check); several relayer keys (one `relayer` is signed).
- Amended 2026-11-17 (branch `feat/evm-sponsor-api`, after its independent review; decided while building, to confirm):
  `requireKnownAccount: false` is accepted only in `local*` envs, by both the schema (`evmSponsorProblems`) and the
  Worker's parser (`parseChain`), with a differential test for both env kinds (`scripts/test/gen-evm-sponsor.test.ts`):
  off, anyone holding a publishable key could make the relayer pay from accounts they make up.
- Address impact: none (no derivation changes).

- Amended 2026-11-18 (branch `fix/evm-relayer-unaccepted-first`, to confirm): two more rules in both parsers' shared
  block (`sponsorTipCapProblem`, `sponsorBatchSizeProblem`, word for word in `packages/env/src/evm-sponsor.ts` and
  `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-config.ts`, the differential test as before): a tip cap that leaves no starting tip after
  the relayer's two bumps (under 3 wei) is refused, and `maxCallsPerBatch` × the chain's largest target `maxDataBytes`
  above 30 KiB (the relayer's calldata limit) is refused.

### D835. The sponsorship allowlist is staff-only, per app and chain, contract and selector, value 0
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: staff-only allowlist in the manifest decided by the user 2026-11-17; its shape decided
  while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-17 (exact calldata and `maxDataBytes` added after an audit finding, the
  same day) · Built: as D834.
- Decision: `evm.sponsor.apps` is the only allowlist: `{ app_…: { chainId: [ { address, selectors, label } ] } }`. A
  partner can't add to it: a change is a manifest edit by staff, `gen` and a deploy. At most 8 apps and 8 targets per
  app (across its chains); every app names at least one configured chain, each with at least one target; a target
  once per chain, never the relayer or a delegate; 1 to 8 distinct 4-byte selectors (no "any function", no bare
  value transfer); `label` is staff-facing, 1 to 64 characters with no control or formatting characters. There is no
  value field: sponsored calls carry 0 (core's approval subject refuses any other value). `sponsoredTarget(config,
  app, chain, to, data)` in the API's parser is the lookup the handlers will use (address in any case, the first 4
  bytes of `data`).
- Exact calldata (after an audit finding, 2026-11-17: a selector-only rule accepts trailing bytes the sponsor pays
  for): every target has a required `maxDataBytes` (4 to 8192), so a call's data is always bounded, and an optional
  `exactCalldata` (1 to 8 distinct lowercase whole-byte entries of 4 to 2048 bytes, each starting with one of the
  target's selectors and no longer than `maxDataBytes`; one shared rule, `sponsorCalldataProblem`, in both packages).
  A selector with entries matches only data exactly equal to one of them; a selector without keeps selector matching
  within `maxDataBytes`. The demo's `checkIn()` is `exactCalldata: ["0x183ff085"]`, `maxDataBytes: 4`.
- Address impact: none.

### D836. Sponsorship limits: the Tech Lead's budgets, per-app below the env's, hard bounds on every number
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: 0.02 test ETH a day overall and 0.01 per app decided by the user 2026-11-17; the other
  numbers and the bounds decided while building, confirmed by the user 2026-11-17 · Built: as D834.
- Decision: per chain, all required but `rpcFallback` and `requireKnownAccount` (default true; false testnet only), no
  hidden defaults: the spec's values `maxGasPerTx` 300 000, `maxFeePerGasGwei` 1, `maxPriorityFeePerGasGwei` 0.01,
  `maxCallsPerBatch` 4, `deadlineMaxS` 600, `minGas` 100 000, `dailyBudgetEth` 0.02, `appDailyBudgetEth` 0.01,
  `lowBalanceEth` 0.05, `perUserPerDay` 30, `perAppPerDay` 2000, `sendsPerDay` 5000, `sendsPerMinute` 60. Hard bounds
  (schema and Worker): ≤ 4 chains; `maxGasPerTx` 50 000–2 000 000; `minGas` 10 000–1 000 000 and below
  `maxGasPerTx`; fee caps ≤ 100 gwei to 1 wei, priority ≤ max; `maxCallsPerBatch` 1–8 (the approval subject's
  limit); `deadlineMaxS` 60–3600; budgets > 0, ≤ 1 ETH, to 1 gwei; `lowBalanceEth` ≤ 10; `perUserPerDay` ≤ 10 000,
  `perAppPerDay` ≤ 1 000 000, `sendsPerDay` ≤ 10 000 000, `sendsPerMinute` ≤ 100 000 (the NEAR relay's bounds where
  they match). Rules: `appDailyBudgetEth` below `dailyBudgetEth` and `perAppPerDay` below `sendsPerDay` (one leaked
  publishable key never uses up the env's day, as D736); one transaction's worst case, `maxGasPerTx` × `maxFeePerGas`,
  fits in `appDailyBudgetEth` (the OP Stack L1 data fee comes on top and is the relayer's to count).
- Open item (for the relayer package, WP5b): the OP Stack L1 data fee is **not** bounded by these manifest rules. Before
  sending, the relayer must estimate it (the chain's GasPriceOracle predeploy) and count it in the transaction's
  worst-case budget reservation, and refuse the send when gas × fee cap plus that fee doesn't fit.
- Addendum 2026-11-17 (branch `feat/evm-sponsor-api`, the API handlers; decided while building, to confirm): the L1
  fee is in the reservation. The handler (not the relayer object) reads the upper bound from the OP Stack
  GasPriceOracle predeploy `0x4200…000F`, `getL1FeeUpperBound(uint256)` (`0xf1c7a58b`), for an upper bound of the
  unsigned transaction's size (calldata + 200 + 128 per authorization bytes), and reserves `gasLimit × maxFeePerGas +
  that bound` from the app's and the env's day budgets before sending; an oracle that doesn't answer a uint256 fails
  closed (`502 evm_rpc_unavailable`, nothing sent), and a bound that doesn't fit is refused like any other reservation
  (`429 app_budget_exhausted` / `budget_exhausted`). Settled from the receipt's `l1Fee`; an OP Stack receipt without
  it is charged the bound. Off the OP Stack (`opStack: false`) the bound is 0 and no read is made. Built:
  `apps/api/src/evm/op-fee.ts` (`l1FeeUpperBound`, `unsignedTxSizeBound`, `worstCaseWei`, `receiptCostWei`), tests
  `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts` ("the OP Stack L1 data fee"), `test/evm-sponsor-units.test.ts`.

### D840. An account delegated anywhere but the pinned delegate is refused
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (number reserved by the shared
  spec) · Built: `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-checks.ts` (`classifyDelegation`), `sponsor.ts` (send step 8, prepare's `delegation`);
  tests `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts`, `test/evm-sponsor-units.test.ts`. The vault's own refusal is WP3.
- Decision: the account's code is read before every send and prepare. No code: sponsorship needs an attached
  authorization (`409 delegation_required` without one). Exactly `0xef0100 ‖ the chain's pinned delegate`: delegated
  to Journear (`journear`; an attached authorization is dropped, never sent). Anything else (a designator to another
  address, the zero-address designator's leftovers, contract code, a malformed designator): `409 delegated_elsewhere`,
  and prepare answers `delegation: "other"`, `executeNonce: null`, `allowed: false`. The API never sends an
  authorization for such an account (it would re-delegate an account the user pointed elsewhere) and never runs a
  batch through code it didn't pin.
- Why: under another delegate the account's behaviour, storage and nonce are that contract's; Journear can't know what
  a batch would do there, and re-delegating it without the user choosing to would take the account from whatever the
  user set up.
- Rejected: offering to re-delegate (the "turn it off" and change flows are Passport Home's, phase 2).
- Amended 2026-11-17 (branch `feat/evm-sponsor-api`, after its independent review; decided while building, to
  confirm): `requireKnownAccount: false` only in `local*` envs (D834's amendment). The reservation is `gasLimit × the
  fee cap` (not the starting fee: the relayer may replace the transaction with fees up to the cap) `+ the L1 bound + the
  OP Stack operator fee's bound` (Isthmus: `getOperatorFee(gasLimit)` on the GasPriceOracle, `0x275aedd2`; a chain whose
  oracle reverts it has no operator fee, 0; any other failure fails closed). Sends start at most at the relayer's
  `maxStartingFees` (the highest fees two × 9/8 replacements keep within the caps; the relayer refuses a start above,
  `fees_too_high`), so a base fee above that is `503 gas_price_too_high`. Settlement adds the receipt's operator fee
  (`gasUsed × operatorFeeScalar ÷ 10^6 + operatorFeeConstant`), or its bound when the receipt doesn't report one.
- Address impact: none.

- Amended 2026-11-18 (branch `fix/evm-relayer-unaccepted-first`, to confirm): `deadlineMaxS` at most 300 (was 3600):
  a user's action that can't go out is cancelled at its deadline at the latest, so a short window bounds how long one
  can hold the relayer's later transactions up. The vault keeps its wider sanity bound on the API's answer (60 to 3600).

### D837. The EVM relayer object, first design (self-repairing): superseded by D851
- Date 2026-11-17 · Status: the object as first built confirmed by the user 2026-11-17, amended after two independent
  reviews; **superseded by D851 (decided by the user 2026-11-18)**. Never merged: PR 70 (branch `feat/evm-relayer-do`)
  is closed unmerged and kept as reference only; nothing of it is on `next`.
- What it was: the same object as D851 (`EvmRelayer`, one per chain and key, the Execute checked and built inside it,
  idempotent by digest, persisted before the broadcast, fee bumps and a deadline self-transfer), but built to repair
  itself: it read every configured endpoint and acted only when they agreed at a common block, decided that a nonce
  was "taken" by something else from the user's account (its delegate nonce and `Executed` log), moved a record that
  could no longer land to a new nonce, filled a nonce gap by itself after 5 minutes, and spread its checks over runs
  with per-run budgets.
- Why it was replaced: each review round's fixes opened new edge cases (which endpoint's word counts, evidence read
  from an account the user controls, a record moved while an older copy could still land, gap fills racing late
  transactions, budgets leaving records unchecked). The Tech Lead chose a design that does only what is safe on its own
  evidence and stops for a person otherwise (D851).
- Kept in D851: the serialised critical section, persist (and `storage.sync()`) before every broadcast, the
  in-object check of the Execute and the authorization, the fee headroom rule, the fake chain and a trimmed RPC client.

### D838. The SDK's gas-free actions: `hana.evm.sendSponsored` by name, EIP-5792 over the same, never transparent sponsoring
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: no transparent sponsoring of `eth_sendTransaction` **decided by the user 2026-11-17** (the
  Tech Lead agreed to this design point); the rest decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** · Built on `feat/evm-sponsor-vault`
  (from `next` @ c6b434f4), not merged, not deployed: `packages/web/src/client/evm-sponsor.ts` (`HanaEvm`,
  `HanaSponsorError`, `isHanaSponsorError`, `EvmSponsorErrorData`, `sponsoredCalls`, `NOT_OFFERED`), `client.ts`
  (`hana.evm`, `sponsoredChains` from `ready`), `ethereum.ts` (`wallet_getCapabilities`, `wallet_sendCalls`,
  `wallet_getCallsStatus`, `EIP5792`, `CALLS_VERSION`), `index.ts`; SDK 0.5.0 (`sdk-version`, the four packages, their
  READMEs and the guide's release notes; **not published**); tests `packages/web/test/client/evm-sponsor.test.ts`,
  `test/client/ethereum.test.ts`; `apps/e2e/tests/evm-sponsor.spec.ts`; docs `docs/integration.md` "Gas-free actions
  (not live)", `docs/architecture.md`.
- Decision: a page asks for a gas-free action by name. `hana.evm.sendSponsored({chainId, calls})` → `{transactionHash,
  status: 'executed'}`: 1 to 8 calls, each copied into a fresh `{to, value: '0x0', data}` (the caller's objects are never
  sent: they could change after the check, and the port refuses shared objects), `value` left out or 0 (`0`, `0n`,
  `'0'`, `'0x0'`), `data` a function call of 4 to 8192 bytes; checked synchronously and sent in the same tick, so the
  approval window opens in the click (D99). Refused before anything is sent: a malformed call (-32602), logged out
  (4100), a chain the vault didn't report (4100 `chain_not_sponsored`, the plain sentence). `hana.evm.sponsorship(chainId)`
  → `{available, reason?, remainingToday?}` from `GET /v1/evm/sponsor/status` (a chain the vault didn't report answers
  `chain_not_enabled` with no request). `hana.evm.sponsoredChains`: the vault's `ready` list (a build property). Errors
  are `HanaSponsorError` (a `HanaError`) whose `data` keeps only exact-shape fields (`status`, `reason`, `requestId`,
  `retryAfterS`, `transactionHash`, `callIndex`, `retryable`, `chainId`), D788's style.
- EIP-5792 (checked against the EIP's current text, 2026-11-18: version "2.0.0", `wallet_sendCalls` params `{version,
  id?, from?, chainId, atomicRequired, calls, capabilities?}` → `{id, capabilities?}`, `wallet_getCallsStatus` → `{version,
  id, chainId, status, atomic, receipts?}` with 100 pending, 200 confirmed, 400 offchain failure, 500 reverted, 600
  partial; `wallet_getCapabilities([address, chainIds?])` keyed by hex chain id, `atomic.status` `supported` | `ready` |
  `unsupported`; errors 5700 unsupported non-optional capability, 5710 unsupported chain, 5720 duplicate id, 5730 unknown
  bundle, 5740 bundle too large; a capability is optional only with `optional: true`): `wallet_sendCalls` runs the batch
  as one `sendSponsored` (atomic: the delegate reverts the whole batch on any failed call), only on a configured chain
  the vault sponsors (5710 otherwise), honours an app's own `id` (5720 for a repeat) or makes a random one, refuses any
  capability not marked optional (5700), more than 8 calls (5740), value, a contract creation; resolves once the batch
  ran. `wallet_getCallsStatus` reads the receipt from the page's own RPC for that chain: 100 until it has it, then 200 (or
  500 for status 0) with `{logs, status, blockHash, blockNumber, gasUsed, transactionHash}`; 5730 for an id this page
  didn't send (256 remembered). `wallet_getCapabilities`: `{atomic: {status: 'supported'}}` on those chains, nothing
  elsewhere (unsupported chains omitted, as the EIP says). No `paymasterService` (ERC-7677) is offered: Journear's relayer
  is not an app-chosen paymaster. viem 2.57.7's own `sendCalls`, `getCapabilities` and `getCallsStatus` run against it in
  the e2e suite.
- Never transparent: `eth_sendTransaction` stays the ordinary path (the user's own fee). Why (the Tech Lead's point): a
  sponsored action is a different thing for the user (one approval that may set up the account, Journear pays) and
  for the page (allowlisted calls only, no value); silently turning a transaction into one would change what the user
  approves and what the page gets back (a relayer's hash, not the user's own transaction).
- Not mirrored in `@hana-id/react` (its hooks don't mirror `hana.near` either): `useHana().client?.evm`.
- Version: 0.5.0 (a minor: new API), the version `EVM_SPONSOR_SDK_MIN` names. The guide's install lines and the READMEs
  name the 0.5.0 tarballs (the doc test asks for the package version); the release notes say it isn't published yet.
- Address impact: none.

Settled while building: the ABI name of `execute`'s second parameter is `nonce_` (it would shadow the `nonce()` getter; names are not part of the selector or the encoding); added, nothing changed: `eip712Domain()` (ERC-5267, `fields` 0x1f), `NonceIncremented(uint256 newNonce)` from the earlier contract, OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall()` (seen only inside a `CallFailed` reason), the ERC-721/1155 receiver functions, `isValidSignature`, `supportsInterface`, `receive()`. The WP1 vector's `contract` block matches all of it (`test/Vectors.t.sol` checks it first).

The package has no `test` script, so `pnpm -r test` never needs Foundry.
- Deployment (not done here): the deterministic deployment proxy `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C` (CREATE2), salt `keccak256("hana-id/evm-delegate/HanaDelegateExecutor/v1")` → `0xfC5e59d87a21045E5A480cFD75fcf1b010e8e4AA`, runtime code hash `0xfcc832fe6c7167e0d45589881b103fed92b3a44fe3dd5d489f43e9d44b1e5fd2`; `CheckIn` with `keccak256("hana-id/evm-delegate/CheckIn/v1")` → `0xa84BBd91a395ae028eE2890DcA0e20570C1Aa39e`, `0x807946bfc8ed8e9b3fe9ef6bdeed6c9dfa519084bcda4a5b17c2059c96d0bb56`. Anyone can deploy the same code to the same address on any chain and check it from the source. **Any change to the code, the compiler settings or OpenZeppelin moves the implementation's address and hash**: say so on the branch, and update every pinned copy (the core signer's table, the manifest's `delegate`).
- Checked-in outputs: `artifacts/<name>.json` (`contractName`, `source`, `license`, `compiler`, `create2` {deployer, saltLabel, salt, initCodeHash, address}, `runtimeCodeHash` (of the code at that address, the immutable filled in), `eip712` (the delegate's name, version, salt and type strings), `abi`, `bytecode`, `deployedBytecode`, `immutableReferences`), written by `pnpm --filter @hana-id/evm-delegate run generate`. `test/Artifacts.t.sol` fails when they are stale and deploys both through the proxy (Foundry's test chain has its canonical code; the test checks it) to prove the address, the code hash and that the deployed code is the artifact's with only the immutable filled; `generate.mjs --check` compares every byte (the ABI too) and that the README's table quotes both addresses and hashes.
- The test vector: `test/vectors/execute-v1.json` is a byte-for-byte copy of the TypeScript signer's `packages/core/test/vectors/evm-sponsor-v1.json` (WP1, branch `feat/evm-sponsor-core`, generated there with viem only): **the core file is the source**. `test/Vectors.t.sol` checks the `contract` block against the contract (type hashes, function, selector), recomputes each case's domain separator, struct hash, digest, RFC 6979 signature and calldata, and runs the calldata from the vector's relayer against the contract deployed at the case's implementation (`deployCodeTo`, so the immutable salt is that address), CheckIn where a call is `checkIn()`, the value case funded. `test_vector_isTheCoreFile` and `generate.mjs --check` fail if the copies differ or the core file is missing (`generate` copies the core file over).
- Verify: a new step `evm` in phase 1, a lane of its own beside the typecheck and the Rust contract: `forge fmt --check`, `forge test`, `node scripts/generate.mjs --check`, in `contracts/evm-delegate`. It runs when a file there, the lockfile, the core vector or the CI and verify definitions change, never in `--quick`; without `forge` on the PATH, or before `pnpm install`, it is skipped and the summary says why (the browsers and cargo-near are the other optional toolchains). `classify` no longer counts `contracts/evm-delegate/` as Rust or web, so an EVM-only change doesn't run the Rust lanes. CI is off (D387): there is no CI job for it; add one (Foundry's toolchain action pinned to a commit) when CI is turned back on, before mainnet. Done 2026-11-18 (D857, branch `chore/ci-on-next`): CI's `evm` job, gated on `evmChanged`, runs the same three commands with Foundry 1.5.1 from its release tarball, checksum-verified against a sha256 pinned in the workflow; it runs once the Tech Lead switches CI on.
- Why: pnpm over git submodules (an extra init in every clone and worktree, gitlinks in `git ls-files`), soldeer (a second registry and lock that `pnpm audit` doesn't see) or vendoring (forge-std is about 1 MB); the npm package named `forge-std` is not its authors', hence GitHub. CREATE2 through the standard proxy, so the address is predictable, the same on every chain and checkable by anyone. MIT so that the code holding authority over a user's account can be read, verified and reused.
- Explorer verification: the metadata is stripped, so a Sourcify exact (full) match is not available; verify with the standard-JSON input (`forge verify-contract`, or `forge build --build-info`) and the settings above (README "Deployment").
- After the independent audit (2026-11-17, no Critical or High; fit to merge and to deploy on Base Sepolia for testing): `isValidSignature` also accepts the 64-byte ERC-2098 compact form (D845), which changed the bytecode, so the address and code hash above are the new ones (the first build's were `0x9Da1…b762` / `0x710d…26ba`, pinned nowhere). More tests (the gas floor at its exact boundary, a target that swallows an inner out-of-gas, the authorization in the same transaction, 1 to 8 calls of any data length, value running out partway, a failing call after others with the cap), measured gas numbers in the README for the relayer's budget, and the duties checklist.
- Rejected: `relayer` = zero meaning anyone (D845); a separate deploy script here (the deploy is a later package; `ArtifactsTest` already deploys through the proxy locally).
