  `sponsoredApprovalContent`. `StatusResult` (and `ready`) may carry `sponsoredChains`: 1 to 4 ascending distinct chain
  IDs, sent only to an SDK of `EVM_SPONSOR_SDK_MIN` (0.5.0) or later. The limits are copied in `protocol.ts` (the root
  entry must not reach `@hana-id/core/evm-sponsor`) and a test keeps them equal. Until the vault's handler exists, the
  vault answers it 4200 (`SPONSORED_NOT_YET`) before anything else. (Replaced by the vault's flow, D855.)
- The popup trusts neither the page nor the vault's framing: it decodes the subject bytes itself
  (`decodeApprovalRequest(subject, { sponsorChains: env.evmSponsor })`, the build's own manifest) and offers no Approve
  ("Journear can’t read this request, so it can’t be approved.") unless the subject decodes strictly (D846: value 0,
  no call to the zero address, the account or the delegate, 1 to 8 calls, one encoding per subject), names the
  context's chain, that chain is sponsored by this build, its delegate is the pinned, non-placeholder
  `SPONSOR_DELEGATES` entry and the build's, its relayer is the build's, its account is the request's address, and
  every call has at least 4 bytes of calldata. The deadline (amended after PR 72's review): refused when it is more
  than 2 hours ahead of the popup's clock or more than 5 minutes past it (`SPONSOR_DEADLINE_AHEAD_MAX_S`,
  `SPONSOR_DEADLINE_PAST_MAX_S`; the manifest allows at most an hour, the margins absorb a drifting clock), and refused
  without a clock; the vault and the API check the exact window against server time and the contract enforces it. Not
  checked by the popup, shown in the details instead: `minGas` (the vault's simulation, D845's duties), the app's
  allowlist (the popup can't see it; the API enforces it).
- The summary: each call goes through the same `evmCall` as an ordinary transaction's call, so every spend warning,
  "can't tell" line and verified-name rule applies unchanged. One call: exactly the summary an EIP-1559 transaction
  with that call gets (headline, lines, warnings, explainable; tested for every known signature, an unknown selector
  and undecodable arguments), with the fee row "none. Journear pays it for you." instead of a maximum fee. Several:
  "{App} wants to do N things in one transaction", grouped by D814 (at most four lines; a group is identical calls,
  same line, target and calldata; a grant's line is its warning's bullet, which names the spender and the amount; a
  call's own extra lines, such as an amount in smallest units, follow its line); order value to others, grants, calls
  (and every call Journear can't read), other value, moves to the user's own account, take-backs. One red "can't tell"
  line for the batch: the call's own when one kind is unreadable, else "part of it is something Journear can’t
  summarise". Every call counts as moving value (a call can move tokens the account holds), so a left-out call makes
  the "not all listed" line red, and a left-out one to someone else or a grant has its own bullet. Nothing is said
  about ETH leaving: a sponsored call carries no value. The setup note is amber, code `account_setup`, ranked after
  the can't-tell, not-listed and spend-permission lines in the amber box, and present exactly when the subject
  carries an authorization nonce.
- What a hostile page gains from free transactions (the question put to this package): (1) the fee as a brake is gone:
  an account with no ETH could run no on-chain call before, and now can run sponsored ones; a page can ask again and
  again at no cost to itself; (2) "Journear pays it for you" may read as Journear vouching for the request.
  Concluded: no extra visible line. The window is exactly as alarming as for the same unsponsored call (tested), every
  request needs its own guarded Approve and is never auto-approved (D36, D839), and the API sponsors only calls staff
  allowlisted for that app (target, selector, exact calldata, value 0; D835) within per-user and per-app limits (D836),
  so a hostile page gets free calls only to contracts reviewed for its own app. The fee was a weak brake for this
  audience (they don't know what gas is) and protected only users without ETH. A standing "free doesn't mean safe" line
  on every sponsored approval would sit on harmless check-ins and dilute the warnings that matter (D809, D814's one
  box per colour). To revisit if an app's allowlist ever takes a selector that grants or moves tokens (`approve`,
  `transfer`, `permit`, `setApprovalForAll`): proposed rule, such a selector needs the Tech Lead's sign-off in the
  manifest change. Raw signing after the setup: it could sign an Execute digest (D833), but it could already sign any
  transaction's hash, so the setup adds no exposure.
- Also on this branch (D810 amended): a NEAR standard value-moving call with arguments that aren't exactly the
  standard's is red and not explained, and a NEAR call Journear doesn't recognise whose name says it may move value gets
  an amber line. The sponsored EVM path needs no counterpart: an EVM call whose calldata doesn't decode exactly against
  a known signature is already "can't tell" (red).
- Known effect: the demo's `checkIn()` is not a selector Journear knows, so its approval carries the red "can't tell"
  line, as the same call unsponsored would. Making it calm is a separate decision (the CheckIn contract and its
  function on Journear's verified list, the demo card's package): made by the user 2026-11-18, D854.
- Address impact: none.
- Amended 2026-11-19 by D877: the fee row reads "Free. Journear pays it for you." ("Free." in bold after a check
  mark), and the local chain is "Local test network".

### D851. The EVM relayer object: simplified and fail-stop (on anything odd it stops and waits for staff)
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: the simplified fail-stop relayer replacing D837's self-repairing design **decided by the
  user 2026-11-18**, the PR (75) confirmed by the user 2026-11-18; the details below decided while building and amended
  after its independent review the same day (marked "Review"), **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18**; item 16 (fee refusals, branch
  `fix/evm-relayer-fee-refusals`) decided while fixing an automated review of the merged code, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (with items 17 and 18) · Built (not deployed; nothing calls it yet: the handlers are PR 71's):
  `apps/api/src/evm-relayer.ts` (`EvmRelayer`; its header states the whole design), `apps/api/src/evm-relayer-staff.ts`
  (the staff tools, for the admin package), `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-chain.ts` (`SponsorChain`), `apps/api/src/env.ts`
  (`EVM_RELAYER`, `EVM_SPONSOR_RPC_<chainId>`), `apps/api/src/index.ts` (the export), `apps/api/src/log.ts` (`chainId`,
  `evmTx`, `evmOps`), `apps/api/scripts/gen-wrangler.ts` (`durableObjectsConfig`); tests
  `apps/api/test/evm-relayer.test.ts` (the review's probes ported as tests), `evm-sponsor-chain.test.ts`, `evm-mock.ts`,
  `apps/api/scripts/test/evm-relayer-staff.test.ts`, `gen-evm-sponsor.test.ts`, `gen-wrangler.test.ts`. Current state:
  `docs/architecture.md` "EVM sponsored actions: the relayer object", `docs/security.md` "The EVM relayer object",
  `docs/operations.md` "EVM sponsorship relay (not live)". Note (D843, 2026-11-18): the staff methods are now reached
  through `AdminRpc` only (`rpc/admin.ts` imports the staff module's three admin-view functions, from staff-only
  methods; the source test's allowlist names it); the admin portal's "Free network fees" page runs them. After D843's
  re-check, a pause carries `leakSeen` when a leak-type condition or a staff Close/Fill/AdoptNonce is seen during it,
  and `staffResume(…, keyConfirmed)` refuses `key_confirmation_required` on such a pause without the confirmation.
- Principle (the user's): do the few things that are safe on our own evidence; on anything odd STOP, raise it in
  `status()`, wait for staff. When unsure whether money was spent, keep the reservation. Nothing in the user's account
  (its code, storage, or logs not from our own transaction hashes) is evidence. Review: no halt may be triggerable by
  a user's request; a nonce, once signed, is never given up.
- Interface (pinned; the handlers code against it; bigints as bigints over Workers RPC): `send({ chainId, execute,
  signature, authorization?, gas, maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas, reservedWei })` → `{ digest, transactionHash,
  relayerNonce, raw: Hex | null, replay, broadcast: 'accepted'|'rejected'|'unknown', rejection: null | { cause:
  'request'|'pricing'|'relayer', code } }` (`raw` null on a replay of a final batch; `broadcast: 'rejected'`: no
  endpoint took the batch and its cancel took the nonce, so don't wait for its receipt; `rejection.cause: 'pricing'`:
  the handler's fees were turned away, reprice and let the user retry; `'relayer'`: our fault; neither charges the
  user a failure); a send priced below the latest base fee × 1.125, or with no tip, is refused `fees_too_low`
  (nothing sent); `lookup(digest)` → `{ digest, relayerNonce, transactionHash, hashes, state:
  'pending'|'cancelling'|'mined'|'closed', minedHash, outcome: 'execute'|'cancel'|'consumed_elsewhere'|null, costWei,
  reservedWei } | null` (kept 7 days after a record is final); `status()` → `{ address, unmined, awaitingConfirmation,
  oldestUnminedMs, nextNonce, halted: null | { reason, since, nonce?, code? } }` (`code` for `relayer_cannot_send`). Errors `Error('evm_relayer:<code>[:<reason>]')`
  (`evmRelayerError`), `relayer_busy:account` for a second unmined batch of one account; a coded error means that call
  sent nothing.
- Evidence: ONE trusted read endpoint (the secret `EVM_SPONSOR_RPC_<chainId>` when set, else the manifest's `rpc`) for
  counts, receipts and blocks; `rpcFallback` (and `rpc`, when the keyed URL is the read one) receive the same raw
  transactions only. No voting, no cross-checks. Confirmed depth: the `safe` block, else head − 12.
- A record is final only by a receipt of ONE OF ITS OWN versions at confirmed depth with the confirmed count past its
  nonce (`mined`, with `minedHash`, `outcome` and the receipt's cost, L1 and operator fees included), or by
  `staffClose(consumed_elsewhere)` (`closed`). A receipt short of that is only `seen`; a reorg (the latest count falls
  to its nonce) un-sees it and the stored raw goes out again. Each unmined record is re-broadcast, bumped after 60 s
  (× 1.125 within the caps, at most 7 batch versions) or replaced by a 0-value self-transfer (the cancel, the 8th
  version) past its deadline or once the batch is definitely refused; every version's hash and raw kept until final.
- Halts (state `halted`, a reason; new sends `relayer_halted`; everything above continues): `nonce_consumed_elsewhere`,
  `nonce_gap`, `foreign_transactions`, `relayer_cannot_send` (a refusal only we can cause, with its code), `stuck_past_deadline`,
  `key_mismatch`, `storage_inconsistent` (the header has each rule, its evidence and why no user can cause it). Nothing
  clears a halt by itself; `staffResume` clears it only after a fresh run finds none of them.
- Staff tools (on the object, reached only through `evm-relayer-staff.ts`; a source test keeps every other file in
  `apps/api/src`, the handlers under `src/evm/` and the routes included, from naming them): `staffStatus`,
  `staffResume`, `staffClose(nonce, 'consumed_elsewhere')`, `staffCancel(nonce)`, `staffFill(nonce)`,
  `staffAdoptNonce(n)`; each acting one takes `who` and a note, re-reads the chain, refuses unsafe use, and is recorded
  (who, when, what, note, done or why refused). They return `{ done, refused, status }`.
- Details decided while building (**confirmed by the user 2026-11-18**):
  1. Review (H1): the object computes the transaction's intrinsic gas (21 000, calldata at 4 a token and at least
     EIP-7623's 10 a token, 25 000 per authorization; no access list is ever sent) and refuses (`invalid_request`) a
     gas below it plus `minGas`, and a raw transaction over 128 KiB, before anything is stored. Not checked here: the
     fee against the current base fee (it needs a fresh read; the handlers set the fee from one, and a fee refusal is
     covered by the next item).
  2. Review (H1): a definite refusal of the batch at send gets its cancel signed at the same nonce at once (persisted
     first), both versions kept, and the caller is told `broadcast: 'rejected'` and `rejection: { cause, code }`. A
     batch refused later (never accepted) gets its cancel on the next run. Re-review (N1): each classified refusal has
     an explicit cause (`REJECTION_CAUSE`; a test enumerates every code): `request` (`gas_limit`, `oversized`: the
     batch's own size or shape) only cancels, so no user can halt the relayer; `relayer` (`insufficient_funds`,
     `nonce_too_low`, `nonce_too_high`, `invalid_transaction`) cancels AND halts `relayer_cannot_send` with the code,
     as does any refusal of our own cancel (item 16 moved the fee codes to `pricing`); otherwise a short-funded relayer would fail every user quietly. An unclassified error is not a refusal
     (`unknown`: the node may hold it). `relayer_cannot_send` replaces the first review's `rejected_unsent`. The
     `rejected` error code stays in the type and is never thrown.
  3. Later, `nonce too low` for a record never accepted does not count as a refusal (it can be our own copy mined
     between the count read and the broadcast); the receipt rule settles it at confirmed depth.
  4. "Stays so" for `nonce_gap` is the same gap seen on two alarm runs in a row (a counter, no clock).
  5. A missing key halts nothing (it is the off switch): nothing is signed, stored transactions are still broadcast and
     checked. A key whose address is not `relayerAddress`, or not the address the records were signed by, halts
     (`key_mismatch`) while records exist. With no records, a new key starts a new nonce life by itself: its own
     pending count, read once.
  6. Review (M2, M3): `staffClose(never_sent)` is removed (closing, adopting and resuming could sign a second batch at
     a nonce whose old raw could still land). In its place `staffCancel(n)`: a record with no receipt whose nonce
     isn't mined at head gets a cancel version (bumped fees), old versions kept; it then resolves by receipt like any
     other. A nonce is never freed. `staffAdoptNonce(n)` refuses n below `nextNonce` (so it is always above every
     record) and needs no unmined record and the chain's latest and pending counts both n.
  7. `staffFill(n)` only at the chain's next nonce (pending count == n, latest ≤ n), with no record at n and n below
     `nextNonce`; the filler is an ordinary record (bumped, checked) with no batch.
  8. `staffResume` also refuses while a record past the confirmed count could not be fully checked (`incomplete_check`).
     `staffStatus` is not recorded (it takes no `who`); refusals are. The last 200 staff actions are kept, 50 shown.
  9. The daily backstop counts each send's reservation with its gas at the fee cap (so a bump never needs
     accounting), settles it to the receipt's cost at confirmation; `consumed_elsewhere` keeps it. 2 × `dailyBudgetEth`
     a UTC day.
  10. `lookup` gives `minedHash`, `outcome` and `costWei` only once `mined`; before that its `transactionHash` is the
      version seen mined, else the latest. Review (storage): a final batch keeps hashes only, never a raw transaction.
  11. The object's internals are JavaScript-private (`#`), so a Workers RPC stub reaches only the public methods; the
      staff methods also need the guard held by the staff module.
  12. Bounds: 8 unmined and 64 records (`relayer_busy`), one unmined batch per account (review M1: the delegate's
      batch nonce is sequential, so a second one can only revert or stall; the handlers add per-app caps and the
      type-4 checks), 16 sends waiting, 8 versions, 45 fetches, 20 receipt reads and 4 signatures a run, 50 000
      remembered batches; the alarm 15 s after a change, doubling to 5 minutes, and review (L3) hourly with no records,
      so `foreign_transactions` surfaces before the next send.
  13. Review (L1): finality needs the confirmed count past the nonce as well as a receipt at confirmed depth, so a
      fabricated receipt alone finalizes nothing. Known limit: an endpoint lying about both the receipt and the counts
      can still finalize a transaction that never landed; the honest counts later halt the relayer (`nonce_gap`), and
      the wrongly settled cost stays wrong (a test shows it).
  14. Review (M4): the relayer's address is derived once per isolate (cached under sha256 of the key, never the key).
      Each send, run and staff call logs `evmOps` (signatures, recoveries, fetches, key derivations: counts, no
      timings). Whether a cold first send stays under the free plan's 10 ms CPU is to be measured at deploy, from those
      counts and Cloudflare's own CPU time per invocation.
  15. Out of scope here (the handlers', PR 71): the account's code check, the simulation, the `Executed` check, the
      L1-fee reservation, the allowlist and per-app caps. The object re-checks the Execute itself (`verifySend`,
      exported and tested as a table).
  16. Fee refusals (branch `fix/evm-relayer-fee-refusals`, confirmed by the user 2026-11-18; amended after its review the same day): a
      batch's fees are the handler's, so a batch refused over its fees is not the relayer broken: `underpriced`,
      `fee_below_base_fee` and `replacement_underpriced` of a BATCH version are cause `pricing` (a third cause): its
      cancel at once, no halt, `rejection: { cause: 'pricing', code }`. Exception: `replacement_underpriced` on a
      batch's FIRST version is cause `relayer` (nothing of ours holds that nonce, so another sender with our key does)
      and halts `relayer_cannot_send` with that code. Before anything is stored, the object reads the latest base fee
      from the trusted endpoint (once per 5 s per instance; a failed read is `rpc_unavailable`) and refuses
      `fees_too_low` when `maxFeePerGas` is below base fee × 1.125 (one block's largest rise) or the tip is below 1 wei
      (geth's default price limit). Cancels and fillers are priced by the relayer from a FRESH base fee (the run's own
      block read; at send a new read): tip max(1.125 × the previous, 0.001 gwei), max fee max(1.125 × the previous,
      2 × base fee + tip), within the caps; when the caps leave no valid one (below base fee × 1.125, or under the
      nodes' +10% over the previous) the relayer halts `relayer_cannot_send` with code `fee_cap_too_low` (staffCancel
      and staffFill refuse with it). A cancel or filler refused over its price is repriced on the next run (no halt;
      `stuck_past_deadline` covers a persistent case); refused for any other reason (funds, nonce, signer) it halts.
      Consequence: a send needs the read endpoint (with it down, sends are refused `rpc_unavailable`; the handlers need
      it anyway). The handlers map `fees_too_low` and `pricing` to 503 `gas_price_too_high` with a short `retryAfterS`,
      everything given back, no failure charged.
      Narrowed (branch `fix/evm-relayer-halt-narrowing`, after an automated review of the merged code, confirmed by the user 2026-11-18):
      (a) a refusal halts only on our own evidence: the trusted read endpoint itself refused (`byRead` in the
      broadcast's answer); a relayer-cause refusal heard only from the fallback cancels the batch, halts nothing, and
      is counted for staff (`staffStatus().unconfirmedRefusal`: count, last time, nonce, code; log
      `evm_relay_refusal_unconfirmed`). (b) A first version's `replacement_underpriced` is the relayer's (halt) only
      when the read endpoint said so AND its pending count shows something past the nonce; otherwise it is `pricing`
      (cancel priced fresh, no halt, counted). (c) `fee_cap_too_low` only for a version that is REQUIRED and impossible
      (a staff cancel, a first cancel or a reprice of a record nothing accepted); a routine bump the caps stop is no new
      version (the latest is broadcast again), and a record an endpoint accepted never raises it.
  17. One unmined batch per account, checked on demand (branch `fix/evm-relayer-account-next`, from integrating the
      API, confirmed by the user 2026-11-18): when an account's earlier batch is still unmined in storage, `send` makes ONE bounded check of
      it inside the critical section on the run's own evidence (the trusted endpoint's latest count past its nonce,
      then its versions' receipts: at most 1 + 8 extra fetches, within the 45 a send may use) and, when that shows it
      mined, marks it `seen` and lets the new batch through; otherwise, or when a read fails, `relayer_busy:account` as
      before (the first batch is untouched). Finality (confirmed depth), nonce order and the caps are unchanged. A reorg
      after the second batch was let through: the first goes back to unmined and is broadcast again, and the relayer's
      nonce order (the first's nonce below the second's) keeps the account's two batches in order, so normally both
      land. Only if the first then never lands (cancelled past its deadline) does the second reach the account with
      the wrong batch nonce: the delegate reverts it (InvalidNonce), and the sponsor pays one reverted transaction.
      Accepted: rare (a reorg of an L2 block plus a lost first batch), bounded, and visible in the receipts.
  18. An unaccepted batch never holds the relayer up (branch `fix/evm-relayer-unaccepted-first`, after the API and
      relayer review, confirmed by the user 2026-11-18). A user could keep their own account's transactions waiting in the pools so that
      ours, a type-4 carrying their authorization, is refused with a text the relayer didn't know ("authority already
      reserved"), leaving our nonce in no pool and every later sponsored transaction (all apps) waiting behind it until
      the batch's deadline. Now: (a) the pools' EIP-7702 texts are classified (checked in go-ethereum's and op-geth's
      txpool source: `authority already reserved` → `authority_reserved`, cause `request`, cancelled at once;
      `in-flight transaction limit reached for delegated accounts`, `gapped-nonce tx from delegated accounts` and
      `address already reserved`, which concern the SENDER, our relayer, → `sender_restricted`, cause `relayer`), and a
      classified refusal is definite even when its text says "limit"; (b) whatever the text, a batch no endpoint ever
      took is broadcast again on each run and is replaced by its cancel before its deadline only when, on TWO
      consecutive runs, none of those broadcasts was taken and the trusted endpoint's pending count equalled its nonce
      (it is in no pool we can see), AND a later record is waiting behind it (its nonce below `nextNonce` − 1). With
      nothing behind it, nothing is blocked, so it is left to the deadline's cancel. (Amended after PR 86's review: a
      provider whose node keeps no pool and forwards to the sequencer never moves its pending count, so one run is no
      evidence; a definite classified refusal such as `authority_reserved` still cancels at once.) Owed before
      enabling, measured on Base Sepolia with the chosen read provider: (1) does `eth_getTransactionCount(pending)`
      rise between `eth_sendRawTransaction` and inclusion (send a low-tip transaction so it waits); (2) does re-sending
      the same raw answer "already known". If either is no, revisit this rule. Safe on
      our own evidence: the cancel takes the same nonce, so whichever lands ends the record by its receipt and the user's
      batch simply doesn't run; no halt. (c) The alarm never backs off while a record is unmined and untaken (15 s).
      (d) `status().oldestUnacceptedMs` gives the oldest untaken record's age for an alert. (e) `send` answers a coded
      refusal as a value, `{ ok: false, refused, reason }`, instead of throwing it: workerd reports any exception
      thrown from a Durable Object's RPC method as an uncaught rejection even when the caller handles it (shown with a
      probe), which filled the logs with `relayer_busy`, `relayer_halted` and the like. The API package must read the
      value (`ok`) instead of catching; anything still thrown is unknown, as before. `lookup`, `status` and the staff
      tools keep throwing their rare coded errors (malformed input, misconfiguration).
- Amended 2026-11-18 (branch `fix/deploy-check-sponsor-rpc`, decided while building, to confirm): the trusted read
  endpoint is **enforced** outside `local*` envs, not only documented as required. (a) The API: `evmSponsorReady`
  returns nothing (every route `503 sponsorship_unconfigured`, the 15-minute cron's relayer checks skipped, as with
  sponsorship off) unless each sponsored chain has `EVM_SPONSOR_RPC_<chainId>` holding an https URL
  (`keyedSponsorRpc`, the same rule `sponsorRpcEndpoints` already used); it logs `evm_sponsor_config`
  `evm_sponsor_rpc_missing` with `chainIds`, never a URL, once per isolate. `local*` envs (the e2e stack, the tests)
  are unchanged and still read `rpc` without it. (b) `deploy-check`'s `evm` group asks wrangler for the API Worker's
  secret NAMES (`wrangler secret list --name <worker> --format json` from `apps/api`; Cloudflare never returns a
  value) and FAILS, naming the secret, the upload command and go-live step 4.12, for each sponsored chain without it;
  an unlisted answer (not logged in, no generated config) fails too. Not changed: the relayer object itself
  (`#context`, `sponsorRpcEndpoints`) still falls back to `rpc` when the secret is deleted while it holds sent
  transactions, so it keeps following them up (cancels, re-broadcasts) rather than stopping mid-flight; no new action
  reaches it meanwhile. Why: a forgotten upload would otherwise run a deployed env on the public endpoint, which the
  relayer then believes, silently. `gen` output unchanged.
- Rejected: everything D837 used to repair itself (several endpoints' agreement, verdicts from the user's account, a
  record moved to a new nonce, gap fills on a timer, per-run budgets that defer a verdict); a stored halt for an RPC
  outage (the run just tries later); review: freeing a nonce by any staff tool, and halting on a refusal the user's
  input could have caused; re-review: treating every refusal alike (either users can halt it, or our own faults go
  unnoticed).
- Address impact: none.
- Amended by D890 (2026-11-23, decided by the Tech Lead): "Nothing clears a halt by itself" has one exception. A pause
  for money (`relayer_cannot_send` · `insufficient_funds`) ends by itself on an alarm run once the wallet is refilled,
  only when every check of D890 passes (not `leakSeen`; the run's own verdict is staffResume's; the counts explained by
  our own records; no code at the relayer's address; the one other endpoint agreeing; at most 3 a UTC day, never within
  30 minutes of the last one); recorded as a staff action and raised as `evm_relay_auto_resumed`. Every other reason
  still waits for staffResume, which is unchanged. The "no voting, no cross-checks" rule above holds for all evidence;
  the other endpoint's answer can only hold the automatic restart back.

## Plain words and the demo check-in, 2026-11-18

### D853. Every user-visible text is written in plain, everyday words (standing rule)
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-18** · Applies to every text a user sees: the approval
  window, Passport Home, the login and email pages, the launcher, errors shown to users, the demo sites, the partner
  SDK's default texts.
- Decision, in the Tech Lead's words: "our audience is not native Web3 users and might be very non-technical savvy so we
  want to keep it as simple and as layman as possible (remember this style for all future wordings)". So: say what
  happens to the user's money, tokens or account in everyday words; no chain jargon above the fold (gas, nonce,
  calldata, selector, contract call, EIP numbers, "upgrade", "smart account"), which may appear only in the folded
  details; short sentences; name the app and what it wants first. Technical precision is kept, one tap away in the
  details, never dropped. A wording that would make a risk sound smaller than it is never counts as plainer (D809).
- Where it lives: `docs/security.md` "Browser" (the approval window's wording rules), and this entry for everything
  else. Reviews of user-visible text check against it.
- Applied to the approval window on 2026-11-18 (branch `feat/plain-approval-wording`, from `next`; decided by the user
  2026-11-18 when they approved rewording everything an end user reads; the texts decided while building, to

## EVM gas sponsorship: the vault and the SDK (branch `feat/evm-sponsor-vault`), 2026-11-18

### D855. The vault's sponsored action: the build decides, prepare's answer is checked hints, one approval, the vault sends
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: the vault submits (D832), one approval (D831), never auto-approved (D839), delegated
  elsewhere refused (D840) decided by the user earlier; everything below decided while building, **confirmed by the
  user 2026-11-18**; the amendments after the independent review of PR 76 and its re-check (the account's setup read by
  the vault, both endpoints for a setup and `rpcFallback` required outside `local*` envs, the setup's own failure text,
  the cross-tab slot, the 50,000-per-call floor, the copied bytes, the capped read) amended while building, to confirm · Built on
  `feat/evm-sponsor-vault`, not merged, not deployed: `packages/web/src/vault/evm-sponsor.ts` (`sponsorChains`,
  `sponsorPreflight`, `parsePrepareAnswer`, `sponsorSubject`, `sponsoredApproval`, `approvedSubject`, `signSponsored`,
  `sendBody`, `parseSendAnswer`, `withSessionProof`, `sponsorApiError`, `SponsorFlights`, `SPONSOR_TEXT`), `vault.ts`
  (`sponsorEarly`, `sendSponsored`, `sponsoredField`), `api.ts` (`evmSponsor`), `signing.ts` (`SPONSORED_ELSEWHERE`,
  replacing D850's `SPONSORED_NOT_YET`); tests `packages/web/test/vault/evm-sponsor.test.ts`; e2e
  `apps/e2e/tests/evm-sponsor.spec.ts` against the TEST-ONLY stand-in `apps/e2e/src/server/sponsor-standin.ts`.
- The chains: only the build's (`HanaEnv.evmSponsor`), each checked again at start (`sponsorChains`: a canonical chain
  ID of a test network, a local chain only in a `local*` build, the pinned non-placeholder delegate, a valid relayer
  that isn't the delegate). They are the signers' `enabledChains` and the status's `sponsoredChains`, sent only to an
  SDK of 0.5.0 or later.
- Before any window or API call: a test app on a mainnet (`mainnet_not_allowed`), a chain not in the list, a call to the
  account, the delegate or the relayer, another action of the account in flight.
- Prepare's answer is hints: read strictly; its relayer and implementation must equal the build's or nothing is shown
  (the subject always names the build's); `delegation: 'other'` refused even with `allowed: true`; `allowed: false`
  refused with its reason (unknown reasons read as `not_available`), all before any window.
- minGas (the spec's open question): the vault signs `maxMinGas`, the highest floor the transaction cap leaves, bounded
  `minGasFloor ≤ maxMinGas ≤ 2,000,000` and at least 50,000 per call (raised from 25,000 after the review of PR 76:
  about twice a first check-in, 23,899 measured, D845). Rejected: simulating in the vault through the
  partner's RPC (untrusted: a low answer would let a call that swallows an inner out-of-gas run degraded, the only
  harm being the user's; a high one would waste budget, and the vault would need a second RPC trust story); asking the
  API for a measured figure (the API has no gas measurement today, `eth_call` gives none without tracing, and the API
  simulates at the final limit anyway). Why the highest floor is sound: the floor only makes the relayer provide gas
  (D845); the API sets the gas limit from it and simulates at exactly that limit, so a batch that can't run is refused
  before sending; the sponsor pays only the gas used, so a high floor only holds more of the day's budget in reserve
  until the receipt settles; and a lying low `maxMinGas` is refused below the per-call floor. To revisit if budgets get
  tight: the API could return a measured `suggestedMinGas` the vault takes within the same bounds. **Before mainnet
  (open):** the floor should come from the vault's own estimate through the build's endpoints. Not built now: before
  the account is set up, a call can't be estimated as the account runs it through the delegate without a state
  override (`eth_estimateGas` with overrides isn't on every node, and `eth_call` measures no gas); after it, `eth_estimateGas`
  of each call from the account works but is a second gas model beside the API's. Decide with the relayer's gas model.
- Clocks: the deadline comes from the vault's server-corrected clock (`Clock`, anchored on the API's time at render
  and every `GET /v1/app`) + min(5 minutes, `deadlineMaxS` − 60 s); refused below 2 minutes. Prepare's `serverNow` is
  used only to detect a wrong clock: the device's own (the popup's) more than 240 s off is "Your device's clock is
  wrong…" (the popup allows 5 minutes past, 2 hours ahead); the vault's more than 60 s off is `bad_answer`. After the
  approval, under 45 s left signs nothing (`deadline_passed`). A lying `serverNow` can only cause a refusal.
- **The account's setup is read by the vault, not taken from the API** (after the independent review of PR 76, its
  Medium): the API is no longer trusted for delegation state. Before building a subject the vault reads the account's
  code and its latest and pending transaction counts itself (`readAccount`) from the chain's public endpoints in the
  build (manifest `rpc` and `rpcFallback`, generated into `HanaEnv.evmSponsor` by `evmSponsorPageChains`; the vault
  page's CSP `connect-src` names them, `apps/api/src/vault/page.ts` `sponsorRpcOrigins`; keyed RPC URLs are the
  API's secrets and never reach a page; a chain without `rpc` is not sponsored by the vault). Each endpoint's chain ID is
  checked; every endpoint that answers must agree on the code and both counts; none answering, another chain, a
  malformed value or a disagreement refuses with "Journear couldn't get this action ready" (`bad_answer`), never falling
  back to the API's word. **The one-time setup needs both endpoints** (the re-check of PR 76): an authorization is signed
  only when two configured endpoints both answered and agree, so it never rests on one provider's word (a lying endpoint
  with a lying API, the honest one unreachable, could otherwise get it signed for an account another wallet set up);
  `rpcFallback` is therefore required outside `local*` envs in the manifest schema and the Worker parser (both refuse a
  chain without it), and a `local*` build with only `rpc` may sign a setup on that one endpoint (local only). A later
  action, which signs no authorization, may go ahead with one endpoint down. Each read checks `res.ok` and reads at
  most 64 KiB of body as a stream before parsing (8 s each). Privacy: those providers see the account's address and the
  user's IP address (security.md, beside the demo balance read). `setupNonce`: no code → the authorization, only when the API said
  `none` and latest == pending == its `accountNonce` (a future nonce would stay usable on a gasless account; a pending
  transaction may consume it); exactly `0xef0100 ‖ the pinned delegate` → no authorization, only when the API said
  `journear` (else `bad_answer`); any other code (another delegate, contract code) → the D840 refusal, whatever the API
  said. Why: a lying or buggy API could otherwise get an authorization signed for an account another wallet set up
  (applying it would silently replace that setup) or for a future nonce.
- Signing: the approved bytes decoded again (`approvedSubject`: compared first with a copy taken when the window was
  built, then chain, pinned delegate, relayer, account, the calls exactly, the time left); one `withChainKey` for the EVM
  key: the authorization only when the subject has an authorization nonce (from `setupNonce`), then the Execute; both
  through core's guarded signers. The send body is built from the decoded subject only.
- A failed batch that carried the setup: "The action didn’t go through. Your account’s one-time setup may still have
  been done. Nothing else changed." (`failedAfterSetup`; an applied authorization stays applied when the batch
  reverts); without the setup: "The action didn’t go through, so nothing changed."
- The answer to the page: exactly `{transactionHash (lowercase), status: 'executed'}`; any other 200 or no answer is
  `api_unavailable` `unknown_outcome`. Errors: 429 `rate_limited`, 410 `session_ended`, other 4xx 4100, 5xx and network
  `api_unavailable`; `data` = `status`, `reason`, and only exact-shape `retryAfterS` (body or header), `transactionHash`,
  `callIndex`, `retryable`; the request ID through D405.
- Concurrency: one action per account and chain, refused (`busy`, `sponsor_in_flight`), not queued: the batch nonce is
  sequential, a queued batch would be built on a nonce the first is about to use, and queueing would let a page line up
  approvals. Held across the vault origin's tabs and frames by the shared Web Lock `hana-evm-sponsor:<chain>:<account>`
  taken with `ifAvailable` (`Locks.requestIfAvailable`; after the review of PR 76), and by a set in the vault first.
  Without the Web Locks API (old browsers: `localLocks`) the slot is per frame, and the API's `nonce_stale` refuses a
  racing tab ("Your account changed…").
- The words (the Tech Lead's plain-wording rule, 2026-11-18): every refusal a page may show is one plain sentence from
  `SPONSOR_TEXT` (no gas, nonce, relayer, contract or delegate; tested), e.g. "Your account was set up by another wallet
  app, so Journear can’t pay network fees for it. Nothing was sent." (D840), "Your last action is still going through.
  Wait for it to finish, then try again.", "Your device’s clock is wrong. Set it to the right time, then try again."
- The e2e stand-in (test only, `apps/e2e`): the three routes with the vault-origin rule, the session proof (core's
  check, each nonce once), the Execute and authorization signatures, nonces; a made-up hash for `executed`; per app and
  account state, a hold switch for the concurrency test. Never in a deployed Worker.
- Address impact: none.
- Note 2026-11-19 (D885): not affected. D885's reviewed NEAR calls add no vault check, API call or network read; the
  sponsor allowlist still decides only what Journear pays for, never what the window says.

### D856. The sponsorship calls prove the user's session: a new identityMessage payload with the body's hash and the wallet proof
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: required before sponsorship is enabled anywhere (the API review's open item, D847 M2);
  the design decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18**; the API's five additions from the review of
  PR 76 amended while building, to confirm · Built on `feat/evm-sponsor-vault`: `packages/core/src/sponsor-session.ts`
  (`evmSponsorRequestHash`, `evmSponsorRequestPayload`, `evmSponsorSessionMessage`, `isEvmSponsorSessionProof`,
  `checkEvmSponsorSessionProof`, root export), the vault's `withSessionProof`; tests `packages/core/test/sponsor-session.test.ts`;
  the API's part specified in `docs/api.md` "EVM gas sponsorship: the session proof of prepare and send", not built
  (the API is PR #71's branch).
- Decision: reuse what exists rather than a new proof type: the session key's Ed25519 signature over `identityMessage`
  (signer, app, session key, `issuedAtMs`, a 16-byte nonce; ±60 s; the `identity-proof:` single-use markers;
  `checkChainSession`), with a new payload `"evm-sponsor-request"` ‖ method ‖ parent origin ‖ chain ‖ account ‖ the
  body's hash ‖ the session's EVM wallet proof (the identity token's, made at login with PRK, so no extra key use), as
  `sessionProof` in the body. The body hash is over the body's own values in a fixed JSON array (no canonicalisation
  question: the API hashes what it parsed), so a proof is for one route, one body, one origin, one app.
- Why the wallet proof: the session signature alone says "this session asked"; the wallet proof (the account's own key
  over this session key and app) says the account is the session's, without a directory read, so the API can refuse
  any other address before any window or chain read. The directory rule (`requireKnownAccount`) adds that the
  account's directory user is the session's path's root.
- The API's check, with the independent review of PR 76's additions (docs/api.md has them): the method from the route
  path, never the body; act only on the parsed object that was hashed (duplicate JSON keys refused, never re-reading the
  raw body); `chainId` a safe positive integer before hashing; the single-use marker kept at least the whole ±60 s
  window either side; for send, the Execute and authorization signers recovered against the body's account and an
  authorization to anything but the pinned delegate refused, as before (the proof binds the session to the body, the
  signatures the account's key to the batch).
- Rejected: a header (`x-hana-session-proof`) with a hash of the raw body (a CORS change on every route, and the other
  proofs are in bodies); a separate signature per field; the EVM key signing each request (a key use per call).
- Address impact: none.
- Note 2026-11-19 (D885): not affected (no new route or proof).

## CI back on for `next`, at no cost (branch `chore/ci-on-next`), 2026-11-18

### D857. CI ready to switch on for `next`, free while the repository is public; the Tech Lead switches it on
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (decided by the user 2026-11-18: CI back on for
  `next`; it must cost nothing; `next` among the branches checked after a merge; saved test reports expire after 3
  days; the Tech Lead enables the workflow; the details below confirmed 2026-11-18, "confirm D857"; the changes after
  the branch's independent review, under "Amended while building", to confirm) · Built:
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ci-changes.mjs` (`evm` output, no schedule), `scripts/test/workflows.test.ts`
  (new; `yaml` 2.9.1 as a dev dependency of `@hana-id/scripts`), `scripts/test/ci-changes.test.ts`,
  `scripts/test/verify.test.ts`, `scripts/verify.mjs` (header), `.github/workflows/publish-sdk.yml` (no pnpm cache in
  its build job), docs/operations.md "CI and git" · Amends D387 and D383;
  completes D841's CI note
- Context: D387 turned CI off on 2026-11-05 because the org's included minutes were used up while the repository was
  private. It is public since 2026-11-13. GitHub's billing docs (read 2026-11-18): standard GitHub-hosted runners in
  public repositories are free and don't use the included minutes; larger runners are billed even for public
  repositories; artifacts share the plan's storage allowance with Packages (the docs don't say public repositories
  are exempt); 10 GB of cache per repository, billed only when the limit is raised above it. `develop` is frozen for
  judging and `next` holds the work.
- Decision: (1) `push.branches` is `develop`, `next`, `main`; PRs as before (`pull_request`). (2) Every job on
  `ubuntu-latest`, with a `timeout-minutes`; a test fails on any other runner, an unpinned action, `pull_request_target`
  or `workflow_run`, top-level permissions other than read, an artifact without `retention-days` ≤ 3. (3) The only
  artifact is the Playwright HTML report with the failed tests' traces, on a failure only, kept 3 days, its traces
  dropped above 25 MB (about 1 MB plus a few MB per failed attempt; no video or screenshots are recorded);
  `test-results/` is no longer uploaded (the same traces again); was 7 days and every failure. (4) Rust caches saved by
  pushes only, so PRs fill none of the 10 GB. (5) No `schedule`: GitHub runs one only on the default branch, `develop`,
  frozen; instead every push (after a merge into `next`, `develop` or `main`) runs Playwright on all three browsers,
  PRs Chromium. GitHub reads the schedule from `develop`'s copy, so until `next` merges into `develop` enabling CI
  also runs `develop`'s old nightly (see "Amended while building"); once it merges nothing runs nightly, and a
  WebKit- or Firefox-only regression is caught on the merge's push rather than overnight. (6) A new `evm` job (D841)
  gated on `evmChanged`; the sandbox job also runs the API's `test:sandbox` with `HANA_SANDBOX_REQUIRED=1`, as
  verify's sandbox lane; Playwright runs with `--forbid-only`; Foundry in the TypeScript job, so the EVM deploy tests
  on anvil (D849) run as on a machine with Foundry. (7) Every checkout with `persist-credentials: false`; no job
  reads a secret; permissions `contents: read`, the `changes` job adding `actions: read`. (8) `concurrency` unchanged
  (a newer push to the same branch or PR cancels the older run). (9) The identity probe stays disabled (D387; Lambda
  before mainnet). (10) `pnpm verify` stays the gate before a merge, CI on or not; its default tier is what CI runs on
  a PR.
- Who does what: the Tech Lead checks the organisation's $0 Actions budget is in place (it already is) and changes the
  repository settings listed in docs/operations.md "CI and git", then switches CI on (`gh workflow enable CI -R
  Hana-Technology/hana-id`, or Actions → CI → Enable workflow). Assistants never enable, run or disable a workflow,
  nor change repository or organisation settings.
- Amended while building (after the branch's independent review, 2026-11-18; to confirm): (a) **`develop`'s nightly
  runs once CI is enabled**: GitHub runs a `schedule` from the default branch's copy, and `develop`'s `ci.yml` still
  has D383's `41 3 * * *`, so until `next` merges into `develop` each night runs `develop`'s old jobs (the first night
  Playwright on WebKit and Firefox, about 10–15 min, since there is no good nightly to measure from; then only
  `changes` and the advisories while `develop` stays frozen). A failure uploads `develop`'s old artifact (the report
  and `test-results/`, no cap, 7 days, or 3 once the repository's retention is 3): about 10–40 MB for one or two
  failing tests, up to several hundred MB if a whole browser fails. Free compute, nothing deployed, no secret read.
  (b) **The $0 budget already exists**: organisation scope, Actions, $0, stop usage on, alerts to two members (read
  through the API 2026-11-18), beside $0 stop budgets for Packages, Codespaces and Git LFS; the Tech Lead's step became
  checking it. Open point, settled by the first run: whether a $0 stop budget blocks free public-repository runs; if
  it does (every job fails at once without a runner, a billing annotation), untick "stop usage" on it and keep the
  alerts. (c) Settings for the Tech Lead before switching on: artifact and log retention 3 days (caps every
  workflow's `retention-days`, a fork PR's edited copy and `develop`'s nightly included); fork PR approval for all
  external contributors; the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` read-only; optionally an allowed-actions list and SHA pinning
  required. (d) Foundry from its release tarball (`foundry_v1.5.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz`), checked against a sha256
  pinned in the workflow (GitHub's asset digest, re-computed on download), in the `evm` and TypeScript jobs, instead
  of `foundry-rs/foundry-toolchain` (which downloads without a pinned hash); `scripts/test/workflows.test.ts` now
  fails on any `curl`/`wget` download without a pinned `*_SHA256` and a `sha256sum -c` per download, and on a
  download piped into a shell. (e) `cache: ''` for setup-node in the `evm` job (its filtered install must not save a
  partial pnpm store under the lockfile's shared key) and in `publish-sdk.yml`'s build job (a release build installs
  from the registry, never from a store a CI run saved). (f) Residuals: a fork's PR runs its own `ci.yml` and can name
  `next`'s push concurrency group to cancel its runs (CI disruption only; the next push re-tests; approval for all
  external contributors closes it); advisories are re-checked only on pushes and PRs now that no nightly runs on
  `next` (Dependabot alerts are on, read 2026-11-18).
- Not verified: that free public-repository minutes never count against the $0 stop budget (they are not billed, so
  they shouldn't; the first run shows it); whether artifact storage is free for public repositories (assumed not:
  hence the size cap and 3 days); the jobs' durations on a runner (estimated from the 2026-11-04 runs, the last before
  D387); the exact label of the read-only token option and of a blocked run's annotation.
- Trade-offs: CI is free only while the repository stays public: making it private again bills every minute from the
  shared allowance (D383's numbers), so switch CI off first. Pushes to `next` and `develop` now take longer (three
  browsers), which nobody waits on. A fork's PR runs its own version of `ci.yml`, with a read-only token and no
  secrets, and a first-time contributor's waits for approval (the repository's policy, read 2026-11-18).
- Rejected: a nightly on `next` (GitHub would ignore a `schedule` there); keeping `test-results/` in the artifact (it
  doubles the traces); `pull_request_target` for fork PRs (secrets and a write token next to fork code); a third-party
  paths-filter action (D383's reason stands).

### D858. The relayed NEAR approval says "someone else pays" once, and its one real risk in amber
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-18**; corrected by the coordinator the same day after an

  knows its effect; today that is only the pinned demo check-in on EVM (D854), and on NEAR, where there is no checked

  another account than the user's, every step in a line, explainable, no warning at all, and every action a Transfer
  (the relayer's NEAR, nearcore) or a FunctionCall that reads as a plain "use {contract} ({method})" (not a token
  transfer, permission or value-like method, D810 as amended, D811). Anything else keeps the "NEAR leaving your
  account" row exactly as decided (D723, D729): a token transfer or permission, a method whose name says it may move
  value, unreadable or non-standard arguments, steps left out of the lines, a call to a contract on the user's own

  account." That advice is what covers the user in the residual case: an account that holds no real money on the real
  network has nothing a replayed approval could take there.
- Adversarial check (concluded): the window makes no claim about what a relayed call does with the user's holdings;
  the amber acts-as-you line, which now leads its box instead of ending a blue one, says that it can use anything the

### D859. Addresses and keys in sentences: a name or a short form there, the whole value once in its own row
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-18**; details decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (PR 80 approved); the review amendments of PR 80 amended while building, to confirm · Amends
  D809, D811, D814 · Built on `feat/plain-approval-wording`: `packages/core/src/decode/summary.ts` (`IdRole`, a code
  part's `role`, `isLongId`, `shortId`), `packages/web/src/auth/render-approval.ts` (`IdBook`, `ID_LABELS`, `fullId`,
  `summaryNodes`, `riskBox`, `renderApproval`), `auth/approve-page.ts` (`accountLine`, the details' "Your account"
  row), `auth/css/approval.css` (`dl.id-rows`, `code.id-full`, `.sr-only`); tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/approval-summary.test.ts` ("D859"), `packages/web/test/auth/plain-words.ts` (`idProblems`, run
  on every window the web tests render), `approve-page.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/tests/approval-summary.spec.ts`.
- Decision: a headline, line or warning names a value by a name when it has one ("your account", a checked contract's
  name, a readable NEAR name such as `stamps.testnet`, shown whole as it is) or by its short form (`shortId`: first 6
  and last 4 characters, a key's prefix kept: `0x3333…3333`, `GCI2FC…UNWJ`, `ed25519:cGfH…izuN`). The whole value
  appears once above the fold, in its own labelled row right under the first sentence that names it ("To", "From",
  "Token", "Collection", "Who gets the permission", "Whose permission", "Owner", "Key", "Program", "Account", "Pool",
  "Fee paid by"), as code in groups of four for comparing (spaced by CSS, so the text and a copy of it are the value
  exactly), never folded or cut. The headline's rows come right after the red box (D809: nothing between the
  headline and the red box), so a control change's key row is right under the danger box (D814); a warning's rows are
  inside its box under its line or bullet. Which values are cut is decided by the summary (a code part's role), never
  by the page's guess: a method name, a token id, a sign-in domain, a NEP-413 recipient, a network passphrase stay
  whole in the sentence as before.
- Two different values with the same short form in one request (compared without letter case, as EIP-55 spellings
  differ only there), or one with the user's own address's short form (the account line shows it), are never told
  apart by it: each is numbered in its sentence and row ("account 1", "account 2"; "key 1" for keys), both rows shown.
- Screen readers: the short form is `aria-hidden` and followed by a spoken "(written out below)" at its first mention,
  "(written out above)" once its row is on the page above, and nothing for a later mention before its row (after the
  review of PR 80); they read the whole value in its row (`IdBook.hint`, the web tests check the pointer's direction).
- The account line reads "Your account: 0x2c75…5c23 (Ethereum-style)" (Stellar, NEAR likewise), with the whole account
  as the details' first row ("Your account"), before the Support ID; no copy button (kept simple, as decided). Screen
  readers get the whole account on the line itself.
- Tests: the short form and the row come from the same value (every rendered window in the web tests is checked: each
  short form has a row whose value cuts to it, each value has exactly one row, a numbered value has a numbered row, no
  sentence holds a whole value that has a row, every short form is hidden from screen readers); look-alike pairs on
  EVM and against the user's own address; a NEAR readable name versus an implicit account.
- Adversarial check (concluded): a short form is easy to grind (an EVM short form is 8 hex characters, about 32 bits),
  so it is never the protection: the whole value is always in view, unfolded, labelled, grouped for comparing, and the
  same value the decoder read (one source, tested). What the change could have made easier, and doesn't: a look-alike
  of another address in the same request, or of the user's own address on the account line, can't hide behind a
  matching short form (both are numbered, both rows shown); a look-alike of an address the user expects from outside
  the request (a contract they know) shows a short form that matches what they remember, which is why the row stays
  in view right under the sentence and not in the details, and the verified-contract names still come only from
  Journear's list. Residual, accepted with D859: a user who reads only the sentence and not the row can be misled by a
  ground short form; before D859 the same user saw the whole value in the sentence, but a 40-character value read in
  a sentence is no stronger a check for that user than the grouped row.
- Address impact: none.
- Amended 2026-11-19 by D876: whole values are shown in one piece (no groups of four; for the counterparty rows the
  Tech Lead's decision for the counterparty rows too; groups one switch away), the label above, and the details' "Your account" row has Copy.

### D860. A reviewed list of well-known tokens: "5 USDC" instead of units
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **decided by the user 2026-11-18**; details decided while building, **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (PR 80 approved); the review amendments of PR 80 amended while building, to confirm · Amends
  D811 · Built on `feat/plain-approval-wording`: `packages/core/src/known-tokens.ts` (`KNOWN_TOKENS`, `knownToken`,

  `knownNearToken`, `realTokenLine`, the warning code `token_lookalike`); tests `packages/core/test/known-tokens.test.ts`
  and additions to `approval-summary.test.ts`.
- Decision: a pinned, reviewed list, by network (EVM chain ID, Stellar network passphrase, NEAR network) and exact id
  (EVM address in any letter case, a Stellar classic asset `CODE:ISSUER` or asset contract `C…`, a NEAR account id), of
  `{symbol, name, decimals, kind: 'token' | 'collectible', sources, read}`. It extends the mainnet demo's list without
  replacing it: `MAINNET_DEMO` stays the source of the demo's amounts and caps, and a test checks every demo token is on
  the new list with the same symbol and decimals. Nothing is ever read from the token itself.
- Seeded conservatively, every id from the issuer's own page, read 2026-11-18: Circle's USDC on Ethereum, OP Mainnet,
  Polygon PoS, Base, Arbitrum One, Ethereum Sepolia, Base Sepolia, Arbitrum Sepolia, OP Sepolia and Polygon Amoy
  (https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses); Circle's EURC on Ethereum, Base, Ethereum
  Sepolia and Base Sepolia (https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/eurc-contract-addresses); 6 decimals as Circle
  states (https://developers.circle.com/gateway/concepts/non-usdc-assets); on Stellar, Circle's USDC and EURC issuers on
  the public network and testnet (the same pages), 7 decimals (https://developers.circle.com/cctp/references/stellar),
  their asset contracts derived from the asset (`Asset.contractId`, derived again in the test; the testnet USDC one
  also matches the constant in Circle's own quickstart) and XLM's on both; on NEAR, Circle's USDC accounts on mainnet
  and testnet (Circle's USDC page; 6 decimals from NEAR's own SDK token list, as Circle states none for NEAR),
  `wrap.near` (wNEAR, 24 decimals, NEAR's own `core-contracts` README) and `wrap.testnet` (NEAR's own SDK list; weaker
  than the mainnet entry, which the README states). Left out (no official source found): Stellar mainnet USDC/EURC
  contract ids as published ids (derived instead), EURC on Arbitrum, OP and Polygon, and every collectible.
- What the window says: a listed token's amount "5 USDC" (its decimals, exact up to six places, otherwise rounded
  against the user, D814), with the line "This is the real USDC token (0x036C…CF7e)." (the id whole in its row, D859;
  first built as "…, checked by Journear.", reworded after the review of PR 80: under a red permission warning it read
  as if the request was checked; "(checked by Journear)" now qualifies only who gets something); an unlisted one "5,000,000 units of an unlisted token" with "Journear doesn’t know this token (…),
  so it can’t tell what 5,000,000 units are worth. Check the amount in {App} first." (now also on NEAR and Soroban
  token calls, as "these units" when the request moves it more than once); a Stellar asset whose code is a listed
  symbol on that network but whose issuer isn't the listed one: shown as "5 of the asset USDC:G…" with an amber "This
  is not the USDC Journear knows (…). It may be a copy." The code is the asset's own identity in the signed request,
  not a contract's claim. It matches the exact listed code from another issuer, and (after the review of PR 80) a code
  of the same shape: letter case ignored, trailing digits dropped, and 0, 1, l, 5, 8 and 2 read as O, I, I, S, B and Z
  (`codeShape`, `imitatedSymbolOn`): "usdc", "USDC2" and "U5DC" are flagged, "USDCX" and "XUSDC" are not (tested); a
  wider look-alike (other scripts, a prefix or suffix) is only "the asset CODE:ISSUER", with its whole id in its row.
  EVM and NEAR tokens carry no such trusted name, so they get no look-alike line (a token
  calling itself USDC there is just unlisted). A collectible on the list never gives an amount a symbol (its numbers
  are item ids); none is seeded.
- Adversarial check (concluded): the symbol is earned by the exact id on the exact network, never by a name: a
  look-alike address, the same address on another chain, an asset with the same code from another issuer, and a NEAR
  account that merely contains the listed name are all unlisted (tested). Wrong decimals would misstate an amount by a
  power of ten, so they come from the issuer or the standard, with the source beside each entry. The "real" line names
  the id it vouches for, whole in its row, so a user comparing with their app sees the same contract.
- Address impact: none.
- Note 2026-11-19 (D885): the reviewed NEAR calls follow the same rule: plain words are earned by the exact account on
  the exact network (and the exact call), never by a name; NEAR's token readings are unchanged.

### D861. SDK errors carry a plain sentence for the user, `userMessage`, beside the developer's `message`
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (a plain sentence in the SDK's errors approved in
  principle by the Tech Lead 2026-11-18, the shape below confirmed with PR 78); the review amendments and the merge with
  PR 76 below amended while building, to confirm · Built: `packages/web/src/client/user-messages.ts` (new:
  `userMessageFor`, `DEFAULT_USER_MESSAGE`), `client/errors.ts` (`HanaError.userMessage`, `ProviderRpcError.userMessage`,
  getters), `src/index.ts` (exports `userMessageFor`); `packages/brand/src/plain-words.ts` (new, `@hana-id/brand/plain-words`:
  `JARGON`, `jargonIn`, `sentencesIn`); tests `packages/web/test/client/user-messages.test.ts`,
  `test/auth/plain-words.test.ts`, `apps/stamps/test/ui/plain-words.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/scripts/test/mail-links.test.ts`;
  docs `docs/integration.md` section 13 ("What to show your user") and section 2 ("After 0.4.1"), `docs/api.md` "Conventions"
- Cause: partners show an error's `message` as it is, and the vault's and the SDK's messages are developer text ("The
  user rejected the request", "The Google token carries a claim outside the allow-list", "The key derivation failed",
  "Test apps (pk_test_ keys) can sign only for test networks…", the CSP and origin advice of `vault_unavailable`). The
  partner guide says to match on `code`, never on `message`, and its vault-load table quotes those messages as the
  developer's help, so rewording them for users would take that help away.
- Decision: `message` stays as it is, the developer's. Every `HanaError` and `ProviderRpcError` also has `userMessage`,
  one or two short plain sentences (what happened, whether anything was done, what to do; no code, key or chain word),
  for the partner to show. It is worked out in the SDK from `code` and `data.reason` (or `data.stage`, Google's
  `data.error`) only, each a short lowercase code, from a fixed table: one sentence per code the SDK can reject with
  (every `ErrorCode`, `RpcCode` and `STRING_ERROR_CODES` entry, tested), closer ones for a few reasons (a test app on a
  mainnet, too many waiting requests, a request too large to show, a reserved raw domain, a NEAR request for another
  network, signed out, a sign-in left unfinished, an old browser, a cancelled Google screen), and "Something went
  wrong in Journear Passport. Try again." for anything else. After PR 78's review: each sentence says only what is true
  for every error that can carry it. The generic 4100 no longer says "Nothing was signed" (a sponsored action, PR 76,
  answers 4100 after signing or sending); `api_unavailable` and the SDK's internal error say to check whether something
  went through before trying again; `busy` is "Journear Passport is finishing something else for this wallet. Wait a
  moment, then try again."; `session_consumed` adds "If that wasn’t you, start again and tell the app’s support." (the
  sign-in page and Passport Home say the same). The sponsored action's reasons (`SPONSOR_REASONS`: the vault's refusals
  and the API codes PR 76 passes on as `data.reason`) take PR 76's own `SPONSOR_TEXT` sentences word for word, for the
  codes those errors come with; `reverted` and `not_executed` take the one that is true with or without the one-time
  setup, and an unknown outcome says to check first. With PR 76 merged, the test reads the reasons and their
  `SPONSOR_TEXT` sentences from `vault/evm-sponsor.ts` itself (its refusals and `apiMessage`'s cases) and holds each
  `SPONSOR_REASONS` sentence identical to the vault's, so a new reason or a reworded sentence there fails until this
  table follows; `HanaSponsorError`, a `HanaError`, has `userMessage` too (tested), and the plain-words scan covers
  `vault/evm-sponsor.ts` and `NOT_OFFERED`. A getter on the class, so the errors' own fields, their
  equality and their JSON are unchanged. `userMessageFor(code, data)` is exported for a code read elsewhere (the SWK
  module's `ext[0]`, a provider error a library wrapped). No protocol change: the vault sends what it sent, and an SDK
  of any version works with any vault.
- Also on this branch: the "Hana" leftover in a message, "This raw request is a Hana signing domain and is never
  signed" (`reason: 'raw_reserved_domain'`, `packages/web/src/vault/signing.ts`), reads "This raw request is in one of
  Journear Passport’s own signing domains and is never signed" once PR 76 had merged (`test/vault/approval.test.ts`). The test-env banner of user mail is reworded
  (the row of "Superseded or amended"). Passport Home's coverage badges read "Safe if the app closes", "Needs the app",
  "Can’t be opened here" (the other apps' "Supported" too, one set of words), their sentences say what happens if the
  app shuts down, without making the risk smaller.
- Why: the Tech Lead's rule (D853) is for every text an end user reads, and a partner page is where most users meet an
  error. Computing the sentence in the SDK from the code keeps it safe to show (nothing a page receives can put words
  in it) and needs no change to the vault's port replies, whose strict shape (`exactKeys`) an older SDK would refuse.
- Rejected: rewording `message` itself (partners log and some may match it; the guide quotes it as the developer's
  help); a `userMessage` sent by the vault on the port (an older SDK refuses an error with an unknown key, so it would
  need a version gate in `vault.ts`, which PR 76 edits, and would put vault-chosen text in front of users); putting it
  in `data` (it is per code, not per call, and `data`'s fields are documented per code).
- Address impact: none.
