### D864. The email that waits to join a wallet can cancel the link from its own sign-in
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (decided 2026-11-18, "ok go ahead with this": build
  the cancel-by-email path owed since D259; the details confirmed with the PR, "confirm D864"); the review amendments
  below amended while building, to confirm; their `cancelled` and `now_active` words **confirmed by the Tech Lead
  2026-11-23** (the linking flows hand-tested on the local stack 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-23: "the whole flow for step 2
  testing seems ok", "ok I just tested this step 3, it looks good", "ok step 4 looks good", "step 5 looks good";
  "confirm the batch"); their SDK sentence for `link_pending` was replaced by D881 item 8, still open there · Built: `packages/core/src/relay.ts` (notices
  `link_waiting`, `link_cancel`), `packages/web/src/vault/login.ts` (`PendingLogin.linkWaiting`, `LinkWaiting`),
  `packages/web/src/auth/email-page.ts` (`showLinkWaiting`, `showLinkCancel`), `apps/email-issuer/src/mail.ts`
  (`linkNoticeMail`, pending "Not you?"); tests `packages/web/test/vault/linking.test.ts`,
  `packages/web/test/auth/email-follow.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/linking-protocol.test.ts`,
  `apps/api/test/email-login.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/scripts/test/mail-links.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/tests/linking.spec.ts`
  (and the stack's chain: views count a pending member past its time as active, as the contract does; `cancel_link`
  refuses an active member; `POST /__e2e/links/expire`) · Amends D259 and D862, with a row of "Superseded or amended"
- Context: a pending link is case B when Google doesn't host the mailbox (D119): someone signed in with a Google
  account, proved this address with one code, and the email waits `change_delay_ms` (24 h in production) to join that
  Google wallet. The notice mail goes to the address so its holder can stop a link they didn't make, but until now
  only the wallet's active sign-in (the Google account) could cancel it (D259's banners), and an email sign-in of the
  pending member was just refused (`link_pending`). The contract already lets the pending identity cancel itself
  (`cancel_link`: `j == member`, nonce `link_change` "cancel" over the root, the member, the epoch and a salt;
  `links.rs`), and the API relays it (`POST /v1/link/cancel`, whose precheck checks the same).
- Decision:
  1. **Where**: no `/link/cancel` page. When an email sign-in is refused `link_pending` and the email is itself the
     pending member, the vault reads `get_identity` again and, instead of the plain `stop`, sends the popup
     `link_waiting {provider: the account root's, effectiveAtMs, prove}`. The partner's `login()` still ends
     `link_pending` exactly as before (codes and data unchanged). A Google sign-in, or an email no longer pending at
     that read, gets the old `stop`.
  2. **The proof**: the sign-in's own token can't cancel: its nonce commits to the login's session, and `cancel_link`
     needs a `link_change` nonce (tested in the vault and the API). So "Cancel this link" sends one more code to the
     same address (the window still has it; no retyping), purpose `link_change`, over the commitment the vault
     computed for **this email only** (`memberIk` = the signed-in identity's own key, `rootIk` and `epoch` from the
     fresh read, a fresh 32-byte salt). The vault accepts the answer only if it verifies against the chain's email
     keys with exactly that nonce and its `sub` is the signed-in email's; then it reads `get_identity` again and
     relays `POST /v1/link/cancel` only while the link is still pending at the same root and epoch. The API's
     precheck and the contract check everything again. No contract, API or issuer change; no derivation or session
     rule touched.
  3. **What the popup says** (D853's plain words): heading "A Google account is being linked to this email"; an amber
     box "This email is being linked with a Google account, so both will open the same Journear wallet. The link
     starts working on {date}. Until then, you can’t sign in here with this email."; "Didn’t do this? Cancel the
     link. We’ll send one more code to this email to check it’s you. If you’re not sure, cancel it."; muted "If you
     linked this email yourself, keep the link. This email opens that wallet from {date}."; buttons **Cancel this
     link** (primary) and **Keep the link** (closes; "The link stays. Nothing changed. This email can sign in here
     from {date}."). The other sign-in is named only by its kind, as the banners do (no address, no `sub`).
  4. **Outcomes** (`link_cancel`), each after a fresh read: `cancelled` ("Link cancelled", green: "This email is no
     longer being linked with that Google account. Anyone signed in to that wallet in this app will be asked to sign in
     again." (the cancel revokes that wallet's shares, D233) and "If you didn’t start this link, change
     your email password. Someone may have used a code from your mailbox."); `already_cancelled` (gone before the
     relay: "This link was already cancelled", the same advice); `now_active` (the waiting period ended meanwhile;
     red: "The waiting period has ended. This email and that Google account now open the same Journear wallet.", "This
     email now opens a wallet that belongs to whoever holds that Google account. Anything you add to it is theirs. If
     you didn’t do this, change your email password. Don’t sign in to {app} with this email, don’t add money to that
     wallet, and tell the app’s support." (the risk for a reader who didn't link it is money put into someone else's
     wallet), muted "Within 7 days,
     whoever signs in to {app} with that Google account can remove this email: the sign-in window shows them a button
     to remove it."); `not_cancelled` (still waiting: "The link wasn’t cancelled", "Nothing changed: the link is still
     waiting.", "Close this window, then sign in to {app} with this email again to try again.", and the code for
     support); `unknown` (the chain couldn't be read after a failure: "We couldn’t check the link", "Journear couldn’t
     be reached, so we can’t tell whether the link was cancelled.", "Sign in to {app} with this email again. If the
     link is still waiting, you’ll see the button to cancel it again."). A failed relay whose cancel did land reads as
     `cancelled`. After a cancel the user signs in again (the login already ended): with this email the sign-in then
     shows case B's choice again (the directory still lists the address for that Google account, D122), never the
     Google wallet.
  5. **The notice mail**, pending case only: "Not you? Change your email password. Then sign in to “{app}” with this
     email before the waiting period ends: Journear Passport will show the new sign-in with a button to cancel it.
     Once the waiting period has ended, don’t sign in to “{app}” with this email, and tell the app’s support." (was:
     sign in with that Google account). The active notice keeps D862's words.
  6. **Limits**: one choice per screen (both buttons disabled at the first tap); the vault reads one answer and waits
     for it at most `AFTERWORD_MS` (5 min); a duplicate relay is refused by the API's token claim (`link_in_flight`);
     a second window's cancel finds the link gone (`already_cancelled`). The cancel revokes the Google wallet's vault
     shares in the scope, as every cancel does (D233), so that wallet's devices sign in again and see the change.
- Who is at the keyboard: someone who just typed a code mailed to this address, twice. One who only knows the address
  never sees the screen (it follows a verified code). The person who made the link with their own Google account and
  this mailbox sees it too, and may keep the link. One who can read this mailbox can now cancel a link its owner made
  (denial of service only: the owner can link again with a code and their Google account, and that reader could
  already sign in with the email once the link was active). No identity can cancel another's link: the offer, the
  vault's check and the contract all bind the member to the signed-in email.
- Not done, for the Tech Lead: (a) after the waiting period the email holder can't remove the link themselves, though
  the contract allows `unlink_identity` by the member itself (the API too, tested); offering "Remove this email from
  that wallet" on the `now_active` screen would be one more branch of the same mechanism. (b) An email sign-in of an
  active member opens the root's wallet with no banner about its own recent link (D259 names the signing-in method
  only when this login made it).
- Amended after the PR's independent review (2026-11-18, amended while building, to confirm): the `cancelled` and `now_active` words above
  (the first said "Nothing else changed", untrue since the cancel signs that wallet's devices out in the app; the
  second said "someone else may be able to open that wallet", naming the wrong party); and the SDK's `userMessage` for
  `link_pending` (D861), which said "Use the wallet’s other sign-in method for now" (right only for the one who made
  the link), is now "This email is waiting to be linked to a wallet. Sign in again and follow the steps in the
  Journear Passport window." It is per code, so a Google sign-in waiting to join an email wallet (an explicit
  `linkAccount`, rare) reads "This email" too.
- Amended 2026-11-18 by D865 (decided by the user, PR 85's review): the pending notice mail's "Not you?" and the
  `now_active` screen's words, which told the email's holder not to sign in after the wait, now send them to sign in,
  where they can cancel or, after the wait, remove the email; the `now_active` screen offers **Remove this email**
  itself (D865, item 3 of its amendment has the words).
- Rejected: a `/link/cancel` page reached from the mail (a link in a security mail is what phishing copies, D862; it
  would need an issuer path for the identity key and a code anyway); accepting the sign-in's own token (needs a
  contract change: a session nonce isn't a `link_change` proof, and a Tech Lead decision and redeploy); continuing the
  sign-in after a cancel (the login already ended for the partner; the email would then face case B's choice anyway).
- Address impact: none.
- Note 2026-11-19 (D881): the banner's own "Cancel this link" (by an active sign-in of the wallet) now ends on a result
  screen in this entry's words ("Link cancelled"; "We couldn't check the link" when the outcome is unknown), and the
  hosted demo says this email's `link_pending` plainly.

### D852. Every sponsored transaction leaves a permanent billing record, in D1 and copied to the usage ledger
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: the requirement decided by the user 2026-11-18 ("we should have necessary records in place so
  in the future when we turn on billing for partners, we can bill for the sponsored transactions as well … for now we
  should make sure we have all historical records for each sponsored tx recorded"); the design decided while building,
  **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** · Built: `apps/api/migrations/0022_evm_sponsor.sql` (`evm_sponsor_billing`, the batch shape on
  `evm_sponsor_sends`), `apps/api/migrations-usage/0009_evm_sponsored.sql` (`usage.evm_sponsored_txs`,
  `usage.record_evm_sponsored`, `usage.evm_sponsored_monthly`), `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-billing.ts`,
  `sponsor-settle.ts` (`moveRow`'s billing statement, `settleFromReceipt`, `settleFromRelayerCost`, `settleAsCharge`),
  `sponsor.ts` (the cron: `mirrorEvmBilling`, `lateBilling`); tests `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts` ("billing
  records"), `apps/api/test-usage/evm-sponsored.test.ts`, `scripts/test/uid-erase.test.ts`. Local only: neither
  migration is applied anywhere; the Tech Lead applies D1 and Neon migrations.
- What exists today: the usage ledger (Neon, `usage.events`, `usage.gas_settlements`, the monthly statements of D92 and
  D325) records the login pool's relayed calls (`login`, `session`, `derive`, `revoke`, `unlock`, `owner_action`, and
  the link and Home ones), each with its NEAR transaction and the settled gas. **The NEAR meta-transaction relay (D736)
  leaves no per-transaction record there**: `/v1/near/relay` and `/v1/near/activate` open no usage event, so what it
  paid exists only as the RateLimiter's day budget counts (no history) and the request log (`nearTx`, kept as long as
  Workers logs are). Adding them would take a new ledger endpoint kind (or a table like this one) and the
  D1-then-copy path used here.
- Decision: a billing record per sponsored transaction that reached the chain: the batch (`executed`, `reverted`,
  `not_executed`: it ran without effect, e.g. an authorization the network skipped), the relayer's deadline
  self-transfer (`cancelled`), or `mined` when only the relayer's cost is known; and one per charge with no mined
  transaction of its own (`lost`, `consumed_elsewhere`), with the kept reservation as the amount, so the books add up.
  No record for a send that never reached the chain (refused, never sent) or for a relayer replay (the original send
  carries the transaction). Fields: org, app, chain, environment (the env's name), transaction hash, block number and
  time, outcome, gas used, effective gas price, the execution cost, the L1 data fee, the operator fee, the total cost,
  the settled amount (what the budgets kept), the number of calls, each call's allowlisted target and selector, whether
  it carried the one-time setup, created and settled times. Amounts in wei; no USD.
- Where: the record of truth is a D1 table (`evm_sponsor_billing`), written in the same D1 batch as the audit row's final
  move (a settled send can't exist without its record; a second settlement attempt writes nothing: keyed on (chain,
  transaction hash), or the send for a charge without one, and unique per send). The cron copies the records to the usage
  ledger (`usage.evm_sponsored_txs` through `usage.record_evm_sponsored`, idempotent on the same key, validating every
  row), so future billing and the monthly statements read one place; queryable per org, app and month
  (`usage.evm_sponsored_monthly`). While the ledger is unbound or unreachable the records wait in D1 and the next run
  copies them. `evm_billing_late` ("Free network fees: a billing record is late") is raised when a settled send has no
  record an hour on, or (with the ledger bound) a record isn't copied within an hour.
- Why D1 first, rather than writing the ledger directly: the usage capture path is best effort by design (it fails
  open, never delaying a request), and a ledger outage must not lose a charge; one D1 batch makes the record exactly as
  durable as the settlement itself.
- No personal data: no account address, user id or IP. The transaction hash is public chain data: anyone can read the
  transaction (and the account it was sent to) on the chain, so storing it reveals nothing that isn't already public, and
  it is the proof that the charge happened. What linked the hash to a Journear user (the audit row, the directory) goes
  with the user's erasure; these records stay on purpose (the business's record of what it paid): `uid-erase` doesn't
  touch them, they have no foreign key to the audit row or the directory, the audit rows' 24-month retention doesn't
  prune them, and in the ledger none of the retention functions or `usage.erase_uid` reads the table (tested).
- What a billing job will need later: a daily ETH/USD rate per chain (as `usage.near_usd_rates` for NEAR), a rule for
  what to charge (the cost, a markup, a flat fee per action), and how to treat `lost` and `consumed_elsewhere` amounts
  (they are Journear's spend, possibly not the partner's).
- Address impact: none.

## NEAR relay billing records (branch `feat/near-relay-billing`), 2026-11-18

From `feat/evm-sponsor-api` @ 69ee88aa (to merge after PR #71, whose migrations it follows), not merged, not
deployed. The Tech Lead, 2026-11-18: "go ahead with NEAR billing records".

### D863. The NEAR meta-transaction relay leaves a permanent billing record per transaction, as EVM sponsorship does
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: the requirement decided by the user 2026-11-18; the details decided while building,
  **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** · Built: `apps/api/migrations/0023_near_relay_billing.sql`, `apps/api/migrations-usage/0010_near_relayed.sql`,
  `apps/api/src/near/relay-billing.ts`, `src/near/relay.ts` (the write after the answer), `src/index.ts` (the handlers'
  execution context, the cron), `packages/console-core` (`near_billing_late`); tests `apps/api/test/near-relay.test.ts`
  ("billing records"), `apps/api/test-usage/near-relayed.test.ts`, `scripts/test/uid-erase.test.ts`,
  `test/migration-0003.test.ts`, `test/migration-0006.test.ts`. Local only: no migration applied anywhere.
- Why a new path rather than the login pool's settlement: `usage.gas_settlements` settles at FINAL the transactions of
  `usage.events`, which the relay never writes (D852 found it leaves no per-transaction record), and the admin Worker's
  settlement job reads those events. So the relay gets EVM sponsorship's pattern (D852): D1 first, then a copy to the
  ledger, with the same FINAL re-read the gas settlements do.
- Decision: one record per NEAR transaction the relay sent for a user that may have reached the chain (a relayed
  delegate action or an activation, success or failure: everything but "certainly not sent"), keyed on (network,
  transaction hash), INSERT OR IGNORE. Written in D1 (`near_relay_billing`) right after the relay's answer, inside the
  request's `waitUntil`: the request path waits for nothing, and the relay's behaviour, answers and limits are unchanged.
  The relay's own figures (EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC) are provisional; the cron (every run, 20 records a run) re-reads each
  transaction at FINAL with the relay account as signer for the settled gas and tokens burnt (the transaction and every
  receipt, refunds included), the status (`executed`, or `failed` when the transaction or any receipt failed) and the
  block (height, time); a transaction still unknown six hours on is `unknown` with the relay's figures. Final records are
  copied to the usage ledger (`usage.near_relayed_txs` through `usage.record_near_relayed`; `usage.near_relayed_monthly`
  per org, app and month) and retried until they land.
- Fields: org, app, environment, network, transaction hash, block height and time, kind (`delegate`/`activation`), the
  relay's answer code, outcome, gas burnt, tokens burnt (yoctoNEAR), the NEAR the relay attached or sent for the user
  (real spend: an activation's transfer, `near.relay.activationYocto`; a delegate's deposits, refused by policy today so
  0), the contract a delegate called and its method names, created and final times.
- Fail open for the relay: a write that fails (migration 0023 not applied yet, D1 unreachable) never fails or delays a
  relay; it is counted on a RateLimiter object (`near-relay:billing`, which needs no migration) and the cron writes
  `near_billing_late` ("Free NEAR transactions: a billing record is late") once an hour while writes fail, a record isn't final an
  hour on, or (with the ledger bound) isn't copied an hour on. Safe to deploy onto the running relay in either order with
  the migration; additive migrations only (a new table; `security_events` rebuilt to widen its CHECK, as 0020 and 0022
  did). `gen sandbox-dev` is unchanged: no new binding, var or secret.
- Pseudonymous: holds no name, email, account id or user id (an activation's receiver is the user's implicit account, so
  it is not stored), and no IP; the transaction hash is public chain data that can be traced to an account. The transaction hash is public chain data: on NEAR it names a transaction whose signer is the
  relay account and whose receiver, for a delegate, is the user's implicit account, so the hash leads anyone to that
  public account on the chain, exactly as an EVM transaction hash leads to the account it was sent to. That reveals
  nothing that isn't already public; Journear's own link from the account to a person (the wallet directory) goes with
  the user's erasure. The records are never pruned and stay through an erasure on purpose (the business's record of what
  it paid): no foreign key, `uid-erase` doesn't touch them, and in the ledger no retention function or
  `usage.erase_uid` reads the table (tested).
- No USD: yoctoNEAR only; `usage.near_usd_rates` (the daily NEAR/USD rate the admin Worker already fetches, D325) can
  price them when billing is decided.
- Records exist only from the deploy on: what the relay paid before (the stamps demo) can't be rebuilt from Journear's
  data, only estimated by hand from the relay account's transactions on a NEAR explorer (docs/operations.md "NEAR relay
  billing records").
- **Amended 2026-11-18 after the independent review of PR 77** (amended while building, **confirmed by the user
  2026-11-18**; its nonce check replaced by the next amendment): (1) the cron reads
  with `tx` `wait_until: 'NONE'` (an answer at once) and takes an outcome as final only when the node says `FINAL`,
  through a client of its own (one endpoint a call, its own RPC health: it can never mark an endpoint down for the live
  relay), with per-record backoff (`next_try_at`, doubling from a minute to six hours, oldest first); (2) a hard budget
  of 10 outside fetches a run, no per-record `block` read (the block hash is kept; height and time only with budget
  left); records final at once without a read: an `ok` relay (its own complete figures: every receipt at
  EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC, summed) and a relay that certainly never ran (`near_rejected`, `relayer_busy` with a hash:
  `not_executed`); `unknown` only after 8 actual reads and six hours, never from starvation; the job isolated (nothing it
  throws reaches the other cron jobs); throughput 960 reads a day, a backlog above it only late; (3) D1 writes: a
  WITHOUT ROWID table, the org and app indexes dropped (the ledger has them), about 5 rows written per usual relay; (4)
  a result sent without a hash counts as a miss; a failed write is parked (a bounded queue on the RateLimiter object)
  and written later; each record keeps the relay key and its nonce, and a daily check of each key's nonce on chain
  against the records counts transactions without one (`nonceGaps`; replaced below); (5) `near_billing_late` once a UTC day with the
  counts, "not final" only past the give-up time; (6) `executed` with `had_failed_receipt` when only a later callback
  receipt failed (the user's own action, read from the receipt ids, decides `failed`); (7) pseudonymous, not "no
  personal data": no name, email, account id or user id, but the hash is public chain data that can be traced to an
  account; (8) the deploy order (docs/operations.md): D1 migrations only with `wrangler d1 migrations apply --remote`
  (0022 then 0023), the ledger's 0009 then 0010, the Worker after them at a quiet moment.
- **Amended 2026-11-18 after the re-check of PR 77 at 2e5b8dc0** (amended while building, to confirm). (1) The daily
  nonce check counted false gaps every day: the relay key object reserves nonces in blocks of 100 and resumes past its
  reservation on each cold start (`NONCE_RESERVATION`, `relayer-key.ts`), and a refused transaction's nonce is skipped,
  so `(hi − lo) − recorded` counted every skipped nonce. Replaced: once a UTC day per relay key, the key's nonce on chain
  (the last included transaction's) must equal a recorded nonce of that key (any outcome but `not_executed`), or be
  unchanged since the last check (nothing included); else ONE `unrecordedLast` for that key that day (the late alert's
  `nonceGaps` renamed). What it proves: the most recent included transaction per key per day has a record. What it
  can't: an unrecorded transaction followed by a recorded one the same day; nor how many are missing. An exact count
  would need a counter inside the relay key object, deliberately not built now so the live relay is untouched. A
  transaction included in the seconds before the check whose record is still being written could be counted once
  (rare; the next day's check is clean). The test models the reservation jump and a refused nonce. (2) A parked row
  that D1 refuses for good no longer blocks the queue: counted as a miss, acknowledged, the drain goes on; any other
  error still stops the drain until the next run. "Refused for good" is a constraint or bind-type error, something
  that isn't a record, or (found while testing: INSERT OR IGNORE skips a row breaking a CHECK or NOT NULL constraint
  without an error) a write that changed nothing and whose row isn't there; a duplicate is fine. The relay's own write
  uses the same test: a row skipped that way is a miss at once, not parked. (3) What a later billing job can rely on: the
  amounts and the time of recording, not block data. Records final from the relay's own figures (`figures_from:
  'relay'`) and `not_executed` ones have no block hash, height or time, and `had_failed_receipt` is always 0 for them;
  only `figures_from: 'final'` records carry a block hash. Unverified: whether newer NEAR versions charge a gas refund
  penalty outside `tokens_burnt`; checked once at deploy time against one testnet transaction's balance change
  (docs/operations.md, the deploy's step 4).
- Address impact: none.

- Context: an active member of an account (an email that joined a Google wallet in case B, or a Google account that
  joined an email wallet in case A) opens the root's wallet at every sign-in, with nothing said after the login that
  made the link (D259 skips the signing-in method's own banner). Someone who reads a mailbox once could link it to

  holder also opens, and anything they put in is that person's. The contract already lets the member unlink itself

- Decision:
  1. **When**: every sign-in whose identity is an active member of an account, without a link made by this login and
     with the follow-up channel (an app with email), after the path is resolved and confirmed (D263) and **before**
     the chain step: nothing opens the shared wallet until the user answers. **No time window**: the contract and the
     API set none on a member's own removal (nor on the root's: its 7-day Remove is the banners' display rule,
     `RECENT_LINK_MS`), so the notice shows for as long as the link exists, until "Keep it" in that browser. So there
     is no "window expired" state.
  2. **The notice** (`member_link`, the root's method by kind only, since when, an opaque `linkId`): heading "This email
     now also opens another wallet"; amber box "Since {date}, this email opens a wallet that a Google account also
     opens. Whoever holds that Google account can open it too."; "If you didn’t set this up, remove this email from
     it."; muted "If you set this up yourself, keep it. We won’t ask again on this device."; buttons **Remove this
     email** (red) and **Keep it**. A Google member reads the same with the words swapped ("This Google account now
     also opens another wallet", "… a wallet that an email also opens. Whoever holds that email can open it too.",
     **Remove this Google account**).
  3. **Keep it**: the login goes on exactly as before; the popup stores `hana.ml.<linkId>` in `localStorage` on
     `authOrigin` (where device tickets live) and answers at once at the next sign-in in that browser. Another browser
     or device asks once too. `linkId` is sha256 of the root's and the member's identity keys and `sinceMs`: a new link
     of the same pair asks again.
  4. **Remove**: first a confirmation: "Remove this email from that wallet?"; red box "After you remove it, this email
     can’t open that wallet any more. Anything in it stays there, and whoever holds that Google account can still open
     it."; "If you added money to that wallet, move it out first. Choose Go back, then Keep it, and sign in to move
     it."; "If you sign in with this email again afterwards, it opens a new, empty wallet of its own."; muted "We’ll
     send one more code to this email to check it’s you." (Google: "Google will ask you to sign in again to check it’s
     you."); **Remove it** (red), **Go back**. Then the login ends `login_cancelled`, `data.reason: 'link_remove'` (a
     new reason, same code; the partner's `login()` doesn't wait on the code step), and `MemberRemove` gets its own
     `AFTERWORD_MS` (5 min) for the proof, so the login's 5-minute limit never cuts the code step short.
  5. **The proof and the checks**: from a fresh `get_identity`, the `link_change` "unlink" nonce for this member only
     (fresh 32-byte salt, the account's epoch); one more code to the same address (or Google with `login_hint`); the
     vault takes it only if it verifies against the chain's keys with that nonce and its `sub` is the signed-in one; it
     re-reads, relays `POST /v1/link/unlink` only while still an active member of the same root at the same epoch; the
     API's precheck and the contract check it all again. No contract, API or issuer change.
  6. **Outcomes** (`member_removed`, after a read): `removed` ("This email was removed"; green "This email no longer
     opens that wallet. Anything in it stays there, with whoever holds that Google account. Anyone signed in to that
     wallet in this app will be asked to sign in again."; "If you sign in with this email again, it opens a new, empty
     wallet of its own."; "If you didn’t set up the link, change your email password."); `already_removed` ("This email
     was already removed", "This email no longer opens that wallet. There’s nothing more to do."); `not_removed` ("This
     email wasn’t removed", "Nothing changed: this email still opens that wallet.", "Close this window, then sign in
     to {app} with this email again to try again.", the code for support); `unknown` ("We couldn’t check the
     removal", "Journear couldn’t be reached, so we can’t tell whether this email was removed.", "Sign in to {app} with
     this email again. If it still opens that wallet, you’ll be asked again."). A failed relay that landed reads as
     `removed`. A removal doesn't mark the link kept, so a failed one asks again.
  7. **What the next sign-in opens**: `unlink_identity` puts the member in the root's `unlinked` list. The issuer's
     case-B lookup and google-match judge the pair `unlinked` (`decide.ts`), so there is no "Link and continue" again;
     the email gets a session token for its own path, which no session ever opened (a member never had a wallet of its
     own: links.rs refuses a joiner with one), so it is a new, empty wallet (tested end to end). The same for a Google
     member.
  8. **Partner signals**: none new beyond the `login_cancelled` reason; `linkChanged` belongs to a session's own
     wallet, and this login opens none.
- Not done: the D864 notice mail's active advice and its "now_active" screen still tell the email's holder not to
  sign in with that email; with this notice, signing in is now the way to remove it (a wording change for the Tech Lead).
  After "Keep it" this browser never asks again, so a user who kept it to move money out first removes it from another
  browser (no settings page lists links).
- Rejected: a 7-day window (the contract sets none; the risk lasts as long as the link); asking after the login (the
  partner would already hold a session on the shared wallet); continuing the login after a removal (it would open a
  new wallet the user hasn't seen explained, and the code step would run inside the login's 5 minutes).
- Address impact: none (no path or key derivation changes; a removed member opens its own path, as before its link).
- Amended after PR 85's review (2026-11-18; items 1 to 3 decided by the user, "yes to all three"; item 4 and the
  details to confirm). Points 2 to 4 above are as first built; these replace them where they differ:
  1. **"Keep it" no longer means "never ask again"**: the main safe button is **Not now** (the sign-in goes on, nothing
     stored, asked again at the next sign-in); a smaller, separate **Don't ask again on this device** (below the
     buttons) stores `hana.ml.<linkId>` as "Keep it" did. Muted line: "If you set this up yourself, you can choose
     Don’t ask again on this device." The confirmation's advice: "If you added money to that wallet, move it out
     first. Choose Go back, then Not now, and sign in to move it. You’ll be asked again next time."
  2. **No notice for an automatic, harmless link**, decided only from recorded data, never from the partner: the
     member's provider and the root's (`get_identity`), the contract's `Member.auto` (`get_account` on the vault's
     RPC: made by automatic linking), and google-match's answer for this very login (the email issuer, from Google's
     userinfo with this login's access token): `decision: 'linked'` (this Google account's verified address is in this
     account) and `googleHosted` (Gmail, or a Workspace address whose `hd` is its domain). A Google member, `auto`,
     `linked`, Google-hosted: case A's silent link of the same person's address: **no notice**. `linked` and not
     hosted (case A after "Link and continue"), `auto` false (`linkAccount`), and every email member (case B is always
     "Link and continue"): `chosen`, the notice as above. Can't be told (no google-match in an app without email
     login, the issuer down, another decision, the account unreadable): **shown**, `how: 'automatic'`: a blue box,
     "This usually happens when that email is your own Gmail or Google Workspace address. If you don’t recognise it,
     remove this Google account from it.", **Not now** first and **Remove this Google account** not in red. The
     chain doesn't record whether a link had a code step or whether the address is hosted; `auto` and google-match
     are what is recorded. The rule inherits D158's accepted residual: a Workspace or Cloud Identity domain whose mail
     isn't on Google still reports `hd` equal to its domain, so its admin-made accounts count as Google-hosted and get
     no notice; the domain's admin controls that mailbox anyway.
  3. **D864's texts corrected** (amends D864): the pending notice mail's "Not you?" is "Change your email password,
     then sign in to “{app}” with this email. During the waiting period you can cancel the link there. After it, the
     Journear Passport sign-in window lets you remove this email from that wallet. Don’t add money to that wallet."
     (the issuer doesn't know the link's date, so no date). The "can't be cancelled any more" screen: red box "The
     waiting period has ended: this email and that Google account now open the same wallet."; "If you didn’t set this
     up, don’t add money to it. Choose Remove this email below, and change your email password."; buttons **Remove
     this email** (red) and **Close**. Remove goes through the same confirmation, then the member's own removal
     (`MemberRemove`, started by `LinkWaiting` on `{choice: 'remove'}`), so there is no "sign in again" step.
  4. **The partner's message** for `login_cancelled` with `link_remove`: "You chose to remove this sign-in from that
     wallet. Finish it in the Journear Passport window. Then sign in again when you’re ready." (the reason picks it;
     other `login_cancelled` keep "The sign-in was cancelled. Nothing was changed."). It is true either way: at that
     moment the removal still waits for its code in the window (first built as "You removed …", corrected after the
     re-check of PR 85).
  5. **Every interactive sign-in has the channel**: an app without email login (record, D269) now gets the follow-up
     channel too (its callback goes to the follow-up mode, the vault always sends its last word), so a member signing
     in through any app of the scope is asked. Its login reads NEAR once more (the last word's `get_account`). An env
     without an email issuer has no email identities, so no links. Tested in the vault.

## The support pages: unlock and confirm (branch `feat/email-support-pages`), 2026-11-18

From `next` @ 0a636344; not merged, not deployed.

### D866. The staff unlock and confirm emails get their pages: one button each, nothing before the press
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (decided 2026-11-18, "start them": build the two
  support pages; the details below, the amendments after PR 88's review and the residuals confirmed with the PR, "OK to
  merge 88 and confirm D866", told: the unlock works only in the browser where the button was pressed, Passport Home
  not covered for now, the pages' and mails' words as in the screenshots, used and expired links remembered 7 days
  without the address, a mail scanner that clicks buttons could press Confirm) · Built: `packages/web/src/auth/support-page.ts` (entries
  `unlock.ts`, `confirm.ts`), `email-storage.ts` (`hana.ug`), `email-api.ts` and `email-page.ts` (`unlockToken` on
  `start`), `pages.ts`, `apps/api/src/pages/host.ts`; `apps/email-issuer/src/support-link.ts`, `handlers.ts`
  (`handleUnlockLink`, `handleConfirm`, `handleUnlock`, `handleUnsuppress`, `STAFF_NOTES`), `challenge.ts`,
  `rate-limiter.ts` (`activateGrant`, `unstaffAction`), `limits.ts`, `mail.ts`; tests
  `apps/email-issuer/test/support-links.test.ts`, `packages/web/test/auth/support-page.test.ts`, the mail-links test
  with no exception, `apps/e2e/tests/support-pages.spec.ts` (three browsers) · Amends D198 and D199 (as below), closes
  D862's open item
- Context: two things stop a user whose only sign-in is email. Too many wrong codes lock the address (D198: until
  midnight UTC once the backstop trips), and a bounce or a spam report stops all mail to it (D199). Staff had a call
  for each (`admin/unlock`, `admin/unsuppress`) that mails the address a one-time link, but the links' pages
  (`/email/unlock`, `/email/confirm`) were never built, so support couldn't use them (D862).
- Decision:
  1. **Paths**: the ones the mails already used, `{authOrigin}/email/unlock#<token>` and `/email/confirm#<token>`. The
     token stays in the fragment (never sent to a server by a browser, never in a referrer or a log); the page sends it
     only in its press's POST body.
  2. **One button, nothing before it**: each page reads and checks the token's form, shows the reason in plain words
     and one button ("Unlock my email", "Yes, this is my email"), and sends nothing on load: an email app's preview or
     a link scanner that opens the link changes nothing. The press is one `POST` (the button is disabled while it runs:
     a double click is one request). A malformed or other-action token is "not valid" at once, with no request.
  3. **The unlock stays D198's grant, with the press in front**: the press (`POST /v1/email/unlock`) makes the grant
     `active`; until then a `start` presenting the token gets nothing. It clears no lock and no counter: the one start
     it lets through takes the ticket slot, then the grant's own 2 checks past the ceiling (D198's bound unchanged:
     ≈ 0.92% a year). Because the grant is used by a `start`, the page keeps the token in this browser's
     `localStorage` on `authOrigin` (`hana.ug`: token, address, end), and `/login/email` sends it as `unlockToken`
     with each start while it lasts, dropping it after a sign-in with that address. So the unlock works **in the
     browser where the link was opened**: the mail says to open it "in the browser where you use the app", and the
     done screen says "in this browser". Pressing again while the grant is unused answers the same (a second browser,
     a reload); once a start used it, "already used".
  4. **Bound to the exact address** (amends D198, where a grant was the mailbox's): the grant holds the address's
     K_sup key, and only a start for that exact address may use it; another `+tag` of the mailbox gets nothing.
  5. **Confirm** (`POST /v1/email/confirm`, reworked): single use, atomically in its object; then one D1 batch writes the
     audit row and removes that exact address's suppression, nothing else; if the batch fails the link is live again.
  6. **One record per link** (`g:` / `u:` + sha256 of the token, the `EmailChallenge` namespace; was `u:` for confirm
     only): the action, the exact address's key, an unlock's mailbox key, the staff `ticket`, the expiry, and the
     address AES-GCM-encrypted under a key derived from the token (readable only during a request carrying it). The
     answer names that address (the page shows it as text); after 24 h, or once used, only a tombstone (action,
     expiry, use time) stays for 7 days, so the page can say "expired" or "already used" rather than "not valid".
  7. **Answers**: `200` (`{unlocked: true, email, expiresAtMs}`, `{confirmed: "unsuppress", email}`), `410 link_used`,
     `410 link_expired`, `400 link_invalid` (unknown, malformed, or the other action's token; replaces confirm's one
     `410 confirm_expired`). Limits: 10 presses per 10 min per IP (`ip:link:10m`, its own window, every env; confirm's
     was the resend window) and 10 an hour per token (`link:1h`). Both from `authOrigin` only.
  8. **Audit and logs**: the press is a second audit row under the staff row's action and ticket, `staff` =
     `email-link` (not an email: never a staff member's row), `detail` `{"step":"link_pressed"}` or
     `{"step":"confirmed"}`; logs `unlock_link_pressed`, `unlock_grant_used`, `suppression_removed`. No address or
     token in any of them. No migration: the existing columns and actions.
  9. **Staff side fixed**: an unlock of a suppressed address, or an unsuppress of one that isn't, mails nothing and now
     uses **no** place in the per-mailbox cap (it was counted, so the unlock after a confirm was refused the same day);
     a mail the provider refuses gives its place back. The answers carry `note`, a fixed plain sentence for staff:
     what the user gets and does. The admin portal has no button for these calls (they are `cloudflared access curl`,
     `docs/operations.md` "Staff calls"), so `apps/admin` is unchanged.
  10. **Words (D853)**: the pages' and mails' texts are in `SUPPORT_TEXT` (support-page.ts) and `mail.ts`; the page's
      done lines are the Tech Lead's ("Your email is unlocked. You can sign in again." / "Thanks: this email is confirmed.
      We’ll send sign-in codes to it again."), each followed by what to do next and nothing to press; expired and used
      say "Ask the app’s support to send a new email."; the confirm page adds "If our emails land in your spam folder,
      mark them as “not spam”. Otherwise we may have to stop sending them again." The mails say what the button does,
      that the link works once, within 24 hours, and "Didn’t ask for this? Ignore this email. Nothing changes."
- Why: a state change that a mail scanner can trigger, or a link that works anywhere for anyone, would lift a
  protection for whoever holds the URL; the press and the binding keep both lifts to the mailbox's holder. Keeping
  D198's grant (rather than clearing the lock on the press) keeps an attacker who caused the lock from guessing again.
- Security: the mail goes to the locked or suppressed address itself, so a support person tricked into sending one
  helps only whoever reads that mailbox. Residuals: the unlock works only in the browser where the link was pressed (an
  in-app mail browser with its own storage needs the link opened again in the user's browser: the page says so when
  storage is refused, not when it is merely another browser); whoever can read that browser's storage within 24 h can
  use the one start (the code still goes to the mailbox). Records written before this branch (an unlock grant stored
  as a number, a confirm record of the old shape) are never usable: a mail sent before the deploy needs a new one.
- Confirmed by the user 2026-11-18: the "this browser" limit of the unlock (the alternative, an unlock bound to the
  presser's network instead of the browser, works across browsers on one network but lets anyone on that network use
  it, was not taken); the pages' words; the 7-day tombstone.
- Rejected: acting on the page's load (link scanners); a GET endpoint; clearing the lock on the press (an attacker's
  fresh day of guesses, the design D198 superseded); a sign-in from the done page (the user goes back to the app).
- Address impact: none.
- **Amended after PR 88's independent review (2026-11-18; confirmed by the user 2026-11-18 with D866):**
  1. **A device ticket no longer hides the unlock.** A returning browser sends its device ticket and the pressed
     unlock together; the issuer took the ticket, whose slot a locked owner has already used up, so the page said
     "unlocked" and the sign-in still answered 429. Now an active grant for that exact address decides. The bound is
     unchanged: one start, its checks in the (mailbox-wide) ticket slot then the grant's own 2 past the ceiling,
     nothing cleared; the ticket isn't used for that start, so its 3 mails a day and its challenge count are untouched
     (an active grant with a ticket the owner hadn't used up is still the one spent).
  2. **Passport Home takes no unlock** (D619, confirmed by the user, stands: Home keeps nothing in storage and its start
     takes no owner proof). The staff note and the runbook say "It works for signing in to an app, not to Passport
     Home yet"; a user locked out of Home waits for midnight UTC. Changing it is the Tech Lead's call (read, never write,
     the auth origin's `hana.ug` from `/home`). Confirmed 2026-11-18: Passport Home is not covered for now.
  3. **The staff place comes back only when the provider clearly refused the mail** (an HTTP error answer, a missing key,
     or the staff pool spent). A timeout or a network error may have sent it: `{mailed: false, reason: "unsure"}`, the
     place stays used, and the note tells staff to have the user check their inbox and spam folder.
  4. **Every unlock press writes its audit row before the grant changes, until one was written** (was: the first press
     only, marked before its row was written, so a second simultaneous press could activate the grant without any
     row). Two presses at once may both write one; a press whose row fails changes nothing.
  5. **The page removes the token from the address bar** as soon as it has read it (`history.replaceState`; kept in
     memory for the button and "Try again"). A reload then says "not valid" (open the email's link again).
  6. **`hana.ug` holds a sha256 of the address**, as the device tickets' keys, never the address.
- **Residuals, stated (review item 7):**
  - A mail scanner that runs scripts and presses buttons could press Confirm for a suppressed address. Accepted: a
    one-button page can't tell it from the user, and the press only resumes mail to the address the link was mailed to
    (the address whose holder asked support), lifting no limit and touching no other address.
  - The unlock works in the browser where its link was pressed (the grant is used by that browser's next start). Kept
    as built (confirmed by the user 2026-11-18). An in-app mail browser (a mail app's
    own viewer, with storage of its own) is the usual way to miss it: the user signs in afterwards in their normal
    browser and is still refused; opening the email's link again in that browser and pressing again works (the press
    answers the same until the unlock is used).

## Free network fees in the admin portal (branch `feat/admin-evm-sponsor`), 2026-11-18

### D843. The relayer's admin tile, its events and the staff tools in the admin portal, in plain words
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: building the admin tile, events and staff tools **decided by the user 2026-11-18**; the
  details below decided while building, to confirm; what the Tech Lead's hand test showed **confirmed by the Tech Lead
  2026-11-23** (hand-tested on the local stack 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-23: "for test 4 I think it looks clear", "test 4
  looks good"; "confirm the batch"), the rest still open (the dated note after "Rejected" below) · Built (not deployed, nothing live): `packages/console-core/src/
  evm-relay.ts` (the views and inputs), `health.ts` (`ApiSystemStatus.evmRelay`), `staff.ts` (the audit actions),
  `apps/api/src/
  evm-relayer-staff.ts` (the admin view: `evmRelayerStaffOverview`, `evmRelayerStaffDetail`, `evmRelayerStaffAct`),
  `rpc/admin.ts` (`systemStatus.evmRelay`, `evmRelayDetail`, `evmRelayAct`), `system-status.ts`, `evm-relayer.ts`
  (`staffStatus().day`); `apps/console/src/audit.ts`; `apps/admin/src/evm-relay.ts` (the words and the two routes),
  `status.ts` (the tile), `security.ts` (event titles and playbooks), `public/app.js` and `app.css` (the tile's words,
  the page `/free-network-fees/<chainId>`); `packages/playbooks` (six playbooks); tests `apps/api/test/
  rpc-evm-relay.test.ts`, `apps/api/scripts/test/evm-relayer-staff.test.ts`, `apps/console/test/staff-actions.test.ts`,
  `apps/admin/test/evm-relay.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`, `apps/admin/test-spa/evm-relay.test.ts`. Current state:
  `docs/operations.md` "Free network fees in the admin portal (D843)" and the relayer's halt table, `docs/architecture.md`
  "Free network fees in the admin portal", `docs/security.md` "The EVM relayer object", `docs/api.md` (AdminRpc and
  the admin routes), `apps/admin/README.md`.
- Details decided while building (to confirm):
  1. **Cost.** `systemStatus` reads the relayer only when the env has `evm.sponsor` (absent: the field is absent and
     nothing is called; `gen sandbox-dev` output unchanged): per chain the object's staff status (storage only) and
     two reads of the trusted endpoint (relayer balance, the pinned delegate's code), each with its own 5 s deadline,
     each failing on its own. The admin's 30 s status cache covers it. A refused block answers `bad_config`, nothing read.
  2. **Plain states.** The tile names its state in words: Working, Paused: needs a person, Low on money (under
     `lowBalanceEth`; red under one transaction's worst cost, deploy-check's floor), Not set up (no block: grey, never an
     issue; the key unset: amber, it is the off switch; the key or the block refused: red), Needs a person (the
     account helper program, the pinned delegate's address, without the pinned code hash, or a second problem worse
     than the main state), Can't check right now. Each halt reason (and each `relayer_cannot_send` code) has one
     sentence and numbered steps, the runbook's table reworded (D853); the code for engineers stays apart. A nonce is
     called a **slot** on these pages.
  3. **Today's spend** is the handlers' own count on the env's day budget (`RateLimiter.spent`, read only, 2.5 s
     deadline; the count `evm_relay_budget_high` fires on), shown against `dailyBudgetEth` (amber from 80%, red when
     used up). The relayer's own backstop count stays in the view (`spentTodayWei`), and `staffStatus()` now says
     which UTC day it counts (`day`), so an earlier day's count is never shown as today's.
  4. **Records.** Slot, action or staff filler, on the network or not, taken by a node or not, cancelling, sent and
     time limit, each copy's hash with a Basescan link built by the admin Worker for a well-formed hash only, the
     refusal code, and the app from `evm_sponsor_sends` by chain and digest (D848; a failed read: "Can't check right
     now"). Never the account, raw transaction, calldata or signature. "Waiting" is amber once the oldest transaction
     not on the network, or not taken by any node, passes 2 minutes (when `evm_relay_stuck` fires).
  5. **Tools by risk.** Resume (primary, offered only while paused); Cancel per slot (not on a slot already on the
     network, not past 8 copies, not without the key); under a folded "Advanced: rarely needed" with a red warning:
     Fill a gap (only with a `nextNonce` above 0 and the key), Close as "used by something else" (slots not on the
     network), Set the next slot number (only with nothing waiting). No tool on a relayer that never sent anything or
     whose records disagree. The relayer checks every one regardless; its refusal is shown in words, never retried.
  6. **Every use audited twice** with the existing `StaffRpc.recordStaffAction` pattern (the Support ID lookup's
     order): `evm_relay.staff_action` (tool, chain, slot, note; target the chain id) before the call, no row no
     action; `evm_relay.staff_result` (the answer) after, its failure only logged. Org-less: no partner's view; the
     feed mails them to the security alias. The audit's detail strings stay at 128 characters except this note (300).
  7. **Replay and stale pages.** The request id is the audit row's key (a replay is `already_applied`, nothing done);
     the page sends back the halt's start and the newest staff action's number it showed (`seen`), and the API acts
     only while the relayer still shows both (`version_conflict` otherwise), so a double submit or a stale tab does
     nothing. Notes: 10–300 characters, trimmed, one line, no control or bidirectional characters.
  8. **The source test's allowlist** gains exactly `rpc/admin.ts`, which may import only the three admin-view
     functions, never the guard, a tool or the binding, and use them only in `hana`-actor methods.
  9. **Events.** The six sponsorship kinds (D848, D852: `evm_relay_stuck`, `_balance_low`, `_budget_high`,
     `_receipt_odd`, `_nonce_taken`, `evm_billing_late`) and the NEAR relay's `near_billing_late` (D863) each have a
     playbook in plain words written from the alert tables as merged (the stuck alert's four causes and 2 minutes,
     `quarantined`, the five NEAR counts); the Feed and notices page shows each event's title and playbook.
  10. **No admin e2e.** `apps/e2e` has no admin portal coverage (the local stack runs no admin Worker), so the local
      relayer on chain 31337 isn't driven from the portal; AdminRpc is tested against the real relayer object (a fresh
      one) and fakes of every state, the SPA in happy-dom over the Worker's own answers (`test-spa/`), and the
      screenshots come from the SPA preview's fake scenarios.
- Amended after its independent review (2026-11-18, to confirm):
  11. **(H1) A possibly leaked key is an engineer's job first.** Every halt that means the relayer's key may be used by
      someone else (console-core `isLeakHalt`: `nonce_consumed_elsewhere`, `nonce_gap`, `foreign_transactions`, and
      `relayer_cannot_send` with `replacement_underpriced`, `sender_restricted`, `nonce_too_low` or `nonce_too_high`)
      has the same steps: tell an engineer now, no money to the wallet; the engineer follows "A relayer key leaked"
      (sponsorship off, the money moved out, the key replaced); the slot tools are the engineer's after that; Resume
      only when the engineer says so. No refill is asked or raised beside such a halt. Resume no longer says "always
      safe": the relayer checks the numbers, not whether its key is safe. After such a halt Resume isn't the primary
      button and needs the tick "An engineer has confirmed the key is safe or replaced", kept in the audit row
      (`keyConfirmed`) and in the relayer's note; the API refuses it otherwise (`key_confirmation_required`). The tile
      says when the records' signer differs from the settings' wallet (the key was replaced since the stop).
  12. **(M1) Replays and races.** The relayer's staff methods take what the page showed (`expect`: the halt's start,
      the newest staff action's number) and check it inside their single-threaded queue (`version_conflict`, recorded
      like any refusal); a small, additive change to the staff methods only, nothing in sending. Each page load carries
      a one-time token (`evmact_…`) that is the audit rows' request id, so the same form sent twice is `already_applied`
      (the request's own id is new per request and couldn't catch that).
  13. **(M2) Cancel only past a slot's time limit**, or during a `stuck_past_deadline` pause: offered so on the page and
      enforced in `evmRelayAct` (`not_past_deadline`) before the relayer is called.
  14. **(M3) The next slot number from the network**, never from an explorer's list (which counts incoming transfers):
      the detail page reads the relayer address's latest and pending counts from the trusted read endpoint, as the
      relayer does, and pre-fills them ("The network says the next slot number is N"); unreadable or still moving: ask
      an engineer, or wait.
  15. **(M4) Deploy order and older pieces.** `systemStatus.evmRelay` is always sent (`absent` included); a missing
      field means an older API: the tile says "This page is newer than the API: deploy the API first" (amber). The page
      and the tools say the same when the API lacks the method, and a tool asks `AdminRpc.evmRelayVersion` before its
      audit row, so nothing is recorded or done; an older console refusing the audit action is said too.
  16. **(L1–L8)** `stuck_past_deadline`'s steps say what to do when Cancel is refused over the fee limit or has no
      button (8 copies); after a refused Resume the answer shows the relayer's latest condition and its steps; the
      fence test also refuses a re-export or a dynamic import of the staff module in `rpc/admin.ts`, and the tool
      mapping is exhaustive (an unknown tool refused, never mapped to another); notes are checked as plain text in the
      API and in the console's audit input too, the filter adding U+061C, U+200B–U+200D, U+2060–U+2064 and U+FEFF; the
      overview has a 6 s deadline (`timeout`: only this tile degrades) and the helper program's code hash is cached 10
      minutes per isolate; a `nonce_gap` with several empty slots: fill each, lowest first.
  17. **The read endpoint (D851 as amended, PR 90).** Outside `local*` envs sponsorship is off without the secret
      `EVM_SPONSOR_RPC_<chainId>`: the tile's own "Not set up" case with the upload step (`readEndpoint: 'missing'`).
  18. **(L2) Closing a slot and billing.** In the code reviewed, `settleAsCharge(consumed_elsewhere)` kept the full
      reservation as the send's cost (counted on the app's and the env's day budgets) and wrote a billing record with
      that amount under the partner's app. Open question put to the Tech Lead, answered 2026-11-18: the partner is not
      charged (D869, a separate PR); the Close tool already says "The user's action in it is marked as not done. The
      app is not charged: Journear covers it."
  19. **(Re-check M, 2026-11-18) A leak seen during any pause.** The thief case: a pause for money, then someone with
      the key empties the wallet. The relayer now marks its pause `leakSeen` when, during it, it sees a leak-type
      condition (foreign transactions, a slot used elsewhere, a gap, a leak-type refusal: console-core `isLeakHalt`),
      or staff close, fill or set a slot; the mark goes with the pause (cleared by Resume). `staffResume` takes
      `keyConfirmed` and refuses `key_confirmation_required` on a marked pause without it, recorded in its staff log,
      so the relayer enforces the confirmation itself, not only the API. The change is confined to the relayer's halt
      and staff code (`#halt`, a new `#markLeak`, `staffResume`, `#staffAct`, the halt call in the alarm). The API's
      check and the page use `needsKeyConfirmation` (the halt's reason or the mark); the page also switches to the leak
      steps when the network counts more of the wallet's transactions than the relayer sent (the detail page's read;
      code `chain_ahead`). The out-of-money steps gain a first step: "Open the relayer wallet on Basescan (its address
      is below). If money went out in transfers nobody at Journear made, stop: tell an engineer now and don't send
      money."
  20. **(Re-check L1) What the tick is.** "An engineer has confirmed the key is safe or replaced" is the acting staff
      member's own recorded statement: a speed bump with an audit trail (the audit row, the relayer's note), not a
      second person's approval; nothing checks that an engineer said it. Two-person approval (a second staffer
      approving a Resume after a leak) is a possible later step.
  21. **(Re-check L2) What the page token is.** The one-time `evmact_…` token protects against the same form being sent
      twice (`already_applied`); it is not a security control (Access, the CSRF checks, the staff list and the relayer's
      own checks are).
  22. **(Re-check L3) A fresh view before the next send.** After any refused, conflicting or unclear answer (a stale
      page, a used token, an outage) the page reads its view and a new token again before anything else can be sent,
      and shows the answer at its top; only a check inside the page itself (nothing sent) stays on the form.
- Rejected: running the tools from the API's own routes (no public route may reach them); a precheck that refuses in
  the API what the relayer would refuse (the relayer is the one guard; a second copy of its rules drifts; the two
  page-level rules above, the time limit and the key confirmation, are the staff process's, not the relayer's);
  retrying a failed tool call (whether it acted is in its own log); showing the users' accounts (staff see a user only
  through the audited Users screen).
- **2026-11-23, the batch confirmation** ("confirm the batch", the note "Confirmed in one batch, 2026-11-23" at the
  end of this file): **confirmed by the Tech Lead** as hand-tested on the page (as renamed by D879): item 2 for the states
  the hand test reached, items 3 and 4, item 5 as far as Resume, and the out-of-money steps with item 19's first step,
  through out of money → refill → Resume as it was then (D890 changed that flow later). **Still open**: items 1, 6, 7, 8,
  12, 15, 16, 21 and 22 (behind the scenes, never on a screen); item 9 (the events' words on Feed and notices); items
  11, 19's leak marking and 20 (the steps after a possible key leak, not reached); items 13 and 14 and the rest of 5
  (Cancel and the rarely needed slot tools); item 17 (the "Not set up" case). Item 10 is replaced by D873; item 18 was
  answered by D869.
- Amended by D879 (2026-11-19): staff read the feature as **Gas sponsorship**, not "Free network fees": the tile

### D867. A "Check in" card on the hosted demo shows and hand-tests a gas-free action, only where the env sponsors it
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: asked for by the Tech Lead (a way to see and hand-test a gas-free action); everything below
  decided while building and amended after the independent review of PR 91 (below); **confirmed by the user
  2026-11-18** ("confirm D867": the card and its words as in the screenshots, only where sponsorship is set up and the
  app allowed, visible with a note and the button off when paused or the day's budget is used up, the waiting line a
  best guess with no SDK progress event for now) · Built: `apps/demo/src/gas-free-card.ts` (`startGasFreeCard`,
  `GAS_FREE_TEXT`, `availabilityOf`, `gasFreeChain`, `checkInCall`, `checkInsCalldata`, `parseCount`), `config.ts`
  (`evmSponsor`, `demoEvmSponsor`), `errors.ts` (`gasFree`, `sdkUserMessage`), `page.ts` (the card after the
  addresses; `clearError` skips a box that doesn't exist); the stack: `apps/e2e/src/stack.ts`
  (`E2E_DEMO_SPONSOR_TARGETS`, `e2eEvmSponsorVar`'s `targets`), `src/server/api.ts` (the demo's app gets them),
  `src/server/partner.ts` (`MockEvm` runs the exact check-in, counts it, answers `checkIns`), `src/build.ts`
  (`DEMO_CONFIG.evmSponsor`), `tests/fixtures.ts` (`DEMO_APP`, named "Journear demo" in every demo spec); tests
  `apps/demo/test/gas-free-card.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `page.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/tests/demo-gas-free.spec.ts`.
- What it is: a card "Try an action with no network fee" with one button, **Check in**, that calls
  `hana.evm.sendSponsored` with exactly one call, Journear's demo check-in (`checkIn()`, D854), as a partner would
  (docs/integration.md "Gas-free actions" now has the same button to copy).
- When it appears (otherwise it doesn't exist: not disabled, not "coming soon"): (1) the env's manifest has an
  `evm.sponsor` block: the demo bakes its chain IDs in as `evmSponsor`, and without the block the key is left out of
  the configuration altogether and the card module returns before touching the page or the SDK. sandbox-dev has no
  block, so its generated `wrangler.jsonc` and baked configuration are byte for byte those of `next` (checked: same
  SHA-256 for both; the built page differs only in the bundle's hashed name; the stylesheet is unchanged). (2) One of
  those chains is in `hana.evm.sponsoredChains` (the vault's build) and has a `DEMO_CHECK_IN` pin in `@hana-id/core`
  (today only 31337; Base Sepolia's line comes with the delegate's deploy, D854): the demo's own EVM chain first.
  (3) Signed in, `hana.evm.sponsorship(chain)` answers available, or not available for a reason that passes
  (`budget_exhausted`, `app_budget_exhausted`, `paused`, `sponsorship_paused`, `not_available`): then the SDK's
  sentence in a blue note and the button off, asked again when the user comes back after a minute. Any other answer
  (`chain_not_enabled`, `app_not_sponsored`, a reason the demo doesn't know) or no answer: no card.
- Why the chain and the address come from the build and core, not the manifest or the API: the manifest's allowlist
  is staff data the page doesn't receive (the demo doesn't know its app id), and the API's answers are hints (D855);
  the vault's chain list and core's pin are what the vault itself checks, so the card can only ask for what the window
  will show as "Journear demo check-in, checked by Journear". The manifest block is the deploy-time switch: no block,
  no card, whatever the SDK says.
- The security bar: the call is a constant from `DEMO_CHECK_IN` and `DEMO_CHECK_IN_CALLDATA`, checked with
  `isDemoCheckInCall` before every send; nothing typed, no URL parameter and no API answer reaches it, and the module
  reads nothing from the URL (tested by a source check and a test page URL full of parameters). No secret is in the
  page. No CSP change: `sponsorship()` calls the `apiUrl` (already in `connect-src`), the count is read from the EVM RPC.
  Server side, the demo's app should be allowlisted for the exact check-in only (`exactCalldata: ["0x183ff085"]`,
  `maxDataBytes` 4), as on the stack.
- The words (D853, as amended after review, below): title "Try an action with no network fee"; "Check in to
  Journear’s demo. It counts your check-ins and doesn’t move any money. The first time, it also turns on free network
  fees for your account. You approve it in the Journear Passport window first. Journear pays the network fee, so it
  costs you nothing."; stages "Approve the check-in in the Journear Passport window." and, once the user is back on the
  page (window focus or the tab shown again: the SDK reports no approval event), "If you approved it, your check-in
  takes a few seconds. If not, go back to the Journear Passport window." (true either way); "Done. You checked in.
  Journear paid the network fee, so it cost you nothing." with "See it on the public record ↗" when the chain is the
  demo's own and has an explorer; "You’ve checked in once so far." / "… N times so far." from `checkIns(address)`
  through the page's EVM provider, on the demo's own chain only. Every refusal is the SDK's own `userMessage` (D861),
  no sentence of the demo's; a rejection is a quiet grey line (the SDK's 4001 sentence), not a red box.
- The local stack: the demo's build has the stack's chain as `evmSponsor`, the API allowlists the demo's app (DEMO_PK)
  for the exact check-in, and the mocked chain runs and counts it, so a person can sign in with email, press Check in,
  approve and see the result (docs/operations.md "Trying the gas-free check-in by hand on the local stack").
- Rejected: a disabled or "coming soon" card where the env doesn't sponsor (the Tech Lead asked for absence); a
  hard-coded chain or address in the demo; a new SDK event for "approved, now sending" (a protocol change for a demo
  stage; the focus-based stage says what is true either way); reading the count through a new RPC (the page's provider
  and CSP already have the chain's RPC).
- **Amended after review** (the independent review of PR 91, 2026-11-18; confirmed by the user 2026-11-18 with D867): (1) the intro says the
  first check-in also turns on free network fees for the account, in the setup note's words (it understated the first
  time); (2) the stage after the user is back says only what is true whether or not they approved ("If you approved
  it, …"; it said "Checking you in" when nothing may have been approved); (3) the done line is "Done. You checked in.
  Journear paid the network fee, so it cost you nothing." (the colon sentence first built was the build brief's, not
  the Tech Lead's); (4) docs/integration.md's button runs after `hana.ready` with the user signed in (before that
  `sponsorship()` answers `chain_not_enabled` and the button never appears), uses `e.userMessage ?? userMessageFor(e?.code,
  e?.data)` and marks the UI helpers as the partner's own; (5) after Done the count is read again 4 s later
  (`GAS_FREE_RECOUNT_MS`) and on the next return to the page, for the same account only, and never shown lower than
  before (the page's node may lag the check-in's block); (6) the architecture text: a failed later check keeps the
  last known state (only a failed first question means no card); (7) the stack takes the check-in's address from core's
  pin (`E2E_CHECK_IN`), not a copy; (8) a test boots the page with exactly the configuration the deployed sandbox-dev

  an SDK that sponsors the chains and allows the app, and checks there is no card and `hana.evm` is never read; it

- Address impact: none.

## A slot lost to Journear's own key is not charged (branch `fix/evm-sponsor-consumed-elsewhere-not-charged`), 2026-11-18

### D869. A sponsored action lost to a transaction Journear's relayer didn't send is not charged to the partner
- Date 2026-11-18 · Status: **confirmed by the user 2026-11-18** (the Tech Lead's words: "go with your recommendation:
  not charged"); the review amendments below to confirm; answering the open question of D843's review (item 18) · Built (not deployed): `apps/api/src/evm/
  sponsor-settle.ts` (`settleNotCharged`; `settleAsCharge` keeps `lost` only; the window names shared with
  `sponsor.ts`), tests `apps/api/test/evm-sponsor.test.ts` ("D869: …"), `evm-sponsor-relayer.test.ts` (the real relayer's
  own detection, staff closing the slot, the reconciler). Current state: `docs/api.md` (the reconciler, the billing
  records, the monthly view), `docs/operations.md` ("Watching it", "Billing records"), `docs/security.md` (the billing
  records). Amends D852 (billing records) and D847 (the reconciler's `consumed_elsewhere`).
- When a relayer slot is used up by a transaction Journear's relayer did not send (`consumed_elsewhere`: the relayer
  stops on it, staff close the slot, the reconciler reads the relayer's `closed` verdict) and the user's action in it is
  lost, the partner is not charged: the send row settles at 0 (`consumed_elsewhere`), the amount set aside goes back to
  the app's and the env's day budgets, and the user's and the app's and the env's day counts, the user's attempts and
  the failure slot are given back (none of it was the user's or the partner's doing). Once: the row moves only from the
  status it was read in, so only one settlement moves it, and that one knows what was already returned: a `rejected`
  row's counts were settled at its rejection (given back then for a cause not the user's, kept for the user's own
  `request` cause), so only its money comes back (found in the automated review of this change: returning them again
  would have eaten into other actions' counts the same day; tests for every prior status and two settlements at once).
  The row is final: no later receipt, mined verdict or correction moves it (they act on open, or settled-at-head, rows
  only).
- The billing record is kept: outcome `consumed_elsewhere`, `settled_wei` 0, no cost figures (`total_cost_wei` NULL), in
  D1 `evm_sponsor_billing` and mirrored to `usage.evm_sponsored_txs`; the monthly view groups it apart (its count is
  Journear's own losses; a billing job summing `settled_wei` never bills it). `evm_relay_nonce_taken` says
  `charged: false`.
- Schema: the existing outcome `consumed_elsewhere` is used only for this case and now means "not charged". After the
  PR's review (below) three in-place edits to migrations that are applied nowhere yet: `0022_evm_sponsor.sql` and
  `migrations-usage/0009_evm_sponsored.sql` allow a correction with no transaction when its outcome is
  `consumed_elsewhere` (`tx_hash IS NULL AND corrects IS NOT NULL AND outcome = 'consumed_elsewhere' AND record_key =
  'fix:' || send_id`, the ledger's with `LIKE 'fix:%'`); `0022` and `0023_near_relay_billing.sql` add the security event
  kind `evm_relay_closed_slot_mined` to their `security_events.kind` lists.
- Amended after its review (2026-11-18, to confirm): (L1) a row settled from a receipt at head, then reorged out, whose
  slot staff then closed (the relayer's verdict `closed` `consumed_elsewhere`) is corrected by the reorg check to not
  charged: the row `consumed_elsewhere` at 0 and a correction record `fix:<send>` at 0 with no transaction superseding
  the first (never an edit), in one D1 batch guarded on the status read and `confirmed_at IS NULL` (two runs at once:
  one moves it); the money it was charged and the counts it kept come back once (the failure slot only when it wasn't
  `executed`, which freed it already; nothing more for a rejected row). (L2) a mistaken close: for 7 days the cron's
  lowest-priority step reads the closed row's own persisted hashes (4 rows, 8 hashes a run) and writes
  `evm_relay_closed_slot_mined` once per row if one mined (playbook `evm-relay-closed-slot-mined`); it never charges.
  Tests for every open prior status (`sending`, `sent`, `timeout`, `unknown`) and the in-flight place freed, the
  ledger round trip of a NULL-cost record and the monthly view with it (PGlite).
- Known, negligible: counts are un-hit in the windows of the row's creation time, so an action whose attempt was
  counted just before UTC midnight and whose row was created just after decrements the next day's attempts count.
- Rejected: charging the reservation (the code before: the partner paid for a loss caused by Journear's own key); a new
  outcome value such as `not_charged_relayer_fault` (a schema change in two migrations for a meaning the existing,
  single-purpose outcome already carries); keeping the reservation as a "loss amount" (the other sender's spend from
  the relayer wallet isn't known, and a billing job could mistake it for a cost).
- Address impact: none.
