- Decision, in the Tech Lead's words: "instead of 'free network fees' I think 'gas sponsorship' is a clearer term for
  admin side (you can maintain free network fees for user side as it's likely clearer to non-Web3 users for this
  term)". So:
  1. **Staff side: one term, "Gas sponsorship".** A name in titles ("Gas sponsorship (Base Sepolia)", "the Gas
     sponsorship page", "Gas sponsorship: paused or slow, needs a look"), "gas sponsorship" in a sentence ("Resume gas
     sponsorship?", "gas sponsorship is switched off"). On staff pages "gas" may now be used where it makes a sentence
     clearer ("gas prices", "gas price limit", "a little ETH for gas"; the wallet is "the relayer wallet" everywhere);
     everything else stays plain (D853's style), and sentences that were already clear are not reworded.
  2. **User side unchanged.** The approval window, the sign-in pages, Passport Home, the hosted demo's card, the stamps
     site, emails to users and the SDK's `userMessage` sentences keep "free network fees" / "no network fee".
  3. **The route** `/free-network-fees/<chainId>` becomes `/gas-sponsorship/<chainId>`. The page exists only on `next`
     (`git grep free-network-fees 7243d2af`, `develop`'s head, finds nothing) and was never deployed, so no redirect
     is kept: the old address is the portal's "Page not found" and reads nothing (a test). The API routes
     (`/api/evm-relay/:chain`) are unchanged.
  4. **Not changed:** internal identifiers (`evmRelayDetail`, `evm_relay.*` audit codes, `evm_relay_*` event kinds,
     the playbook ids `evm-relay-*`, tables, manifest keys); the partner side (the to-confirm list); the NEAR relay's
     staff titles but one (item 12 below; the NEAR relay is a different feature and is deliberately NOT called gas
     sponsorship); the API's error strings to developers
     (`sponsorship_paused`'s "Free network fees are paused for now, try again later").
- Reworded beyond the term (old → new):
  1. The paused tile's line: "Nobody gets free network fees until a person fixes it." → "Gas sponsorship is stopped
     for everyone until a person fixes it."
  2. The key not loaded: "…so nobody gets free network fees. Removing the key is also how they are switched off on
     purpose." → "…so gas sponsorship is off for everyone. Removing the key is also how it is switched off on purpose."
  3. The helper program missing: "…so users' free network fees can't work." → "…so gas sponsorship can't work."
  4. `fee_cap_too_low`: "Network fees are higher right now than the relayer is allowed to pay…" → "Gas prices are
     higher right now…"; "Wait: network fees usually fall again within an hour." → "Wait: gas prices usually fall
     again within an hour."; "…ask an engineer to raise the relayer's fee limit (maxFeePerGasGwei in the settings)." →
     "…raise the relayer's gas price limit (maxFeePerGasGwei in the settings)."; the refusal "Network fees are above
     the relayer's limit right now. Try again later, or ask an engineer to raise the fee limit." → "Gas prices are above
     the relayer's gas price limit right now. Try again later, or ask an engineer to raise that limit.";
     `stuck_past_deadline`'s "If Cancel is refused because network fees are above the relayer's limit, ask an engineer
     to raise the fee limit." → "If Cancel is refused because gas prices are above the relayer's gas price limit, ask
     an engineer to raise that limit."; `no_valid_replacement`'s "…or its fee limit leaves no room for a higher fee" →
     "…or its gas price limit leaves no room for a higher fee". One limit (`maxFeePerGasGwei`, a price per unit of
     gas), one name: "gas price limit" (after the review).
  5. Fill a gap (the tool's text and its confirmation): "It costs a small network fee from the relayer wallet." → "It
     costs a little ETH for gas, from the relayer wallet." (what is spent; "ETH", not "test ETH", so it stays true on
     a main network).
  6. The page's subtitle: "Journear pays users' network fees on {network} through its relayer." → "Journear pays
     users' gas on {network} through its relayer."
  7. The tile's "affects", shown on the tile and on each of its issues (paused, low balance, budget): "Users' free
     network fees on EVM test networks (Journear pays their fees): while it is paused, nobody gets them" → per
     network, "Users' actions on {network} whose gas Journear pays: while it is paused or switched off, no new action
     there gets its gas paid" (the "Gas sponsorship" tile with no network known: "Users' actions on EVM test networks
     whose gas Journear pays: while it is paused or switched off, no new action gets its gas paid"). Scoped after the
     review: a stop on one network doesn't stop logins, the NEAR relay or other networks, and the relayer still looks
     after what it already sent; on a low-balance or budget issue it says what a stop would do, not that one happened.
  8. Not set up: "…nobody is offered free network fees." → "…gas sponsorship isn't offered to anyone."; settings
     refused: "…free-network-fee settings, so nobody gets free network fees." → "…gas sponsorship settings, so gas
     sponsorship is off for everyone."
  9. `evm_relay_balance_low`'s title: "Free network fees: the paying account is running low" → "Gas sponsorship: the
     relayer wallet is running low"; its playbook "The free network fees wallet is running low" → the same "Gas
     sponsorship: the relayer wallet is running low" (one name for the wallet, "the relayer wallet", as every other
     staff text says; after the review).
  10. Playbooks: "the relayer that pays users' network fees stopped" → "…pays users' gas stopped"; "While it is paused
      nobody gets free network fees" → "While it is paused gas sponsorship is stopped for everyone"; "reservations for
      sponsored network fees" → "…sponsored gas"; "take the app off the free-fee list" → "…off the gas sponsorship
      list".
  11. The audit labels: "Network fee relayer tool used" / "…tool result" → "Gas sponsorship tool used" / "Gas
      sponsorship tool result" (org-less rows: no partner sees them).
  12. Decided while building, after the review: the NEAR relay's billing event and playbook "Free NEAR transactions: a
      billing record is late" → "NEAR relay: a billing record is late", matching its siblings "NEAR relay daily budget
      running high", "NEAR relay account running low" and the "NEAR relay" tile. Staff only: `near_billing_late` is
      written with no organisation (`apps/api/src/near/relay-billing.ts`, the insert names no `org_id`), so the feed
      mails it to the security alias alone, and only the admin portal shows it. No other NEAR title changed.
- Tests: the admin's check that no halt or refusal sentence uses a protocol word refuses a bare "gas" but allows the
  agreed phrases ("gas sponsorship", "gas price(s)", "gas price limit"), and refuses "free network fee"; a status test
  holds the scoped "affects" line on every issue of every network; an SPA test runs every preview scenario's status

- Rejected: a redirect from the old path (never deployed: only local copies of `next` ever served it);
  renaming the internal identifiers (display text only; a rename there touches stored audit codes and event kinds).
- Address impact: none (no path, key or derivation changed).
- To confirm: (1) the sentences reworded above, in particular "Gas sponsorship is stopped for everyone", the scoped
  "affects" line, "gas prices" and "gas price limit", and "a little ETH for gas"; (2) the audit labels "Gas

  **2026-11-23** ("confirm the batch"): of (1), the term on the page, the tile and its titles, "Gas sponsorship is

  on the rarely needed Fill a gap), (2) and (3). (4) is decided (the note below).

## The sign-in window says what a link did, asks before Remove, and says what became of it (branch `feat/link-notice-wording`), 2026-11-19

### D881. The notice after a link names the wallet and why; Remove asks first; Remove and Cancel end on their outcome; the window's title is the screen's
- Date 2026-11-19 · Status: **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-19** (the notice, from the hand test: "the messaage feel
  confusing, it says 'opens this wallet too' but doesn't say what wallet etc"; the Remove confirmation and result:
  "yeah I think we need a confirmation screen as you suggested, it's too abrupt and I didn't even know what happened";
  the guestbook: "yes change the guestbook one to match the check in card"); every sentence below decided while
  building and amended after PR 105's independent review, **to confirm**; the notice, Remove's confirmation and the
  results the hand test reached **confirmed by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** (hand-tested on the local stack: "Step 1
  looks good."; "I carried on and it looks ok to me"; "confirm the batch"), the split at the end of "To confirm" · Built: display text, screens and the
  window's title only, in the sign-in window's pages, Passport Home's one sentence, the SDK's one sentence and the
  hosted demo; no vault, API, issuer or contract change, nothing new in the vault's notices.
  `packages/web/src/auth/email-page.ts` (`FRESH_TEXT`, `CHANGE_TEXT`, `changeFailure`, `kindName`,
  `HOME_SIGN_INS_SECTION`, `showBanners`, `showRemoveConfirm`, `startChange`, `showChangeResult`, `answer`,
  `readNotice`), `email-storage.ts` (`bannerAction`, `isBannerAction`), `dom.ts` (`DomOptions.titleFromHeading`,
  `SIGN_IN_WINDOW`), `login-page.ts`, `callback-page.ts` (`bannerChangeAt`, `showChangeNotProved`),
  `home-callback-page.ts`, `home-devices.ts`, `client/user-messages.ts`; `apps/demo/src/errors.ts`, `near-card.ts`,
  `index.html`; tests `packages/web/test/auth/email-follow.test.ts` ("D881"), `callback-follow.test.ts` ("D881"),
  `window-title.test.ts` (new), `test/client/user-messages.test.ts`, `apps/demo/test/errors.test.ts`, `page.test.ts`,
  `apps/e2e/tests/linking.spec.ts`, `home-sign-ins.spec.ts`, `google-cancel.spec.ts`, `hand-browser.spec.ts`,
  `demo.spec.ts`, `demo-near-shots.spec.ts`; docs `operations.md` (the hand-test flows A, B, D, E, G and the linking
  table), `architecture.md`, `security.md`, `integration.md`, `apps/e2e/README.md`.
- Decision:
  1. **The notice after a sign-in that added a way to sign in** (a banner with `fresh: true` that is active). The
     vault's banner names only the kind that joined; the window knows the case itself. Every case that sends one:
     - *Case A, Google-hosted* (the user had an email wallet, pressed Sign in with Google and picked the Google account
       with the same Gmail or Workspace address; joined at once, nothing to decide, D119): heading "You can now sign in
       with Google too"; "You already have a wallet here, made when you signed in with your email address. Your Google
       account uses the same address, so signing in with Google now opens that same wallet. Nothing was moved or lost,
       and you can sign in either way."
     - *Case A, not hosted* (the same, after "Link and continue" and a code to the address): the same heading; "You
       already have a wallet here, made when you signed in with {a…@domain}. You confirmed that address with a code, so
       signing in with Google now opens that same wallet. Nothing was moved or lost, and you can sign in either way."
     - *Case B, Google-hosted* (the user had a Google wallet, typed the same Gmail address at Sign in with email, chose
       "Link and continue" and signed in with Google; the email joined at once): "You can now sign in with email too";
       "You already have a wallet here, made when you signed in with Google. You chose to link your email address, so
       signing in with it now opens the same wallet. Nothing was moved or lost, and you can sign in either way." (with
       Remove, as before: the Google sign-in is the wallet's own).
     - *Case B not hosted* and *`linkAccount`* send a fresh banner that is **waiting**: its line ("An email will be able
       to open this wallet from {date}.") and the "Signed in" heading are unchanged.
     "here", not "in this app": a wallet belongs to the app's scope, which can hold several of the partner's apps, so
     the email wallet may have been made in a sibling app; "here" sits under "Signing in to {app} at {site}". Under the
     line, smaller: "You can see every way to sign in to your wallet in Passport Home, under “Ways to sign in”." (D874's
     section lists the wallet's own sign-in and every added one, active or waiting; when D875's older lines are shown
     too, their own note points to Passport Home instead). The tick stays green; no amber.
  2. **The address**: shown only in case A not hosted, and only as the masked `a…@domain` that the vault's `link_code`
     notice gave this window and its previous screen showed (`email-page.ts` `showLinkCode`, `codeLinkTo`, forgotten
     when the user leaves that path for an email sign-in): no new data flow and no new notice field. Case A hosted:
     this window never held the address (the Google sign-in came back through `/login/callback`; the vault's sealed
     address can't be read here). Case B: the address was typed in an earlier page load of the window, and the page
     stores no address (`email-storage.ts`), so it is gone. Nobody else's address is ever shown (D259, D874).
  3. **Remove asks first** (the first-7-days banner and D875's older line, both the wallet's own sign-in's), in D865's
     shape: "Remove the {email address | Google account} from this wallet?"; a red box "After you remove it, the
     {kind} can’t open this wallet any more. Your money stays in this wallet."; "If you sign in with that {kind} later,
     it opens a new, empty wallet of its own. It won’t be added back automatically." (true: an unlinked pair is never
     re-matched, the issuer's `unlinked` decision, so that sign-in opens its own path; an explicit `linkAccount` could
     add it back only before it opens a wallet of its own, which the sentence doesn't promise); muted "Google will ask
     you to sign in again to check it’s you." or "We’ll send one more code to your email address to check it’s you.";
     **Remove it** (red) and **Go back**. Go back shows the banners again, with nothing written and nothing marked seen
     (D875: only Done does). One press per screen, the buttons disabled, as D865's (the sign-in window has no timed
     press guard: D36/D878's guard is the approval and export windows'; none was added). An email root's code goes
     straight to the address this window proved (as D864 and D865 do).
  4. **Cancel this link** (a waiting link; any active sign-in of the wallet) asks nothing: cancelling is the safe side.
  5. **The outcome**, for both: the window remembers which change it started in its email context
     (`hana.email.<relayId>`: `bannerAction` = change, the sign-in's kind, the proof's method, the outcome's slot,
     whether the sign-in finished; kinds only), so the vault's next notice, also after the Google proof's round trip
     through `/login/callback`, shows as that change's outcome instead of closing the window. An older page reads the
     field along with the rest (the read spreads the stored object), keeps it and stores it again unused; it only
     shows the old screens. While the vault works: "Removing the {kind}" / "Cancelling the link", "This takes a few
     seconds…" (only for a proof; never for an answer that isn't one). The vault's `done` (its word after a change,
     `banners: []`):
     - Removed: "The {kind} was removed"; green "The {kind} no longer opens this wallet. Removing it didn’t move any
       money."; "Devices signed in to this wallet, this one too, will be asked to sign in again."; the "If you sign in
       with that {kind} later…" line; and "Didn’t add it yourself? Someone else may have used this wallet while it was
       added. To be safe, move your money to a new wallet. Signing in the same way opens this same wallet, so use a
       different email address or another wallet app." (plain text, not a box, so someone tidying their own second
       sign-in isn't alarmed; Passport Home's sentence for the same risk now says "money" too: "Signing out doesn’t move
       your money: if someone else may have your wallet’s key, move your money to a new wallet.").
     - Cancelled: "Link cancelled"; green "The {kind} is no longer being linked to this wallet, so it won’t open it.";
       the same "Devices signed in…" line (the API revokes after a cancel too).
     Who is signed out, traced: after a change the API revokes every vault share of the wallet's path in its scope,
     every app of it (apps/api `links.ts` `revokeAccountShares`, D233; a failed revocation is logged and those shares
     end at their own limit). A session open in a tab doesn't stop at once: the vault checks its share about once a
     minute while the tab is shown, every 5 minutes when idle, at once when a hidden tab is shown, and before any
     signature (`packages/web/src/vault/vault.ts:21-26`, `STATUS_READ_MS` :487, `STATUS_IDLE_READ_MS` :505,
     `confirmHolder` :1131, `shareConfirmed` :1150); a `'revoked'` answer ends it. A session without a share
     (`'none'` persistence) ends with its tab. So "will be asked to sign in again" holds for each, and no time is
     promised. D864's and D865's "Anyone signed in to that wallet in this app…" now drop "in this app" (the revocation
     covers every app of the scope): "Anyone signed in to that wallet will be asked to sign in again."
     The vault's `stop` carries the API's code only (no reason), so the outcome is told by code (`changeFailure`):
     - `token_invalid` (the proof wasn't this sign-in's, or the vault couldn't check it: its own failures send the same
       code): "The {kind} wasn’t removed" / "The link wasn’t cancelled"; "Nothing changed. The {kind} still opens this
       wallet." / "Nothing changed. The link is still waiting." + "We couldn’t check it was you."; for a Google check
       "If you picked a different Google account, try again with the one you signed in with."; "Close this window, then
       sign in to {app} again to try again."
     - `link_refused` (the contract's rules, prechecked or its own refusal, which is reverted: the sign-in already gone,
       the link already active or cancelled, the sign-ins changed, a nonce that doesn't match): "Nothing was changed.
       The ways to sign in to this wallet may have changed after this window opened."; "Close this window, then sign
       in to {app} again to see them as they are now."
     - Nothing changed, proved from apps/api: refused before anything is relayed (`links.ts`: `rate_limited` :211,
       `rate_limiter_unavailable` :213 and :304, `bad_request` :248-250, `token_expired` from `loginTokenRefusal` :258,
       `nonce_mismatch` :259, `near_unavailable` :103 and :267), a relay that certainly didn't run (`NOT_EXECUTED`
       :65: `near_unavailable`, `near_rejected`, `relayer_busy`, `relayer_unconfigured`, `method_not_allowed`), or the
       contract's refusal (`panics.ts` :13-17: `links_unavailable`, `link_pending`; reverted): "Nothing changed. The
       {kind} still opens this wallet." / "…The link is still waiting." + "Journear couldn’t do this just now."; "Close
       this window, then sign in to {app} again later to try again." ("later": a day's limit can be what refused it,
       100 changes a day per wallet, `links.ts` :56).
     - Anything else (`api_unavailable` for no answer, `link_in_flight`, `relayer_unavailable`, `timeout`, …: may follow
       a send): "We couldn’t check the removal" / "We couldn’t check the link" (D865's and D864's headings);
       "Something went wrong, so we can’t tell whether the {kind} was removed." / "…whether the link was cancelled.";
       "Sign in to {app} again. If the {kind} still opens this wallet, you’ll see it there with Remove." / "…If the link
       is still waiting, you’ll see Cancel this link again." The window's own endings after a change take this group
       too, as nobody can say what the vault did: the 10-minute follow limit (the vault's 5-minute wait can end while
       the user is still on Google's screen), a slot that is gone (403/410), a notice that can't be read, and a proof
       whose write failed (it may have reached the vault).
     - The check didn't finish (the vault does nothing with an answer that isn't a proof, so nothing changed): an
       email check left or failed at the code step ("The check was cancelled before the code was entered.", "The code
       was wrong.", "The code expired.", "Too many codes were asked for.", "We couldn’t send a code to check it’s
       you."), and a Google check cancelled or failed on Google's screen ("Google didn’t finish checking it’s you.",
       shown by `/login/callback`, which relays that answer and would otherwise hand over to a follow-up mode waiting
       for nothing). Each with "Nothing changed. The {kind} still opens this wallet." / "…The link is still waiting."
       and "Close this window, then sign in to {app} again to try again."; the callback's screen has the same "Signing
       in to {app} at {site}" line.
     Each failure shows "Error code (for support): {code}", and leaves the banner or line for the next sign-in (nothing
     marked seen). **Close** goes on as Done does, on the email page and on the callback: a finished sign-in to the
     sharing sheet when the app asks (D411), else closes.
  6. **The keep answer** (D875) is still written once per slot: only Done writes `{choice: 'keep'}`; Go back writes
     nothing; Remove it and Cancel write the proof (or the check's error) into that slot instead; the result's Close
     writes nothing.
  7. **The window's title is the screen's**: the sign-in window's pages (`/login`, `/login/callback`, `/login/email`,
     `/home/callback`) set `document.title` to each screen's heading, or back to the page's built title when a screen
     has none (`dom.ts` `titleFromHeading`), so a Google sign-in's follow-up screens no longer read "Sign in with
     email". Other pages keep their one title (each already true for all its screens).
  8. **`link_pending`, in the SDK and the hosted demo** (true for an email waiting for its Google wallet, D864, and
     for a waiting Google account): the SDK's `userMessage` was "This email is waiting to be linked to a wallet. Sign
     in again and follow the steps in the Journear Passport window." and is now "This sign-in is waiting to be linked
     to a wallet, so it can’t open one yet. Sign in again and follow the steps in the Journear Passport window." (no
     version bump: SDK 0.5.0 isn't with partners yet, and the guide says these sentences may be reworded at any time;
     `integration.md` doesn't quote it). The demo (was "Something went wrong (link_pending)…"): "This sign-in is
     waiting to be linked to a wallet, so it can’t open one yet. The Journear sign-in window says what to do."
     `relayer_unconfigured` (was "Journear’s relayer isn’t set up on this environment yet. Tell the Journear team."):
     "The demo’s free NEAR transactions aren’t set up on this test version yet. Tell the Journear team."
  9. **The guestbook in the check-in card's words** (D867): "Written to the guestbook on NEAR testnet.[ Your NEAR
     account was created for it.] Journear paid the network fee, so it cost you nothing." (Journear's NEAR relay sends
     it and pays). Same case, same pass: the stage "Sending it. Journear pays the network fee…" (was "Sending it
     through Journear’s relayer, which pays the fee…"); the balance line "…creates it (Journear sends it a zero-value

## The local stack's relayer alarm (branch `fix/e2e-local-alarm-cadence`), 2026-11-19

From `next` @ 365ded2d; not merged, not deployed.

### D882. The local stack's relayer alarm: only a change from outside the alarm comes soon; while halted the product runs every 15 s
- Date 2026-11-19 · Status: the finding and the local fix decided while building (test tooling and tests only, no
  product code), to confirm; one open question for the Tech Lead (below) · Built: `apps/e2e/src/server/workers.ts`
  (`MemoryStorage`: `setAlarm`, `sync`, `runAlarm`; `MemoryNamespace` routes a direct `alarm()` call through
  `runAlarm`); tests `apps/e2e/test/stack.test.ts` ("soonAlarmMs: only a change from outside the handler fires soon"),
  `apps/api/test/evm-relayer.test.ts` ("while halted, the alarm comes back on its own cadence", and the next alarm
  asserted in the two `relayer_cannot_send` insufficient-funds tests); docs `apps/e2e/README.md`,
  `docs/operations.md` ("Trying the staff admin portal by hand on the local stack"). Number: D879 and D881 are taken on
  `feat/admin-gas-sponsorship-wording` and `feat/link-notice-wording` (not merged), so this is D882.
- What happened: on the hand-run local stack, after `staff-demo out-of-money` paused the relayer
  (`relayer_cannot_send`, `insufficient_funds`, one transaction waiting), its alarm ran about 4 times a second for 24
  minutes (5,714 `evm_relay_rebroadcast` log lines) until the lane was reset. Measured on this branch's own stack:
  77 such lines in 20 s before the fix, 1 after (then one every 15 s).
- The finding (product, nothing changed): in that state the product runs every 15 s, with no backoff and no spin.
  `#schedule` sets `now + EVM_RELAYER_ALARM_MS` on every run while a record is unmined and no endpoint took it
  (`urgent`), halted or not, and `alarm()` catches everything and sets 15 s itself. Pinned now for each pause, each
  halted run starting when its alarm is due: `relayer_cannot_send` (at send, and found by a later run) and
  `stuck_past_deadline` every 15 s exactly (5 runs each); `nonce_consumed_elsewhere`, `nonce_gap` and
  `foreign_transactions` (records a node took) 15 s after a change (the 60 s fee bump) else doubling, so 15 s, 30 s,
  60 s in turn; `key_mismatch` (nothing can be signed, so nothing changes) doubling to 5 minutes. None ever at or
  before now.
- The cause (local only): the in-memory storage fired any alarm asked for at most 15 s ahead after `soonAlarmMs`
  (250 ms on the hand-test lane and on the main stack's relayer). The relayer's own `now + 15 s` always fell in that
  window, so it ran again every 250 ms, for ever.
- Decision (the local stack): `soonAlarmMs` applies only to a change from OUTSIDE the alarm handler.
  1. An alarm set from outside the handler (a send, a staff action) at most 15 s ahead fires after at most
     `soonAlarmMs`, as before: the first run after a send or a staff tool still comes in 250 ms.
  2. An outside `sync()` (a request confirming its writes: the relayer's send does it after leaving a pending alarm
     at most 15 s away in place) brings that pending alarm's timer forward the same way, so a send made while the
     relayer's own 15 s alarm is pending is still looked at in 250 ms.
  3. An alarm the handler sets for itself, from anywhere in its awaited run, fires at the time it asked: 15 s, or the
     backoff, as deployed. The stored alarm (`getAlarm`) is always the time asked for; only the timer is shortened.
  4. An outside set or sync while a run is in progress makes that run's own later set soon too (in workerd the
     handler's set replaces the request's: there is one alarm; here the request's "soon" carries over). One outside
     change shortens at most that run's next alarm, so nothing loops.
  5. Which run a call belongs to follows the async context (Node's AsyncLocalStorage), not a flag: a request served
     while a run awaits is outside it; a nested run, or two runs side by side, each have their own; a call after its
     run ended is outside. A lane control's direct `alarm()` call (`POST /__e2e/lane/run`, a scenario's `until`) is
     a run too, so what it sets keeps its time.
  Who depended on the fast repeat runs: nothing in the suite (the test lanes' alarms run only by their controls; the
  scenarios reach each state with `run` and `until`). On the hand-test lane each staff tool's result shows at once or on
  the first run after it (250 ms: the tool's own reschedule is an outside set); checked by hand-equivalent requests for
  Fill a gap, Cancel, Close, Set the next slot number and Resume after a refill. The hosted demo's gas-free check-in
  never waited on the relayer's alarm: the send request itself polls the chain for the receipt (`waitForReceipt`) and
  answers "done"; the relayer's own record settles on the run 250 ms after the send.
- Open question for the Tech Lead (product, not changed): should the relayer back off while it is paused with a
  transaction no endpoint took? Today it tries every 15 s for as long as the pause lasts (5,760 tries a day of RPC
  calls and `evm_relay_rebroadcast` warnings). Backing off (up to 5 minutes, as for an accepted record) would cut that,
  but a refill or a fix would then be noticed up to 5 minutes later unless staff press Resume (Resume checks the
  network at once). While NOT paused the 15 s is deliberate (that record may hold every later one up).
- Rejected: (a) dropping `soonAlarmMs` (every hand step after a send or a staff tool would wait 15 s); (b) a flag set
  for the handler's duration (it would leak to a request served while the handler awaits, and a nested or concurrent
  run would clear it early); (c) a lower bound on any repeat timer (it would still run several times faster than
  deployed and hide a real spin); (d) changing the relayer to back off while paused (a product decision: the open
  question above).
- Security: test tooling only; nothing in production changes.
- Address impact: none.
- To confirm (decided while building): items 2 and 4 (an outside sync, or an outside change during a run, makes the
  next alarm soon).
- Open question answered by D890 (2026-11-23): while paused for money the relayer now runs every 15 s for the pause's
  first 10 minutes, then every 60 s (with or without a record waiting), so a refill is noticed within about a minute and
  restarts it by itself (D890's checks); about 10,000 provider calls a day instead of 35,000. Other pauses keep the
  cadence pinned above.

## A free network fee moves into the details (branch `feat/free-fee-in-details`), 2026-11-19

From `next` @ 032711e8; not merged, not deployed.

### D884. A fee the user doesn't pay is only in the folded details: "Free. Sponsored by {App}."
- Date 2026-11-19 · Status: **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-19** while hand-testing a relayed NEAR approval: (1) "for
  'network fee' it currently says 'free for you. Someone else pays it.'. Can we word it something like 'Sponsored by
  [XXX]' where [XXX] could be the partner's name?" and (2) "I'm thinking if we should move network fee into 'Show
  details' as regular users might not be interested, unless the network fee is not free."; the table below proposed by
  the coordinator, answered "go"; the details decided while building, to confirm; the free fee's row under "Show
  details" **confirmed by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** (hand-tested: "yes first row network fee looks as you expected.";
  "confirm the batch"), the split at the end of "To confirm" · Amends D858 and D877 (and D853's
  word list for this one line) · Built: `packages/core/src/decode/summary.ts` (`FREE_FEE`; `SPONSORED_FEE` and
  `RELAYED_FEE` are it), `packages/web/src/auth/render-approval.ts` (`renderApproval`'s fee rows, `sponsorText`,
  `NO_APP_NAME`, `nearDelegate`, `NEAR_DELEGATE_HEADING`, `NEAR_DELEGATE_NOTES.relayer`, `NEAR_SENT_FOR_YOU`,
  `NEAR_DELEGATE_NONE`, `sponsoredDetails`), `auth/css/approval.css` (`dl.fee-facts`); tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/render-approval-fee.test.ts` (new: every kind of request, free or not, and the app's name),
  `render-approval-sponsored.test.ts`, `render-approval-near.test.ts`, `approval-summary.test.ts`,
  `packages/core/test/approval-summary.test.ts` (every summary the tests build: a free fee is `FREE_FEE` exactly on
  the two free kinds, a paid fee never reads as free), `evm-sponsored-approval.test.ts`, `demo-check-in.test.ts`,
  `plain-words.ts`; `apps/e2e/tests/approval-summary.spec.ts` ("D884"), `evm-sponsor.spec.ts`,
  `approval-plain-shots.spec.ts` (the screens).
- Decision:

  | Case | Main view | Under "Show details" |
  |---|---|---|
  | Fee is free for the user (a sponsored EVM action; a relayed NEAR action) | No fee row | First: "Network fee: ✓ **Free.** Sponsored by **{App}**." |
  | The user pays the fee (an EVM transaction, a NEAR transaction, a Stellar transaction) | The fee row, as before | The same as before (no fee row) |

  A fee row in the main view now means "you pay this". {App} is the app's registered name, the value the window's
  header shows ("From **Journear demo**"). Both kinds of free fee read the same (`FREE_FEE`). The Network row stays in
  the main view (which network is a safety fact, D726). The amber one-time setup note of a first sponsored EVM action
  is unchanged. A request that costs no fee at all (a message, typed data, raw signing, a Stellar authorization) has
  no fee row, as before.
- Where in the details: the first row, in a row of its own (`dl.jp-kv.facts.fee-facts`), above the user's account row
  (D876) and the Support ID, before any technical data: the user who opens the details to ask "does it cost me
  anything?" finds the answer first. D877's look is kept there: "Free." in bold after a check mark, words in the text
  face, the app's name bold as in every sentence. The check mark stays: it marks the answer the row gives (free) at a
  glance among technical rows, and it follows D877's colour rule unchanged (the success colour on a calm window, the
  plain text colour on a window with a red box, so it never reads as "safe" beside a danger). It is decorative
  (`aria-hidden`), as before.
- Every other sentence that says who pays for a free action, old → new (each in `render-approval.ts`):
  (1) the relayed NEAR details' heading "NEAR transaction, fee paid by a relayer" → "NEAR transaction, sent for you";
  (2) its note "Someone else (a relayer) sends this for you. They pay the network fee and prepay any NEAR it attaches
  or sends; if an action fails, that NEAR comes back to your account. The actions run as your account." → "Someone
  else sends this for you, sponsored by **{App}**. They pay the network fee and any NEAR it attaches or sends. If an
  action fails, that NEAR comes back to your account. The actions run as your account." (the refund rule kept);
  (3) the main view's row "NEAR it sends, paid by someone else: {amount}" → "NEAR it sends, not from your account: {amount}"
  (the app is named in the details, not here: "sponsored" stays off the main view, D853, and a long name doesn't sit
  in a label); (4) the main view's total "None of your NEAR (someone else pays the fee and any NEAR it sends). Tokens it
  moves are yours." → "None of your NEAR. It can move tokens you hold." when the action holds a contract call, "None of your NEAR." otherwise (who pays is in the details now); (5) the
  sponsored details' heading "EVM action, network fee paid by Journear" → "EVM action, sent for you by Journear", and
  its row "Paid by: Journear’s relayer 0x…" → "Sent by: Journear’s relayer 0x…" (true on the chain, but beside
  "Sponsored by {App}" it read as a second, different payer). Unchanged: the amber setup note ("turns on free network
  fees": what it does, not who pays), the amber acts-as-you line (it says nothing about the fee), the check-in's
  lines, a NEAR transaction's "Relays a meta transaction signed by …: your account pays its network fee." (the user
  pays), a Stellar fee bump's line "The network fee is paid by {account}." (an account the request names, not the
  app; "to confirm" 8). There are no `summary*` files in `packages/web/src`: the summary's strings are
  `packages/core/src/decode/summary.ts`'s. D858's "Cost to you: nothing. Someone else pays the fee." no longer exists
  (removed by D858's own correction).
- What the window can and cannot know: it can't see who pays in the end, or who will relay a NEAR action. What it can
  guarantee is that the user's account pays no fee: a sponsored EVM action is decoded only when its relayer is this
  build's own (`packages/core/src/decode/evm-sponsored.ts:58-62`; any other relayer makes the request unreadable, with
  no Approve: the page's claim of sponsorship is never taken), and the outer transaction of a NEAR delegate action is
  signed and paid by whoever relays it, never the user's account (nearcore). `freeFee` is set by the summary from the
  decoded kind alone (`summary.ts` `sponsoredAction`, `nearActions` with `relayed`), never from anything the page or
  the vault sends. So "Sponsored by {App}" is an attribution, as the Tech Lead asked, not a fact the window checked.
- Why naming the app is fair, case by case (the code today):
  - EVM, Journear's relayer: its wallet pays the gas on the chain; only apps on the sponsorship allowlist get it
    (`apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-config.ts:88-89`); every settled send writes a billing record carrying the app and its
    org (`apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-billing.ts:48-56`, `JOIN apps a ON a.id = s.app_id`), copied to the usage ledger
    (D852). No billing job charges partners yet (D852: records now, billing "in the future"): today Journear pays and
    the cost is recorded against the app. Fair as an attribution: the app asked for the action and turned on free fees
    for its users; it is not "the app's money" until billing is on ("to confirm" 7).
  - EVM, a send lost to a transaction Journear's relayer didn't send (D869, `consumed_elsewhere`): settled at 0, not
    charged to the partner (`apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-settle.ts:343-346`). The user's action didn't run; the user paid
    nothing. The line was a statement about the fee of an action that didn't happen; still not misleading about the
    user's cost.
  - NEAR, Journear's relay: the relay account pays; one billing record per transaction with the app and its org
    (`apps/api/src/near/relay-billing.ts:122-134`, written after the answer, `apps/api/src/near/relay.ts:535`). It
    refuses any delegate action that attaches NEAR (`apps/api/src/near/delegate.ts:233-234`, D732), so NEAR in a
    relayed action is never Journear's. Billing is off here too (D863: records only).
  - NEAR, relayed by the partner itself: the partner pays the gas and any attached NEAR; Journear has no record. "Sponsored
    by {App}" is literally true. Relayed by someone the app handed the signed action to: the app arranged it; the
    attribution is to the party that asked for the action, which is as far as the window can see.
  - Journear's own apps (the hosted demo "Journear demo", the stamps site): Journear pays and records it against its
    own app; "Sponsored by Journear demo" is true.
- The main view still answers "will this cost me anything?" without the fee row? For each free action after the
  change: the sponsored check-in says "It doesn’t move any money or tokens."; a sponsored token move says the amount in
  its headline; a sponsored permission says it in its red or amber line; a sponsored call Journear can't read says "It
  could take your money or tokens." in red; a relayed NEAR action that can take the user's NEAR or tokens keeps "NEAR
  leaving your account" ("None of your NEAR. It can move tokens you hold.", an amount, "All of it", "Unknown", "NEAR
  locked up for staking", tested); NEAR the action attaches reads "NEAR it sends, not from your account". Two kinds
  said nothing about cost once the fee row left; after the review of PR 107 (decided while building, to confirm) each
  gets one line, only where nothing stronger answers cost: a plain relayed NEAR call (`noNearLeaves`; since D885 not
  the stamps' collect and the guestbook on their reviewed accounts, whose own line "… doesn’t move any money or
  tokens." answers it) the row "NEAR leaving your account: None of your NEAR." (nothing about tokens: the summary
  sees none move, and the amber "acts as you" line says the call can use what the user keeps with that contract); a
  sponsored EVM action Journear reads whose calls move nothing it can see (a generic call such as `deposit()`, taking a
  permission back, `withdraw`; alone or batched with the check-in; no warning but the setup note) the line "None of
  your ETH is used." with the chain's coin (`noCoinUsed`; true: the subject decoder refuses any value on a sponsored
  call and only the build's relayer can submit the batch, `contracts/evm-delegate/src/HanaDelegateExecutor.sol`). Never
  "tokens it moves are yours": a contract that already holds a permission from the user can move tokens the window
  can't see. Not on the check-in (its line says it moves no money), an amount in a headline, a grant, a call Journear
  can't read, or a total row. A test holds that every free action's main view says something about cost.
- The app's name: exactly the header's value (`msg.appName`, the same string the "From" box and the headline show; no
  new source). Its rules apply as they do everywhere: stored NFC, trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, one display-safe line,
  not like a web address and never "Hana", "Journear" or "Passport Home" in any case, spacing or look-alike alphabet
  (`packages/console-core/src/names.ts` `normalisePartnerAppName`, `appNameProblem`, D686, D765); the vault's config
  and every popup message take only a display-safe line of 1 to 200 characters (`packages/web/src/vault/config.ts`,
  `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` `isAppName`: no control, format, bidi or invisible character). Shown as every
  sentence shows it: its own `strong.app-name` element, the text exactly as given (no shortening: the "From" box
  doesn't shorten it either), bidi-isolated by the page's CSS (`strong { unicode-bidi: isolate }`), so right-to-left
  letters can't reorder the words around it; a long name wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`). Nothing but the full stop
  follows it in the fee line (tested), so a long name can't push the window's words into a misleading order. A name
  that reads like a sentence would read so in the headline and the header already; here it is folded and in bold.
- No name to show (empty or blank; not reachable today, every popup message carries a registered name): "Free.
  Sponsored by the app." and "… sponsored by the app." in the relayed note (`NO_APP_NAME`): whole and true sentences.
- Address impact: none (display only; nothing that is signed, decoded or derived changed; no guard changed).
- Rejected: "Free for you. {App} pays it." in the main view (the Tech Lead chose the details, and "pays" claims more
  than the window knows); "Sponsored by" alone (says nothing a user can use, and the word list's jargon without a
  name); hiding the Network row too (which network is a safety fact); keeping "Journear pays it for you." for EVM
  (true on the chain, but the two free kinds should read the same and the partner is the sponsor in the business
  model); naming the app in the main view's "NEAR it sends" row (puts "sponsored" above the fold and a long name in a
  label; the details say it); the fee row at the end of the details (after raw data).
- To confirm: (1) the placement, first in the details above "Your account"; (2) the check mark kept there, with
  D877's colour rule; (3) "the app" when there is no name; (4) "NEAR it sends, not from your account", "None of your
  NEAR. It can move tokens you hold." (an action with a contract call) and "None of your NEAR." (without); (5) the
  details' "EVM action, sent for you by Journear", "Sent by" and "NEAR transaction, sent for you", and the relayed
  note's words; (6) the two cost lines built after the review, "NEAR leaving your account: None of your NEAR." (since
  D885 not on Journear's reviewed NEAR calls: the stamps and guestbook on their reviewed accounts) and
  "None of your ETH is used.", and where they show; proposed, not built: after "None of your ETH is used." a short
  true warning "It may still use tokens you've already let this program use."; (7) decided 2026-11-23, see the note
  below; (8) a
  Stellar fee bump paid by another account keeps its main-view line "The network fee is paid by {account}." (a fee the
  user doesn't pay, said in view, but naming an account the request names, not the app); (9) texts outside the window
  left as they are: the hosted demo's card "Journear paid the network fee, so it cost you nothing." (`apps/demo`, not
  this branch), the stamps site's "Fare paid" blurb "Free for you: Journear pays the network fee, so you need no
  NEAR." and "It was free for you." (Journear's own apps, where Journear does pay). The hosted demo's cards (D881)
  say "Journear paid the network fee, so it cost you nothing." for the check-in and the guestbook while the window's
  details say "Sponsored by Journear demo.": both true, the demo being Journear's own app; the card speaks after the
  action ran, the window never claims zero cost (D858). The SDK's default user messages say "Journear's free network
  fees…" (`packages/web/src/client/user-messages.ts`): left for the partner-side terms (D879's open question 4).
  **2026-11-23** ("confirm the batch"): (1) and (2) **confirmed by the Tech Lead** (hand-tested); (7) decided (the note
  below); still open: (3), (4), (5), (6), (8) and (9).
- After the review of PR 107 (2026-11-19):
  - The attribution: "Sponsored by {App}" was built as the Tech Lead asked. The Tech Lead was told on 2026-11-19 that
    partners are not charged yet (an earlier statement in this work that they are billed was wrong: today Journear's
    relayers pay, and the cost is recorded against the app). Keeping it, softening it (for example "Free for you,
    through {App}.") or dropping the name is the Tech Lead's open decision. The reviewer's point: any page can ask for a
    NEAR delegate signature, so any app gets "Sponsored by {App}" on one; it costs the user nothing either way.
  - **Decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** (asked "Sponsored fees: are partners meant to pay eventually?", answered
    "yes"): "Network fee: ✓ Free. Sponsored by {App}." **stays as built**; the softer "Free for you, through {App}." is

  `e2e-stamps.testnet` (`collect`)" with the amber "This acts as you: `e2e-stamps.testnet` can use anything you keep

- **How the existing reviewed mechanisms work** (read for this decision; reused, no parallel system):
  - The EVM demo check-in (D854): `packages/core/src/demo-check-in.ts:21` pins, per chain id, the contract's
    deterministic CREATE2 address and runtime code hash, both from the checked-in artifact
    `contracts/evm-delegate/artifacts/CheckIn.json` (a test ties them; the code hash is checked on chain by a person
    before a chain is added, never at approval time). `isDemoCheckInCall` (`:29`) matches chain, address (any case),
    calldata exactly `0x183ff085` and value 0. `verified-contracts.ts:138` lists it as "Journear demo check-in"
    (`DEMO_CHECK_IN_NAME`, `:68`). `decode/summary.ts` `demoCheckIn` (next's `:450`, used at `:473`, `:633`, `:664`)
    gives the headline "{App} wants to check you in" and the lines "This is Journear’s demo check-in. It doesn’t move
    any money or tokens." and "It uses **Journear demo check-in** ({address}, checked by Journear).". `CheckIn.sol` has
    no owner, no upgrade and nothing payable, so the address is the code. The sponsor allowlist (`evm.sponsor`, D855's
    vault checks, the API's `exactCalldata`) decides what Journear *pays for*; it plays no part in what the window says.
  - The verified list's other entries (Sodax, D44): pinned data in the bundle, by chain and exact address, each from
    the protocol's own sources; "(checked by Journear)" after a spender's name asserts that identity.
  - The reviewed token list (D860): `known-tokens.ts:83`, by network and exact id, each from the issuer's own page;
    the token's own metadata is never read.
  - The NEAR network row (D726, D729): `render-approval.ts:850` `nearNetworkLine`, "NEAR test network (checked by
    Journear)" when the vault checked the claim (`:856`: a transaction's block hash on the env's RPC, a test app's
    delegate key, nonce and expiry on both providers, D263's rule).
  - D858's relayed-NEAR summary: `nearActions` (next's `summary.ts:1664`) builds the lines; `noNearLeaves` (`:1701`)
    drops the repeated "None of your NEAR" row when every action is a transfer or a plain "use {contract} ({method})"
    and nothing warns; `actsAsYou` (`:1657`, code `acts_as_you`) is pushed for every relayed call to another account
    (`:1707`); the fee row is `RELAYED_FEE` (`:1651`).
  - So "checked by Journear" means one thing on every surface: Journear itself checked the fact in front of it (which
    contract or token this is, which network), from its own sources, never the app's word. On the check-in and now on
    these NEAR entries it also stands for a contract whose code a person read and that can't change.
- **What makes a NEAR entry safe to trust.** A NEAR account's code changes only through a `DeployContract` (or
  `UseGlobalContract`) action the account itself sends: a transaction signed by one of its access keys, or a receipt
  its own code creates. So an account with **no access key** whose code **creates no such action** can never change its
  code or be deleted. Per contract, from the source in this repository and the docs:
  - `contracts/hana-stamps/src/lib.rs`: no owner, no admin or upgrade method, no `#[payable]` method (near-sdk refuses
    a deposit on `collect`), no promise of any kind (no transfer, no cross-contract call, no deploy). sandbox-dev's
    `near.demoStamps` was deployed 2026-11-13 by `deploy-stamps` (deploy and `new()` in one transaction, the code hash
    checked against its build: `9pjHDkQQ5j37cU8kiVcnebh22788f6vAkS5JAY1pSNvA`) and **locked** the same day after the
    Tech Lead's hand check (lock transaction `wUxYjzymRJ825xVs5zzr386LBfLocVsZz1fo1jAXDfU`, `view_access_key_list` `[]`;
    `docs/operations.md` "Hosted stamps demo", `docs/hackathon.md`).
  - `contracts/hana-guestbook/src/lib.rs`: the same (no owner, no upgrade, nothing payable, no promise). sandbox-dev's
    `near.demoGuestbook`: code hash `2cGY7mcQevAjB5nssu8VNYkkSiqSiSdimB98QYXbKJxb`, **locked** 2026-11-12 (lock
    transaction `HqnP7FRupTXdAUkKwVspAwRsY2ov3AWpwJLs4rR3VqDr`, no key left; `docs/operations.md` "Hackathon demo
    guestbook (NEAR)", D743).
  - The local e2e stack: its own models of both contracts (`apps/e2e/src/server/stamps-contract.ts`, `chain.ts`, held
    against the real wasm call by call, D805), on a mocked testnet; test only, never deployed.
- **The binding chosen: (a), a reviewed record beside each entry, no new network read.** Pinned data in core
  (`REVIEWED_NEAR_DEPLOYS`, by env name): the code hash, the lock date and the lock transaction, as recorded when a
  person checked them, and the sha256 of the account id checked (never its name). The account itself comes only from
  the env's manifest (`near.demoStamps`, `near.demoGuestbook`, CLAUDE.md), into the popup only through the build
  (`HanaEnv.nearReviewed`, generated by `gen-envs` only for an env with a record; the e2e stack sets its own for its
  models). **The build enforces the record** (after the review of PR 106: CI is off, so a test alone wasn't enough):
  `gen-envs` (`nearReviewedOf`) throws when the env isn't on testnet or when a manifest account's sha256 isn't the

- **Per contract, not per app.** The reading says what the contract's code does with this exact call, which is the
  same whoever asks; the window names the asking app from the vault (`{App}`), never from the request, and the EVM
  check-in is per contract too. A per-app list would need app ids in the build (D1 data, not the manifest) and would
  add no safety: an unreviewed app making the exact reviewed call has exactly the reviewed effect (tested: "Some Other
  App wants to collect the Arrival stamp for you").
- **The match rule** (`reviewedNearCall`, `reviewedNearMessage`); anything outside it is not a match, and the summary
  is the one the request gets with no entry at all (tested field for field, and the rendered page byte for byte):
  - the NEAR test network (`network: 'testnet'`: the only network a build has; the vault checks the claim as D726,
    D729 say, and a live app's amber "could also be used on the real NEAR network" line stays);
  - the receiver exactly the build's account for that contract (no case folding, no prefix or suffix: look-alikes such
    as `stamps-reviewed.testnet.evil.testnet` don't match), never the user's own account, and not two contracts named
    the same account;
  - exactly one action, a function call of the contract's one reviewed method (`collect`, `add_message`), deposit
    exactly 0, gas above 0 and at most 30 Tgas (`REVIEWED_NEAR_MAX_GAS`: the sites attach 10, a call burns under 2);
  - the arguments strict JSON (UTF-8, no duplicate key, no lone surrogate) of exactly the reviewed shape, no other key:
    `collect` `{stamp}` for `arrival`, `sponsored`, `own_fare`, `layover`; `{stamp: 'postcard', note}`; `{stamp:
    'signature', proof: {message, nonce, recipient, signature}}` with `message` exactly "Stamp my passport: " + the
    sender, `recipient` exactly the contract's account, `nonce` and `signature` standard padded base64 of 32 and 64
    bytes in their one canonical form, and the signature **verified** (ed25519, strict) by the sender's own key (an
    implicit account: the key is the account id) over the NEP-413 payload, as the contract's `proof_is_valid` checks
    it (after the review of PR 106: a shape-only check made "the message you signed" untrue for a forged proof; the
    check is math on the request's bytes, no new trust); `add_message` `{text}`;
  - relayed or direct as the site sends it: Own fare only as the user's own transaction (the contract refuses it
    relayed), every other stamp only relayed; the guestbook either way (the hosted demo has both);
  - typed slots only: the stamp is one of the contract's six (a string: a number, boolean or null is no match), shown
    by the title the stamps site gives its slot (`REVIEWED_STAMP_TITLES`, tested against
    `apps/stamps/src/ui/labels.ts`); a note or a message is shown (`reviewedText`) only when it is exactly what the
    contract stores (already trimmed as Rust's `str::trim` trims, 1 to 140 or 200 Unicode scalar values) and one
    display-safe line (no control, format, bidi or invisible character, no variation selector or zero-width joiner, so
    no emoji sequence), with **no run of more than two combining marks** (`COMBINING_RUN`: two cover every accent one
    letter takes, e.g. Vietnamese) and **no quotation mark** (`QUOTE_LIKE`: every Unicode Quotation_Mark and look-alikes
    such as double primes, ditto and ornaments, except the single quotes U+0027, U+2018, U+2019, U+201B, U+FF07, which
    are also the apostrophe in "don't"); otherwise not a match. After the review of PR 106 (a note of 40 combining

- **Review notes, the amber line per entry** (D858's default: it stays; it may go only where the method can't move or
  spend anything of the user's and the binding guarantees the code). It goes for every entry here:
  - `collect`: not payable (a deposit is refused; the rule also requires 0); no promise, so it can't move NEAR or any
    token anywhere; the only thing a user "keeps with it" is their passport, and `collect` only ever appends one stamp
    to the caller's own passport after checking it isn't there (`stamps.iter().all(|s| s.stamp != id)`, then
    `passports.insert(caller…)`); it never removes or changes a stamp, and nothing else in the contract does. Storage is
    the contract's own balance. Locked, no upgrade: the code is the code read.
  - `add_message`: not payable, no promise; it appends one message attributed to the predecessor; no method removes
    or edits one (the ring drops the oldest beyond 50, whoever wrote it, which the guestbook's README says). Locked.
  - The Signature message: its signature only lets the stamps contract check, inside `collect`, that the caller owns
    the account (the message names that account and the recipient is the contract: useless for anything else Journear
    knows of, and it moves nothing). The two NEP-413 amber lines asked the user to judge a recipient; for this exact
    message Journear has judged it.
  - What the new lines claim, each from the source: no money or tokens move (relayed: the relayer pays the fee and no
    deposit is attached; direct: the user pays the fee, which the fee row says, and the call itself moves nothing); the
    note and the message are public and can't be deleted (stored on a public contract with no delete method); the
    stamp checks the signed message. D858's rule (no zero-cost claim unless Journear fully knows the effect) holds:
    these are the only NEAR requests whose effect it fully knows; the test allowlist names each sentence.
- **What "checked by Journear" asserts here**, the same as everywhere: Journear itself checked that the account is its
  reviewed contract (on this env, from its manifest, deployed from the reviewed source and locked), not the app's word.
  It asserts no more than on the EVM check-in (whose address is its reviewed, ownerless code) and no less; the plain
  lines are Journear's reading of that code for this exact call. No wording had to change.
- **The Signature stamp's message after D886** (merged 2026-11-19: headline, amber box, "For" row, "The message" label,
  the message, a blue note that a signature counts on every network): for the reviewed message the two NEP-413 amber
  lines stay out, and the "counts on every network" note, which would sit beside "Signing it doesn’t move any money or
  tokens." as a mixed signal, is replaced by a blue note true for this signature: "This signature names your account
  and the stamps program. The program accepts it only from your account, to collect this one stamp." For a test app
  (whose own note the page leaves out on a message): "This app is a test version, so don’t keep real money in this
  account. This signature names your account and the stamps program, which accepts it only from your account, to
  collect this one stamp." Why true: the message names the account and the recipient is the program; its reviewed
  `proof_is_valid` checks the caller is that account and the recipient itself, and `collect` stores each stamp once
  per account. It says nothing about other verifiers, which Journear can't know.
- **Whose words** (after the review of PR 106): entries are per contract, so any app, a hostile one too, gets the
  reading, and the app chooses the note or the message (the hosted demo pre-fills it). So the window never says "your
  note" or "your message": "The note", "The message", the headline "… wants to add a message to the demo guestbook",
  and "It’s posted under your account. Anyone can see it, and you can’t delete it.", true whoever wrote the words.
- **Near-misses** (each tested: summary equal to the no-entry one; the page byte for byte for a set of them):
  mainnet; no entries in the build; the other contract's account; look-alike and different accounts; the user's own
  account; another method or another case of it; any deposit (1 yocto, 1 NEAR); gas above 30 Tgas; the call twice;

  marks, any quotation mark (straight, curly, low, guillemets, primes, ditto, fullwidth), an emoji with a variation
  selector or a joiner; a numeric, boolean or null stamp; a proof for another account or recipient, of the wrong

- Not changed: what is signed, how requests are decoded, any guard, the vault, the API, the contracts, the fee rows and

## The hosted demo's NEAR card in plain words (branch `feat/demo-plain-wording-2`), 2026-11-23

From `next` @ 0c47747b, not merged, not deployed. The second plain-wording pass on the hosted demo (`apps/demo`): what
D881 left, listed there (the NEAR card's refusals that still said "Journear's relayer", and "NEAR testnet" across the
page).

### D889. The demo's NEAR card says what happened in plain words, checks first when a send may have gone out, and names networks as the approval window does
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the rule is the Tech Lead's standing one (D853, D879: on the user side "network fee", never
  gas, relayer or testnet; D881 listed this pass); every sentence below decided while building, **to confirm** · Built:
  display text only, in `apps/demo/src/errors.ts` (`NEAR_VAULT_REASONS`, `RELAYER_REASONS`, `RELAY_REFUSED`,
  `RELAY_DOWN`, `CHECK_LIST`, `nearMessage`), `near-card.ts` (`STAGES`, `guestbookDone`, `NEAR_NETWORK_LABEL`,
  `SEND_UNCONFIRMED`, the balance line, "Sign a transaction"'s result titles), `page.ts` (`STELLAR_NETWORK_LABEL`, the
  EVM label from `@hana-id/core` `evmChainInfo`, the badge, the login stage), `index.html`; tests
  `apps/demo/test/errors.test.ts`, `page.test.ts`, `near-fakes.ts`, `brand.test.ts`, `plain-words.test.ts` (new: the
  brand's plain-words check over the demo's strings), `apps/e2e/tests/demo.spec.ts`, `demo-near-shots.spec.ts`,
  `hand-browser.spec.ts`; docs `operations.md` ("Hosted demo", the hand test's flow G), `apps/demo/README.md`. No error
  code, SDK reason name, request, retry or SDK string changed; `packages/web` untouched.
- How each sentence was made true (traced 2026-11-23 on `next` @ 0c47747b):
  - The vault's NEAR refusals (4100 with `data.reason`) all come before its approval window (the SDK's
    `user-messages.ts` D871 note): "nothing was signed".
  - The relay's answers (`apps/api/src/near/relay.ts` `handleNearRelay`, `handleNearActivate`): every refusal before
    `relayThrough` is certainly not sent (policy, signature, the sender's floor and copy mark, the minute and day
    windows, the budget, the chain reads, the nonce and height checks). The relay key object (`relayer-key.ts`
    `relayNearTimed`, `sendWithRetry`) marks its own before-broadcast refusals `notSent`, but sends the same codes
    (`relayer_busy`, `relayer_unavailable`, `near_unavailable`) after a broadcast too, and `relayAnswerBody` doesn't pass
    `notSent` to the page. So, as the SDK's `NEAR_RELAY_REASONS` does: a code that may follow a send says to check
    before trying again (here: "Check the guestbook list for your message before you try again"); a new approval
    would sign a new request, which could write the message twice. "Nothing was sent" only where the API can't have
    sent anything. `contract_rejected` keeps "Nothing was stored.": the guestbook write is one `add_message` call, and
    a call that fails changes nothing.
  - A bare `api_unavailable` (no status, no reason) in the write is the SDK's own fetch failing or timing out
    (`packages/web/src/client/near.ts` `post`): for the relay the request may have reached Journear, so it says to
    check first too (before, the page's generic "Could not reach Journear's service. Check your connection and try
    again.").
  - "Sign a transaction" sends with the page's own NEAR reads (`near.ts` `sendTx`): after the approval only the send
    can fail, so the result no longer says "not signed" (it was signed). Since PR 111's review the send follows the
    API's broadcast rule (`apps/api/src/near/rpc.ts`, D435): it moves to `rpcFallback` only when an endpoint gave no
    JSON-RPC answer, with the same signed bytes, and an answer is final. `near_send_failed` ("signed, didn’t go
    through") only for an outcome whose status is `Failure`, or an invalid transaction from the first endpoint asked,
    before any failover; every other case is the new page code `near_send_unconfirmed` ("signed, not confirmed",
    check first): TIMEOUT_ERROR, any error after a failover (the first endpoint may have forwarded the bytes, and the
    fallback answers InvalidNonce because they landed), no endpoint answering, an outcome without a status. Before,
    any error body was "didn’t go through … your message wasn’t stored", which a failover could make false and lead to
    a second write.
  - NEAR's own refusals of the relay's transaction (`near_rejected`: an invalid transaction, never included, the API's
    NOT_EXECUTED; `delegate_rejected`: the delegate failed in the sender's receipt) never ran the guestbook call, so
    they say the message wasn't stored, as the SDK does. (Corrected after PR 111's review: the first version said they
    "come without `notSent`", which confuses broadcast with execution: `notSent` says nothing was broadcast.)
  - `delegate_nonce_used` (the API's, and the vault's `near_delegate_nonce_used`) is refused before anything is sent
    or signed: another request already used this one's number. It may have been this message (another tab, a
    reload), so the sentence still says to check.
