## The sign-in window's Remove and Cancel are findable (branch `feat/remove-findable`), 2026-11-23

From `next` @ 0c47747b; not merged, not deployed.

### D887. A banner's Remove or Cancel is a small outlined button on its own line, after "Don't recognise it?"
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23**: the button and its question (hand test of flow E:
  "I was testing around 6 in Step 2 but didn't notice the 'Remove'. where was it?"; to the proposal "a small button,
  plus 'Didn't add it?' in front of it": "yes let's do it"), then the question's words, after PR 108's review ('Change
  to "Don't recognise it?"'); the labels, the accessible names, the outline, the same treatment for the other two
  banners and the matching sentences decided while building, **to confirm** · Amends D875 (item 2's line, item 5's
  Home sentences) and D881 (item 9's advice after a removal that can't be checked), with a row of "Superseded or
  amended" · Built: display only, no vault, API, issuer or contract change and nothing new in the vault's notices:
  `packages/web/src/auth/email-page.ts` (`BANNER_ACTION_TEXT`, `showBanners`' `actionLine`, `showChangeResult`'s
  advice), `packages/web/src/auth/css/sign-in.css` (`p.banner-action`, `div.older-links`),
  `packages/web/src/auth/home-sign-ins.ts` (`SIGN_IN_TEXT`, `pointerText`); tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/email-follow.test.ts` ("D887", and the D875 and D881 blocks), `home-sign-ins.test.ts`,
  `apps/e2e/tests/fixtures.ts` (`seenText`, `actionUnderSentence`), `home-sign-ins.spec.ts`, `linking.spec.ts`,
  `google-cancel.spec.ts`, `hand-browser.spec.ts` (case A now goes on to the email's next sign-in); docs
  `architecture.md`, `operations.md` (hand-test flows A, D, E and F), `integration.md`, `apps/e2e/README.md`.
- Context: D875's older line ended its sentence with **Remove** drawn as a link (`button.link`: the link colour,
  underlined, no box), as D259's banners end theirs with **Remove** and **Cancel this link**. Looking for it on
  purpose, the Tech Lead didn't see it.
- Decision:
  1. **The older line**: the sentence as before ("An email address also opens this wallet, since {date}." / "A Google
     account …"), alone in its paragraph. Under it, on its own line: "Don’t recognise it?" and the design system's
     small outlined button **Remove it** (`jp-btn jp-btn-secondary jp-btn-sm`: 32 px high with a mouse, 44 px on a
     touch screen from the tokens). With two older lines each sentence has its own pair under it (8 px between a
     sentence and its pair, 16 px between lines). The muted note and **Done** follow as before; Done stays the one
     primary button (large, filled, last). The line has no box, colour, icon or amber.
  2. **The question** (the Tech Lead's choice after review): "Don’t recognise it?" rather than "Didn’t add it?",
     because it is true in every case the window can't tell apart: the person added the sign-in, it was added
     automatically (a Google account with the wallet's own address, D119, which the notice doesn't mark), or someone
     else added it. "Didn’t add it?" was untrue for the automatic link (the email's next sign-in read "A sign-in method
     was added: Google on {date}. Didn’t add it?" after the person had just signed in with Google), where Passport
     Home already asked "Don’t recognise this Google account?". British "recognise", as everywhere in the product.
  3. **The names** (WCAG 2.5.3, after review): a button's accessible name starts with its visible words, then what it
     changes, in a visually hidden span inside the button (`.sr-only`, given its own rule in `sign-in.css`):
     **Remove it** is "Remove it (the email address)" / "Remove it (the Google account)"; **Cancel this link** is
     "Cancel this link for the email address" / "… for the Google account"; the just-added **Remove** is "Remove the
     email address from this wallet" (the confirmation's own question, D881). So a voice user's "Click Remove it"
     matches, and a screen reader's list of buttons tells two lines apart. Each button is also described by its
     sentence (`aria-describedby`). No `aria-label`. Each hidden part starts with a space and a word or a bracket:
     Chromium puts a space before an absolutely positioned child's text, so a colon came out "Remove it : the …".
  4. **The outline** (after review): the system's secondary button draws its border in `--jp-border-strong`, 1.83:1
     against the window in light and 1.65:1 in dark, under the 3:1 a control's edge usually needs; being seen as a
     button is the point here. These buttons only (not the system's secondary button) take `--jp-fg-faint`, the
     system's stronger control border (what an input and a secondary button show on hover): 3.01:1 in light, 3.99:1
     in dark against the window.
  5. **The other two banners, the same way** (decided while building): the first-7-days banner ("A sign-in method was
     added: {email | Google} on {date}.") and the waiting banner ("An email will be able to open this wallet from
     {date}." / "A Google account will …") keep their sentence, box and icon; the action moves to its own line under
     the sentence, inside the box: "Don’t recognise it?" and **Remove it**, and "Don’t recognise it?" and **Cancel
     this link**. Why: the same link-in-a-sentence, so the same reason to miss it; one pattern for the three; Passport
     Home asks the same question before telling people to press these buttons.
  6. **A way to sign in this sign-in just added** (`fresh`: the "You can now sign in with … too" screen, and a waiting
     link `linkAccount` or "Link and continue" just made): the small button alone on its own line, no question (the
     person just did it): **Remove** (without the question in front, "it" would point nowhere) or **Cancel this
     link**.
  7. **Unchanged**: Remove still opens D881's confirmation first ("Remove the … from this wallet?", **Remove it** /
     **Go back**), so a mis-press costs nothing; Cancel still doesn't ask (D881). What Done writes and when a line
     counts as seen are D875's (only Done). The button ids (`banner-unlink-{i}`, `banner-cancel-{i}`, `banner-done`).
  8. **The words that point to them match**, and Passport Home marks a button's name with quotation marks, as it does
     elsewhere ("choose “Share my name”", "under “Ways to sign in”"):
     - "Don’t recognise it? Sign in to this app the way you signed in here, and choose “Remove it”. If you’re not
       sure, remove it." (was "Didn’t add it? … choose Remove. …"; "If you’re not sure" kept: still the natural next
       step for someone unsure whether they recognise it);
     - the automatic Google link: "Don’t recognise this Google account? Sign in to this app the way you signed in
       here, and choose “Remove it”." (D865's softer words; no push to remove);
     - "Don’t recognise it? Sign in to this app the way you signed in here, and choose “Cancel this link”. If you’re
       not sure, cancel it.";
     - "Once you press “Done” in the sign-in window, that browser stops offering to remove it. Not offered? Try
       signing in in a private window.";
     - the waiting email's own row "Didn’t set this up? Sign in to this app with this email and choose “Cancel this
       link”. …" and an added sign-in's own row "… choose “Remove this email” when asked. …": only the quotation marks;
     - the result after a removal that can't be checked: "Sign in to {app} again. If the {kind} still opens this
       wallet, you’ll see it there with a button to remove it." (was "with Remove").
     A unit test ties Home's sentences to the window's labels and question word for word.
  9. **Left as they are** (a different question, not the banners'): the notice mail's "Not you?" (to the email's
     holder: did you link it); the waiting email's own screen (D864) "Didn’t do this? Cancel the link." and Home's
     "Didn’t set this up?" for the same row (about starting the link, asked of the email that waits); the member's
     own screen (D865) "If you don’t recognise it, …" / "If you didn’t set this up, …"; the removal's result "Didn’t
     add it yourself? Someone else may have used this wallet while it was added." (D881: about the risk after
     removing). The mail's "shows the new sign-in with a button to remove it" and the older line's note already match.
- Why: findable, not louder. An outline gives it the shape people scan for when they look for a button; the question
  says who it's for and points at it. Small and neutral keeps Done the obvious next step and keeps the line from
  reading as a warning (D875's reason for a quiet line: most people did add the sign-in, and a loud line at every
  sign-in trains them to press Done unread).
- Trade-off: a button catches the eye more than a link and adds a line per action (two older lines: about 90 px more;
  the 480 × 640 sign-in window still shows Done without scrolling). The question leans a little toward removing;
  the confirmation step is the guard.
- Rejected: a box, colour, icon or amber around the older line (louder; a warning look for what most people did
  themselves, against D875); Remove in red (danger only behind a confirmation, `ui.ts` `BTN`); a full-size button
  (competes with Done); keeping the link and only adding the question (the link inside text was what got missed);
  "… Remove" after the question (reads as a list; "Remove it" answers it); a name that is only "Remove it" (two
  lines' buttons can't be told apart out of context); an `aria-label` that doesn't start with the visible words
  (a voice user's "Remove it" wouldn't match); "Didn’t add it?" (untrue for an automatic link; replaced by the
  Tech Lead); an "automatic" flag in the notice so the window could ask differently (not display-only: a new notice
  field, which an older window refuses during a deploy, D875 (e)); restyling the system's secondary button for
  every page.
- Address impact: none (display only; no path, key or derivation input changes).
- To confirm: (1) the words **Remove it**, **Cancel this link**, and **Remove** alone on a sign-in just added; (2)
  the names "Remove it (the email address)", "Remove it (the Google account)", "Cancel this link for the email
  address", "Cancel this link for the Google account", "Remove the email address from this wallet"; (3) the same
  treatment, the question included, on the first-7-days and waiting banners; (4) Home's quotation marks around
  button names, and "If you’re not sure, remove it." / "… cancel it." kept after "Don’t recognise it?"; (5) the
  stronger outline (`--jp-fg-faint`) on these buttons only; whether every secondary button should get a 3:1 edge is a
  design-system question for later; (6) the small size (32 px with a mouse, 44 px on touch) and its 12 px label
  (13 px on touch).

## Gas sponsorship restarts by itself after a refill (branch `feat/evm-relayer-auto-resume`), 2026-11-23

From `next` @ 0c47747b; not merged, not deployed (gas sponsorship is off everywhere).

### D890. A pause for money ends by itself after a refill, on the relayer's own evidence only (the one exception to "nothing clears a halt by itself")
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the automatic restart **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23**, after hand-testing an
  out-of-money pause ("Why can't we auto resume after refilling? why did we decide we need someone to look at it before
  resuming?"; to the proposal below: "yes I want this"), with three staff-page fixes from the same test (a fresh
  "Check again" on the tile, the out-of-money steps reworded so nobody sends money twice, the tile's words once the
  money is there); the checks beyond the Tech Lead's four, the bounds, the cadence, the second endpoint, the amounts and
  the sentences decided while building, to confirm; three of them **confirmed by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** from their
  description, not hand-tested ("confirm 1 to 8": the daily and 30-minute bounds, the relayer-code check on every run,
  shipping switched off), the split at the end of "To confirm" · Built: `apps/api/src/evm-relayer.ts` (`#autoRestart`,
  `#autoCheck`, `#autoBlocked`, `#resumeVerdict` and `#endHalt` shared with `staffResume`, the money cadence in
  `#schedule`, `staffStatus().autoRestart`, `status().autoRestartedAt`), `evm/sponsor-chain.ts`
  (`sponsorSecondEndpoint`), `evm/sponsor.ts` (the cron raises `evm_relay_auto_resumed`), `evm/sponsor-settle.ts`,
  `evm-relayer-staff.ts`, `migrations/0024_evm_relay_auto_resumed.sql`; `packages/console-core` (`EvmRelayAutoRestartView`,
  the event kind and title); `apps/admin/src/evm-relay.ts` (`moneyExplained`, `autoBlockedWords`, `testEthUp`, the
  states "Paused: needs money" and "Restarting by itself"), `status.ts` (`?fresh=1`, `FRESH_MIN_MS`, `STALE_AFTER_MS`,
  `checkAgain`), `security.ts`, `public/app.js`; `packages/playbooks` (`evm-relay-auto-resumed`, `evm-relay-paused`);
  `apps/e2e` (the admin lane's second endpoint and the scenarios `money-arrives`, `refill`, `out-of-money-again`);
  tests `apps/api/test/evm-relayer.test.ts` ("D890: …"), `evm-mock.ts`, `migration-0003/0006.test.ts`,
  `test-anvil/halts.test.ts` (9d, 9e), `apps/admin/test/evm-relay.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`,
  `test-spa/evm-relay.test.ts`, `apps/e2e/tests/admin-portal.spec.ts`. Current state: `docs/security.md` "The EVM
  relayer object", `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/operations.md` "EVM sponsorship relay", `docs/go-live-after-freeze.md`.
- The Tech Lead's four conditions, as agreed: (1) the only pause reason is out of money; (2) no sign of the key being
  used elsewhere was seen during the pause; (3) the wallet is back above the low-balance mark; (4) a fresh check finds
  nothing else wrong. Every other pause reason keeps waiting for a person, exactly as before.
- **The argument.** A thief draining the wallet must move its money, and an account's money moves only in these ways.
  Auto-restart is only as safe as this list is complete:
  1. *Our own sponsored actions, their bumps and cancels, staff fillers.* Each uses one of the relayer's own slots
     (nonces), is a record with its own receipts, and costs at most its gas at the gas price limit (plus the OP Stack
     L1 data fee and operator fee, which `receiptCostWei` counts); the day's backstop caps them (2 × `dailyBudgetEth`).
  2. *A transaction signed with the key somewhere else.* It uses a slot: the count goes above `nextNonce`
     (`foreign_transactions`), or one of our waiting slots is used (`nonce_consumed_elsewhere` at confirmed depth), or a
     gap, or a leak-type refusal. Each already halts or marks the pause `leakSeen` (D843 re-check M). Two windows the
     halts didn't cover, now closed for the restart: such a transaction mined at one of our slots but not yet at
     confirmed depth (no condition yet: the restart needs every record below the latest count to have its own receipt,
     `unexplained_slot`), and one waiting in the pool at our slot (our rebroadcast is turned away: the restart needs
     every waiting record taken by an endpoint, and in a money pause the record's refusal stays a condition).
  3. *An EIP-7702 authorization signed with the relayer's key and carried by another account's transaction.* It is
     valid only at the relayer's current count and, when applied, raises it by one (EIP-7702): seen as (2). But it
     installs code (`0xef0100` + an address) at the relayer's own address, and from then on anyone can call that
     address and move its money with **no further slot used**: no count would ever show it, and the relayer never read
     its own code (the handlers read the user's account's code, the admin the helper program's). A key leak handled with
     "Set the next slot number" but without replacing the key could leave that in place. So the restart needs no code
     at the relayer's address (on both endpoints), and code found there by the trusted endpoint marks the pause
     `leakSeen` (the leak steps; Resume needs the key confirmed).
  4. *The OP Stack L1 data fee and operator fee* are charged only on the relayer's own transactions: part of (1).
  5. *Anything else:* an account's balance also falls by nothing a user's batch does (its calls may not target the
     relayer, and with no code at the relayer nothing can call into it); money sent to it only raises it. **An L1→L2
     deposit transaction** sent from Sepolia with the same key (`OptimismPortal.depositTransaction`): per the OP Stack
     spec (from the spec, not yet tested; go-live "Checks on Base Sepolia" item 1), for an account with no code its L2
     `from` is the same address (not aliased), its `value` is taken from the relayer's L2 balance, and its L2 count rises
     whether it succeeds or fails (this predates Regolith, which only added `depositNonce` to receipts). It never sits in
     the L2 pool, so `pending` can't show it before it lands; once it lands the count is past `nextNonce`
     (`foreign_transactions`), so it is (2).
- **The exact conditions**, all of them, checked in this order on an alarm run only (`#autoCheck`; never by a
  request): the pause's reason is `relayer_cannot_send` with `insufficient_funds`; not `leakSeen`; fewer than 3
  automatic restarts this UTC day; the pause began 30 minutes or more after the last automatic restart; the settings
  readable and a second endpoint configured; the key loaded and the records' signer; the pause at least 60 s old;
  **the run's own verdict is staffResume's** (`#resumeVerdict`, the same code: no condition, a gap seen once
  included, and complete) on that run, which is the fresh check (it read the counts, the receipts and rebroadcast what
  waits); every record below the run's latest count has its own receipt and every record waiting at head was taken by
  an endpoint (not refused, no price refusal); the run left room for the reads below (≤ 41 of the 50 subrequests); then
  fresh reads of the trusted endpoint: the latest and pending counts not below the run's, not above `nextNonce`, every
  record below them with its own receipt; the balance at least **`lowBalanceEth` plus every waiting record's gas at the
  gas price limit (× 2 on an OP Stack chain)**; no code at the relayer's address; then the **one other endpoint**
  (`sponsorSecondEndpoint`: `rpcFallback`, else `rpc` when the keyed URL is the read one) gives the same latest count,
  a pending count from it to `nextNonce`, a balance at least the same amount, and no code. A failed read waits for the
  next run. Then the halt ends exactly as staffResume ends it (`#endHalt`). staffResume itself is unchanged in every
  state, the key confirmation gate included.
- **"No sign of the key used elsewhere", precisely:** the pause not `leakSeen` (set by any leak-type condition any run
  saw during it, the pause's own reason, a staff Close, Fill or Set the next slot number during it, and now code at the
  relayer's address); no condition on this run (a gap seen once included); the run's and a fresh read's counts
  explained by our own records alone (above); no code at the relayer's address; the other endpoint agreeing.
- **One trusted endpoint, and why a second check for this one decision.** D851 takes every piece of evidence from one
  read endpoint. Until now a person who refilled also looked at the wallet on the explorer before pressing Resume; the
  restart drops the look after the refill (the look before sending money stays the first step). A lying or lagging
  endpoint could under-report the count (hiding a thief's transaction) or show a refill that isn't there. So the
  automatic restart, and only it, also asks the one other configured endpoint (outside `local*` envs always set:
  `rpcFallback` is required there, a different provider) and waits for a person when it disagrees or doesn't answer.
  It can only hold the restart back: it is never evidence for a halt or a mark. A `local*` env without one never
  restarts by itself (`no_second_endpoint`). Cost: 5 calls, only on a run where the balance already covers it.
  Residual risk: both endpoints wrong the same way (both behind the same sequencer feed): a thief's transaction in the
  last moments before the check is unseen, it restarts, and the next runs see the transaction: for 10 minutes after an
  automatic restart the relayer runs every 15 to 60 s, records or not (amended after the review: it used to go hourly
  with nothing waiting), so a leak halt follows within about a minute. What a restart on a leaked key costs: users' actions go through for that time (no user's
  money is at risk: the relayer only pays gas for Executes each user signed), and money left in the wallet can be
  taken, which the thief can do with or without the restart. Each restart is raised as an event.
- **The amount.** The restart needs `lowBalanceEth` plus what is waiting at the gas price limit ("back above the
  low-balance mark", with what is waiting paid for); exactly that much restarts it (tested below, at and above).
  staffResume needs no amount: it passes once the waiting records' copies are taken, which a node checks against each
  one's own gas × max fee; that is why a wallet at about 1.0001 test ETH could be resumed. The tile's old "Send at least
  1.01 test ETH" was `lowBalanceEth` (0.01) + `dailyBudgetEth` (1) of the local stack's settings (`refill`, `explainChain`):
  the minimum of nothing. Now the tile asks for the real minimum of whichever restart applies, less the balance it read,
  rounded up to 0.0001: for a restart by itself `restartWei` (as above); for Resume `resumeWei` (what waits, at its own
  fees) plus one action's worst cost, so the next action doesn't pause it again; with the day's budget as context.
- **Bounds.** At most 3 automatic restarts a UTC day (`EVM_RELAYER_AUTO_RESTARTS_PER_DAY`); a pause that began within
  30 minutes of the last one (`EVM_RELAYER_AUTO_RAN_OUT_AGAIN_MS`: the money ran out fast) waits for a person however long
  it lasts; never in a pause's first 60 s (`EVM_RELAYER_AUTO_MIN_PAUSE_MS`: several runs looked at the chain first).
  Each restart is recorded as a staff action is (who `relayer (automatic)`, when, `resume`, done, a note with what it
  saw: the trusted endpoint's balance, the amount needed, its counts and the block, no code, the other endpoint's counts
  and balance; `auto: true`), so a page read before it acts on nothing (`version_conflict`), and raised by the API's
  15-minute cron as `evm_relay_auto_resumed` (one per restart, the status's `autoRestartedAt`; title "Gas sponsorship:
  restarted by itself after the relayer wallet was refilled", playbook `evm-relay-auto-resumed`; D1 migration 0024
  rebuilds `security_events` to allow it). **D851's review rule holds:** nothing a user sends to the API can halt or
  restart it (send, replays, status and lookup never run it; a refused send stores nothing and sets no alarm; tested).
  A transfer on chain by anyone can meet one condition only, the balance: that is money given to Journear, not a
  request, and every other condition is the relayer's own evidence; at worst someone restarts gas sponsorship by
  funding it, as a staff refill would, within the bounds above.
- **The cadence (D882's open question, answered).** While paused for money: every 15 s for the pause's first 10 minutes,
  then every 60 s, with or without a record waiting (never hourly): a refill is noticed within about a minute (it restarts within 2 minutes, after the review). Cost, with
  D882's measure of about 6 provider calls a run (now 7 with the run's balance read only when everything else allows a
  restart; usually the waiting record's refusal decides first, with no extra read): 5,760 runs a day before, about 1,480
  now (40 in the first 10 minutes, then 1,440), so about 35,000 calls a day become about 10,000. Other pauses keep their
  D882 cadence (unchanged here).
- **The staff page.** (a) **Check again** on the Gas sponsorship tile: `GET /api/status?fresh=1` (staff only, as the
  page): it skips the page's 30 s cache and reads every part again (about 20 outbound calls, two of them on the relayer's
  network: its balance and the helper program's code, the latter cached 10 minutes in the API), at most once per 10 s
  per isolate (`FRESH_MIN_MS`; sooner, the last read answers and the page says when the next fresh one can be taken).
  The tile says when its reading is older than 15 s: "This reading is from 25 s ago. Money sent since then shows after
  Check again." (b), (c) the words (staff side, D853 and D879): before the money arrives, **Paused: needs money**:
  "The relayer wallet is out of money, so gas sponsorship is paused for everyone. It restarts by itself once the wallet
  has enough." Steps: the safety check (unchanged: "Open the relayer wallet on Basescan (its address is below). If money
  went out in transfers nobody at Journear made, stop: tell an engineer now and don’t send money."); "Send at least
  {amount} to the relayer wallet ({0x12ab…cd34}; its whole address is below) from {faucet}. That is the least it needs
  to restart by itself. A day of gas sponsorship can use up to {budget}."; "It restarts by itself within 2 minutes
  of the money arriving. You don’t need to press Resume."; "Send it once. The balance on this page can be up to 30 s
  old: press Check again to see the new amount before you send more." The money there: **Restarting by itself** (amber):
  "The relayer wallet has money again ({balance}). Gas sponsorship restarts by itself within 2 minutes." Steps:
  "Nothing to do: don’t send more money, and you don’t need to press Resume."; "If it still says this after 2 minutes,
  press Check again. If it is still paused then, press Resume on the Gas sponsorship page." When it can't restart by
  itself (**Paused: needs a person**): "… It can’t restart by itself this time: {why}." with Resume's amount and "Then
  press Resume on the Gas sponsorship page.", or with the money there "The relayer wallet has money again ({balance}),
  but gas sponsorship can’t restart by itself: {why}." with "Don’t send more money.", the wallet check, "Then press
  Resume …"; {why}: "it has already restarted by itself 3 times today (UTC), the most it may", "it ran out of money
  again within 30 minutes of restarting by itself, so a person should look first", "this environment has no second
  network server to check the wallet with", "the relayer’s key isn’t loaded". The two servers disagreeing: "…, but gas
  sponsorship hasn’t restarted by itself: the two network servers it checks with don’t agree about the wallet." with
  the wallet check and Resume. Restarted: **Working**, the line "Last restart: Restarted by itself after a refill, 4 s
  ago (1 of 3 today)"; the staff log row "The relayer itself · Restarted by itself after a refill". A line "Restarts by
  itself: Yes, once the wallet has {amount} · 0 of 3 automatic restarts used today" (or "No: {why}") during a pause for
  money. No second "running low" issue beside a pause for money (it asked for money twice, in two amounts). The Resume
  tool says "You don’t need Resume for this pause: it restarts by itself within 2 minutes of the money arriving.
  Resume still works if you want it to restart now." A leak sign keeps the leak steps, never a refill.
- **Also found, fixed after the review:** at send, when a batch was refused for a relayer-side reason
  (`insufficient_funds` among them), its cancel was signed and stored but not broadcast until the next run (`code ??=
  this.#afterBroadcast(…)` in `#sendLocked` skipped the broadcast because `code` was already set). Now it is broadcast
  at once, as D851 item 2 says, and its own refusal counts only when the batch's didn't.
- **Amended after its security review (2026-11-23; the coordinator's call with the reviewer's recommendation, to
  confirm by the Tech Lead; the review found the restart stricter than staff Resume, and "no halt and no resume by a
  user's request", the bounds, the atomicity and the migration sound).** Safe to merge; NOT to be switched on before
  the checks on Base Sepolia (go-live) are recorded. Changes:
  1. *A common race read as a disagreement.* Our own waiting transaction often lands between the trusted endpoint's read
     and the other's (Base: 2 s blocks). A difference in the latest count made only of slots our own records hold
     (each waiting or with its own receipt) is now `counts_moving`: no restart that run, no alarm. Every check records
     how many runs in a row found the same blocker (`streak`); a disagreement is logged as an error, and named to staff,
     only from the second run.
  2. *Code at the relayer's address checked everywhere* (decided): one `eth_getCode` on the trusted endpoint per run, at
     the first send's nonce read (code there: nothing stored or sent) and in staffAdoptNonce (refused, never a re-baseline
     over code); code is a leak-type halt (`relayer_has_code`, console-core `isLeakHalt`), or marks a pause `leakSeen`.
     This closes the channel the counts can't see: a delegation planted before the relayer's first send (when it reads
     the pending count once) or before a staffAdoptNonce re-baseline. A code read that fails makes the run incomplete
     (no halt; staffResume and the restart wait). Staff words: "A program has been attached to the relayer wallet. Only
     someone with the relayer’s key can do that, and it lets them move the wallet’s money at any time." with the leak
     steps. Its event is the halt's (`evm_relay_stuck`, with the reason); the paused playbook names it among the leak
     signs. Cost: one more provider call a run.
  3. *Another condition seen during a pause for money* (a wrong key loaded then restored, a slot stuck past its time
     limit, another refusal code, a gap seen twice) now marks the pause `otherSeen` (the first such reason): the
     restart then waits for a person (`other_seen`), whatever clears later.
  4. *The second endpoint must be another provider:* outside `local*` envs a configured URL of the read endpoint's
     provider is skipped (the Worker compares the hosts' last two labels, `sponsorProviderOf`, stricter than the
     manifest's registrable domain; the manifest also checks `rpcFallback` against `rpc`, not against the keyed secret);
     none left: `no_second_endpoint`, said to staff.
  5. *Staff see every persistent blocker:* "Restarting by itself" only while the relayer's own latest check waits for the
     money or names a blocker seen once; a blocker seen on two runs in a row is named ("it can’t reach its second network
     server to check the wallet", "the network’s main server isn’t taking its waiting transaction", "it can’t read the
     wallet from the network right now", "it has too much to check on each run right now", "it can’t finish checking the
     network", "the network shows a transaction it can’t match to its own yet", "its own check of the network still finds
     a problem", "the two network servers it checks with don’t agree about the wallet"), with the wallet check and
     Resume. The money counts as arrived by this page's balance read or the relayer's own.
  6. *Watched after a restart:* for 10 minutes after an automatic restart the alarm runs every 15–60 s, records or not.
  7. *The trusted pool itself:* `accepted` is sticky and any endpoint's, so the restart now needs the TRUSTED endpoint
     to have taken (or already hold) each waiting record on that very run (the broadcast's answer says which endpoint
     took it: `byRead`); a thief's transaction holding our slot in that pool while the fallback takes ours blocks it
     (`waiting_not_taken`). "Every used slot has its own receipt" means one was seen at some point (`seen`), not re-read
     on that run (a reorg un-sees it on a later run).
  8. *The at-send cancel* is broadcast at once (above).
  9. *Words true in every state:* "within 2 minutes" (the 60 s cadence, one more run, the 60 s minimum age) everywhere;
     the Resume tool says "The wallet already has enough for Resume, if you want it to restart now." only when the
     balance covers what Resume needs, else "Resume needs at least {X} in the wallet first: before that it says no.";
     the restart's amount now also includes **one more action's worst cost** (`maxGasPerTx` at the gas price limit, ×2
     on OP Stack), so it doesn't restart into an immediate second pause that then needs a person (chosen over a manifest
     rule `lowBalanceEth` ≥ that cost: no schema rule, and the tile's X is exactly the code's threshold); the step reads
     "That is the least it needs to restart by itself, with room for the next action."
  10. *A switch, default off:* the chain's `autoRestart` (manifest `evm.sponsor.chains.<id>.autoRestart`, optional
      boolean, default false; `switched_off` otherwise): the restart stays off in every deployed env until the six
      checks on Base Sepolia (go-live) are recorded; staff Resume always works. On in the local stack's admin lane and the
      tests that need it.
  Tests: each condition alone (code at first send, while working, while paused, at staffAdoptNonce, at staff Resume,
  planted then cleared; another condition then cleared; the second endpoint a block ahead; the trusted pool refusing
  while the fallback takes; a fresh balance read failing; settings unreadable and switched off; eviction between checks;
  a foreign transaction at the next slot after the refill; the streak; the watch after a restart; the at-send cancel);
  the anvil lane's 9f (the relayer key's EIP-7702 authorization carried by another account: count +1, code, a leak,
  never a restart, cleared to the zero address). Not tested alone: `busy` (it needs a run of over 41 fetches, which the
  fake chain can't stage without many dozens of records) and an eviction in the middle of a check (the check writes
  nothing before its one final write, so an eviction then leaves the pause exactly as it was; tested between checks).
- Rejected: restarting by itself for any other reason (each needs a person's judgement, D851); the balance alone (the
  thief case: money there says nothing about who moved it); the second endpoint for staff Resume too (the Tech Lead kept
  Resume as it is; a person can look at the explorer); backing off to 5 minutes while paused for money (a refill noticed
  up to 5 minutes late); the event raised by the relayer object itself (D1 writes inside the relayer's queue; the cron
  already reads its status every 15 minutes); a minimum of `lowBalanceEth` + `dailyBudgetEth` (the old "1.01": not a
  minimum).
- Address impact: none (no path, key or derivation input changes).
- To confirm: (1) the checks beyond the Tech Lead's four (the counts explained by our own records, no code at the
  relayer's address, the second endpoint); (2) the bounds: 3 a UTC day, 30 minutes since the last restart, 60 s into a
  pause; (3) the cadence (15 s for 10 minutes, then 60 s); (4) the amounts (restart: the low-balance mark plus what waits
  at the gas price limit; Resume: what waits at its own fees plus one action's worst cost) and rounding up; (5) the
  sentences above, the labels "Paused: needs money" and "Restarting by itself", "network server(s)"; (6) Check again's
  10 s floor and the 15 s "old reading" note; (7) the event's title and its "info" playbook; (8) **for the Tech Lead**:
  should staff Resume and every run also check the relayer's own code (today only the automatic restart does: code at
  its address is a leaked key whatever the pause), and should the at-send cancel be broadcast at once (above); (9) on
  Base Sepolia before enabling: that a deposit transaction from L1 raises the relayer's L2 count (above), and the second
  provider's `pending` count behaviour (D851 item 18's checks, now for `rpcFallback` too).
  **2026-11-23** ("confirm 1 to 8", from the description, not hand-tested; quoted in "Confirmed in one batch,
  2026-11-23" at the end of this file): **confirmed by the Tech Lead**: of (2), at most 3 automatic restarts a UTC day
  and a person needed when it runs out again within 30 minutes ("At most 3 automatic restarts a day. If it runs out
  again within 30 minutes, a person is needed."); of (8), the relayer-code check on every run, amendment 2 ("The
  planted-code check runs on every check, not only at restart."); amendment 10, shipping switched off behind
  `autoRestart` ("It ships switched off until the six real-network checks are done."). Still open: of (2), never in a
  pause's first 60 s; (1), the second endpoint's exact rule included (amendment 4); (3); (4), with amendment 9's extra
  action's cost in the amount; (5); (6) Check again's timings; (7); of (8), the at-send cancel broadcast at once; (9)
  (checks on Base Sepolia before it is switched on).

## Passport Home's structure (option A), and step 1: the shell (branch `feat/home-shell-step1`), 2026-11-23

### D888. Passport Home takes structure A; step 1 is its shell: a top bar that holds who is signed in, Sign out and the sign-in's notice and covers nothing, the guard started over by any change of layout, one section pattern, one 1040 px width
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the structure, "wallet" as the main noun and Back inside Home **decided by the Tech Lead
  2026-11-23**; step 1's details decided while building, to confirm; two of them **confirmed by the Tech Lead
  2026-11-23** from their description, not hand-tested ("confirm 1 to 8": the desktop shift when the notice appears,
  the guard starting over), the split at the end of "To confirm (the Tech Lead)" · From the Passport Home design review of
  2026-11-19 (three structures A, B, C; its "Step 1: the shell, no wording change" and its quick wins) · Built on
  `feat/home-shell-step1`: `packages/web/src/auth/home-page.ts` (`topBar`, `HOME_SKIP_TEXT`, `renderAccount`,
  `replaceWho`, `renderShell`, `COPY_FAILED`, `appPage`, `frontPage`), `auth/css/home.css` (the shell, the section
  pattern, the app page, `.home-who-lines-N`), `auth/home-email.ts` (`titleTag`); tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/home-page.test.ts` ("the shell (D888)"), `home-export.test.ts` ("D888: a change of layout
  around the move flow starts the guard over"; a selector), `apps/e2e/tests/home-shell.spec.ts` (new, three browsers).
  Notes on D553 and D878.
- **The Tech Lead's decisions** (2026-11-23):
  1. **Structure A** ("for the home structure I like option C but let's go with A, as you said C could be added
     later"): the user's wallets as a list, then one wallet's page with tabs Addresses / Security / Move wallet; "Your
     account" for what covers every wallet (Devices, Your name); "Other apps" last. Built in the review's five steps.
     Option C's task-led front page may be added later as a front door. Option B is rejected: the page would stay long,
     and the move-wallet flow would stay at its bottom.
  2. **"Wallet" is the main noun** in Passport Home in place of "app" ("Your wallets", "Wallet details"): what people own
     is a wallet, and several apps can share one. Applied from step 2 onward, with a plain-wording review of each
     renamed string. **Built in step 2, D893** (its old → new table).
  3. **The browser's Back button works inside Home**: it returns to the wallet list instead of leaving Home and losing
     the 15-minute in-memory sign-in. To be built in step 2 or 3 with same-URL history entries that carry no data. This
     amends the spirit of D555 ("the page never changes its own URL": the URL still never changes) and keeps D553
     (nothing stored: no state in the history entry, no storage). **Built in step 2, D893** (each entry holds one
     opaque marker, `home:{random tag}:{step}`, nothing of the person, a wallet or an app).
- **Step 1, built here**: the shell only. No wording changes (one new string, the skip link's, below), nothing moves
  between pages, no button does anything new, no API, vault, issuer or contract change; Home still keeps nothing and
  takes no owner proof (D553, D619); the page never changes its URL (D555); no inline style attribute or handler (the
  bar's height reaches CSS through the CSSOM, which the CSP allows). Where a shell choice was neutral between the
  structures, the variant that suits A was taken: A's top bar, A's 1040 px frame and one width for the wallet page, A's
  spacing and section cards (`options/a` and `options/shared/proto.css` of the review).
  1. **A top bar that covers nothing** (as amended after PR 109's review, below). The static lockup header
     (`HOME_HEADER`, unchanged) is now the page's one `header`. While signed in, the page puts in it "Signed in with
     Google" / "Signed in as {address}" and Sign out (moved out of the page's heading row; the same ids, words and
     behaviour), in a plain part of the header (no `nav`: it holds no navigation; step 2 adds a labelled one when there
     is some). The sign-in's notice (`#home-banner`: "ends in about N minutes", the end, and signing in again: "Finish
     signing in with Google in the other window." with Cancel, or the email code screens) is the bar's last row: the bar
     grows when it shows and **nothing is ever drawn over the page**. Its words, timing, buttons and live region are as
     before (D553); the live region is one element kept for the page's life. A sign-in again that fails (the browser
     blocked its window, Google's cancel, a check that failed) is said there too, under the notice, with Dismiss, no
     longer at the top of the page's content. The email code screens' titles there are no headings (a paragraph in
     the heading's place, `homeEmailStep` `titleTag`), so no heading comes before the page's `h1`.
     - **On a desktop** (a mouse, a window at least 641 × 600 px) the bar stays at the window's top (sticky); focus that
       scrolls the page stops below the bar as it is at that moment, the notice included (`scroll-padding-top` from
       `--home-bar-h`, which a ResizeObserver keeps on the root); an email code screen in the stuck bar is never taller
       than the window (`100dvh`) and scrolls inside itself. Scroll anchoring is off there (`overflow-anchor: none` on
       the root and the body): when the bar grows, what is in view moves down by as much in all three browsers, out
       from under the bar, instead of being kept in place under it.
     - **On a phone or a tablet** (any other window) the bar scrolls with the page, in option A's phone layout: the
       lockup and Sign out on the first row, who is signed in on its own line under them (an email address wrapping at
       its own break points), then the notice. The code screens are in the page's flow, so the page scrolls to every
       control however short the window (checked at 390 × 844, 320 × 568, 640 × 360 and 320 × 300).
     - **When the notice comes, changes or goes**: on a desktop what is in view moves by the bar's change (above). On a
       phone, scrolled past the bar, what is in view stays put: Chromium and Firefox anchor scrolling, and where the
       browser didn't (WebKit, every iPhone: it reports `overflow-anchor` but doesn't anchor here) the page scrolls by
       what is missing, in the bar's ResizeObserver callback, before the paint (not when the bar's width changed too, a
       window resized). At the page's top the page moves by the bar's change. The warning and the end keep one height
       (the longest of their sentences, ui.ts `reservedLine`), so the one becoming the other moves nothing. Item 5 makes
       any remaining move harmless for the guarded buttons.
     - **The who line keeps its height** when the sign-in ends and the address is masked (D689): the page measures the
       line's box against its line height and keeps that many lines (a class on the bar's account part, at most 4) for
       the rest of that sign-in, so the bar's height doesn't change then.
  2. **The copy line keeps its space.** "This browser can't copy for you. …" / "This browser didn't allow the copy. …"
     keeps the space of the longest sentence it may say on that page (ui.ts `reservedLine`, as D878's line), at the foot
     of the addresses' card (of the Support ID's box when there are no addresses), so nothing anywhere moves when it
     appears or goes; its words and 4 seconds are unchanged. (A reserved line also loses the page's 8 px paragraph
     margin on Home: D878's own line under the move flow's buttons grew by 8 px when its words appeared.)
  3. **One section pattern**, on the front page and an app's page: sections 40 px apart with no dividers (A's rhythm;
     the dividers were on some sections only), each section's parts 12 px apart and a sub-heading 24 px below what is
     above it (this closes the extra gap under "Your name"'s heading). The tools (Devices and auto-approve, Ways to sign
     in, Your name, Move this wallet) sit in a card each (A's section cards, without A's icons or header rows). "Your
     apps" and an app's details are wrapped in `section` elements (layout only).
  4. **One width**: the bar and the page share one column of at most 1040 px (was 760 px), and everything on a page
     uses it: the app lists (three cards a row on a desktop), the app's box (its apps side by side), the tool cards, and
     on an app's page the addresses (one card, a row per chain, as A) beside the Support ID (a quiet box) from 900 px,
     one above the other below that. Reading text (sentences, alerts, the move flow's steps) stops at 720 px. The lockup
     is 148 px (128 px on a phone; was 168 px).
  5. **A guarded button that moved starts the move flow's guard over.** The page calls the guard's `rendered()`
     (Continue, Show key and Copy key off again until a fresh 1 s wait and a new arming gesture) whenever the bar's
     height changes, the notice is redrawn, the refusal at the top of the page changes, or anything above the move flow
     on an app's page changes height (its details, devices, ways to sign in, the name: ResizeObservers). And a
     catch-all, whatever moved a button (an element nobody watches, a scrollbar, WebKit's page move, the key's box
     growing when the key is shown): in capture-phase `pointermove`, `pointerdown` and `keydown` listeners, registered
     before the guard's own, the page compares each guarded button's place in the page (its top and left plus the
     scroll, so scrolling alone changes nothing) with its place when the guard last started over or saw an input; if
     it differs, the guard starts over before the input reaches it. So a press aimed at what was under the pointer
     can't land on a guarded button as an action (the first review's scenario: an email user, the box ticked and the
     guard armed, finishes "Sign in again" in the notice; the notice goes; a second tap would have landed on Show key).
     `approve-guard.ts`, `key-reveal.ts` and `home-export.ts` are untouched (D878: the guard byte for byte, its hash
     test unchanged); the page wraps the guard it hands the move flow. Without ResizeObserver, the page's own triggers
     and the catch-all still do it.
  6. **Toasts on a phone** start below what is left of the bar in the window (`--home-bar-bottom`, kept by the page on
     scroll and on the bar's resize; 16 px from the top once the bar has scrolled away), and never lower than 40 % of
     the window (`40dvh`), whatever the bar holds: a toast never sits on Sign out or the notice's buttons, and never
     lands below the window.
  7. **Accessibility and targets**: a skip link before the bar ("Skip to content", shown when it has focus; it moves
     focus to `main#app` and never follows its `#app`, so the address doesn't change); one `header`, one `main`, no
     `nav`; explorer links at least the controls' height (32 px, 44 px on a touch screen, `--jp-control-sm`); the
     address labels in sentence case as written ("Ethereum-style (Ethereum and similar networks)") instead of 11 px
     capitals (a CSS `text-transform` only: the strings were already in sentence case).
- **Amended after PR 109's review (2026-11-23).** The first build hung the notice under the bar, over the page, and

## "Passport" alone is not an app name (branch `fix/app-name-passport`), 2026-11-23

From `next` @ e20a1c00; not merged, not deployed.

### D891. An app may not be named "Passport", or read as the wallet or as Journear vouching for it
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the "Passport" rule **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** ("4 yes" to "Refuse "Passport"
  alone as an app name. With "Sponsored by {App}", an app named "Passport" would read as the wallet itself
  sponsoring."); refusing an edition word beside it ("Passport Plus", "Passport Pro", "Passport One") **decided by
  the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** ("Refuse", then "narrow it", note below), its positions to confirm; which other forms count
  as the wallet, the punctuation rule, the imitation-letter rule and the vouching rule
  decided while building and after PR 112's review, **to confirm** (list at the end) · Amends D686 as extended by D765
  ("Passport" on its own stayed allowed), with a row of "Superseded or amended"; answers D884's follow-up for the
  app-name rules · Built: `packages/console-core/src/names.ts` (`passportProblemIn`, `passportNameIn`, `APP_NAME_PASSPORT_TIER_WORDS`,
  `lookalikeLettersIn`, `APP_NAME_BADGES`, `sentenceClaimIn`, `vouchingWordIn`, `APP_NAME_CLAIM_STEMS`,
  `APP_NAME_CLAIM_WORDS`, the merged `LOOKALIKE` table, `appNameProblem`); tests
  `packages/console-core/test/names.test.ts` (refused and allowed tables, the awkward real names, a property test, a
  timing test), `apps/api/test/rpc-changes.test.ts` (settings refuse them), `scripts/test/sql.test.ts` (the CLI),
  `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts` (mails don't show them).
- Why: partner-chosen app names sit inside Journear's own sentences in the approval window ("From {App}", "{App} wants
  to…", and in the details "Network fee: Free. Sponsored by {App}.", D884). Users know Journear Passport as
  "Passport" (the badge "Secured by Journear Passport", Passport Home), so "Sponsored by Passport." reads as the wallet
  paying, "From Passport Support" as the wallet's staff, and "Sponsored by Acme Verified." as Journear vouching.
- How names are compared: `nameSkeleton` (NFKC, so full-width and styled letters fold; accents dropped; Cyrillic,
  Greek, Armenian and other look-alikes; digits and symbols for letters: 0 3 4 5 7 $ @ ₱; i, l, 1, | and ! all read as
  l; core's partner-name confusables merged in, D44), then "rn" read as "m" and "vv" as "w" ("Joumear", "VVallet").
  The rules below that count words split the name into words first (runs of letters and digits; a run of one-letter
  words is one word, "P a s s p o r t"; two words that join into "passport" count too, "Pass Port"), so each message
  can name the word as the partner wrote it.
- **Refused, in this order** (the first rule broken gives the message):
  1. A web-address shape (D686).
  2. "Hana", "Journear" or "Passport Home" (D686, D765).
  3. **Letters that only imitate others**: any letter from Lisu, Cherokee or Coptic, the IPA, phonetic and
     small-capital blocks, spacing modifier letters, or Latin Extended-D and -E ("ꓑassport", "Ꮲassport", "ᴘassport",
     "ⲣassport", "Passpoɾt", "ᴊᴏᴜʀɴᴇᴀʀ", "Acme. ꜰʀᴇᴇ"); and a word that mixes two of Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Armenian and
     Georgian ("Pаssport", "Passport Іd", "Passport ΙD", "Acme. Verіfied", "ϷΑЅЅРОRТ"). Akan and Ewe's ɛ and ɔ stay. A
     word wholly in one other alphabet ("Москва Shop") or in a script with no Latin look-alikes ("東京 Market",
     "LINE株式会社") stays allowed. Why structural and not a bigger table: the table can never list every look-alike;
     these blocks exist in a name here only to imitate Latin, and mixing alphabets inside one word is the imitation.
  4. **A check mark, shield, lock or medal** (☑ ✅ ✓ ✔ √ 🗸 🗹 🛡 🔏–🔓 🎖 🏅 🥇 💯 👍 …; a superset of core's
     `CHECK_MARKS`, a test keeps it so): only Journear's own badge carries a check mark (D44).
  5. **"Passport" as the wallet** (`passportProblemIn`):
     - *alone*: the whole name is "Passport" with at most two of the, a, an, my, your, our, near, wallet, official
       before it and at most TM, SM, an s (plural or possessive), one digit or one letter after it ("Passport",
       "Passports", "Passport's", "Passport 2", "Passport X", "Passport™", "Passport℠", "A Passport", "The Official
       Passport", "My NEAR Passport", "Near Wallet Passport"; ® and © are not letters, so "Passport®" is "Passport");
     - *a wallet word right after or before it* (after it also past edition words or one one-character word:
       "Passport Pro App", "Passport X Wallet"; a trade mark glued on doesn't hide it: "Passport Wallet™"), plural too: wallet, app, account, login, sign-in, sign-on, sign-up,
       support, help, security, team, official, pay, vault, verify, recovery, admin, staff, service, auth, connect,
       key, relayer, sponsor, gas, by; ID and from after it only ("Passport Wallets", "Passport ID", "Passport Keys",
       "Admin Passport", "Wallet by Passport");
     - *an edition word* (the Tech Lead 2026-11-23, narrowed the same day, note below): plus, pro, premium, prime, max,
       ultra, lite, mini, basic, classic, one, beta (and "pros") as the last words of a name that is "Passport" and
       them ("Passport Pro", "My Passport Plus", "Passport Pro Max", "Passport X Pro", "Passport Pro™"), run together
       ("PassportPlus"), or premium, pro, plus, lite, ultra or beta right before it with nothing but a determiner
       before ("Premium Passport", "My Pro Passport"); a brand of the partner's own or words after it make it theirs
       ("Acme Passport Plus", "Capital One Passport", "Passport Mini Golf");
     - *a claim word right before or after it* (the claim stems below: "Verified Passport", "Passport Safe", "Secure
       Passport");
     - *the start of another name*: the name begins with "Passport" (after at most two of the prefixes) and then a
       separator (comma, bracket, bar, slash, colon, semicolon, middle dot, bullet, quotation mark, an en or em dash,
       a dash beside a space) or "by", "from" or "of" ("Passport | Acme", "Passport (Acme)", "Passport from Acme",
       "Passport, by Acme"). Principle: such a name reads as "Passport, a product of Acme", the wallet with a maker;
       "{Brand} Passport" reads as the brand's own product and stays allowed ("Gitcoin Passport", "Human Passport",
       "Holonym Passport", "World ID Passport", "Galxe Passport", "Immutable Passport", "WD My Passport"), as does
       "Passport" followed by words of the partner's own ("Passport XYZ", "Passport Photos Co", "Passport Travel",
       "Passport Parking", "Passport Labs", "Passport Inc", "Passport Network", "Passport Protocol",
       "Passport-Health").
  6. **A claim word after sentence punctuation** (`sentenceClaimIn`): sentence punctuation is Unicode's terminal
     punctuation (`\p{Term}`, `\p{Sentence_Terminal}`: full stops, "!", "?", "‽", ":", ";", the Arabic, Devanagari,
     Ethiopic and CJK stops) but commas, "…", the look-alike dots and colons ꓸ ∶ ꞉ ː ⸱ ⁏, an en or em dash or
     horizontal bar anywhere, and any hyphen or dash (or the minus sign) beside a space; "Dr.", "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Ms.",
     "St.", "Jr.", "Sr.", "Mt." before a space are abbreviations. Only the words **after** the first break count, so a
     brand before it stays ("Trust: Crypto & Bitcoin Wallet", "Stay Safe!", "Dr. Trust"). A claim word is one that
     starts with a claim stem (verif, certif, offici, guarant, warrant, approv, recommend, endors, authent, genuin,
     legit, refund, reimburs, secur, protect, trust, safe, audit, authoriz/authoris, licens/licenc, regulat, vetted,
     reviewed, sponsor, checked, validated, harmless, riskless, riskfree, feeless, scamfree, reversib, and the Spanish,
     Portuguese, French, German, Italian and Malay forms ofici, garant, aprob, segur, sicher, gratis, gratuit,
     kostenlos, percuma, selamat, disahkan, rasmi, dijamin, jaminan), or a whole claim word (insure, insured, insures,
     insuring, free, freely, fee, fees, risk, risks, cost, costs, costless, nocost, nofee, nofees, norisk), or a pair
     ("no charge", "costs nothing", "zero cost"), read alone or joined with the next word ("Sa fe"). "Insure" is a
     whole word only, so "Allstate: Insurance Quotes" stays allowed.
  7. **A vouching word at the end** (`vouchingWordIn`, decided while reviewing PR 112, to confirm): verif…, offici…,
     checked, certif…, approv…, audited, endors…, authent…, genuin…, legit… as the name's last word or the first word
     after a bracket, bar, slash, backslash, comma, middle dot or bullet ("Acme Official", "Acme Verified", "Acme
     (Official)", "Acme | Certified"): "From Acme Official" and "Sponsored by Acme Verified." read as an endorsement.
     At the start of a name they are part of a brand and stay ("Verified Voting", "Official Charts Company", "Genuine
     Parts Company", "Certified Angus Beef"); safe, free, secure and trust stay allowed outside rule 6 ("Trusted
     Shops", "Secure Trust Bank", "Free People", "Safeway", "Acme Safe"): too common in real names.
- Sentence-shaped names with no listed word ("Acme. Sign it", "Acme. Nothing leaves your account", "Acme. Sent for
  you") can't be closed by any word list. The remaining defence is how the **window** sets the name apart: today its
  own bold `strong.app-name`, bidi-isolated (D884); quoting the name inside Journear's own sentences (such as the fee
  line) is an open option for a later approval-window change (for the Tech Lead, below).
- Awkward real names (tested, `names.test.ts` "awkward real-world names"): allowed "Yahoo!", "Yahoo! Japan", "Yum!
  Brands", "Jeopardy!", "Panic! at the Disco", "Westward Ho!", "Guess?", "Who? Weekly", "Dr. Martens", "Dr. Oetker",

  Générale", "Moët Hennessy", "Cirque du Soleil", "Safe{Wallet}", "Under Armour", "Procter & Gamble", and the store
  titles "Free Now – Taxi & more", "Garena Free Fire: Winterlands", "Safe Haven: Mental Health", "Allstate: Insurance
  Quotes", "Free! Magazine", "Stay Safe!", "Trust: Crypto & Bitcoin Wallet", "Safe{Wallet}: Multisig", "Safe -
  Multisig wallet". A run of about 300 more real company, app and wallet names (banks, payment apps, exchanges, NEAR
  and Stellar wallets and dapps, shops, games, "{Brand} Passport" products) found two refusals: "Insure.com" (D686's
  address rule, unchanged) and "Passport Secure Travel" (a claim word next to "Passport", accepted). Still refused
  and accepted: "A.P.C.", "J.Crew", "U.S. Bank", "Booking.com" (D686's address rule, unchanged: such a company
  registers "APC", "JCrew", "US Bank"); "Journear demo" (D765); "Yahoo! Finance Free", "Acme: Official Store" (a claim
  word after the break; the earlier "rare shapes" note was too strong: copied store titles do have this shape, and
  they register without the claim word); "GM Genuine", "Too Legit" (a vouching word last); real names in Cherokee,
  Lisu or Coptic script, or in IPA letters (none expected among partners).
- The messages a partner sees on **Branding** (staff in "Create an app", the CLI as "App name: …"), in the voice of
  D686's, each naming what triggered it: 'The name must not have "ID" right after "Passport": it reads as part of the
  wallet. Users call Journear Passport "Passport". Your brand first, as in "Acme Passport", or "Passport" with words
  of your own, as in "Passport Photos Co", is fine' (and "right before", "put "{word}" next to", "be "Passport" on
  its own or with only "{words}" around it", "start with "Passport" followed by another name"); 'The name must not
  have a word like "{word}" after sentence punctuation (a full stop, "!", "?", ":", ";", "…", an en or em dash, or a
  hyphen or dash with a space beside it): …'; 'The name must not end with "{word}" or have it after a bracket, bar or
  comma: "From Acme {word}" reads as an endorsement. …'; the imitation-letter and check-mark messages.
- Existing names: the rule applies where `appNameProblem` is called, which is the API's create and every rename
  (`apps/api/src/changes/settings.ts` `appName`), the operator CLI (`scripts/lib/admin-sql.ts` `assertAppName`), and
  the email issuer's `displayAppName` when it writes a mail. Nothing rewrites stored rows. So an app already stored
  under a name the rule now refuses keeps its name and keeps working; the approval and sign-in windows show the stored
  name as before (they apply only the display-safety rule, `isAppName`); **its code mails say "an app" and their
  subject names no app** (D686's handling, tested for the new shapes); a rename must pass. The registered names
  checked ("Stamp Trail", "E2E Partner", "Sodax Demo", the fixtures) all pass; "Journear demo" was already refused by
  D765 (Journear's own stored row, written to D1 directly by the e2e suite).
- Speed: every rule is linear in the name (64 characters at most); a test runs adversarial 64-character names
  ("P" × 64, "p a s s p o r t " × 4, ". " × 32, "Wallet Passport " × 4, …) and requires each under 20 ms (each takes
  well under 1 ms).
- What it misses: claim words and imitation outside these lists and blocks; sentence-shaped names without a listed
  word (above); edition words outside the list and version forms (open for the Tech Lead, note below).
- Follow-up (recorded, not built here): three implementations of the same idea will drift: console-core's
  `nameSkeleton`, core's `nameSkeleton` (verified-contracts.ts, a different table) and PR 114's partner-label folding
  (`foldLetters`, `DIGIT_FOLD`), with word splitting written twice, two claim vocabularies and `CHECK_MARKS` not
  shared. After PR 114 merges, one leaf module (for example a `@hana-id/core/text-safety` subpath, as console-core
  already imports `@hana-id/core/support-id`) should hold the merged confusables, skeleton, word splitting, claim
  stems, brand words and check marks, each rule keeping its own policy, with one test tying them together.
- **2026-11-23** ("confirm 1 to 8", from the description, not hand-tested; quoted in "Confirmed in one batch,
  2026-11-23" at the end of this file): of the list below, (3), (4) and (5) **confirmed by the Tech Lead**: "Letters
