## Partner labels, piece 2 of 5: storage, the guarded change, the staff veto, the switches, delivery (branch `feat/partner-labels-storage`), 2026-11-23

From `next` @ e575d586; not merged, not deployed; migrations 0025 (API) and 0004 (console) applied nowhere. Nothing in a
deployed env changes: every proposal is refused and `GET /v1/app` carries nothing unless the manifest turns
`partnerLabels.enabled` on, which no checked-in manifest does (only the local e2e stack's lane runs with it on).

### D894. Partner labels live in D1 as guarded changes of their own table, with a staff veto and no required review; delivered only by a fresh `GET /v1/app`, nothing rendered yet
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the staff veto (option 1) **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** ("go with 1"); the rest of
  the design decided while building, within D892's adopted recommendations, **to confirm** (the list at the end) ·
  Built: `apps/api/migrations/0025_partner_labels.sql`; `apps/api/src/labels/` (`sql.ts` the predicates, `store.ts`
  views and the plan read, `document.ts` parse, network rule, preview and diff, `propose.ts` ConsoleRpc's list,
  preview, propose and remove, `lifecycle.ts` notices, ack and cancels, `staff.ts` the feed, Block, Allow and the
  switches, `cron.ts` activation and lapses, `drift.ts`, `deliver.ts`); `rpc/console.ts` and `rpc/admin.ts` (the new
  methods; `cancelChange` / `cancelChangeByLink` take an `lc_` id); `handlers.ts` (`partnerLabels` in `GET /v1/app`);
  `index.ts` (the hourly job); `env.ts` `PARTNER_LABELS`; `scripts/gen-wrangler.ts`; `packages/env` (`partnerLabels`,
  `partnerLabelsProblem`); `packages/console-core/src/labels.ts` (inputs, views, `LABEL_STORE_LIMITS`), `layouts.ts`
  (`labelChangeDigest`, domain `hana-id/label-change/v1`), `ids.ts` (`lc_`, `pl_`), `types.ts` (two step-up kinds,
  three security event kinds, the RpcCode `label_invalid`), `rpc.ts` (`changeIdInput` takes `gc_` or `lc_`),
  `audit-words.ts`, `staff.ts` (two org-less staff actions); `packages/core` (the `./partner-labels` subpath,
  `previewLabelDocument`, `LABEL_STELLAR_NETWORKS`, `AppConfig.partnerLabels`); `packages/web/src/vault/partner-labels.ts`
  (the vault's type and pure check, called by nothing); `apps/console` (`actions.ts` kinds `labels.set` and
  `labels.remove`, `audit.ts`, migration `0004_label_step_ups.sql`); `apps/admin` (the staff screen, its tools, the
  notices, the blocked mail, the status tile: below); `apps/e2e` (the lane's labels and the hand-test scenarios).
- **The Tech Lead's decision (option 1, "Staff veto, no required review").** Asked whether a person at Journear must review
  each label change during its 24-hour wait, the Tech Lead chose, in their words, "go with 1", of: "1. Staff veto, no
  required review … Each label change appears in the staff feed during its 24-hour wait, showing exactly what users
  would see. If nobody objects, it goes live. If someone does, one press blocks it. … It can be tightened later with no
  rebuild. If a partner abuses it, required review can be switched on for that partner or for everyone." Their reason:
  "having to review everything is a burden on our time", and other providers (Privy and others) let apps write free text
  with no review at all. **Accepted risk:** a mildly misleading phrase that passes piece 1's text rules can go live if
  nobody looks during the wait. What bounds it: the phrase is one short object phrase in a sentence Journear builds,
  always attributed ("{App} says: …", "These are {App}'s words. Journear hasn't checked them.", piece 3); the real
  amounts, recipients and every warning still show beside it; the org's security contacts get the notice with a cancel
  link; staff get a security event when a change is proposed and when it goes live; staff can block it at any time,
  switch the org's labels off, or require review for that org or for everyone, all without a deploy.

#### Where it lives (option B of the proposal)
- **`partner_labels`**: an entry, one document's place, owned by one org in one scope (so one environment, D51), never
  moved (trigger). Removal (`removed_at`) is final; staff's entry switch is `off_at` (+ `off_version`).
- **`label_changes`**: each version of an entry's document: the TEXT exactly as proposed, its schema version
  (`journear-labels/1`), its sha256 and size, what it describes (`context_key`), the apps it is attached to (1–8, each a
  live app of that scope and org, checked by trigger at insert), the version in force when it was proposed
  (`previous_id`: the diff and piece 3's "changed on {date}"), who proposed it (the member and the API-verified step-up
  `sub`) and the lifecycle columns. What a version says and where it applies are written once (trigger); rows are kept
  60 months (trigger, as `app_changes`). No column claims the contract's code was checked: reading the code hash is
  piece 5, and the matcher still requires it equal at match time.
- **`label_controls`** (`'*'` or an org: `labels_off`, `review_required`, `version`) and **`label_control_log`**
  (append-only: every switch of every target, entries included, with the staffer and the note).
- `scopes.labels_version`: bumped by every label write in the scope (proposal, removal, cancel, block, allow, lapse): the
  compare-and-swap version and part of the step-up's nonce. `security_events` gains `label_proposed`, `label_blocked`,
  `label_live` (rebuilt as 0023 and 0024 did). Console `pending_actions.kind` gains `labels.set`, `labels.remove`
  (console migration 0004, the table rebuilt; rows live 5 minutes).
- Why a table of its own and not `guarded_changes`: that table's `app_id` is NOT NULL and its kinds are a CHECK, while a
  label version is on a scope and several apps; widening it means rebuilding the table every guarded change, origin row
  and drift query reads. The lifecycle is the same one, written for the new table: the same commit-point writes
  (`app_changes` first, `changes/cas.ts`), the same step-up check (`changes/step-up.ts`), the same notice, ack, cancel
  link, 7-day lapse and hourly job. No change to the contract, to how owners are proven (the API's step-up check,
  unchanged, with a new nonce layout for the new change) or to the vault's trust model.

#### States (a version's `state`, computed from its row, the clock and the switches)
- `proposed` (no notice yet) → `announced` (the admin Worker's notice was accepted; in force at `active_from` = the ack
  + `appChangeDelayMs`, 24 h in production, 60 s on sandbox-dev; never a waiver) → `in_force`; or, when review is
  required for its org or for everyone and no staff member allowed it, `waiting_review` once its time came.
- Ends: `cancelled` (an owner, or the emailed link, while it waits), `lapsed` (not announced within 7 days of its
  proposal, or still held for review 7 days after its time), `blocked` (staff, before or after it took effect),
  `replaced` (a newer version of the entry took effect; the hourly job then ends it), `removed` (the owner removed the
  entry). Switched off is not a state of a version: an entry is served only while no switch (its own, its org's,
  everyone's) is off; the view says which (`off`) and whether it is served now (`served`).
- In force (`labels/sql.ts` IN_FORCE): recorded `active` by the hourly job, or pending, announced, its time passed and
  no review hold. An entry's document is its newest version in force. Nothing waits for the hourly job: delivery uses the
  predicate (as origins and policies do, D701).

#### Who can do what
- **Propose** (`ConsoleRpc.proposeLabels`, through the console's step-up kind `labels.set`; no screen yet, piece 4):
  exactly who may propose an origin or a policy today, an on-chain `Owner::Oidc` of the scope, with a Google step-up the
  API verifies itself, whose nonce is `labelChangeDigest` over the signer, the scope, the entry (`""` for a new one), the
  document's sha256, the sorted apps and the scope's `labels_version`. Refused in order (writing nothing, the token not
  used): the switch off (`env_mismatch`); the parser's and text rules' problems (`label_invalid`, each "code at path:
  message", the parser's stable codes and plain messages, at most 20); a network other than the scope's environment's
  (`label_invalid`, `wrong_environment`: test scopes describe the NEAR test network or the Stellar test network, live
  scopes the main ones); piece 1's refusals of a context Journear reads itself (known tokens, reviewed contracts,
  standard methods: `journear_reads_this`, `reserved_method`); a scope not of the org; an entry not of the scope, removed,
  or switched off by staff (`forbidden`: ask Journear first); an app not a live app of the scope in the org, or listed
  twice; a version already waiting for the entry; another live entry of the scope describing the same contract; the
  limits (below); the version, the nonce, the owner, the token's single use. The same document on the same apps as the
  version in force is a no-op (`noChange`, nothing written, the token not used).
- **Preview** (`ConsoleRpc.previewLabels`): every check above but the step-up and the write; answers the preview (for
  each format: the line "{App} says: …", the sentence's parts marked whose words they are, the rows; with example
  values, built by the matcher's own renderer, `previewLabelDocument`), the sha256, the size and the version. The
  console's `labels.set` builds the step-up from it and shows it on the confirmation page.
- **Remove** (`ConsoleRpc.removeLabels`, step-up kind `labels.remove`): the same proof (the nonce over the entry and the
  version, no document), immediate: the version in force ends, a waiting one is cancelled; it only ever returns the window
  to the plain view.
- **Cancel** a waiting version: an owner (`ConsoleRpc.cancelChange`, no step-up, as for guarded changes), the emailed link
  (`cancelChangeByLink`, its token's hash: the console's `/cancel/lc_…#t=` page and `POST /api/cancel` take an `lc_`
  id, its audit row names the entry and no app, and opening the link alone changes nothing). **Staff never cancel a
  label change; they Block it** (decided after the security review, to confirm): `AdminRpc.cancelChange` and the
  admin's `POST /api/changes/:id/cancel` refuse an `lc_` id ("Staff don’t cancel request label changes. Open it on
  Partner labels and use Block this change, with a note."), so every staff stop has its note and audit row first.
  `expediteChange` and the guarded notice's `ackNotice` take a `gc_` id only.
- **Announce**: only the admin Worker's notice cron (`AdminRpc.labelNotices` → email the security alias and every
  security contact, each with the preview, the diff and the cancel link → `AdminRpc.ackLabelNotice`, `system` actor only,
  after every send was accepted). No staff expedite exists for labels.
- **Staff** (`AdminRpc`, through the admin portal; each tool recorded in the staff audit log first, no row no action, and
  applied only while the change is as the page showed it: the scope's `labels_version` and the state): **Block this
  change** (a note of 10–300 characters, required; any version proposed, announced, held or in force; one in force stops
  being served at once and any older version of the entry still in force ends with it (`end_reason`
  `blocked_successor`, shown to staff as "Ended when the newer version was blocked: neither shows"), so users then see
  the PLAIN window for those requests, never the earlier labels; final: the partner proposes again, another full wait. A
  waiting version that is cancelled or blocked never replaced anything: the version in force stays); **Allow** (only while review is required and
  the version isn't allowed yet; it lifts the hold and nothing else: its own time still applies); the switches (below).
  Staff never propose or edit a document, and nothing staff do can make a version take effect before its time
  (tested: Allow pressed before the notice or before `active_from`, review switched off while versions wait, and a
  switch turned back on after versions were blocked, replaced, cancelled or lapsed while it was off; none serves
  anything early or anything that ended).
- **Required review** (`label_controls.review_required`, for one org or for everyone, default off): a version whose time
  has come waits for Allow however long, until it lapses 7 days after its time (decided: the partner then proposes again;
  a held change neither goes live by itself nor waits forever; the partner gets a mail saying so). Switching review off
  lets a held version whose time has passed take effect at once (it went through the notice and the delay). **Review
  holds only versions due after it was turned on** (`label_controls.review_since`, after the security review): a
  version whose time had already come when review was turned on stays in force, whether or not the hourly job had
  recorded it, so the outcome never depends on the job's timing (before the fix, turning review on could put a live
  version back to waiting and bring back the older one). The hourly job re-checks the hold in its own activation and
  lapse statements, so a review switch or an Allow landing between its read and its write is never overridden.
- **Kill switches** (`AdminRpc.labelControl`): one entry, one org's labels, every partner label: off at once (the next
  `GET /v1/app` read), and back on (a separate act with its own note) only re-serves versions that passed the guarded
  path, including one whose time came while the switch was off (the staff confirmation says so); a switch never makes
  a waiting version take effect. **While an org's or everyone's switch is off, proposals are refused** (decided after
  the security review, to confirm): "Journear has switched request labels off for your organisation: ask Journear
  security before proposing new ones" (or "…off for now…"), so an org switched off for abuse can't keep mailing its
  contacts and filling the staff feed. An entry switched off refuses its own new versions likewise. Each switch writes `label_control_log` and, for an
  org's or an entry's, the org's `app_changes` (the partner sees it in its audit and the feed's digest).

#### The ledger, the feed and drift
- `app_changes` kinds: `labels.proposed`, `change.announced` and `change.cancelled` with detail `kind: 'label_set'` (the
  cron's lapses carry `reason: not_announced | not_reviewed`), `labels.activated`, `labels.blocked` (with the note and
  `wasLive`), `labels.allowed`, `labels.removed`, `labels.switched_off` / `switched_on`, `labels.review_on` / `review_off`
  (org-level). Security events: `label_proposed` (at the proposal), `label_blocked`, `label_live` (when the hourly job
  records it in force), each once per version, no document text; the feed emails them to the security alias and the org's
  contacts.
- **Drift** (`labels/drift.ts`, hourly beside `changes/drift.ts`): a `drift` event (detail `what: partner_label` and a
  `finding`) for a version in force without the `labels.proposed` row of its exact sha256 and apps or without an
  announcement no later than its `active_from` (`unannounced`: a bare D1 write that skipped the notice or the delay); a
  version in force whose text no longer hashes to its sha256 (`text_changed`; the trigger refuses an in-place edit, so
  this needs the trigger dropped too); an `allowed_at` without a staff `labels.allowed` row (`not_allowed`); a blocked
  version no longer blocked (`unblocked`); a cancelled or lapsed version back to waiting or in force (`uncancelled`,
  added after the review); a removed entry back (`not_removed`); a switch that isn't what its last log row set
  (`control`). Once per finding. An older version un-ended by hand after it was replaced (or ended with a blocked
  successor) is caught only indirectly, when its own ledger rows don't explain it. The hourly job and the drift check
  log a failure at error level (`labels_cron`, `label_drift_detection`) and are thrown like the guarded changes' (after
  the review: they were silent); before migration 0025 is applied they skip with one warning line each.
  **Retention:** a label ledger row (`labels.*`, a `change.*` row of kind `label_set`) is kept while its entry exists
  (`changes/retention.ts`), and `label_changes` rows are not purged at all yet ("kept 60 months" is a floor). **Residual, the same as today's for origins and policies** (docs/security.md):
  someone who can write D1 freely can also forge the ledger rows and the log, and then drift sees nothing.

#### Delivery (`GET /v1/app`) and the vault
- Only on the vault's own read (request `Origin` = `VAULT_ORIGIN`) and only with `PARTNER_LABELS = "on"`:
  `partnerLabels: [{id, changeId, version, sha256, text, effectiveSince, previousEffectiveSince}]`, the requesting app's
  served documents: the entry's newest version in force, the app among its attached apps, the entry's org and scope the
  app's own NOW (a scope moved to another org serves nothing of the old org's), not removed, no switch off, nothing
  proposed, announced, held, blocked, lapsed or cancelled. At most 16 entries; the org's limits keep it under 32 KiB of
  documents per app. Read from D1 on every request (no isolate cache), answered `cache-control: no-store` as every API
  answer; a failed read leaves the field out (no labels), never fails the config. Switch off: no field at all, as before.
- The vault: `AppConfig.partnerLabels` is typed unknown; `verifyDeliveredLabels` (pure) re-hashes each text, requires the
  schema version this build knows, re-parses with the vault's own copy of core's parser and text rules, requires the
  env's network, drops an entry named twice, a malformed one and anything over the cap; a dropped document means the
  plain view. NOTHING CALLS IT YET: piece 3 renders labels and must hold each to a read under a freshness window like
  `POLICY_FRESH_MS` (D62), so a switch or a block reaches users within seconds and a failed read means no labels.
- `@hana-id/core/partner-labels` is imported by exactly two sources outside core, the API's `labels/document.ts` and the
  vault's helper (core's dormancy test now asserts exactly that, and that core's root entry still doesn't export it).

#### Limits (`LABEL_STORE_LIMITS`, to confirm)
- A document 16 KiB (core's `LABEL_LIMITS`); attached to at most 8 apps; an org holds at most 16 entries (not removed);
  an org's documents in force or waiting at most 64 KiB together; the documents attached to one app at most 32 KiB
  together (what its `GET /v1/app` can carry); at most 10 proposals per org in a rolling 24 hours (the org-wide limits
  are checked again inside the proposal's own write, so concurrent proposals in different scopes can't pass them; the
  per-app one is serialised by the scope's version, an app being in one scope); one waiting version
  per entry; one live entry per contract per scope. A staff note 10–300 characters, one line of plain text (no
  control, direction or invisible character). The lapses: 7 days. The
  staff feed: every waiting version, and those proposed or decided in the last 14 days, at most 200. Drift: at most 100
  findings per check and run, 500 versions re-hashed per run. ConsoleRpc costs (hot-DB statements): list 2, preview 1,
  propose 7, remove 6.

#### What each attacker can and cannot do
| Attacker | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| A hijacked partner console account (a member's session; or an owner's Google account too) | With an owner's Google account: propose labels, which reach users only after the notice to the org's security contacts (with a cancel link), the full delay and the staff feed's wait, in the partner's voice; remove labels (back to the plain view). With a session alone: cancel a waiting change, preview, list. | Propose or remove without an on-chain owner's step-up for exactly that change (the API verifies the token itself); act before the notice and the delay; speak as Journear or claim safety (piece 1's text rules); change amounts or recipients (the window shows the request's own values, piece 3); remove or lower a warning (D892 recommendation 4); reach another org's apps (entries are the org's, per scope, checked at write and at every read); survive a staff block or switch. |
| A hijacked partner page (XSS, a bad dependency) | Send forged requests, as today. | Change any label (they come only from D1 through the console's guarded path); make the vault read labels other than the API's for its own app; forged requests match nothing, or fail a declared constraint (piece 1's matcher). |
| A D1 compromise (or a buggy script with D1 write) | Write any document and mark it in force, skipping the notice, the delay and the staff veto; clear a block or a switch. | Escape drift detection without also forging `app_changes` and `label_control_log` rows (the same residual as origins and policies today); get past the vault's own parser and text rules (they, not the re-hash, bound what can be shown: the attacker writes the hash too, so the re-hash only catches corruption); make the window drop a warning or show values that aren't the request's. |
| A malicious staff member | Block changes and switch labels off (a denial: users see the plain view; the partner is told of a block by email, an org's or entry's switch is in its audit); Allow a held change; turn a switch back on. Every act is in the staff audit log first, with the staffer and the note, and the API's ledger. | Propose, edit or expedite a document (no such staff method exists); make a version take effect before its time or without its notice; make a switch-on serve a version that didn't pass the guarded path. |

#### Rejected
- Reusing `guarded_changes` (above). Storing the parsed document (the server stores the text and the schema version, and
  every reader re-parses with its own parser, D892's versioning rule). Required review by default (the Tech Lead's option
  1). A staff proposal or expedite path for labels (nothing in the threat model needs it; staff only ever turn labels
  off). An "Unblock" for a blocked change (blocked is final; the partner proposes again and waits again). A waiver
  (`no_session`, `loopback`) for label changes. Serving labels on every `GET /v1/app` read, or from the isolate cache
  (only the vault needs them; a switch must reach the next read).
- Address impact: none (nothing signed, decoded or derived changes; nothing is rendered yet).

#### To confirm (with the Tech Lead), as the security review framed them
1. The limits above. 2. The two names: staff say "partner labels", partners read "request labels"; each screen and mail
that uses one explains it once ("the words the approval window shows your users for your app’s requests"; the staff
screen: "…(partners call them request labels)"). 3. A change held for review lapses 7 days after its time (the partner
is mailed). 4. Block is final, no unblock: a mistaken block costs the partner a new proposal and another full wait; the
expected handling is to tell the partner (reply to the blocked mail) and, if it must go live sooner, there is no staff
shortcut by design. 5. Staff Block only, never cancel (decided after the review). 6. Proposals refused while the org's
or everyone's labels are switched off (decided after the review; only an entry switch refused one before). 7. The
staff- and partner-facing sentences (below). 7. The audit titles and security event titles in
`packages/console-core/src/audit-words.ts` ("Request labels proposed", "Request labels blocked by Journear", "Request
labels now shown to users", "Request labels proposed: shown to users after the wait unless Journear blocks them", …).

#### The sentences (from the code, to confirm)
- **Partner notice** (`apps/admin/src/email/messages.ts` `labelsProposed`; to the security alias and every security
  contact): subject "Request labels proposed for {app}"; heading "Request labels proposed", lead "New words for your
  app’s requests are waiting. They are not live yet, and you can cancel them."; body "Someone with owner rights in your
  organisation proposed request labels for {apps}: the words the approval window will show your users for your app’s
  requests, in your app’s name. Unless someone cancels them, they go live {24 hours} after this email. Journear may
  block them if they would mislead users." With staff review on for the org: "…in your app’s name. Journear reviews
  them first: they go live only after Journear allows them, at the earliest {24 hours} after this email, unless someone
  cancels them. If Journear hasn’t allowed them within 7 days of that time, they lapse and nothing changes."; the rows
  Apps, Organisation (its name and id), Scope, Describes, "Change: Set request labels
  ({lc_…})", Proposed at; "What users would see (example values):" each line and its rows; "What changes:" each changed
  line (or "Nothing users see changes: every line stays as it is now."); the button "Cancel this change"; "If you did not
  expect this change, cancel it. The page asks you to confirm; opening the link alone changes nothing. An owner can also
  cancel it in the console."
- **Blocked mail** (`labelsBlocked`, the feed's own mail for a `labels.blocked` row; the `label_blocked` security event
  then goes to the security alias only, so the partner gets one message): subject "Journear blocked a change to request
  labels for {app}"; "Journear blocked a change to the request labels of {apps} ({lc_…}): the words the approval window
  shows your users for your app’s requests. Your users will never see it." (in force: "Your users see the plain approval
  window for these requests from now, without your earlier labels either."; in force while Journear had them switched
  off: "Your users weren’t seeing it: Journear had already switched these labels off. When they are switched back on,
  neither these nor your earlier labels will show.");
- **Lapse mail** (`labelsLapsed`, for a change held for review that lapsed): subject "A change to request labels lapsed
  for {app}"; "A change to the request labels of {apps} ({lc_…}), the words the approval window shows your users for
  your app’s requests, lapsed: Journear didn’t allow it within 7 days of its time, so your users never see it. Nothing
  else changed." and "To try again, change the labels in the console. To ask why it wasn’t allowed, reply to this email
  or write to your Journear contact."; "Journear’s note: “{note}”"; "To ask why, reply to this
  email or write to your Journear contact. To try again, change the labels in the console; the new change waits {24
  hours} again."
- **The console's cancel page** for an `lc_` link: "Cancel this change to request labels", "This cancels the change to
  your app’s request labels announced in the email (the words the approval window would show your users). It never
  takes effect. You don’t need to sign in."
- **The staff screen** (`apps/admin/public/app.js`, "Partner labels" under Security): subtitle "The words partners write
  for the approval window, shown to their users as “{App} says: …”. Every change waits its time after the partner’s
  security contacts are emailed. Nothing is needed for it to go live; block one that would mislead users."; panels
  "Waiting" (soonest live first), "Decided in the last 14 days", "Switches"; on a change, "What users would see (example
  values)", "Compared with what users see now", "Staff tools". States: "Waiting for the notice email", "Goes live {time}",
  "Waiting for a staff Allow", "Live", "Blocked by staff", "Cancelled by the partner", "Lapsed", "Replaced by a newer
  change", "Removed by the partner". Tools: "Block this change" (note label "Why (the partner is sent this note; it is
  kept in the audit log)"; confirm "Block this change? Users will never see it, and the partner is told Journear blocked
  it." or, in force, "Block this change? Users stop seeing it at once, and the partner is told Journear blocked it.");
  "Allow" (confirm "Allow this change? It goes live at its time, or at once if its time has passed."); "Switch these
  labels off" (confirm "Switch these labels off? Users of these apps see the plain approval window, without the
  partner’s words, until staff turn them back on.") and "Turn these labels back on" ("…A version that passed its wait
  shows again, including one whose time came while switched off; a change still waiting keeps waiting."; the org's and
  everyone's say the same of versions); "Switch every partner label off" / "Turn every partner label back on"; "Require review for
  everyone" / "Turn review off for everyone"; one organisation's four switches by its id. A stale page: "This change moved
  since you opened the page (someone may have acted, or it went live). Nothing was done. Reload the page and look again."
  Every staff sentence passes the portal's plain-words checks (`test-spa/labels.test.ts`, D853, D879).
- **Feed and notices**: "Partner label changes waiting" with the count and a link. **System status**: the tile "Partner
  labels" (group Partners): OK with no switch off; a warning "Partner labels are switched off {for everyone | for N
  organisations}; N sets of partner labels are switched off", with "{who} see the plain approval window, without the
  partner’s words. To turn a switch back on, open Partner labels."; review on is a detail line; Unknown when the API
  can't be read or is older.

#### For piece 3 (requirements recorded after the security review, not built now)
- Labels are used only from a fresh read, as policies are (`POLICY_FRESH_MS`, 10 s): a switch or a block reaches users
  within seconds, and a failed read means no labels.
- When two delivered entries describe the same contract (the server refuses it; a D1 write could make it), drop both.
- App names can be renamed at once, outside the 24 h wait, while staff reviewed the preview under the old name: decide
  in piece 3 whether an `app.renamed` of an app with labels is flagged in the staff feed (or holds its labels).
- `label_live` can arrive up to an hour after a label actually goes live (the hourly job records it; delivery uses the
  predicate): say so on the staff screen, or record it at the first served read, in piece 3.
- Each screen and mail that names "partner labels" or "request labels" explains the name once (checked now for the
  staff screen, the Feed and notices panel, the notice, the blocked and lapse mails and the cancel page).
- Test note (optional now): run the partner-labels e2e in its own lane, or add a lane action that drains the feed with a
  capturing sender after label scenarios, then restore the strict "Caught up" check in `admin-portal.spec.ts` (loosened
  to `expectFeedsRead` in this branch; reviewed as legitimate); that would also cover the blocked mail end to end.
- Note, 2026-11-23 (D896, built in piece 3 and amended after PR 123's review): the freshness window, the duplicate
  drop and the `app.renamed` recommendation are in D896. **For piece 4** (recorded by that review): the console's
  preview must warn a partner that declaring a payment format turns every payment, and every value-moving classic
  operation, to an account outside its address book red in its users' windows.
- Note, 2026-11-23: piece 4 is D899 (the console's Request labels tab, its warnings and review; `listLabels` and
  `previewLabels` gained read-only fields).

### D895. Passport Home step 3: a wallet's page as three tabs (Addresses, Security, Move wallet), the phone's "Sign in again" chip, and the move flow in wallet words
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the tabs and the chip **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-23** (structure A, D888; the chip's
  "Yes", D888's open list); the details below decided while building, **to confirm** (the list at the end) · Built on
  `feat/home-step3-wallet-view` (from `next`), not merged, not deployed: `packages/web/src/auth/home-page.ts`
  (`HOME_WALLET_TABS`, `walletTabs`, `selectTab`, `showView`'s tab branch, `appPage`, the chip: `updateChip`,
  `chipSoon`, `HOME_TEXT.tabs`, `tabsWallet`, `tabsApp`, `chip`, `chipEnding`, `chipEnded`, `MOVE_WORDS`),
  `home-export.ts` (words and one heading level only, below), `css/home.css` (the head, the tabs, the panels, the chip;
  `#home-app-extras` → `.home-tools`); tests `packages/web/test/auth/home-page.test.ts` ("a wallet’s tabs (D895)", "the
  phone’s “Sign in again” chip (D895)"), `home-export.test.ts` (the move flow on its tab, Back and Forward between
  tabs, "the phone’s chip showing or going starts the guard over"), e2e `apps/e2e/tests/home.spec.ts` (tabs and chip,
  three browsers) and the Home specs opening tabs (`homeTab`). Notes on D888 and D893. No API, vault, issuer or contract
  change; `key-reveal.ts`, `approve-guard.ts` and `guard-hint.ts` unchanged.
- **The page** (option A's `a2`–`a5`): the head stays above the tabs: "Your wallets", the `h1` ("Wallet details", or
  "App details" where the person has no wallet), the apps that use the wallet (a labelled group, no longer a heading),
  the question and the coverage line (a label and a sentence, no longer a heading), "Check now". Then the design
  system's tabs: **Addresses** (open first, by default: the addresses and the Support ID), **Security** (Ways to sign
  in, Devices and auto-approve, Your name, in the mock-up's order; step 4 fills it out) and **Move wallet** (the move
  flow alone, the last tab, set to the right on a wider screen). On a phone the three tabs share the width (no sideways
  scroll at 390 or 320 px; under 360 px their icons go).
- **Real tabs**: a `tablist` named "This wallet" ("This app" on "App details"), three `tab` buttons (`aria-selected`,
  `aria-controls`), three `tabpanel`s (`aria-labelledby`; the others `hidden`; each a stop for Tab). One tab stop for
  the list; the arrow keys, Home and End move focus between tabs (roving tabindex) **without opening one**; Enter or
  Space (a button's click) opens it (manual activation: opening a tab adds a history entry, and leaving "Move wallet"
  locks an opened wallet, so an arrow key must not do either by accident). Reduced motion: no transition on the tabs.
- **History**: each tab opened adds one entry in D893's scheme (`home:{tag}:{step}`, nothing else). Back and Forward
  move between the tabs opened, then to "Your wallets"; opening the tab already open adds nothing; "Your wallets"
  goes back to the list's own entry however many tabs were opened (`history.go(-step)`); a wallet opens on Addresses
  every time; nothing is read on a tab change, a Back or a Forward.
- **Move wallet locks when left**: leaving the "Move wallet" tab (another tab, Back, Forward elsewhere, the way back)
  locks and erases a wallet opened there, by the move flow's own `leave()` (the same call as leaving the page, D580,
  D893): no key exists while its panel is hidden. Forward back to the tab shows it collapsed, never a key. The other
  tabs keep what they show (the devices, the ways to sign in, the name) for as long as the wallet's page is open.
- **The phone's "Sign in again" chip** (the rule as revised after PR 122's review, **to confirm**): a small primary
  button, "Sign in again" with a clock icon, fixed at the window's foot in the middle, outside the page's content. It
  shows whenever all of these hold, and then STAYS (it no longer hides over controls, so it doesn't flicker): signed
  in; the bar's notice offers "Sign in again" (the warning or the end); the bar is not stuck (a phone or a tablet: on a
  desktop the bar, and so the notice, is always in view; CSS also hides the chip there); the notice is scrolled out of
  view; and the open view is not a wallet's "Move wallet" tab. While it shows, the page gets room at its foot (from the
  chip's top to the window's bottom, plus 16 px: `--home-chip-space`, `body.home-chip-on`), so the last control can
  always be scrolled clear above it. It is **never shown on "Move wallet"**, in any screen of the move flow, so it can
  never be under or near Continue, Show key or Copy key, by construction (the notice in the top bar stays the way to
  sign in again there). It is re-checked whenever something that matters changes: every redraw of the page (a view or
  tab change, a list or section redraw), the notice's redraw, the bar's resize, and, once a frame, scroll and resize.
  When it shows or goes, the move flow's guard starts over once. Hidden, it takes no click and no focus (`visibility:
  hidden`). Pressed, it scrolls to the top and puts focus on the notice's "Sign in again"; it leaves nothing (the tab
  stays open). Its accessible description says "Your sign-in to Passport Home ends soon." or "…has ended."; the bar's
  live region still announces the notice. (The first build hid it wherever any control or focusable panel was under
  it and kept 48 px from guarded buttons: the review found it then showed at one scroll position only, at the page's
  foot, and that a change inside the move flow without a scroll could leave it near a guarded button until the next
  scroll; replaced by the rule above.)
- **How the safety rules are proven.** (a) Leaving "Move wallet" erases the opened key from the page and from memory:
  unit tests for another tab, Back, "Your wallets" and Forward to a tab opened after it (the secret zeroed, the move
  flow `closed`, the key's box masked, the key's text nowhere in the document), checked to fail when the page doesn't
  call `leave()` on a tab change; e2e in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with the real derive for another tab, "Your
  wallets" and Forward (three derives, the key read off the page and then searched for in the page's text, markup and
  fields), and Back (D893's test, now Back to Addresses). The chip's press is not a way of leaving: it is never on
  "Move wallet", and pressed elsewhere it keeps the open tab (unit, e2e). (b) The chip is never on "Move wallet": unit
  tests on the flow's closed and expanded screens, after a screen change with no scroll, and after Back to the tab;
  e2e in the three browsers at 320, 360, 390 and 430 px (the closed and expanded screens at every 60 px of scroll),
  and `home-shell.spec.ts` sweeps the flow's guarded confirmation, Continue on screen, top to end in 40 px steps with
  the warning up at 1280, 390 and 320 px: never shown. Elsewhere (the list, Addresses, Security) the e2e sweeps check
  it shows at every position out of the notice's view and that the last control ends at least 16 px above it.
- **The move flow in wallet words, and its heading level** (`home-export.ts`: WORDING AND STRUCTURE ONLY). Nothing
  changes in what is derived, shown, timed, wiped or copied, in any guard, or in how a path or key is derived: with
  every string literal blanked, the file before and after is the same text (SHA-256 prefix `9a5157a48a9a119a` for
  both, checked again after PR 122's review); 9 lines changed, all string literals, one of them the title's tag (`'h3'` → `'h2'`, so the move flow's screen
  titles sit under the page's `h1` in their own panel instead of under "Your name"). `key-reveal.ts` is unchanged.

  | Where | Old | New |
  |---|---|---|
  | Collapsed | "Passport Home can show you the private key of your wallet in this app, so that you can import it into another wallet app." | "Passport Home can show you this wallet’s private key, so that you can add the wallet to another wallet app." |
  | Expanded (the user's wallet) | "…so that you can import it into another wallet app. The wallet keeps working in the app as before." | "…so that you can add the wallet to another wallet app. The wallet keeps working in its apps as before." |
  | Not offered from a link | "You came to this app through a link. … open Passport Home yourself, without the link, and find the app in your list or by its name." | "You came here through a link. … open Passport Home yourself, without the link, and find it under “Your wallets”, or by searching for the app’s name." |
  | Expanded (an app with no wallet of theirs) | "…If it finds one, it can show you its private key, so that you can import it into another wallet app." | "…so that you can add the wallet to another wallet app." |
  | A different address on record | "The address Journear had on record for you in this app is different from this wallet’s." | "Journear’s record shows a different address for this wallet." |
  | Open | "The wallet is locked again 5 minutes after you signed in, when you leave this app’s page, and when you close or reload Passport Home." | "The wallet locks again 5 minutes after you signed in, when you leave “Move wallet”, and when you close or reload Passport Home." |
  | A key shown | "…It is erased from this page 5 minutes after you signed in, when you leave this app’s page, and when you close or reload Passport Home." | "…when you leave “Move wallet”, and when you close or reload Passport Home." |
  | NEAR's first note | "…If that app removes this key from the account, this app loses the wallet too." | "…If that app removes this key from the account, Journear and the apps that use this wallet can no longer use this NEAR account." |
  | Move title | `h3` | `h2` (the panel's section) |

  And in `home-page.ts`: the coverage line no longer adds a move hint on the wallet's page (it said "…below."; the tab is
  right there; `coverageText` keeps it for its callers); for a wallet two or more apps use, the question and answers

  to this wallet.", "Journear can no longer sign you in to this wallet: the sign-in these apps used is gone. If they

### D896. Partner labels piece 3: the approval window shows a matching label as the app's words, after everything Journear says; anything else is the plain window or one line in Journear's voice
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: built on `feat/partner-labels-window` (from `next` @ 5dd1adfa, `next` @ 39cb14be merged in),
  not merged, not deployed; amended after PR 123's security review (the review passed with 12 fixes and two findings
  of the commit review, all built: "After PR 123's review" below); the design, placements, values and every sentence
  decided while building or while reviewing, **to confirm** (the list at the end); within D892's adopted
  recommendations and D894's requirements for piece 3 · Built:
  `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`hana:approve-request` `partnerLabels`, `APPROVAL_LABELS_MAX_BYTES`,
  `APPROVAL_LABELS_MAX`, `APPROVE_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`); `packages/core/src/partner-labels/context.ts`
  (`labelContextKey`, `labelOnNetwork`, `withoutSharedContracts`), `match.ts` (what the request is first, `valueTo`,
  `fee_bump`, `operation_mismatch`, muxed accounts, `source_not_user` not described), `text-rules.ts`
  (`text_row_word`, `idValueProblem`), `schema.ts` (`LABEL_LIMITS.rows`); `packages/web/src/vault/partner-labels.ts`
  (`PARTNER_LABELS_FRESH_MS`, `PARTNER_LABELS_WAIT_MS`, `MAX_WINDOW_LABEL_BYTES`, `windowLabelTexts`; the duplicate
  drop in `verifyDeliveredLabels`); `vault/vault.ts` (`applyServedLabels`, `labelsForWindow`, `refreshLabels`);
  `vault/approvals.ts` (`WindowLabels`, `labelsFor`, the one-read hold); `auth/render-labels.ts` (`windowLabelDocuments`,
  `labelOutcome`, `labelBox`, `labelBoxName`, `LABEL_MISMATCH`, `LABEL_NOT_LISTED`); `auth/render-approval.ts`
  (`ApprovalRenderContext.partnerLabels`, `labelFacts`, `windowLabel`, `journearAfterWarnings`, the red and amber items,
  the box's one place); `auth/approve-page.ts` (parses what the vault sent); `auth/css/approval.css`
  (`div.partner-label`, the divider rules); `apps/e2e/src/server/api.ts` (`PARTNER_LABELS` on in the local stack's API,
  `/__e2e/labels`, `/__e2e/labels/remove`, `/__e2e/app-reads`). `approve-guard.ts` unchanged (its sha256 test passes).
  No checked-in manifest turns `partnerLabels.enabled` on.

#### The design
- **Where a label comes from.** Only the vault's own `GET /v1/app` read. The vault keeps what `verifyDeliveredLabels`
  passed (its own sha256, its own copy of core's parser and text rules, the env's network, an entry named once, and **no
  two entries describing the same contract**: chain, network and account or contract, the API's `context_key`; both
  are dropped) with the time that read was sent, on the server-corrected clock and the monotonic one. When a sign
  request goes to the window, the vault attaches the texts of the documents for that request's chain (NEAR's for NEAR,
  Soroban's and classic payments' for Stellar, none for EVM) only if that read is younger than
  **`PARTNER_LABELS_FRESH_MS` = 10 s** (equal to `POLICY_FRESH_MS`, a test holds it) on both clocks. Older, the request
  is held for **one** fresh read, at most **`PARTNER_LABELS_WAIT_MS` = 3 s**, then sent with what is fresh by then, or
  with none (a request cancelled, expired or whose window closed while it waits is sent nothing). A failed, late or
  empty read, a missing field, a refused document, more than 32 KiB of text for the window: no labels, the plain
  window, never an error and never a blocked request. When the last answer had no documents, no read is made for the
  window (a label going live mid-session shows from the vault's next read; only the safe direction waits).
  Auto-approved requests never read for labels.
- **How long a label keeps showing after a staff Block or switch-off** (corrected after the review): a NEW window shows
  it for at most 10 s after the switch (the vault never sends stale texts; the 3 s wait only delays a window, it never
  adds age); a window ALREADY showing it keeps it until the user decides or the request's `APPROVAL_TTL_MS` (5 min)
  runs out, about 5 min 10 s in the worst case.
- **Cost** (recorded after the review): an app with labels and no policy pays one `GET /v1/app` round trip per approval
  window after 10 s idle (up to 3 s when the API is slow; a partner-opened window's 8 s adopt timeout bounds it).
  Accepted for now; piece 5 may revisit.
- **What the window gets.** `hana:approve-request` gains `partnerLabels`: 1 to 16 non-empty texts, at most 32 KiB
  together, present only when there are fresh documents for the request, so every other request is the message older
  pages take; its message cap is the approval cap plus 33 KiB, so a request the window takes without labels it also
  takes with them (and the vault sends it without them should the validator ever refuse). The window trusts the vault
  for this exactly as for the app's name, its test-app flag and the auto-approve note: it can't check freshness or the
  hash and doesn't pretend to. What it can check it checks again: it parses each text with its own parser and text
  rules, keeps only the build's network, and drops two documents for one contract (`windowLabelDocuments`).
- **Matching: what the request is, first** (after the review). The window runs `labelRequestOf` and `matchLabel` on its
  own decode. Each matcher first decides whether the request is one the document speaks about; only then its code hash;
  only then its shape. A structural failure on a request the document doesn't speak about is `not_described`.
  - A **payment document** (classic) speaks about every classic transaction that moves the user's value to another
    account: a payment, either path payment, an account creation, an account merge, a claimable balance (each
    claimant), each from the user's account (the operation's source, else the transaction's), anywhere in the
    transaction. If any of them goes to an account outside the address book: `not_in_address_book` (the red line),
    before anything else. If none moves value to anyone else (a trust line, an offer, a swap back to the user, value from
    another account): not described. Otherwise it must be exactly the one payment described: two operations
    (`more_than_one_action`), another operation (`operation_mismatch`), the asset, amount, fee and memo constraints, a
    displayable memo; and the transaction's and operation's sources the user's (`source_not_user`, not described: the
    user's value moved to an unlisted account was already red). Muxed accounts are their base account (an M… form of a
    listed account is listed; the user's M… form is the user); the destination is kept as the request has it.
  - A **Soroban document** speaks only about a request that calls its contract at the top level (a router whose
    nested authorization reaches it is not); a **NEAR document** only about a call to its account.
  - A **fee bump** is not described yet (`fee_bump`): its fee is another envelope's.
  - Facts: `user` the vault's address; `networkChecked` only where the vault checked the NEAR network itself (D726,
    D729: a transaction on the env's network or a test app's delegate action); `reviewedNear` the build's
    `HanaEnv.nearReviewed`; **no code hash** (reading it is piece 5). So NEAR and Soroban documents produce nothing at
    all in the window yet (every request to their contract is `couldnt_check`, whatever its shape, tested); classic
    payments need no code hash and render fully. The rendering is chain-agnostic: piece 5 only fills
    `ApprovalRenderContext.labelFacts.codeHash` (tests inject it).
- **Outcomes** (`labelOutcome`; a warning wins over a match): a match, the partner's box; `not_in_address_book` at a
  classic destination, the red line; any other `described_mismatch`, the amber line; `not_described` and
  `couldnt_check`, nothing at all (byte for byte the window without labels, tested by comparing rendered HTML with and
  without the documents, and in the browser before and after the label's removal). Anything thrown while reading labels
  is no label (the plain window), with a console warning that holds no text. The partner's words never appear for a
  request that doesn't match.
- **The box.** `div.partner-label`, a group named for screen readers ("What {App} says"), its own bordered box in the
  normal text colour (no green, blue, check mark, icon or alert role): "**{App}** says: {sentence}", then "These are
  **{App}**’s words. Journear hasn’t checked them." (core's `partnerAttribution`, word for word), then a row per field
  the sentence doesn't already show (the partner's row label, the request's own value; at most 3, the parser's
  `LABEL_LIMITS.rows`). No partner "To" row (Journear's own "To" row is the destination; the address book's name is not
  shown for a classic payment). In the sentence Journear's verb and joining words are plain text; the partner's object
  phrase and every value are set apart, each in its own outlined span with its direction isolated (D885's box decision);
  ids and amounts in mono; an account whole (`fullId`, D876). Values as D892 item 6 says: an enumeration's label; "your
  account" only for the user; an address book name only for an exact entry; a token amount as the app's description
  ("25,000,000 units, which Coffee Club says are 2.5 USDC"); dates, durations and counts as Journear writes them.
- **Placement** (after the review). One place for every request, built by one function: Journear's headline, red box
  and the rows it names, the amount, Journear's lines and facts, the amber box, the request's own facts (a memo row, a
  message), the page's notes (the test-app note, the mainnet demo's banner, the out-of-policy line), **then the
  partner's box**, then only the folded details. Every element Journear rendered before keeps its text, order and style;
  no alert of any source comes after the box. The red not-listed item and the amber mismatch item are appended last to
  their colour's items (rank 5), so a box's lead never changes when another warning is there. Why not "the headline
  becomes '{App} says: …'" (D892 recommendation 3, proposal 4.1): with a red box the partner's line would sit above it
  (D809), Journear's amount and recipient would move down, and up to 8 partner rows before the amber box would push it
  down (D886's rule for partner-sized content). At 390 px the box now adds about 95 px for a one-line sentence with no
  rows (it was ~255–300 px with the rows the review removed).

#### Every new sentence (exact)
- The box: "{App} says: " followed by the sentence's parts; "These are {App}’s words. Journear hasn’t checked them."
  (the Tech Lead's alternative, listed by the review: "These are {App}’s words, not Journear’s."); its name for screen
  readers "What {App} says".
- Amber, a described request that doesn't match (`LABEL_MISMATCH`, reworded after the review): "{App} describes this
  kind of request, but this one doesn’t match, so Journear isn’t showing {App}’s description. If you’re not sure what
  this does, reject it."; as a bullet beside another amber line: "Doesn’t match how {App} describes this kind of
  request".
- Red, value from the user's account to an account not in the app's address book (`LABEL_NOT_LISTED`): "This isn’t one
  of the accounts {App} has listed for payments. If you expected to pay {App}, don’t approve."; as a bullet: "Not one of
  the accounts {App} has listed for payments".
- With no app name to show (none today, D686): "The app says: …", and "the app" inside the lines (D884's rule).
- All pass the plain-words check (D853, `@hana-id/brand/plain-words`, a test over the module's sentences and every
  rendered window above the fold). No sentence says a request is safe or checked.

#### What the red line covers, and what it doesn't
- Covered (a payment document in force): a payment, a strict-send or strict-receive path payment, an account creation,
  a merge of the user's account, a claimable balance (any claimant), from the user's account (G… or its M… form) to an
  account outside the address book (G… or M… of an unlisted base account), alone or anywhere in a transaction of
  several operations.
- Not covered: a Soroban token transfer (`transfer` on a token contract: a Soroban document's own contract only, and
  only after piece 5); value that leaves through an offer (`manageSellOffer`, `manageBuyOffer`: no destination); a
  trust-line-plus-clawback pattern or any value moved by another account's operation; a liquidity pool deposit; a
  `setOptions` signer or weight change (an account takeover, not a value move); a fee bump (not described yet); a NEAR
  transfer. Those show Journear's own window and warnings as before (tested byte for byte: an offer, a pool deposit, a
  signer change and a Soroban token transfer under a payment document).
- **A listed account others share** (after PR 123's second review): an exchange's or an anchor's deposit address, where
  the memo or the muxed id picks who is credited, lets a hijacked page get the app's box on a payment that credits the
  attacker: memo `99999` to a listed till matches ("{App} says: pay for order 99999"), and so does the till's M… form
  with id 99. Journear's own Memo and To rows still show those values, and the partner box never shows the address.
  Guidance for piece 4, shown where a partner adds an address-book entry: "List only accounts that only you control,
  never a shared deposit address." The alternative for the Tech Lead, beside the muxed item below: refuse to match a
  muxed destination at all (the plain window).

#### The security argument
- **A hostile partner with a label in force** (its owner's Google account, after the notice, the 24 h wait and the
  staff feed) **can** make the window show, for a request that is exactly the call its document describes: one verb from
  Journear's list, one object phrase of at most 30 characters, its enumeration labels and up to 3 row labels, all
  passing piece 1's text rules (row labels also refuse Journear's row names and amount, account, fee and network
  words), always under "{App} says:" and "These are {App}’s words. Journear hasn’t checked them.", in a plain box below
  everything Journear says. **It cannot**: speak in Journear's voice; put words above or among Journear's lines, facts
  or warnings of any source; remove, lower, reorder or reword a warning; change or contradict an amount, a recipient or
  the fee (they are the request's, decoded by the window itself; no partner row repeats the destination; an id value
  that reads as an amount, a token, a claim or Journear's words is not shown, and the request gets the amber line);
  show anything for a request that doesn't match; describe away a payment to an account it hasn't listed by any of the
  five operation types above (the red line; the not-covered list is above); use a soft verb on something that moves value; describe a contract
  Journear reads itself, or a standard token method; reach another org's users.
- **A compromised API or D1** can serve any document with a matching sha256 (it writes both), skip the wait, the notice
  and the veto, and serve two entries for one contract. It cannot get past the vault's parser and text rules, which run
  again in the window: what it can show is bounded exactly as a hostile partner's is (the re-hash only catches
  corruption). Two documents for one contract are dropped by the vault and by the window. It cannot keep a label in a
  new window more than 10 s after it stops serving it (a window already open keeps it, up to the request's 5 min), and
  it cannot block or fail an approval through labels (every failure is the plain window). It cannot change what is
  signed: the approval digest covers the request only, never the labels. It can make the red line appear on a
  legitimate payment by serving a document whose address book lacks the account (a denial in Journear's voice, the same
  as a hostile partner's own document).
- **A hijacked partner page** can't change labels and can't make the vault read another app's; its forged requests
  match nothing (plain), mismatch (amber) or send the user's value to an unlisted account by one of the five operation
  types (red), which makes the tampering more visible. Remaining routes it has around the red line are the "not covered" list
  above.
- **A malicious staff member** can only block or switch labels off (D894): users then see the plain window.
- **The phishing attempts tested** (`packages/web/test/auth/render-labels.test.ts`, `approve-page-labels.test.ts`, in the
  real window code): bidi overrides and isolates, a zero-width space, Cyrillic and Greek look-alikes, full-width
  letters, Journear's name plain and as "J0urnear", "Passport", "verified", "safe", "free", "press Approve", a fake
  "Warning" row, rows named "Total", "To", "Network", "Memo", "Amount", "Sends", "From", "red alert", "25 XLM", "USDC
  refund", long numbers, amounts in words, an account written as text, "your account", a link word, quotation marks,
  markup, a line break, "nothing", a check mark, an emoji, an overlong phrase: each refused at delivery, so the window
  is byte for byte plain. Request ids that read as Journear's words or amounts ("Journear-checked", "1XLM", "USDC-25",
  "Free", "Verified-9", "approve-1") and a memo with a hidden direction mark: the amber line, the value not shown. A
  phrase the rules let through ("the danger zone order") stays inside the attributed box with no alert style. Long
  values wrap inside the box at 390 px with no sideways scrolling, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- **Residual**: an order number or item id is still the request's own text (plain ASCII, none of the refused words:
  Journear's names, claim and lure words such as paid, bonus, gift, reward, airdrop, claim, done, success, scam, free and
  their plurals, shorthand amounts such as 1M or 10k, and a 2 to 6 capital run glued to digits or to 1 to 3 digits by a
  hyphen, such as 1SOL or SOL-1; ordinary ids such as A1B2C3, INV-2026-0042 and Hanami-12 pass), in mono under the app's
  attribution; a word filter is a first filter (D892 item 16); an app's name can change at once (below); the routes
  around the red line listed above; a listed account others share (above); a matching payment whose fee is far above
  normal still gets the box when the document sets no `feeAtMost` (Journear's own fee row shows it).
- **Row names** (after the second review): a field label can't be any of the window's own row names (a test reads them
  from `render-approval.ts`, so a row added there later fails until the rules refuse it) nor the generic money and
  identity words (asset, source, through, offer, buy, sell, for, limit, name, code, call, sequence, destination,
  address, beneficiary, spend, currency, worth, due, …). The partner's box is built inside its own guard: anything that
  throws while building it is the plain window.

#### After PR 123's review (2026-11-23): what changed, each decided while reviewing, **to confirm**
1. The box comes after every alert of any source (the out-of-policy line and the demo banner are page notes), built by
   one function; tested with every alert source and through the real page.
2. **Red for every value-moving classic operation** to an account outside a payment document's address book (the list
   above), anywhere in the transaction. Piece 4's console preview must warn a partner that declaring a payment format
   turns every payment, and every value-moving operation, to an account it hasn't listed red (recorded for piece 4,
   here and in D894's "For piece 3").
3. What the request is comes first; a structural failure on a request a document doesn't speak about is
   `not_described` (the false amber cases: two non-payment operations, a router swap, a Soroban document on a classic
   transaction). NEAR and Soroban documents produce nothing until piece 5.
4. Row labels may not be Journear's row names or amount, account, fee and network words (`text_row_word`, a tightening
   of piece 1's rules, nothing deployed); request ids that read as Journear's words, claims, tokens or amounts are
   `value_not_displayable` (amber); no partner "To" row; **a row the sentence already shows is dropped** ("1042" showed
   three times).
5. Fee bumps not described (plain window) for now.
6. **Muxed accounts are their base account** for matching; the destination is never swapped for the book's G… (the
   commit review), and the box shows nothing of it.
7. The time a label keeps showing after a switch-off, corrected (above).
8. Any throw while reading labels is no label, never "can't be shown".
9. The box is a named group; at most 3 rows (`LABEL_LIMITS.rows`, a tightening of piece 1); Journear's facts (the memo
   row) and notes are above it.
10. The amber line's wording (above); the attribution kept, its alternative listed.
11. Tests: the explicit wait for the vault's read in the e2e (`/__e2e/app-reads`), the queue's hold when cancelled,
    expired or its window closed (`approvals-labels.test.ts`), items 1, 3, 5, 6 and path payments.
12. The cost of the fresh read (above).
- The commit review's two findings: (1) the payment's source check, restored, comparing base accounts; another source's
  payment is `source_not_user`, now classified not described (the plain window), unless it sends the user's value to an
  unlisted account (red); (2) the muxed destination kept as the request has it (above).

#### The `app.renamed` question (D894's requirement for piece 3): recommendation, not built
- An app's name can change at once (`app.renamed`), outside the 24 h wait, after staff saw the preview under the old
  name. **Recommendation: flag it, don't hold it.** When an app with labels in force or waiting is renamed, record a
  security event (say `label_app_renamed`, with the old and new names, no document text) that the staff feed shows
  next to the entry ("Renamed while its labels were live: {old} → {new}") and the org's security contacts get with the

### D898. Cancelling a waiting sign-in from Passport Home: option A built (Home opens the app to cancel it); cancelling inside Home waits for the Tech Lead
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: **option A built** (the coordinator, 2026-11-23: "Build OPTION A now"), its details
  **decided while building, to confirm**; options B and B+email **for the Tech Lead** (nothing of them built). Branch
  `feat/home-waiting-sign-in-actions` (from `next`), not merged, not deployed. Built: `packages/web/src/auth/home-sign-ins.ts`
  (`cancelTarget`, `isPlainHttpsOrigin`, `openToCancel`, `SIGN_IN_TEXT.cancelOpen*`), `css/home.css`; tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/home-sign-ins.test.ts` ("D898 option A …"), e2e `apps/e2e/tests/home-sign-ins.spec.ts` ("D898
  option A …", three browsers). No API, issuer, vault or contract change. Follows the Tech Lead's "Cancel/Remove inside Home: yes,
  later" (D888's open list, D895 and D897's "not in this step").
- **How it works today** (read from the code and D259, D864, D874, D875, D881, D887):
  1. A *waiting* sign-in is a pending member (`Standing::Pending`, `links.rs`): an explicit link (`linkAccount`) or an
     email joining a Google wallet (case B), pending for `change_delay_ms` (never before the unpause floor). The wait is
     the owner's chance to notice a link someone else made and stop it before it opens the wallet: the notice mail and
     every sign-in window of the account show it with Cancel (`docs/security.md`, "Accounts").
  2. The model has **one** action on a waiting sign-in: `cancel_link` (immediate; drops the pending member; bumps the
     epoch). The contract allows it to the pending identity itself, or to **any active identity of the account** (the
     root or an active member), each with a JWT whose nonce is `link_change` "cancel" over (signer, scope, root,
     member, epoch, salt). "Remove" is `unlink_identity`, for an *active* member only (root or the member itself): it
     does not apply to a waiting one. So in Home the action is **Cancel this link**, as in the window.
  3. The window: at every sign-in of the account the vault's last word lists each pending member with **Cancel this
     link** (D259; D887: small outlined button after "Don’t recognise it?"; D881: ends on its outcome, `done` "Link
     cancelled" or `stop` with the code). Cancel is a **fresh sign-in of this login's own method over the vault's
     `link_change` nonce** (Google with the vault's nonce and `login_hint`; email: a code over the commitment), checked
     by the vault, relayed by the vault through `POST /v1/link/cancel`. The waiting email's own sign-in can cancel its
     link too (D864).
  4. `POST /v1/link/cancel` (`apps/api/src/links.ts`) is **app-gated**: `x-hana-key` (an app's publishable key), the
     vault or auth origin acting for one of that app's allowed partner origins (`checkCaller`), the app's link-change
     limits; the token verified and a client of the app's scope; every contract rule prechecked; relayed through the
     session pool; then every vault share of the account in the scope revoked and the directory synced.
  5. Home today (`home-sign-ins.ts`): the waiting row with its amber box, "Don’t recognise it? Sign in to this app the
     way you signed in here, and choose “Cancel this link”. If you’re not sure, cancel it." (`cancel_at_sign_in`), and
     since D897 the line "1 more starts opening it soon. Check it below.". Read-only: D874 recorded why (no app key or
     partner page for the relay; the issuer's Home route can't mint a `link_change` code).
- **What proves authority, and what Home holds**: the window's Cancel rests on a *fresh proof by an active identity of
  the account over a nonce that names this one change* (the contract checks it; nothing weaker can reach
  `cancel_link`). Home holds a 15-minute Home identity: a token whose nonce commits to Home's own key (`home` purpose,
  audience the shared client, the exit client or `hana-home`), which the contract never accepts for a link change
  (`homeGate` answers `{provider, sub}` only; exit-client tokens "never a link or an owner action", D468). So Home must
  get the **same fresh `link_change` proof** the window gets; its session alone is weaker and is not enough.
- **What doing it inside Home would take** (none of it exists):
  1. *A relay route Home can call*: `/v1/link/cancel` needs an app key and a partner origin; Home has neither and must
     not borrow a partner's (it would act in a partner's name and bill its quota). So a new **`POST
     /v1/home/link/cancel`**: `homeGate` (origin, per-IP limit, Home token and signature), body `{proofJwt, memberKey,
     epoch, salt, scopeId}`; the proof verified with no app (`verifyLoginToken`) and its audience a client of that scope;
     **stricter than the contract**: the proof's identity must be the Home identity itself (same provider and `sub`) and
     **active** in the account (never the pending one, never another pending), and `memberKey` must be **pending** in
     that account (an active member or the root is refused: removing an established sign-in stays out of scope); the
     same precheck, relay, share revocation and directory sync as `/v1/link/cancel`; Home's own limits and usage (no
     partner billed). Tests for every refusal.
  2. *A Google proof*: a Google sign-in with `nonce = link_change` "cancel", `prompt=select_account` (Home never learns
     the address, so no `login_hint`), through a new mode of the child window and `/home/callback`. The contract takes it
     only from a client of the scope: Journear's **shared client** in a scope that allows it. A scope on the **partner's
     own Google client** ("Needs the app") can't get such a token from Journear's pages at all, and the **exit client**
     can't make link changes. So Google cancels from Home would work only for wallets on the shared client.
  3. *An email proof*: the issuer's `POST /v1/email/home/start` mints only `home` and `home_session`; `start` (which has
     `link_change`) is app-gated. A new Home kind `link-change` (a code to the signed-in address, a `link_change` token
     for `email:{scope}` while the scope holds its email client) is an **issuer change** with its own limits and review.
- **Options**:
  - **A. Guidance only, no server change** (small, web only; **built**, below): the waiting row keeps its words and gains, under "Don’t
    recognise it?", a small outlined **Open {App} to cancel it** that opens the app's first web address in a new tab
    (where the sign-in window offers Cancel), and the steps in a sentence. No new authority, no new route, nothing to
    review beyond a link. It doesn't make cancelling one press from Home.
  - **B. Cancel inside Home, Google on the shared client first** (**for the Tech Lead**): items 1 and 2 above (a new API route, a new child mode),
    Home's confirmation, result and failure screens in D881's words (below). Authority equal to the window's plus Home's
    session and the "same identity, active, member pending" checks (stricter). Covers wallets on the shared Google
    client; others keep today's pointer, and the row says which applies. Its own security review.
  - **B+email** (**for the Tech Lead**): B plus the issuer's `link-change` kind (item 3), so an email owner can cancel from Home too. A second
    service changes; larger review.
  - **C. Both A and B**: A everywhere B can't reach.
- **Recommendation**: **C, built in two changes**: A now (it helps every wallet today, with nothing new to trust), then B
  as its own server change with its security review; email (item 3) after B proves out. Reason: the waiting period
  exists for exactly this, and Home is where the notice mail sends people, but B is a new server check and only reaches
  shared-client wallets, so it should be decided and reviewed on its own.
- **Option A as built**: on a waiting sign-in's amber box ("Don’t recognise it?" row, `cancel_at_sign_in`: the viewer is
  an active sign-in of the wallet), where Journear's record of the wallet's apps has one to open:
  1. **Which address**: the first app in the listing's order that is active (not paused, not closed) and has a web
     address on record that is a plain `https://host[:port]` exactly as the browser writes an origin (no user name or
     password, no path, query or fragment, at most 512 characters); its first such address. Only Journear's record
     (`GET /v1/home/apps`), never anything of the waiting sign-in. Anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, `data:`,
     `https://a@b`, a path) gives no link, and the box keeps today's sentence.
  2. **The box**: "Don’t recognise it? If you’re not sure, cancel it."; a small outlined link **Open {App} to cancel it**
     (its name adds "(opens in a new tab)"; an external-link icon; D887's look) that opens the address in a new tab
     (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the address unchanged: the new tab has no opener and no referrer);
     "Opens {address} in a new tab." (the link's description; the address as text, wrapping at its own break points);
     "There, sign in the way you signed in here, and choose “Cancel this link”."; for a wallet of several apps,
     "Cancelling it there stops it for every app that uses this wallet.". The amber box, the summary line ("1 more
     starts opening it soon. Check it below.") and the section's "sign out of it first" line stay.
  3. **Without a link** (no active app with such an address): the box says what it said before, "Don’t recognise it?
     Sign in to this app the way you signed in here, and choose “Cancel this link”. If you’re not sure, cancel it."
  4. Nothing else in the section changes; the click guards and the phone's chip are untouched.
- **Words, if B is built** (D881's family, for Home): the row's action, after "Don’t recognise it?", a small outlined
  **Cancel this link** (named "Cancel this link for the {email address | Google account}"); the confirmation "Cancel
  this link? The {email address | Google account} will never open this wallet. You can't undo this: it can only be
  added again, and then it waits again." with **Cancel the link** / **Go back**, then the sign-in ("Sign in with Google
  to confirm it’s you"); the result "Link cancelled. The {…} won’t open this wallet."; failures as D881's: "Nothing
  changed" (not this sign-in, the sign-ins changed, refused before anything was sent), "It may not have been cancelled"
  (can't tell: "Show again" to check), each with **Close**; the line and the row update without a reload.
- Not changed by any option: the delay, what a waiting sign-in can do, derivation paths or keys. **Address impact: none.**
- **To confirm**: for A, (1) the sentences above; (2) the first active app with a plain https address (a paused or closed
  app is skipped; an app that is first in the listing but has no address gives way to the next); (3) the address as
  text under the link; (4) no link for `http:` addresses (the local stack's own apps show today's sentence). **For the
  Tech Lead**: B or B+email; for B, the words above, the "same identity as Home's" rule (stricter than the window, where
  any active method of the login may prove), and Google-only at first.

### D899. Partner labels piece 4: the console's Request labels tab, a form (never JSON by hand) with core's own problems, the approval window's own preview, and the review before D894's fresh sign-in
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: built on `feat/partner-labels-console` (from `next` @ 4aa20190, `next` @ 060727c5 merged
  in), not merged, not deployed; within D892's adopted recommendations, D894's guarded path and D896's requirements for
