  tab), `apps/console/web/src/labels/` (`Editor.tsx`, `Preview.tsx`, `model.ts`, `problems.ts`, `examples.ts`,
  `units.ts`, `Diff.tsx`), `window/` (`frame.ts`, `window.css`: the popup's stylesheet in a shadow root), `pages/Action.tsx` (the review of `labels.set` and `labels.remove`),
  `pages/Consent.tsx` (now a lazy wrapper of `ConsentView.tsx`), `App.tsx` (the tab's lazy chunk), `pages/Apps.tsx`
  (the tab); `apps/console/src/writes.ts` (`GET …/scopes/:scope/labels`; the cancel route takes an `lc_` id),
  `actions.ts` (the review's `decoded`; returning to the tab), `audit.ts` (`change.cancelled` may carry `changeId`),
  `env.ts`; **API (read-only additions)** `apps/api/src/labels/propose.ts` (`listLabels`, `previewLabels`),
  `store.ts` (`labelView`'s partner note, `REVIEW_ON`, the plan's `review_required`), `rpc/console.ts`;
  `packages/console-core/src/labels.ts` (`LabelListAnswer`, `LabelPreviewAnswer`, `LABEL_RECENT_MS`,
  `LABEL_RECENT_PER_ENTRY`, `LabelEntryView.removedAt` / `recent`, `LabelChangeView.text`); core's dormancy test (the
  console is the fourth importer); `apps/e2e` (the console in each browser lane: `src/server/lane-console.ts`, ports
  base+37–39 and +42–44, `src/build.ts` builds the SPA, `tests/partner-labels-console.spec.ts`).

#### No new authority; the API and console-core changes (read-only)
- Proposing, removing and cancelling are D894's ConsoleRpc paths unchanged: `labels.set` / `labels.remove` with an
  on-chain owner's fresh Google step-up bound to exactly the document, the apps and the scope's labels version; an
  owner's immediate cancel of a waiting `lc_` change (D894 had the RPC; the console's cancel route took only `gc_`).
- `ConsoleRpc.listLabels` now also answers: each listed version's `text` (the version in force and the waiting one: the
  editor starts from it and "what users see now" is built from it); `recent`, the versions that ended in the last 14
  days (`LABEL_RECENT_MS`), newest first, at most 5 per entry (`LABEL_RECENT_PER_ENTRY`), without text, a blocked one
  with Journear's `blockNote`; entries removed in the last 14 days (`removedAt`); `enabled` (`PARTNER_LABELS` is on
  here); `orgOff` (Journear's switch over the org's or every partner's labels); `reviewRequired`. Still two statements.
  Why the note: the task asks for "blocked with Journear's note", and the blocked mail already sends it to the org's
  security contacts; the console now also shows it to the org's viewers (to confirm).
- `ConsoleRpc.previewLabels` now also answers `diff` (D894's `diffOf` against the version in force, every line `added`
  for a new entry) and `reviewRequired`, so the confirmation page is the review.

#### The design
- **Where.** An app tab, **Request labels**, between Signing and Branding: the entries of the app's scope (labels are a
  scope's, attached to named apps), reachable from every app of the scope. The editor is `…/labels/new` and
  `…/labels/:labelId`. A lazy chunk (the decoder, the Stellar SDK and the window's renderer), and the consent preview is
  lazy too, so the console's first page shrank (326 KB, from 339 KB; sizes after PR 126's review below).
- **The list.** Each entry: what it describes ("Payments to your Stellar accounts", "NEAR program {account}", "Soroban
  contract {id}"), its apps, badges (Live; In force + Not shown to users yet for NEAR and Soroban; Switched off by
  Journear; Removed; the waiting state), "What users see now" (core's `previewLabelDocument` lines, as the API's preview
  and the staff feed), "Waiting to go live" with its time and **Cancel this change**, "Earlier changes" (blocked with
  the note, cancelled, lapsed, replaced, ended with a blocked successor, removed), **Change these labels** (only with no
  change waiting and the entry not switched off) and **Remove these labels** (a fresh sign-in). Times on the server's
  clock (D701), one re-read when a waiting change's time comes.
- **The editor.** A form per kind: classic Stellar payments (shown to users today), a NEAR program and a Soroban
  contract (each marked "Not shown to users yet"; D896: no code hash until piece 5). Apps; your accounts (the address
  book); lists of values (NEAR, Soroban); per request the verb (Journear's list; a verb the parser refuses for that
  request, a "nothing moves" verb on one that can move value, is offered disabled with why, found by asking the parser,
  not by a second rule), the phrase, the conditions (a payment's memo, assets, highest amount and fee in XLM; a NEAR
  call's attached NEAR exactly or at most, most gas in TGas, who sends it; a Soroban call's fee and who sends it), the
  arguments and their limits, the values shown, and the sentence built from parts with Earlier / Later / Take out
  buttons. The draft (`model.ts`) writes the document on the scope's network (never a choice: the API refuses another);
  **Advanced** shows that text and takes edits; the form reads it back when it can, else says "The form can’t show this
  text" with why, and keeps the text as typed (that exact text is what is proposed). A read-back is checked by writing
  the text again: anything the form would drop makes it not representable, so nothing is silently lost.
- **Problems.** Every problem is core's `parseLabelDocument` and text rules, run in the browser on every keystroke,
  placed beside the control that writes its path (`problems.ts`; a path no control writes goes to "Fix these first"),
  with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and a polite status line ("2 problems to fix." / "No problems: ready to
  review."). The form's own checks are only what JSON objects can't hold twice (two requests, lists, values or NEAR
  arguments of one name). Review is off while any problem remains.
- **The preview.** For a payment: the approval window's own `renderApproval` (packages/web, imported as the consent
  preview is, D352) over example payments built with the Stellar SDK and read by `decodeApprovalRequest`, with the
  document as the window's labels: **A payment that matches** (to the first listed G… account, an allowed asset, within
  the limits, the memo it asks for), **A payment that doesn't match** (only the memo changed: the amber line), **A
  payment to an account not in your list** (only the payee changed: the red line); Light / Dark (the design system's
  `.jp-light` / `.jp-dark`); at most 390 px wide; drawn inside a shadow root with the popup's own stylesheets attached
  there only (after PR 126's review, below), with Journear's example mark first in the frame. For NEAR and Soroban: "Not shown to users yet" and core's preview lines.
- **The warnings, where they apply.** On the accounts: "List only accounts that only you control, never a shared
  deposit address." (D896) and, for payments, the muxed note; on a payment format: the red-line warning naming the five
  operation types; on the fee: the suggestion with "Use 0.01 XLM".
- **Proposing.** **Review the change** builds the `labels.set` action (the API's checks run there: a refusal is shown
  before any Google step); its page is the review: the apps, "What changes for users" (Added / Changed / Removed against
  what users see now, the before struck through), "What users would see (example values)", and when it goes live (the
  true sentence when Journear reviews); then D894's fresh sign-in. The outcome page says it was proposed and how it goes
  live. Refusals in plain words: not switched on here, switched off by Journear (the API's own sentence), a change
  already waiting and the limits (the API's sentences), a version conflict (with Reload; the form keeps what was
  typed), the parser's problems as a list; after Google, a version conflict and "not switched on" have their own lines.
- **Not switched on here.** The tab says so and the editor still works (the preview is the browser's); Review isn't
  offered and the line says why. This follows the API: `previewLabels` and `proposeLabels` refuse `env_mismatch` while
  `PARTNER_LABELS` is off; `listLabels` answers.
- **Partner text is text.** React text nodes in the console; the window's DOM helpers use text nodes only. Tested with
  markup in a staff note, a diff line and an API refusal.

### D900. Partner labels piece 5: NEAR and Soroban labels show only for code Journear tied to the label (NEAR: both of the vault's own providers agree on the code hash at a final block; Soroban: the transaction's own footprint, enforced by the network), with no new trust
- Date 2026-11-23 · Status: the design written before building (this entry), then built on `feat/partner-labels-contracts`
  (from `next` @ 590db716), not merged, not deployed; within D892's adopted recommendations (5: labels bind to the
  contract's code; a mismatch hides the label and never blocks approval) and D896's requirements for piece 5; every
  choice and sentence below decided while designing or building, **to confirm** (the list at the end). No checked-in
  manifest turns `partnerLabels.enabled` on. **Address impact: none** (nothing signed, decoded, derived or digested
  changes: the approval digest covers the request only, as before).
- **Trust: nothing new.** No API change, no new provider, no simulation service, no paid dependency. NEAR: the vault reads
  the code hash from the two NEAR providers it already reads and already requires to agree for a test app's delegate
  action (the manifest's `rpc` and `rpcFallback`, D263, D729), and only decides whether the partner's box may show.
  (After PR 128's review: "two providers" protects only when the two endpoints are independently operated; sandbox-dev's
  are one operator today. **Settled by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24 (D903):** one operator is accepted on testnet, so it is
  no longer a blocker for switching labels on in a testnet env; a production network must name two different
  operators in its manifest, checked by the schema and `deploy-check` once the schema admits another network.)
  Soroban: no read at all; the code comes from the transaction the user signs, and the network refuses to run it on
  other code. The partner console gains one read-only route on its existing NEAR endpoint (a convenience the partner
  confirms; nothing trusts it).

#### Q1. Who reads the code hash, from where, and what happens when it can't
- **NEAR: the vault**, as it reads the other chain facts the window relies on (D726's block check, D729's delegate
  check). Not the window: it would need its own RPC reads and its own two-provider rule after the request is already on
  screen, and it already trusts the vault for the labels' texts, the app's name and the network check. Not the API: a
  compromised API would then decide which code a label is tied to (today it can only serve documents the vault and the
  window re-parse).
- **What is read:** `view_account` at **final** finality (as the delegate check's `view_access_key`), from **each** of
  the env's two providers on its own (no fallback from one to the other: `NearView.reads(…, independent)`), only for a
  request whose receiver is the account of a fresh label document of the app (no read for any other request, so an app
  without NEAR labels costs nothing). In a `local*` env with one provider, that one (as `requireIndependentNear`);
  anywhere else with one provider, no read (no code hash).
- **The agreement rule** (`agreedCodeHash`, pure): every provider asked answered; each answer has a `code_hash` that is
  canonical base58 of 32 bytes; none names a global contract (`global_contract_hash` or `global_contract_account_id`
  present and not null: code shared by another account can change without this account's own action; verified after
  PR 128's review: nearcore's `AccountView` reports such an account's `code_hash` as the all-1s default, which the
  matcher refuses anyway, and a provider that omits the global fields gives that all-1s hash, `no_contract_code`, now
  couldn't check, the plain window); all the hashes equal. Anything else (a provider down,
  late, answering an error, an unknown account, two different hashes, a global contract, a malformed answer) is **no
  code hash**: the matcher's `no_code_hash`, `couldnt_check`, the plain window, silently, exactly as without labels.
  Never an error, never a blocked approval.
- **Latency bound:** the read runs inside the one wait piece 3 already has (`PARTNER_LABELS_WAIT_MS` = 3 s), in parallel
  with the labels' own fresh read when that is due too; each provider's read has the same 3 s timeout. So a request to a
  labelled NEAR contract waits **at most 3 s once**, and only when no fresh answer is kept; after the wait it goes with
  what is known then (a read still running means no code hash: plain).
- **Caching** (`NEAR_CODE_FRESH_MS` = 10 s, equal to `PARTNER_LABELS_FRESH_MS`, a test holds them equal): the outcome
  for an account (the agreed hash, or "couldn't check") is kept in the vault frame's memory for 10 s on both clocks (as
  labels); an older one is read again. A failed read is kept too, so a broken provider costs each request at most one
  wait per 10 s, never more.
- **Staleness:** a contract upgraded at block B: final finality trails the head by about two blocks (a second or two on
  testnet); so a **new** window can still show the old label for at most about 10 s + that lag after the upgrade lands
  (the same 10 s as a staff switch-off, D896), and a window **already open** keeps it until the user decides or the
  request's 5 minutes run out (as D896's switch-off). After that, the hash differs: `code_hash_mismatch`, the amber line
  (D896's to-confirm 7, as specified).
- **Soroban: nobody reads it; the transaction carries it.** A Soroban transaction lists every ledger entry it may read
  or write (its footprint, in `sorobanData`), and the network runs it only within that list: the host's storage refuses
  any key not declared (`soroban-env-host` `storage.rs`: in enforcing mode every `get` and `has` checks the footprint
  first, `Storage/ExceededLimit` otherwise, read 2026-11-23), and to call a Wasm contract the host reads the contract's
  instance, takes the Wasm hash from it and asks storage for that `ContractCode` entry before it runs the code, cached
  module or not (`host/frame.rs` `instantiate_vm`, read 2026-11-23). So when the footprint declares **exactly one**
  `ContractCode` entry, of hash H, any Wasm the transaction runs is H, the labelled contract included, or the
  transaction fails. The window takes that H as the code hash (`sorobanFootprintCode`): none or several distinct is no
  code hash (`couldnt_check`, plain); one other than the document's is `code_hash_mismatch` (amber). This is stronger
  than a read: it is enforced when the transaction runs, so an upgrade after the user approved makes the transaction
  fail instead of running new code. Calls a partner's contract makes to Stellar's built-in token contracts need no
  `ContractCode` and still match; a call into another Wasm contract (a second `ContractCode`) does not (v1's "nothing
  nested", D892).
- **An authorization entry** (`stellar_auth`: the user authorises a call someone else sends) carries no footprint:
  nothing ties it to code, so it never matches (`no_code_hash`, the plain window). Recorded as not covered.

#### Q2. What a match requires (all of it, or nothing)
- **NEAR** (piece 1's matcher, unchanged but for the fact's source): the network the vault checked itself (D726,
  D729: so a live app's delegate action never matches); the receiver exactly the document's account, never the user's
  own, never a reviewed account; **the vault's agreed code hash for that account equal to the document's** (the window
  uses it only when its account is the request's receiver); exactly one action, a function call of a described method
  (a batch never matches); relayed or direct as declared; the deposit exactly or at most as declared (absent: exactly
  0); the gas at most as declared; the arguments strict JSON (D885's rules), every declared argument present unless
  optional, of its type and within its bounds, none undeclared; every field's value showable. The access-key context
  needs no rule of its own: the decoders already refuse a request from any account but the user's, signed with the
  user's own key.
- **Soroban** (piece 1's matcher, the code hash now the footprint's): a transaction (not a fee bump) that calls the
  contract at its top level; the footprint's one `ContractCode` equal to the document's Wasm hash; exactly one
  operation, an `invokeContract`; the transaction's and the operation's source the user's; **every authorization entry
  exactly this call with nothing under it** (so the user authorises no token transfer, no approval and no other call
  beyond the described one); a described function; its arguments in order, of their types, within their bounds, no
  more and no fewer; the fee within `feeAtMost`.
- Outcomes as D896: a match is the box; a described request that doesn't match (a code-hash mismatch included) is the
  amber line; `couldnt_check` (no code hash, a malformed one, an account with no code of its own, the NEAR network
  unchecked) and `not_described` are the plain window, byte for byte. Everything that decides whether the document
  speaks about the request (the account or contract, the source, a call of a described method or function) comes before
  the code (after PR 128's review).

#### Q3. Contracts their owner can upgrade
- Accepted for v1, as the format already says: a label pins one code hash, so an upgrade turns the partner's words off
  on its own. Users see the amber line ("… doesn’t match, so Journear isn’t showing …") until the partner's new labels,
  with the new hash, go live after the guarded wait (24 h in production). That is the safe direction (words never
  outlive the code they were written for) and the cost lands on the partner who upgraded. The vault does **not** read
  the account's access keys: a full-access key means "its owner can redeploy", which every partner contract has, and
  refusing such accounts would leave labels for nobody; the hash read at approval time is what limits it. (Journear's
  own reviewed entries still require a locked account, D885: they lower a warning; a partner label lowers nothing.)
- **The console says so** where a NEAR program or Soroban contract is described (sentences below), and suggests the
  order: propose the labels with the new code first, upgrade soon after they go live.
- **Recommended later, not built:** (a) a document may name two code hashes (the old and the new) to bridge an upgrade
  without an amber stretch; (b) the staff feed's "the code changed since this label was written" (it needs the admin
  Worker's own chain reads); (c) a daily mismatch count to the partner (D892 recommendation 10). None is needed for
  safety.

#### Q4. What value can move, and when a soft verb may be used
- **Journear's own facts already state the amounts**; this piece adds no Journear sentence. NEAR: the request's
  attached deposit is in Journear's rows ("NEAR leaving your account", "NEAR sent for you", D858, D884); the only
  amount a NEAR label may show itself is that deposit (`nativeAmount`, `binding: 'request'`, D892 item 6). Soroban: a
  match has no authorised token call beyond the call itself (above), and Journear's own lines for any token call stay as
  they are. No simulation is needed or run: NEAR has no dry run (the proposal's 6.2), and Soroban's bounds are the
  footprint and the authorization entries, decoded, enforced by the network.
- **The soft-verb rule, now at match time too** (a soft verb says no value moves; piece 1 checked only the document):
  NEAR, a soft verb matches only a request whose deposit is exactly 0 (the parser already requires the document to say
  so; the matcher checks the request again). Soroban, a soft verb matches only a transaction whose footprint lets it
  change **nothing but the labelled contract's own stored data** (every read-write entry a `contractData` of that
  contract: no account, trust line or other contract's data, so no balance in XLM, a classic asset or another
  contract's token can change). Otherwise `value_may_move`, a described mismatch: the amber line, never the soft words.
  An authorization entry has no footprint, so a soft verb never matches one (and it has no code hash anyway).
- **Soroban allowances (residual, after PR 128's review):** under a value verb, the labelled contract can spend a SEP-41
  allowance the user granted it earlier: `transfer_from` needs only the spender's authorization, and the contract
  calling the token directly is authorized implicitly, so no authorization entry of the user's shows it; the
  transaction's footprint then declares the user's balance read-write. Soft verbs are protected (the footprint may
  write only the contract's own data). What the user sees of such a write: Journear's red box for any unknown
  contract call ("Journear can’t check what this does. It could take your money or tokens. If you’re not sure, reject
  it."), above the partner's box; and, only in the folded details, under "Ledger entries it may change": "account G…"
  for XLM, a trust line as its raw XDR, or "contract data (persistent) of C…: {key}" for another contract's token. No
  line in the main view names the balance.
- What that does not cover (residual, the same as today without labels): what the user keeps **with the labelled
  contract itself** (NEAR: the amber "This acts as you" line stays on a relayed call; Soroban: the red "can't tell" line
  stays); NEAR NFT approvals the user gave that contract earlier.

#### Q5. Journear's reviewed NEAR calls (D885)
- Journear's reading wins, and the partner's box is never added under it: the parser refuses a document for a reviewed
  contract (`journear_reads_this`, compared by the record's sha256) and the matcher refuses the build's reviewed accounts
  (`LabelChainFacts.reviewedNear`, for envs the record doesn't hold). Recommended to keep: the reviewed reading is
  complete and in Journear's voice; a second description under it could only contradict it. The vault reads no code
  hash for a reviewed account (no document can describe it).

#### Q6. Threats
| Attacker | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| A hostile partner with a label in force | What D896 says, now for NEAR and Soroban calls too: its words in the box for exactly the described call to the code it pinned, under its name, after everything Journear says; a soft verb over a call that moves nothing Journear can see (deposit 0; a Soroban call that changes only its contract's own data) while its own code does what it does with what the user keeps there (the amber or red line stays) | Show its words for another contract, another code, a batch, a nested authorization, a deposit or a write outside its contract the document doesn't allow; remove or lower a warning; make the vault read a hash from anywhere but the env's two providers |
| A hijacked partner page | Send forged requests, as today; deploy nothing it doesn't already control | Make a request match a label unless it is exactly the described call to the pinned code; a forged Soroban footprint naming the right hash but running other code fails on the network |
| A compromised API or D1 | Serve any document (D896), so any account, hash and words within the text rules | Choose the code hash the vault reads (it comes from the two providers); show words for code other than what the document pins; block or fail an approval |
| One malicious or compromised NEAR provider | Make the code hash unreadable (a denial: the plain window); **if the env's two endpoints are run by one operator, everything the next row says** | Make a label match: both providers must answer the same hash, **but only when the two endpoints are independently operated. sandbox-dev's are not** (`rpc` test.rpc.fastnear.com and `rpcFallback` rpc.testnet.near.org, both run by FastNear; `independentEndpoints` compares URLs only). This weakens the existing two-provider checks (D263, D729) the same way. Settled 2026-11-24 (D903): accepted on testnet, where these checks rest on one operator; a production network must declare two different operators (`rpcOperator`, `rpcFallbackOperator`) |
| Both NEAR providers colluding (or one operator behind both, or one endpoint in a `local*` env) | Report the document's hash for an account running other code, so the box shows over a call the partner didn't describe | Change what is signed or shown by Journear: the request's own values, every warning and the amber acts-as-you line stay. The same trust a test app's delegate check already puts in them |
| A contract upgraded between the read and the signature (TOCTOU) | NEAR: the user's signature authorises the call to whatever code runs when it executes (a relayed action until its `maxBlockHeight`), as it does today without labels; labels change nothing signed. The old words could be on screen up to ~10 s + finality after the upgrade (new windows) or 5 min (an open window) | Soroban: run the call on other code: the footprint names the hash, so the transaction fails |
| A look-alike account name | Nothing: the document names one exact account (no folding), the matcher compares exactly, and the hash read is for the request's own receiver | Match `stamps.example.testnet.evil.testnet` to a label for `stamps.example.testnet` |
| A hostile partner whose Soroban contract holds the user's allowance (after PR 128's review) | Under a value verb, a call that spends a SEP-41 allowance the user granted the contract earlier (`transfer_from` needs only the spender's authorization; the contract is the direct invoker), the box beside Journear's red box; the balance write is only in the folded details | Do it under a soft verb (the footprint may write only the contract's own data) |
| A Stellar asset contract address labelled (after PR 128's review) | Nothing that changes anything: the code binding is empty for it (it runs built-in code, not a Wasm, so a footprint can declare any `ContractCode` and still run it), and every function of it that changes anything is reserved; what remains are its read-only functions | Label `trust`, `transfer`, `approve`, `mint` or any other of its state-changing functions |

  built and decoded as the window does.

#### After PR 128's review (2026-11-23): what changed, each decided while fixing, **to confirm**
The review found the Soroban footprint argument sound ("the only Wasm this transaction can run is H", checked against
soroban-env-host's footprint-enforced storage, `instantiate_vm` and Stellar's authorization docs) and the NEAR logic
sound, and asked for these:
1. **One operator behind both NEAR providers.** The two-provider guarantee holds only when the endpoints are run by
   different operators; sandbox-dev's are not (both FastNear). The threat table, security.md and
   `docs/go-live-after-freeze.md` (question 7) say so; it also weakens D263's and D729's checks. **A must-fix before
   any env turns labels on, and a Tech Lead decision:** (a) a second, independently operated testnet RPC provider
   (recommended); (b) a self-hosted node; (c) accept it for testnet with the wording softened. `envs/` is unchanged.
   **Decided 2026-11-24 (D903): (c) for testnet, enforced on production:** "for 2nd NEAR provider, can we just do 1 on
   testnet? but enforce this only on production." On testnet the checks rest on one operator, said plainly; a
   production manifest must name two different operators.
   The console now says "Journear checks the code on the NEAR network when a user approves." (true whatever the
   providers).
2. **Stellar asset contracts.** A Stellar asset contract runs built-in code with no `ContractCode`, so the footprint
   binding means nothing for such an address (any declared hash passes). It can't be told apart from the request
   robustly (its instance entry's key is every contract's; its address comes from an asset the request doesn't name),
   so it isn't refused by address. Instead every one of its functions that changes anything is reserved
   (`SAC_STATE_CHANGING`, checked against soroban-env-host `main` on 2026-11-23, protocol 26: init_asset, approve,
   transfer, transfer_from, burn, burn_from, clawback, set_authorized, mint, set_admin, and `trust`, CAP-73, which
   needs the address's authorization and creates a trust line); what remains are its read-only functions (allowance,
   balance, authorized, admin, decimals, name, symbol), which change nothing but its own time to live. A test
   enumerates the list. security.md's earlier "few non-token functions (all views)" was wrong about `trust`; corrected.
3. **Allowances** (above: the threat row and the residual).
4. **What the request is, before its code.** `matchSoroban` now checks the source (the transaction's and every call
   here) and that a described function is called before the footprint's code; `matchNear` checks that a described
   method is called before the code. So a request from another source, or of an undescribed function or method, is the
   plain window with either code (it gave amber with another code). Tested in core and in the window, byte for byte.
5. **No-code hashes.** The parser refuses the all-1s NEAR hash ("This is the code hash of an account with no program
   (all 1s): use the code hash of the program you deployed.") and the all-zero Wasm hash ("This is all zeros, which is
   no program’s code: use the Wasm hash of the code your contract runs."); the console's read answers `codeHash: null`
   for the all-1s hash and the editor says "This account has no program on the NEAR test network.", never offering it.
6. **No code read where no label can match:** the vault reads nothing for a request whose network it doesn't check
   (a live app's delegate action, another network). Tested: no RPC call.
7. **Console wording.** NEAR, live apps only, once: "From a live app, a call someone else sends for your user always
   shows Journear’s plain window: your words show only on the user’s own transactions." (the rule: a live app's
   delegate action names no network the vault checks, D726, D729). Soroban: "…signs in full, sent from their own
   account (not an account you pay from, and not wrapped in a fee bump), that runs only…". The preview's note for a
   live app's relayed example: "This example is a call someone else sends for the user, which shows Journear’s plain
   window from a live app (see above). Set “Who sends it” to “Only when the user sends it” to see one."
8. **`no_contract_code` is couldn't check** (the plain window, not amber): an account with no code of its own (or a
   global contract on a node that omits the fields) ties the label to nothing. The vault's and the console's tests now
   use nearcore's real shapes (all-1s with the global field set; the fields omitted).
9. **For the Tech Lead** (added to the list below).
10. The partner-labels module's header no longer counts its importers (core's dormancy test lists them).

### D901. Passport Home: a history entry only for "Move wallet"; the email sharing and the name in one card, "What these apps get from you"
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: both **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** ("go with your recommendations": D895's "For the
  Tech Lead to decide" (a), and D897's "For the Tech Lead to decide"); D895 (b), the tab's name "Move wallet", **kept** by the
  same answer; the details below decided while building, **to confirm** (the list at the end) · Built on
  `feat/home-back-and-sharing-card` (from `next`), not merged, not deployed: `packages/web/src/auth/home-page.ts`
  (`selectTab`, `replaceStep`, `leaveMoveStep`, `rewind(to)`, the Security panel's card, `HOME_TEXT.getsTitle`,
  `getsLine`), `home-devices.ts` (`emailView`, `emailExpanded`, `emailSummary`, `emailAbout`, `HOME_EMAIL_TITLE`,
  `HOME_EMAIL_SHOW`, the email part's body; `devicesSummary` without the email; the two intros),
  `home-profile.ts` (the wallet page's part: `h3`, `home-gets-part`), `css/home.css` (the card's parts); tests
  `packages/web/test/auth/home-page.test.ts` ("D901: only “Move wallet” adds a history entry…", "D901: “Your wallets”
  from “Move wallet”…", "D901: tabs pressed while the page’s own Back is on its way…", "D901: one card for what the apps
  get from the person"), `home-export.test.ts` ("D895, D901: leaving “Move wallet” by …"), `home-devices.test.ts`
  ("D901: the email part…"), `home-profile.test.ts`; e2e `apps/e2e/tests/home.spec.ts`, `home-devices.spec.ts`,
  `home-export.spec.ts` (three browsers). `home-export.ts`, `key-reveal.ts`, `approve-guard.ts`, `guard-hint.ts`, the
  API, vault, issuer and contracts are unchanged. Supersedes D895's "History" bullet (one entry per tab opened).
- **1. Back and the tabs.** On a wallet's page, only entering "Move wallet" adds a history entry (D893's scheme,
  `home:{tag}:{step}`, nothing else; the address never changes). Addresses ↔ Security changes what the wallet's entry
  shows, in the page's memory only: the entry keeps its marker and nothing is written to the browser (no
  `replaceState` is needed: the marker would be the same string). So:
  - Back from Addresses or Security goes to "Your wallets"; Forward shows the wallet on the tab it was on.
  - Back from "Move wallet" returns to the tab the person entered it from, with focus on that tab.
  - Another tab pressed on "Move wallet" (decided while building, see (a) below) sends the browser back one entry
    (`history.go(-1)`, the page's own traversal, as "Your wallets" already does), and that entry then shows the tab
    chosen; Forward reaches "Move wallet" again, collapsed, never a key. So "Move wallet" ↔ another tab, however often,
    leaves at most one entry over the wallet's (the reviewer's "50 toggles leave 50 entries" is gone).
  - "Your wallets" goes back to the list's own entry, as before (`history.go(-1)` or `(-2)`).
  - A browser that refuses "Move wallet" its entry: the tab still opens, Back from it leaves the wallet's page, and the
    list's entry is never the one replaced. A browser where the page can't go back (`history.go` throws): the tab
    chosen takes "Move wallet"'s entry, which stays "Move wallet"'s slot, so entering "Move wallet" again reuses it
    (never more than one entry over the wallet's; Back from the tab in that slot shows the wallet's entry, on the tab it
    last showed). A tab pressed while the page's own Back is on its way: the entry added when it lands is for the view
    then on screen (one for "Move wallet" at most); a second way back asked for meanwhile ("Your wallets" right after
    another tab) waits for the first to land, then goes on from where the browser really is. A traversal that lands
    after the page stopped waiting (`REWIND_GIVE_UP_MS`, 10 s) on the entry it was going to changes nothing on screen.
  - **The lock holds on every way out**, unchanged: leaving "Move wallet" by another tab, Back, "Your wallets" (and
    Forward elsewhere, where that can still happen) runs `moving.leave()` in `showView`, before and apart from anything
    history does. Proven by `home-export.test.ts` "D895, D901: leaving “Move wallet” by …" (Addresses, Security, Back,
    "Your wallets", a browser that refused the entry: the secret zeroed, the flow `closed`, the key's box masked, the key
    nowhere in the document; and, after another tab, Forward back to "Move wallet" collapsed), checked to fail on all
    four tab and Back cases when the tab change's `leave()` is removed; and e2e `home-export.spec.ts` with the real
    derive in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (Back; Security; "Your wallets"; Addresses then Forward and Back twice).
    D895's case "Forward to a tab opened after it" no longer exists: no entry is ever added after "Move wallet".
  - Nothing is read on a tab change, Back or Forward (as before; opening Security by a press still reads the devices
    once, D897).
- **2. One card for what the apps get.** On a wallet's Security tab the email sharing and "Your name" are one card,
  after "Ways to sign in" and "Devices and auto-approve" (the order asked for; no better order found). Its title is an
  `h2` (the card is a `section` named by it): **"What these apps get from you"** for a wallet two or more apps use,
  **"What this app gets from you"** for one app (also on "App details"); its line, option A's a3: **"Your email and your
  name, if you chose to share them."**. Two parts, each a `section` named by its `h3`, each with its own line and button,
  exactly the pattern of D897's sections:
  - **"Your email"** (`home-devices.ts` `emailView`, from the devices' one read, so no new request): its line before a
    read **"Whether you share your email address with this app."** ("…with these apps." for a shared wallet; "this
    app" for one app everywhere in the card, as its title and the name's line say, after PR 130's review); after the
    Security tab's read, D897's email sentence moved here ("Your email is shared with Sodax." / "…with this app." /
    "…with Sodax and Sodax Earn." / "…with 3 apps."), or the two sentences the wallet's page used to say under the
    devices, now the line: "You aren’t sharing your email address with this app." and "Passport Home can’t tell right
    now whether you share your email with this app." ("these apps" as above). Then **"Show email sharing"**: the same rule as "Show devices" (the tab's read while at most a minute old,
    else one new read), after which each app the email is shared with is the same card as before ("Your email is shared
    with Sodax: ada@…", "Stop sharing email", its confirmation unchanged, D765), and a small "Show again". A failed tab
    read is the same quiet note: "Passport Home couldn’t check this just now. “Show email sharing” tries again." A stop,
    its outcome ("Your email is no longer shared with this app. Its new sign-ins don’t include it.") and a refusal are
    said in this part, with the focus there; the devices' section no longer shows the email at all.
  - **"Your name"** (`home-profile.ts`, unchanged but for its heading level): its line, "Show name sharing", the per-app
    "Share my name with {App}" / "Stop sharing my name", every sentence as before.
  - "Devices and auto-approve" on a wallet's page: its sentence is now **"Where you’re signed in to this wallet, and
    what those devices may sign without asking."** (was "…, what those devices may sign without asking, and whether you
    share your email with the app."), on "App details" **"Where you’re signed in to this app with Journear, and what
    those devices may sign without asking."**; its read line no longer ends with the email sentence. Pressing "Show
    email sharing" never opens the device cards (they keep waiting for "Show devices").
  - Not changed: the account view "Devices and auto-approve" (under "Your account") still lists the email sharing with
    the devices, app by app (a per-app card there would split one list in two); the account view "Your name"; every
    request, guard, confirmation and refusal sentence.
- **After PR 130's review (2026-11-24)**, applied on the same branch (merged with `next` at `e2d7a142` first):
  1. **A late landing no longer changes the screen.** On "Move wallet", another tab, then "Move wallet" again, with
     the browser's traversal landing after 10 s, used to flip back to the tab (the move flow dropped, the key erased:
     the safe direction). The page now remembers where its own traversal goes and ignores that landing whatever the
     entry. Unit test.
  2. **`history.go` throwing no longer piles up entries** (it did: 5 toggles, 7 entries): "Move wallet"'s entry is
     reused, above. Unit tests, one of them proving the key is erased on that path (`home-export.test.ts`).
  3. **The test's history is faithful**: `FakeHistory.go` changes `index` and `state` only when the traversal lands
     (with `hold`, at `release()`), as browsers do. With it, "Move wallet" → another tab → "Your wallets" before the
     first traversal landed left the list on screen over the wallet's entry (the next Back did nothing visible); the
     page now chains the second way back after the first lands, from the browser's real entry (`rewind` reads the
     entry's marker, no longer assumes it). Unit test; D893's "a view opened while the page's own Back is on its way"
     test now expects the browser on the wallet's entry until the traversal lands.
  4. **No read while a stop is on its way**: "Show devices" and "Show email sharing" are disabled then (a read landing
     after the stop cleared its outcome sentence, and the focus landed on an empty note). Unit test.
  5. **A stop answered after the person moved to another wallet** (or reopened the same one) applies what it stopped
     but says nothing and moves no focus on the page now open. Unit test.
  6. **Wording**: one form, "this app", in the card for one app (above); on a wallet's page the devices' warning for an
     account Journear couldn't confirm is now "Passport Home couldn’t confirm that this sign-in is still part of your
     account, so it offers no stop for now. Show your devices again in a moment." (the account view keeps "…and shows
     no email sharing here for now…", where the email is listed).
  7. Kept, still to confirm: "Show email sharing" offered when the line already says nothing is shared (e). (Confirmed by
     the Tech Lead 2026-11-24: the D906 note under "To confirm" below.)
  Each fix was checked to make its test fail when undone.
- **Headings now** (Security): `h2` "Ways to sign in", "Devices and auto-approve", "What these apps get from you"; `h3`
  "Your email", "Your name" (D895's "No `h3` on the page" no longer holds).
- **Accessibility**: the card and both parts are `section`s named by their headings; the email part's heading takes the

### D903. "These are {App}'s words, not Journear's."; Elite, Platinum, Deluxe and version numbers refused beside "Passport"; one NEAR operator accepted on testnet, two different ones required on production
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: items 1 to 4 **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24**; the details listed under "To confirm"
  decided while building · Amends D896 and D899 (the line), D891 as narrowed (the edition words, the version forms)
  and D900 (item 1, "To confirm" 11), with rows of "Superseded or amended" · Built: `packages/core/src/partner-labels/words.ts`
  (`partnerAttribution`), `packages/web/src/auth/render-labels.ts` (`labelBox`), `apps/console/web/src/pages/app/Labels.tsx`
  (`LABELS_INTRO`), `apps/console/web/src/pages/Action.tsx` (the review's first line);
  `packages/console-core/src/names.ts` (`APP_NAME_PASSPORT_TIER_WORDS`, `APP_NAME_PASSPORT_TIER_WORDS_BEFORE_AT_END`,
  `VERSION_RE`, `passportProblemIn` kind `version`, `passportSpan`); `packages/env/src/schema.ts` (`rpcOperator`,
  `rpcFallbackOperator`, `apiRpcFallbackOperators`, `nearOperatorProblems`, `operatorKey`), `scripts/lib/deploy-check.ts`.
  Tests: `packages/core/test/partner-labels-text.test.ts`, `packages/web/test/auth/render-labels.test.ts`,
  `apps/console/web/test/labels.test.tsx`, `apps/e2e/tests/partner-labels-{window,contracts,console}.spec.ts`,
  `packages/console-core/test/names.test.ts`, `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`, `scripts/test/sql.test.ts`,
  `packages/env/src/index.test.ts`, `scripts/test/deploy-check.test.ts`.
- **Address impact: none.** Nothing signed, decoded, derived or digested changes: the line is display text, app names
  enter no path, and the operator fields are read only by the manifest's rules and `deploy-check`.

**1. The line under a partner's words (the Tech Lead 2026-11-24).** In the approval window's partner box, and so in the
console's preview of it (the same renderer), the attribution is now:

> These are {App}’s words, not Journear’s.

(was "These are {App}’s words. Journear hasn’t checked them.", D896, D899). The app's name is handled as before: text
only, in the window's bold, direction-isolated `strong.app-name`, never markup, at most 64 characters (the app-name
rule), the window's typographic apostrophe. Decided while building: "’s" after every name, one ending in "s" too
("These are Coffee Beans’s words"), as the window's amber line already writes "{App}’s description" (one app, a
singular name); with no name the box says "The app says:" and the line "These are the app’s words" (lower case
mid-sentence; it said "The app’s" before). The console's intro on the Request labels tab and the review's first line
quote the new sentence. Tested: markup, quotes, a right-to-left name, 64 characters, an "s" ending, a name ending in
"’s" ("Ben & Jerry’s’s", left as written: see To confirm), each only ever text.

**2. App names: more edition words, and version numbers (the Tech Lead 2026-11-24).** D891's edition rule (as narrowed) gains
**Elite, Platinum and Deluxe**:
- after "Passport", as the other edition words: "Passport Elite", "My Passport Platinum", "Passport Deluxe™",
  "PassportElite" refused; "Acme Passport Elite", "Passport Elite Travel", "Passport Platinum Club" allowed;
- before "Passport" only when the name ends there (decided while building): "Elite Passport", "My Deluxe Passport",
  "PlatinumPassport" refused; "Elite Passport Travel", "Deluxe Passport Covers", "Platinum Passport Club" allowed (the
  six older before-words keep their rule, words after or not). Why: passport-holder shops and passport services use
  these words before "Passport" with words of their own;
- plurals ("Passport Elites") and longer words ("Passport Elitist") pass, as before.

**Version numbers**, the pattern (`VERSION_RE`, on the NFKC text, any letter case, any script's decimal digits):
`(v | ver | version)` then up to three spaces or dots and a number with optional `.number` parts ("V2", "v2.0", "V 2",
"V.2", "v  2", "Version 2", "ver. 3"), **or** a number with at least one `.number` part ("2.0", "3.1.4"); a whole word
(no letter or digit right before or after it, a trade mark after it allowed: "2.0™"), in brackets or not; glued to a
word that reads "Passport" on the folded form too ("PassportV2", "Passport2.0", "Pa55portV2", "Pass portV2": the split
is made per word on the compared key, after PR 129's review). The rule takes every such number out of the name and checks what is left: if that is
"Passport" alone (the alone rule: with at most two of the/a/an/my/your/our/near/wallet/official before it), the name
is refused as a version of the wallet; if what is left breaks another rule, that rule's message is given ("Passport Pro
2.0" names "Pro"; "Passport V2 Wallet" names "Wallet", a name that passed before). A plain number is not a version:
"Passport 2" stays the alone rule's (one digit), and "Passport 10", "Passport 24", "Passport 360", "Passport 2026"
stay allowed. So refused: "Passport 2.0", "Passport V2", "Passport v2.1", "My Passport V2", "Passports 2.0", "V2
Passport", "2.0 Passport", "Passport Version 2"; allowed: "Acme Passport 2.0", "Gitcoin Passport 2.0", "WD My Passport
V2", "Passport V2 Travel", "Web 3.0 Passport", "Passport 4x4", "Passport 3D", "Passport 1.5L", "Passport MV2", "v2.0
Wallet". The message: 'The name must not have a version number such as "2.0" with "Passport": it reads as a version
of the wallet, as "Passport 2.0" would. Users call Journear Passport "Passport". Your brand first, as in "Acme
Passport", or "Passport" with words of your own, as in "Passport Photos Co", is fine'.
- Trade marks (found while building; the first fix was incomplete, PR 129's review found the rest): NFKC spells "™" as
  the letters "TM", which hid the word beside "Passport" ("Passport™ Wallet", "Passport™Wallet", "Passport ™ Pro",
  "Passport TM Wallet", "Passport (TM) Wallet", "Passport™V2" all passed on `next`). Now: the signs ™ ℠ ® © Ⓡ and
  "(TM)", "(SM)", "(R)", "(C)" are read as a space (after the name as written is read, so what the written name alone
  refuses stays refused: "Passport (TM) Acme" starts with "Passport" and a bracket); "TM" or "SM" written as its own
  word right after "Passport" is skipped; "TM" or "SM" typed between "Passport" and a joined word is read past
  ("PassportTMWallet"). Letters "tm" or "sm" inside a word, and a brand "SM", are untouched ("Passport Tmall",
  "Passport Smart", "PassportSmart", "SM Passport", "SM Entertainment Passport", "Passport SMS", "Passport TM Travel"
  pass, as on `next`). "Acme Passport™", "Gitcoin Passport™" and "Passport™ Travel" still pass.
- "Passport Home" (D765) with a number or trade mark between (after PR 129's review): version numbers, whole numbers
  standing alone and trade-mark signs are taken out before that rule too, so "Passport 2.0 Home", "Passport v2 Home",
  "Passport 2 Home", "Passport 365 Home" and "Passport™ Home" are refused as "Passport Home" ("Passport 24 Homes"
  passes, as "Passport Homes" does).
- Kept: every allowance D891's narrowing recorded ("WD My Passport Ultra", "Acme Passport Plus", "Capital One
  Passport", only "Pros" as a plural, the ordinary business words), and its tests pass unchanged. Stored names are not
  rewritten: a stored app whose name the rule now refuses keeps working, a rename must pass, and its code mails say "an
  app" (tested for the new forms). Speed: adversarial 64-character version and edition names are each under 20 ms;
  the version and trade-mark steps on 2,000-character inputs stay under 200 ms (the glued split's pattern is bounded).
- The differential check (after PR 129's review): about 370,000 names (every one, two and three-word combination of
  63 tokens: "Passport" spellings, determiners, brands, wallet, edition and own words, trade marks in each form,
  version and plain numbers; four-word names after "Passport"; every name the tests quote) against `next`'s rule:
  **none refused on `next` passes now**; 29,718 are newly refused, each by a rule above. The newly refused with a word
  of the partner's own fall in two groups, both the older rules' own shapes: "Passport" and a number or trade mark
  and "Home" ("Passport 10 Home", "Passport™ Home Covers", as "Passport Home Rentals" is refused) and a before-word
  with a version number or trade mark beside "Passport" ("Pro PassportV2 Travel", "Pro v 2 Passport Co", as "Pro
  Passport Co" is refused).
- What it still misses: Roman numerals ("Passport II", "Passport III"), Ultimate, Enterprise, Uno, Gold (still
  allowed, D891's open list); a look-alike "v" from another alphabet ("Passport ν2", Greek nu); a plain number as a
  version ("Passport 10"); a comma or a space as the version's dot ("Passport 2,0", "Passport 2 0": a comma would
  also refuse "Passport 1,000", and "2 0" can't be told from the plain "20").

**3. NEAR providers: one operator accepted on testnet, two different ones required on production (the Tech Lead
2026-11-24).** The Tech Lead's words: "for 2nd NEAR provider, can we just do 1 on testnet? but enforce this only on
production." So (D900 item 1, option (c), enforced on production):
- **Testnet**: accepted as it is. sandbox-dev's `rpc` (test.rpc.fastnear.com) and `rpcFallback` (rpc.testnet.near.org)
  are both run by FastNear; there the "both providers agree" checks (a member's path, D263; a test app's delegate
  action, D729; a NEAR label's code hash, D900) rest on one operator, and the docs say so. It is no longer a blocker for
  switching labels on in a testnet env (that switch is still its own step). `envs/sandbox-dev.json` is unchanged.
- **Not in force yet (after PR 129's review):** the manifest's `network` admits only `testnet` today
  (`z.enum(['testnet'])`), so any other network is refused before this rule runs, and `deploy-check` loads manifests
  through that schema; the rule is reached only in tests that build a production manifest by hand. It takes effect
  when the schema admits another network. **The names are a declaration, checked in review, not proof:** "FastNear"
  and "FastNear Inc", "fastnear.com" or a name with a look-alike letter compare as different operators; nothing but a
  reviewer reading the manifest catches that (no suffix stripping, on purpose: the reviewer's call).
- **Production** (any network but testnet; the schema admits only testnet today, mainnet is parked): the manifest must
  say who runs each endpoint, since a different domain is no proof (near.org's endpoint is FastNear's). New fields:
  `rpcOperator` and `rpcFallbackOperator` (strings, trimmed, 1 to 64 characters with a letter or digit, no control,
  bidi, zero-width or other invisible character: after PR 129's review), and
  `apiRpcFallbackOperators` (one name per `apiRpcFallbacks` URL, in order). The rule (`nearOperatorProblems`):
  everywhere, `rpcFallbackOperator` needs `rpcFallback`, and `apiRpcFallbackOperators` needs `apiRpcFallbacks` and
  the same count; on a production network, `rpcFallback`, `rpcOperator` and `rpcFallbackOperator` are required, and
  the two operators must differ, compared after NFKC, lower-casing and dropping everything but letters and digits
  (`operatorKey`: "FastNear", " FASTNEAR ", "Fast Near", "Fast-NEAR" are one operator); with `apiRpcFallbacks`,
  `apiRpcFallbackOperators` is required, and they may share an operator with `rpc` (the API only fails over to them,
  D435, and never compares two answers). The schema refuses a manifest that breaks it, and `deploy-check` fails on it
  again for a production network, whatever groups it reads (as it does for `hanaOrgId`). On testnet the fields are
  optional and may name one operator for both. Proven on a synthetic production manifest (sandbox-dev's, parsed, with
  `network: "mainnet"`, as the dashboard rules are tested) and in `deploy-check`; every committed env validates.
- **EVM sponsor chains and Stellar** (considered, not built): `evm.sponsor` is refused on any network but testnet
  (D834), so a production rule for its `rpc`/`rpcFallback` could never run today; the same declaration belongs there
  when sponsorship is decided for a production network (D855's two-provider account read has the same weakness).
  Stellar's endpoints are not in the manifest: a partner's page gives its own to the SDK, and nothing of Journear's
  compares two Stellar providers (a Soroban label's code is the transaction's own footprint, D900). Also open: the
  pinned CKD key's sources (`ckdNetworkKeySource.rpcs`, ≥ 3 "providers") are counted by registrable domain, so two of
  them can be one operator in the same way; a production re-pin should count operators (mainnet-readiness 2.12).

**4. Confirmed as built (the Tech Lead 2026-11-24), no change:**
- the red line stays when users of an app with a payment description pay other people (D896, "To confirm" 13: kept;
  no "my users also pay other people" option);
- a staff Block stays final, with no Unblock (D894);
- Journear's note on a blocked change is shown to every member of the partner's organisation, viewers included (D899,
  "To confirm" 2);
- "Move wallet" keeps its name (D895 (b)); the other Passport Home answers are recorded in D901.

- **To confirm** (decided while building): (1) the field names `rpcOperator`, `rpcFallbackOperator`,
  `apiRpcFallbackOperators`, and the comparison ignoring case, spaces and punctuation; (2) that the API's fallbacks need
  a name on production but may share an operator; (3) the version pattern above, a plain number not counting, and a
  version number before "Passport" ("V2 Passport") refused too; (4) Elite, Platinum and Deluxe before "Passport" only
  when the name ends there; (5) "’s" after every app name, also after one ending in "s" or already in "’s" ("Ben &
  Jerry’s’s words"); (6) reading trade marks past "Passport" (signs, bracketed forms, "TM"/"SM" as a word right after
  it); (7) "These are the app’s words" when an app has no name; (8) real product names now refused as versions:
  "Passport V8", "Passport V60", "Passport 24.7", "Passport 1.1.1.1" (each with "Passport" alone; with a brand or own
  words they pass); (9) a name can still word the line awkwardly: an app named "Your wallet’s words, not Acme" would
  read "These are Your wallet’s words, not Acme’s words, not Journear’s." A name with "Journear" is refused, and the
  name stays bold and isolated, so it can't pass as Journear's own words; not a regression (the old line had the same
  shape); (10) "Passport Home" refused with a number or trade mark between the words.

### D902. Passport Home cancels a waiting sign-in itself (D898's option B): Google on the shared client, a fresh Google proof of the same account, Home's own route, stricter than the window
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: **B decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** ("build D898's option B", through the coordinator's
  brief: B only, Google on the shared client, D898's words, B+email not built); every detail below **decided while
  building, to confirm** (the list at the end) · Built: `apps/api/src/home/link-cancel.ts` (new: `POST
  /v1/home/link/cancel`), `apps/api/src/links.ts` (`precheckChange` exported with `activeActor`, `linkRootWindow`),
  `apps/api/src/index.ts`, `apps/api/src/usage/event.ts`, `packages/console-core/src/usage-event.ts` (endpoint
  `home_link_cancel`, appless), `apps/api/migrations-usage/0011_home_link_cancels.sql` (new, **not applied anywhere**,
  listed in `go-live-after-freeze.md` 1.1), `packages/core/src/protocol.ts` (`hana:home-cancel-params`),
  `packages/web/src/auth/login-page.ts` (`checkHomeCancel`, `HOME_CANCEL_SIGN_IN_TITLE`), `home-api.ts` (`linkCancel`),
  `home-link-cancel.ts` (new: the flow), `home-sign-ins.ts` (which rows offer it, the row's steps, the line and the row
  after a cancel), `home-page.ts` (its deps, the messages); tests `apps/api/test/home-link-cancel.test.ts` (new),
  `apps/api/test-usage/ledger.test.ts`, `scripts/test/usage-migrate.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/protocol.test.ts`,
  `packages/web/test/auth/home-link-cancel.test.ts` (new), `login-page.test.ts`, `plain-words.test.ts`,
  `apps/e2e/tests/home-sign-ins.spec.ts` ("D902 …", three browsers; option A's test now gives its wallet a coverage
  other than shared), `apps/e2e/src/server/api.ts` (the local stack runs the Worker's route whole; its relayer stand-in
  applies `cancel_link` on the session pool to the mocked chain, every other session-pool method still unconfigured); docs `architecture.md`, `security.md`, `api.md`, `operations.md` (hand-test F, step 5a),
  `go-live-after-freeze.md`, `README.md`, `apps/e2e/README.md`. No contract, issuer or vault change; no `envs/` value.
- **Which rows**: a waiting email or Google account (`pointerFor` `cancel_at_sign_in`: the viewer already opens the
  wallet and is not the waiting one), Home signed in with Google, the wallet's coverage `shared` with a client (the
  listing's `googleClientId`, else Home's shared client). Every other row keeps D898 option A's "Open {App} to cancel it"
  or the plain sentence: email sign-ins (B+email is not built), wallets on a partner's or Hana's own client, the exit
  client. The section's last line reads "Passport Home can cancel a link that is still waiting, but can’t remove a
  sign-in yet." where any row offers it (else the old line), and "If you’re already signed in to this app, sign out of it
  first." is not said for such a row.
- **The flow** (`home-link-cancel.ts`; one at a time; nothing is sent to the API before step 5):
  1. **Cancel this link** (small outlined, named "Cancel this link for the {email address | Google account}") under
     "Don’t recognise it? If you’re not sure, cancel it." opens the confirmation in the row: "Cancel this link?"; "The
     {kind} will never open this wallet. You can’t undo this: it can only be added again, and then it waits again.";
     muted "Sign in with Google to confirm it’s you"; **Cancel the link** (the one danger button) and **Go back**
     (nothing changes).
  2. **Cancel the link** opens `/login?mode=home` in the click (before any await), then, while it loads: the wallet's
     ways to sign in read again on both providers alone (they must agree, as the list's own read), and on NEAR
     `get_scope.allow_shared` and the client among `get_config.shared_clients`. The row must still be waiting, the viewer
     still active; the root and the epoch for the nonce come from this read, never from the list on screen (a stale
     page can't send a stale nonce). Otherwise the child closes with nothing posted.
  3. The child's hello gets `hana:home-cancel-params` {signer, clientId, scopeId, rootKey, memberKey, epoch, salt (32
     bytes), nonce, relayId, relayKey}; the child recomputes `linkChangeNonce(signer, scope, "cancel", root, member,
     epoch, salt)` itself (the action fixed, never read from the message) and goes to Google: the shared client,
     `/login/callback`, the account chooser (`prompt=select_account`, no `login_hint`), `max_age=0`. Its heading: "Sign in
     with Google to confirm it’s you". Home's row shows the same heading, "A Google window is open. Choose the Google
     account you signed in with here." and **Go back** (closes the child; nothing sent).
  4. Google's answer through the login relay (5 minutes at most): checked against Google's keys for that client, that
     nonce, the claim allow-list, a fresh `auth_time` when present, and the same `sub` as Home's sign-in; Home's
     identity must still be the one the flow started with. The row: "Cancelling the link" / "This takes a few seconds…".
  5. One `POST /v1/home/link/cancel` signed by the Home key; never sent again by the page.
  6. Outcomes, each with **Close**: "Link cancelled" / "The {kind} won’t open this wallet." / "Devices signed in to this
     wallet will be asked to sign in again." (the API revokes the account's shares); the summary line recounts at once
     and the row shows only its name and the result until Close, then is gone (no reload, no chain read). **"Nothing
     changed"**, with the reason: not this sign-in ("The link is still waiting." "We couldn’t check it was you." "If you
     picked a different Google account, try again with the one you signed in with here."), the sign-ins changed ("The
     ways to sign in to this wallet may have changed since this page showed them." "Close this, then choose “Show again”
     to see them as they are now."), refused before anything was sent ("The link is still waiting." "Journear couldn’t do
     this just now. Try again later."), the check didn't finish ("The link is still waiting." "Google didn’t finish
     checking it’s you.", or the blocked-window sentence), Home's sign-in ended (its own sentence; Home is told). **"It
     may not have been cancelled"**: "Something went wrong, so we can’t tell whether the link was cancelled. Choose “Show
     again” to check." with **Show again** (reads the list on both providers) and Close; the row is kept. Each failure
     shows "Error code (for support): {code}". "Nothing changed" is said only for codes refused before the relay, or a
     contract rule that reverted (`contract_rejected` with a `reason`, `link_pending`); anything else, a network failure
     or an answer that isn't `{result: null}` is "It may not have been cancelled" (`cancelOutcome`).
- **The route's contract** (`POST /v1/home/link/cancel`, body exactly `{jwt, memberKey, epoch, salt, scopeId}`; `200
  {result: null, nearTx}`), checks in order, each refusing with nothing relayed: (1) `homeGate` (Origin = auth origin,
  10/min per IP, the Home token, the Home key's signature over this body, 5/min per Home key, the counter used once);
  (2) the Home identity is Google (`403 google_only`); (3) the shape (`400 bad_request`); (4) the proof genuine,
  unexpired, allow-listed claims, with a nonce (`verifyLoginToken`, no app); (5) the proof's `(provider, sub)` equals
  Home's (`403 home_account_mismatch`); (6) its `aud` a shared Google client in force (`403 not_shared_client`), admitted
  for the scope (`checkClientScope`), not paused, its kid active (`chainGate`); (7) the chain now (`precheckChange`,
  `activeActor`): member in the proof identity's account, the nonce that change's, the identity not the member (`422
  not_allowed`) and not pending (`409 link_pending`), the epoch current, the member pending; (8) the panic cache, one
  relay per proof (the `link-tokens` claim shared with `/v1/link/cancel`: `409 link_in_flight`), the account's
  link-change windows shared with the window's route (10/min, 100 a day). Then `cancel_link` from the session pool; the
  account root's vault shares revoked in every app of the scope; the directory synced with the member as the hint; one
  usage event `home_link_cancel` for Journear's own org.
- **Threats** (who could try what, and what stops them):

  | Who, trying what | What stops it |
  |---|---|
  | Another website posting to the route (CSRF) | No cookie; `Origin` must be the auth origin; every request is signed by the Home key, which lives only in Home's page memory |
  | Someone replaying a captured request or proof | The Home counter is single use; the proof's nonce names one epoch and the first cancel moves it; one relay per proof across isolates and both routes (`link-tokens`) |
  | A page left open for hours (a stale list) | The root and epoch come from a fresh two-provider read at the press; the API and the contract check the epoch and that the member is still pending |
  | A cancel aimed at another wallet's waiting sign-in | The member must be in the proof identity's own account; the nonce commits to that root and member; the contract checks it again |
  | A different Google account than Home's session | The page compares `sub`s before sending; the API refuses `home_account_mismatch`; Home's identity must be unchanged since the flow started |
  | A stolen Home session (key and token) alone | Can't make a `link_change` proof: that needs a new Google ID token of the same account over this change's nonce. "Fresh" is asked of Google (`max_age=0`, the chooser), not proved: Google sends no `auth_time`, so anyone who can drive the victim's browser while it is signed in to Google gets the proof with one click in the chooser, the same as Home's derive and export |
  | The waiting sign-in itself, or another waiting one, cancelling from Home | Refused (`not_allowed`, `link_pending`): Home is stricter than the contract and the window |
  | A token of a partner's own client or the exit client | `not_shared_client`; the exit client can't make link changes on chain either |
  | The waiting period ending during the flow | The fresh read refuses an active row; the API's precheck and the contract refuse an active member (reverted): "Nothing changed" |
  | Double-submit (two presses, two tabs) | One flow at a time per page; the request is sent once; the second copy of a proof is `link_in_flight` |
  | A flood draining the session pool | Per-IP and per-Home-key minutes, the account's change windows; a precheck refuses anything that isn't a live pending link (no gas), and pending links are bounded by the add limits |
  | A lying or stale NEAR provider | Both providers must agree for the page; a wrong root or epoch only makes the API or the contract refuse |
  | Logs or the ledger leaking identities | No token, `sub`, identity key or path logged, returned or in the usage event (tested) |
- **Why the usage ledger changed** (decided while building): every relay must have a ledger row, or the admin's daily
  nonce check raises `nonce_unexplained` for the session key; a `link_cancel` row needs an app (a partner would be named
  and billed). So a new appless endpoint `home_link_cancel`, written for Journear's own org (`HANA_ORG_ID`, else
  `org_legacy`), through migrations-usage 0011 (widens the two checks and `record_event`; the reports and settlement
  unchanged: it is a `scope` row of Journear's org, from the session pool). **0011 must be applied before an API with
  this route is deployed**; it is applied nowhere now.
- Rejected: relaying through the Home pool (its keys' `method_names` would need a deploy step, and D456 keeps each pool
  to what it relays; the session pool already relays `cancel_link`); calling `/v1/link/cancel` with an app's key
  (D874); a `login_hint` (D898 item 2: Home shows the chooser; the API's `sub` check covers a wrong pick); refreshing the
  list from the flow's read (a row that vanished would lose its result screen; Show again reads); a usage event under a
  partner's app.
- Not changed: the delay, what a waiting sign-in can do, derivation paths, keys, the contract, the issuer, the vault, the
  sign-in window's own Cancel. **Address impact: none** (no path, key or derivation input changes; a cancel only
  removes a member that never opened anything).
- **To confirm** (decided while building): (1) the sentences not in D898: "A Google window is open. Choose the Google
  account you signed in with here.", "Devices signed in to this wallet will be asked to sign in again." on the result,
  each "Nothing changed" reason line above, "Close this, then choose “Show again” …", and the section's last line "Passport
  Home can cancel a link that is still waiting, but can’t remove a sign-in yet."; (2) "Sign in with Google to confirm
  it’s you" as both the confirmation's muted line and the sign-in step's heading (Home's row and the child window);
  (3) the screens inside the row (the row keeps its name; a cancelled row shows only its name and the result until
  Close); (4) Cancel the link as a danger button (D881's Cancel asked nothing; D898's B asks first); (5) the fresh
  two-provider read before Google, and its root and epoch used for the nonce; (6) the codes in each outcome group (an
  unknown contract refusal is "It may not have been cancelled", though it reverted); (7) limits: 10/min per IP, 5/min
  per Home key, the account's change windows shared with the window; (8) the session pool, and the usage endpoint
  `home_link_cancel` for Journear's own org (migration 0011); (9) the coverage rule: `shared` only, whatever client the
  wallet's own sign-ins use; (10) Google only: an email owner keeps option A or the sentence (B+email later, or never).
- **Amended after PR 131's independent security review** (2026-11-24; no Critical, High or Medium; the contract's own
  `cancel_link` bounds the route to removing a still-waiting member of the prover's own account), decided while
  building, **to confirm**:
  1. **A refused proof no longer signs the person out of Home.** The route answers what `verifyLoginToken` refuses with
     401 (`invalid_token`, e.g. an unknown key after Google rotates while the API's key cache is stale; `token_stale`)
     with **403** and the same code; the page treats a 401 as "Home's sign-in ended" only for Home's own gate's codes
     (`HOME_GATE_401_CODES`), any other 401 as "Nothing changed … Journear couldn’t do this just now.", and a 403
     `invalid_token` as "We couldn’t check it was you." (`api.md` says a proof refusal is never 401.)
  2. **Partner statements**: the guard that refused Home rows of foreign scopes on a partner's statement now refuses any
     row with no app (kind `home`, or kind `scope`: owner actions and Home link cancels) of a scope where the org has no
     app, deleted ones included (`apps/admin/src/statement.ts`). No new event kind, no migration.
  3. **The result's devices line is now true when shown**: the route answers `sharesRevoked` (whether the revocation was
     written); "Devices signed in to this wallet will be asked to sign in again." only when it is `true`, else "Devices
     already signed in to this wallet stay signed in until their sign-in ends." (new sentence, to confirm).
  4. The redundant pending line in `precheckChange` (`activeActor`) is gone: the contract's own rule, checked just after,
     refuses a pending actor with the same `409 link_pending` (the test still holds).
  5. Tests the mutation run asked for, each failing when its check is removed: the account's limit shared with the
     window's route in both directions; 5 a minute per Home key; the one-relay claim kept after `contract_rejected` and
     after a timeout, and refused Home-first and window-first; the page's "this sign-in is no longer one that opens the
     wallet" check; the 403 proof refusal; `sharesRevoked` false and true; the statement guard for `scope` rows.
  6. **Fresh sign-in, as it holds**: the threat row above and `security.md` now say "fresh" is requested of Google, not
     enforced: Google sends no `auth_time` with `max_age=0` (as recorded for Home's derive, D604), the page checks it only
     when present and the server not at all. No server-side check is added while Google doesn't send the claim.
- Note 2026-11-24 (D906): the sentence of item 3 above, "Devices already signed in to this wallet stay signed in until
  their sign-in ends." (shown after a cancel when the devices could not be signed out), is **confirmed by the Tech Lead**
  ("confirm all"). Every other point to confirm in this entry, (1) to (10) and the other amendments, stays open.
- **Not verified** (nothing here was run against them): real Google (only the local stand-in, which accepts
  `prompt=select_account` with `max_age=0`); the real `hana-signer` contract and real session-pool relayer keys (only the
  API's mocked chain and the local stack's stand-in); migration 0011 on real Neon (PGlite only) and the daily nonce
  check against real `home_link_cancel` rows; the admin's and the partner console's report and statement screens with a
  `home_link_cancel` row (only `buildStatement` and the ledger functions); dark mode of the new screens (light only).
