     quote stays.
  2. **Reader unclear:** the SDK's `NOT_OFFERED` ("Free network fees aren’t offered on this network.",
     `packages/web/src/client/evm-sponsor.ts`). It is the developer's `message` of the SDK's own refusal for a chain
     the build doesn't sponsor, but it is also that reason's `userMessage`, the vault answers the same refusal with the
     same words as its `message`, and `packages/web/test/auth/plain-words.test.ts` treats it as the SDK's one user
     sentence. Changing only the SDK's copy would give one refusal two `message`s depending on where it was refused.
     If wanted: "Gas sponsorship isn't offered on this network." as the SDK's `message` only, the `userMessage` kept.
  3. Not the old term: the SDK's developer message "calls[i].value must be 0: Journear pays network fees only for calls
     that send no ETH" and the tooltips "The chains Journear Passport pays network fees on …", "Runs `calls` … with
     Journear paying the network fee", "Whether Journear pays network fees for this app on `chainId` right now": they
     say plainly who pays; kept.
  4. The NEAR relay's "gasless" (the SDK's `near.ts`, the READMEs, the guide's "gasless calls", "a relayed action's
     free fee only in the details", the stamps README): a different feature, deliberately not called gas sponsorship
     (D879, item 4).
  5. Names, not prose: the files `gas-free-card.ts`, `demo-gas-free.spec.ts`, `guide-gas-free.ts`; the ids `#gas-free…`
     and `GAS_FREE_TEXT`; the guide's anchors `gas-free-actions-not-live` and `gas-free-errors`; the window's CSS class
     `fee-free`; the plain-words lists' `'gasless'`.
  6. Internal comments and READMEs that call the demo's card after its file ("the gas-free card", "the gas-free check-in
     card": `apps/demo/src/*.ts`, `apps/demo/README.md`, `apps/e2e/src/*.ts`, the comments of `apps/e2e/tests/*.spec.ts`,
     `apps/e2e/partner/app.ts` "Gas-free EVM actions (D838)", `apps/e2e/README.md`'s demo card paragraph,
     `docs/operations.md`'s "Trying the gas-free check-in by hand on the local stack" and its card line): read only by
     Journear's engineers and tied to the file names; renaming the prose and not the files would make them disagree.
  7. **Outside this repo:** the sample partner repo's README and `src/hana/sponsor.ts` say "gas-free actions" and cite
     the guide's old section name "Gas-free actions" (now "Gas sponsorship (not live)"). Not touched here.
  8. The SDK's `delegate_nonce_used` `userMessage` (D889's note proposes a tighter sentence): users read it.
- **2. Reduced motion in the brand package.** What moves: nothing in the logo (the mark, wordmark and lockup files
  and `markSvg()` are plain filled paths with no `<animate>`, style or script; the package has no motion in code). All
  of it is in `components.css`: the button, login provider and icon field spinners (`jp-spin`, 0.7 s, for ever), the
  loading placeholder (`.jp-skel`, 1.4 s, for ever), the radio's dot, the toasts coming and going and their 5 s bar, the
  modal's rise, the error's fade, the field's shake, the tag and list fades, the save bar's rise, and about 25
  transitions (buttons, inputs, toggles, tabs, cards, choice cards, rows, the progress bar, the strength meter, the
  slider). The package already had a rule from the design system, but it reached only elements with a `.jp-*` class
  (not the spinner inside a button, the radio inside `.jp-check`, the toggle's knob, the toast's bar, the progress
  bar's fill), only some `::before`/`::after`, and it shortened animations that repeat for ever without stopping them,
  so they flickered (PR 116's review found it on Passport Home in Firefox and WebKit; Home stopped its own placeholders).
  **Decision:** the rule now covers every `.jp-*` element, everything inside one, and their `::before` and `::after`
  (12 selectors), and ends each animation and transition at once: 0.01 ms, run once, no delay; the slider's thumb in a
  rule of its own (a browser that doesn't know `::-webkit-slider-thumb` drops only that one). A spinner is a still ring,
  the placeholder a still bar, nothing slides or fades. "End at once" rather than "remove": a piece that animates into
  its final look still gets there, and code that waits for an animation to end still hears it (none of the consumers
  does today; the stamps site's own art has its own rule). Under reduced motion a toast's 5 s bar is empty from the
  start; the toast still closes on its own timer.
- **The consumers** (each imports `components.css`; the admin portal holds a copy made by `sync-brand`, re-run here):
  the approval and sign-in windows and Passport Home (`packages/web`: their own modal rise, placeholders and tab
  transitions already stop; the tab scroll is smooth only without reduced motion), the partner console (its own rule
  for everything), the admin portal (its nav links' own rule; its `.jp-toast .bar` duration isn't marked important, so
  the rule wins), the stamps site (its own rule for all its art), the demo (its spinners had a rule; its results' fade,
  `.result` with the brand's `jp-fade`, had none: it sits inside a `.jp-card`, so the brand's rule now reaches it, and
  the demo's own rule names it too). None adds motion back; no consumer has SVG animation.
- Tests: `packages/brand/test/brand.test.ts` holds the rule's 12 selectors and its declarations, the thumb's rule, and
  checks that every rule in `components.css` that animates or transitions is a `.jp-*` element or inside one with a
  covered pseudo-element (over 30 rules; the three that repeat for ever, two spinners and the placeholder, among them), and that the logo files and
  `markSvg()` carry no animation, style or script. `apps/e2e/tests/home.spec.ts`, the test that already emulates
  reduced motion, now also builds a `.jp-btn` spinner and a `.jp-check` radio in Home and checks the spinner runs once
  in under 1 ms and the radio's `::after` too, and that the spinner turns for ever again without reduced motion (all
  three browsers; with the old rule it fails in all three). `packages/web/src/auth/css/home.css`'s comment on Home's own
  placeholder rule now says the brand's rule no longer keeps the repeats; Home's rule is kept. The admin's `gen-wrangler` test holds its copy to the brand.
- Rejected: `animation: none` (a piece whose final look comes from its animation would stay at its first frame, and
  code waiting for an animation's end would wait for ever); a rule per component (the next component would be missed);
  removing the consumers' own rules (they still cover their own classes).
- Address impact: none (no path, key or derivation changed).
- To confirm: (1) the API texts 1 to 3, in particular "Gas prices are too high for sponsorship right now" (2 and 3
  go beyond "free network fees": D879 proposed them); (2) "a sponsored action" as the name of one action in the docs
  (items 9 to 11) and "Gas sponsorship for EVM actions" in the SDK's tooltips; (3) the `delegate_nonce_used` sentence;
  (4) `NOT_OFFERED` left as the user's words (left 2); (5) the demo card's internal name left (left 6) and the sample
  repo left (left 7); (6) the reduced-motion rule: everything inside a `.jp-*` element, ended at once rather than
  removed, the toast's bar empty under reduced motion; (7) **for the Tech Lead, behaviour not changed:** under reduced
  motion a spinner becomes a still three-quarter ring. Where it is the only sign that something is happening (the
  partner console's sign-in button while it works, `apps/console/web/src/pages/SignIn.tsx`, and the email sign-in
  test's button, `apps/console/web/src/pages/app/EmailLogin.tsx`), a long wait can look stuck. The other choice is to
  keep loading spinners moving under reduced motion, slower or as a gentle pulse, and stop only the rest; (8) item 3a,
  "too high for sponsorship" with its 15 s retry kept.
- Note 2026-11-24 (D906): **answered by the Tech Lead** ("confirm all"): (7) reduced motion: the loading spinners now
  fade slowly instead of standing still (built in D906, which amends item 2's still ring); and the two developer
  messages reworded to "Gas prices are too high for sponsorship right now, try again later" (text 2 and item 3a) are
  confirmed. Still open: (1) for texts 1 and 3 ("Gas sponsorship is paused for now", "Gas prices are moving too fast
  right now"), (2) to (6), and in (8) item 3a's 15 s retry.
- Not verified: a real device with its own reduced-motion setting (only Playwright's emulation, in Chromium, Firefox
  and WebKit); the slider's thumb (no page uses `.jp-slider` today); nothing deployed.

## Who runs the pinned CKD key's sources, one display-safety module (branch `feat/key-source-operators-text-safety`), 2026-11-24

From `next` @ 663520d0, with `next` @ f8c5c51d (D905) merged in; not merged, not deployed. No `envs/` value changes;
every committed env validates as it is. Numbered D904 when it was built; it sits after D905, which reached `next` first.

### D904. The pinned CKD key's sources: accepted on testnet, three different operators required on production (as D903 for the NEAR providers); the text-safety checks in one shared module
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: item 1 **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** ("go": D903's open point treated as D903 treats
  the NEAR providers: accept on testnet, enforce on production); item 2 a refactor with **no behaviour change**; the
  details under "To confirm" decided while building · Amends D100 (the sources' count on a production network) and
  closes D903's open point (item 3, last bullet), with a row of "Superseded or amended" · Built:
  `packages/env/src/schema.ts` (`ckdSourceOperators`, `ckdSourceOperatorProblems`, `MAX_CKD_SOURCE_OPERATORS`),
  `scripts/lib/deploy-check.ts`, `scripts/lib/ckd.ts` (`fetchCkdKey`'s check before reading; `ckdSources` with no
  well-known list); `packages/core/src/display-safe.ts` (escapes only) and its new subpath `@hana-id/core/display-safe`
  (`packages/core/package.json`, both export maps), `packages/console-core/src/names.ts` (`isDisplaySafeName`),
  `apps/email-issuer/src/bytes.ts` (`isDisplaySafeLine`), `packages/env/src/schema.ts` (`operatorName`),
  `packages/env/package.json` (now depends on `@hana-id/core`). Tests: `packages/env/src/index.test.ts`,
  `scripts/test/deploy-check.test.ts`, `scripts/test/ckd.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/display-safe.test.ts`,
  `packages/core/test/index.test.ts` (the export list gains the subpath), `apps/email-issuer/test/mail-html.test.ts`,
  `packages/console-core/test/rpc.test.ts` (after review).
  Docs: `envs/README.md`, `docs/operations.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
  `docs/mainnet-readiness.md` (2.12), `README.md` (fetch-ckd-key), `packages/core/README.md` (the entry point, marked internal after review).
- **Address impact: none.** No key or path derivation changes: `ckdNetworkKey` keeps its value, nothing that derives
  reads `ckdNetworkKeySource` or the new field (only the manifest's rules, `deploy-check` and `fetch-ckd-key` do), and
  the display-safety refactor changes no accepted or refused text (proven below), and no text enters a derivation.

**1. Who runs the pinned CKD key's sources (the Tech Lead 2026-11-24).**
- **What reads the sources, and the quorum**: `ckdNetworkKeySource` is written and read only by `fetch-ckd-key`
  (`scripts/lib/ckd.ts`) and checked by the schema; no page, Worker or derivation reads it (the vault trusts the pinned
  `ckdNetworkKey` alone). `readCkdKeyAgreed` asks every source at once and needs **all of them**: each must answer,
  report the env's chain, the same block hash at the lowest final height and the same key; one failure or one
  disagreement and nothing is written. So the quorum is unanimity, and a wrong pin needs every source to give the same
  wrong answer. What that costs an attacker is the number of different operators behind the sources: two hosts of one
  operator are one answer (sandbox-dev's three hosts on three domains are two operators: FastNear runs
  `test.rpc.fastnear.com` and `rpc.testnet.near.org`, dRPC `near-testnet.drpc.org`).
- **The rule** (`ckdSourceOperatorProblems`), on any network but testnet: a pinned key (one that isn't the `UNSET`
  placeholder) needs its `ckdNetworkKeySource`; every recorded host needs an operator in `ckdSourceOperators`; and the
  recorded hosts must be run by **at least `MIN_CKD_SOURCES` (3) different operators**, compared by D903's
  `operatorKey` (NFKC, lower case, letters and digits only). Why three and not two: under unanimity two different
  operators already stop one lying operator (the other must agree), but D100 asked for three independent providers so
  that two colluding or compromised providers still can't pin a wrong key, and every login trusts that pin; three keeps
  D100's margin, now counted by who runs the hosts instead of by domain. A further source of an operator already
  counted adds nothing and costs nothing (it must agree too). The registrable-domain rule (≥ 3 domains) stays,
  everywhere. On testnet the map is optional, may name some hosts only, and may name one operator for several hosts;
  sandbox-dev names none and is accepted as it is.
- **The shape**: an object from host to operator name (`{"near-testnet.drpc.org": "dRPC"}`), not D903's parallel
  array. Keys follow `rpcs`' host rule (lower-case host, optional port, no scheme, path or query); values D903's
  operator-name rules (trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, a letter or digit, display-safe); 1 to 20 hosts
  (`MAX_CKD_SOURCE_OPERATORS`). Why a map: `fetch-ckd-key` rewrites `ckdNetworkKeySource` whole on every pin, its hosts
  in the order it read them, so a list inside it would be lost at each re-pin and a list beside it could be silently
  paired with other hosts (a re-pin that swaps one host for another keeps the count, and the old operator's name would
  label the new host and pass); a map can't pair wrongly, stays as it is across a re-pin, and lets a host be declared
  before it is first read. Hosts declared but not recorded are allowed everywhere (that is how one is declared ahead)
  and count for nothing.
- **Checked three times**: the schema (its `superRefine`); `deploy-check` again on a production network, whatever groups
  it reads (as for D903's rule); and `fetch-ckd-key` on a production network **before reading anything**, on the hosts
  it is about to read ("Declare each host's operator in envs/<env>.json ckdSourceOperators (or pass --rpc of another
  operator) first."), so it never writes a manifest the schema would then refuse. Found while building:
  `ckdSources` crashed on a network with no well-known list (`WELL_KNOWN_RPCS` has testnet only); it now tops up from
  none there.
- **Not in force until the schema admits another network**: `network` accepts only `testnet`, so on every manifest
  that loads today the rule returns nothing; it runs in tests on hand-built production manifests (sandbox-dev's, parsed,
  with `network: "mainnet"`, as D903's are). **A declaration checked in review, not proof**: "FastNear" and "FastNear
  Inc", "fastnear.com" or a name with a look-alike letter compare as different operators; a reviewer reading the
  manifest is the check that each name is who really runs the host.

**2. The text-safety checks in one shared module (a refactor, no behaviour change).**
- **Where**: `packages/core/src/display-safe.ts` (`isDisplaySafeLine`, `isDisplaySafeText`), already core's one rule
  (D118), now also served on the subpath `@hana-id/core/display-safe` (it imports nothing, so a Worker or
  `@hana-id/env` uses it without core's root entry, the reason the copies existed). Why core: it is the lowest package
  every caller can depend on; it has no workspace dependencies and is shipped to partners, so it can't depend on a
  private package, and a new package would have to ship as a fifth SDK package for core to use it. `@hana-id/env` had no
  workspace dependencies and now depends on `@hana-id/core` (no cycle: core depends on no workspace package; checked on
  every `package.json`). The source now spells the default-ignorable code points as escapes (it held the invisible
  characters themselves). The shipped SDK gains one entry point (after PR 133's review marked internal in `packages/core/README.md`, not a
  supported export: the Tech Lead's point A below); its declarations
  carry no internal reference (the pack check's rule), and after PR 133's review the shipped file says nothing about
  which workspace packages call it (that is here and in the module's test).
- **Moved onto it** (each was a copy of the same rule): the app-name rule's `isDisplaySafeName`
  (`packages/console-core/src/names.ts`, used by `normaliseAppName` and the console's users screen), the email issuer's `isDisplaySafeLine` (`apps/email-issuer/src/bytes.ts`), and D903's operator names
  (`packages/env/src/schema.ts`, so `ckdSourceOperators` too). Core's own callers already used it.
- **Proof of no change**: every existing test passes unchanged (one test's list of core's export paths gains the new
  subpath). New tests compare the rule as it was against the module on every code point U+0000 to U+10FFFF (lone
  surrogates included), alone and inside text: core's two patterns (`packages/core/test/display-safe.test.ts`) and the
  operator names' own pattern (`packages/env/src/index.test.ts`); these two are what guards the rule now (mutating one
  escape in the module fails 4 tests in each). Console-core's every-code-point test against core became a tautology
  once its rule was core's, so after PR 133's review it checks that `isDisplaySafeName` is core's function itself, as
  the email issuer's test does. A differential run against `next`'s own files (each old module or its
  exact lines, beside the new ones) on 3,392,336 inputs (every code point alone, between letters and between two lines,
  and 50,000 random strings from controls, the invisible set, Latin, CJK, Arabic, emoji with joiners and selectors,
  tags, private use and lone surrogates): **no difference** for core's `isDisplaySafeText` and `isDisplaySafeLine`,
  console-core's `isDisplaySafeName`, `normaliseAppName` and `normalisePartnerAppName` (1,164,112 inputs), the email
  issuer's `isDisplaySafeLine`, the operator character rule, and the whole manifest schema with each string as
  `rpcOperator` (242,621 inputs, issues and messages compared) and in `apiRpcFallbackOperators` (48,525).
- **Left as they are, each a different rule today (not unified; to confirm, below)**: the partner label text rules
  (`packages/core/src/partner-labels/text-rules.ts`) are an allow-list (Latin letters, digits, space and `- ' ’ , &`),
  stricter than any deny-list, and carry no copy; nothing to share. The others refuse a different set:
  - `packages/brand/src/email.ts` `MAIL_INVISIBLE_SOURCE` (strips text for mails; the admin's mails use it too): the
    shared set, controls but tab and LF (**CR stripped**, which multi-line text allows), and the braille blank
    **U+2800** too. Left in brand, which has no dependencies (the design system every page and Worker uses).
  - `scripts/lib/admin-sql.ts` (the admin CLI's app names, before the API's `appNameProblem`): Cc Cf Co Cn Zl Zp. It
    **refuses unassigned code points** (engine-dependent, which the shared rule avoids on purpose) and **accepts the
    default-ignorables the API's rule refuses** (U+034F, the Hangul fillers U+115F U+1160 U+3164 U+FFA0, U+17B4 U+17B5,
    U+180B to U+180F but U+180E, every variation selector): a name the CLI writes can be one the console's rename
    refuses.
  - `packages/env/src/evm-sponsor.ts` and `apps/api/src/evm/sponsor-config.ts` (a sponsored target's staff label): Cc
    Cf Zl Zp: **accept private use and the default-ignorables**.
  - `apps/demo/src/near.ts`, `apps/stamps/src/ui/text.ts` (per character, replacing with U+FFFD): Cc Cf Co **Cs** Zl
    Zp: **refuse lone surrogates** (the shared rule accepts them) and accept the default-ignorables.
  - Hand-written lists: `packages/console-core/src/labels.ts` `labelNote` (a staff note on a label), `evm-relay.ts`
    `isPlainNote`, `apps/admin/src/plain.ts` (`plainString`): narrower ranges (no private use, tags, variation selectors
    or Hangul fillers; `plain.ts` keeps tab, LF and CR and only the bidi controls of Cf).
- **For the Tech Lead**: (A) the subpath `@hana-id/core/display-safe`: **(a)** internal and unlisted, as built (the
  export exists for Journear's own packages; `packages/core/README.md` says it is not part of the supported SDK surface
  and may change without notice; the pack check still loads it), or **(b)** a supported partner export (a row in the
  README's table and in the partner guide). (B) **Three different operators on production, not two**: with unanimity
  two operators already stop one liar; three keep D100's margin against two colluding.
- Note 2026-11-24 (D906): both points **confirmed by the Tech Lead** ("confirm all"): (A) **(a)**, the subpath
  `@hana-id/core/display-safe` stays internal, not a supported partner export (as built); (B) three different operators
  for the pinned CKD key's sources on production, kept at three. The list below stays open.
- **To confirm** (decided while building): (1) the field name `ckdSourceOperators` and its shape, a map from host to
  operator rather than a list beside `rpcs`; (2) a pinned key on production needs its recorded source (else the rule
  had nothing to count), the `UNSET` placeholder exempt so a new env's first pin can load (`fetch-ckd-key` and the rule
  now both read "placeholder" as "contains UNSET", as the build does); (3) declared but unrecorded hosts allowed
  everywhere, and partial maps on testnet; (4) `fetch-ckd-key` refusing before it reads on production, and topping up
  from no list on a network without one; (5) `@hana-id/env` depending on core; (6) whether each rule left as it is
  should take the shared rule: the admin CLI's app names (it accepts what the API refuses, refuses unassigned code
  points), the sponsor labels (private use, fillers), the demo and stamps pages (fillers; lone surrogates refused
  there, accepted by the shared rule), the mails (U+2800 and CR), the staff notes' lists; (7) the shared rule accepting
  a lone surrogate (unchanged: not Cc, Cf, Co, Zl or Zp), which an operator name in a manifest can hold through a JSON
  `\ud800` escape; (8) the two checks built after review, below: one operator per host on every network, and a
  manifest refused for a key twice in one object.
- **Built after PR 133's independent review** (2026-11-24; nothing blocking; address impact none and no behaviour
  change confirmed by the reviewer's own runs), decided while building, **to confirm**:
  1. **One host, one operator** (`operatorConflictProblems`, `packages/env/src/schema.ts`; was open point 6): the
     review showed sandbox-dev on `mainnet` with `apiRpcFallbackOperators: ["FastNear", "dRPC"]` (naming
     rpc.testnet.near.org FastNear) and `ckdSourceOperators["rpc.testnet.near.org"] = "Pagoda"` passing the count with
     three operators where there are two. Now every field that names who runs a host must agree (`operatorKey`) when
     two name the same host: `rpcOperator` (`rpc`'s host), `rpcFallbackOperator`, each `apiRpcFallbackOperators` entry
     (when the count matches) and each `ckdSourceOperators` key; D903's fields are checked against each other too. **On
     every network** (a contradiction is wrong on testnet as well); only names declared on both sides are compared, so
     every committed env (none declares an operator) validates. In the schema and again in `deploy-check`. D903's test
     manifests named rpc.testnet.near.org both "Lava" (`rpcFallbackOperator`) and "FastNear" (the first API fallback,
     the same URL): their fixtures now name it "Lava" in both (`packages/env/src/index.test.ts`,
     `scripts/test/deploy-check.test.ts`), what D903's tests assert unchanged.
  2. **A manifest with a key twice in one object is refused** (`duplicateJsonKey`, `packages/env/src/json-duplicates.ts`;
     `loadEnv` through the new `parseManifest`): `JSON.parse` keeps the last of two equal keys silently, so
     `{"a": "FastNear", "b": "FastNear", "c": "dRPC", "b": "Lava"}` read as three operators while a reader sees FastNear
     twice, and review is the control for these declarations. Any object at any depth; keys compared as JSON reads them
     (`"a"` and `"\u0061"` are one); the error names the path ("envs/sandbox-dev.json has a key twice in one object
     (network): …"). Every committed env has none and parses to exactly what it did (tested). The scripts that edit a
     manifest's text load it through `loadEnv` afterwards, as before.
  3. The tests each fail when their check is removed (run by hand: the schema's and `deploy-check`'s cross-check, its
     comparison, the duplicate refusal and the detector's comparison, console-core's identity, a mutated escape in the
     module, `includes` turned back to `startsWith`).
- **Not verified**: nothing here is in force on any manifest (the schema admits only testnet); `fetch-ckd-key`'s
  production path ran only against fake endpoints; no real mainnet RPC operator list was drawn up; the differential run
  covers the callers above, not the rules left as they are.

     until their sign-in ends.": confirmed (D902, amendment 3).
  4. "Show email sharing" offered even when the line already says nothing is shared: confirmed (D901, (e)).
  5. Reduced motion: the loading spinners switch to a slow pulse instead of standing still: built here (below; D905,
     "To confirm" 7).
  6. The two developer messages reworded to "Gas prices are too high for sponsorship right now, try again later" (D905,
     text 2 and item 3a): confirmed.
  7. Three different operators for the pinned CKD key's sources on production: kept at three (D904, (B)).
  8. `@hana-id/core/display-safe` stays internal, not a supported partner export: confirmed (D904, (A) (a)).
- **5. The loading spinners under reduced motion.** D905 ended every animation of the brand's components at once, so a
  spinner became a still three-quarter ring, and a still ring can look like a frozen page during a long wait (the
  partner console's sign-in button, its email sign-in test's Execute button, the stamps site's working slot). **Decision:** under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the loading spinners stop turning and
  fade instead: `animation: jp-spin-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite !important`, with `@keyframes
  jp-spin-pulse{50%{opacity:.6}}`, so the ring goes from full opacity to 60% and back every 2 seconds, for ever. Opacity
  only: no turning, no movement, no change of size; the ring keeps its shape and stays where it is (its gap at the
  right). Everything else keeps D905's rule and ends at once.
- **The values**: 2 s a cycle (slow enough not to read as motion, quick enough to show within a moment that the page is
  working); 0.6 at the middle, because the brand's spinners as shipped sit in a disabled button (`.jp-btn[disabled]`,
  `opacity:.45`), so the ring's real opacity is the product of the two: with 0.4 it ran between about 45% and 18%, with
  0.6 between about 45% and 27%; ease-in-out (no sudden step).
  Nothing flashes: one soft fade out and back in every 2 seconds.
- **Which spinners**, all of the product's own stylesheets searched (every `@keyframes`, `infinite` and `rotate(` in
  the repo outside `legacy/`): the brand's three (`.jp-btn .spin`, `.jp-provider .spin`, `.jp-iconfield .spin`), used by
  the partner console (its sign-in and Execute buttons), the stamps site (the collect button) and available to every
  page; the demo's own (`.progress::before` while signing in, `.stage::before` on the NEAR card); the stamps site's own
  (a working slot's line, `.pp-slot[data-status='working'] .pp-text::before`). The sign-in and approval windows and
  Passport Home (`packages/web`) and the admin portal draw no spinner today (their `base.css`, `home.css` and
  `app.css` rules cover a modal, placeholders, tabs and nav links: unchanged).
- **How each wins over the rule for everything**: the brand's spinner rule sits in the reduced-motion block after the
  rule for everything and is more specific (`.jp-btn .spin`, two classes, over `[class^="jp-"] *`, one), both
  important, so it wins in every browser whatever the order. The demo's rule is `body .progress::before, body
  .stage::before` (one type more than the brand's `[class*=" jp-"] *::before`, for when they sit inside a `.jp-card`);
  the stamps' is `.pp .pp-slot[data-status='working'] .pp-text::before, .pp .jp-btn .spin` (over its own `.pp *`). The
  partner console's own rule (`*`, no specificity, duration only) outranks nothing and names no animation, so the
  brand's pulse stays; a comment there says to keep it so. Each consumer uses the brand's exact declaration (its tests
  read it from `components.css`).
- **Found while building**: the demo's reduced-motion `.result { animation: none; }` lost to `.result`'s own animation
  later in the same file (same specificity, later wins). Inside a `.jp-card` the brand's rule still ended the fade at
  once, so nothing moved; it is now `body .result` and stops it wherever it sits.
- **Not a spinner, unchanged (still ends at once)**: the loading placeholders (`.jp-skel` and Passport Home's
  skeleton lines), the stamps site's marching outline on a working slot (`pp-march`; its line's spinner pulses), the
  inked stamp, toasts, the modal, fades, shakes, the radio's dot and every transition.
- **JavaScript**: nothing picks a spinner's behaviour from `prefers-reduced-motion`. The two scripts that read it
  (Passport Home's tab scroll, smooth only without it; the stamps site's inked animation, skipped with it) concern
  neither spinners nor this change.
- Tests: the brand's (the spinner rule's three selectors and its one declaration, the keyframes changing opacity alone,
  each spinner selector outranking all 12 of the rule for everything, the spinners still turning without reduced
  motion, every rule that uses `jp-spin` being one the pulse names, nothing else using the pulse or keeping a repeat,
  the placeholder the only other repeat); the demo's, the stamps site's and the partner console's (their rules as
  above, the brand's declaration, nothing else moving); e2e in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: Home (the three brand
  spinners run `jp-spin-pulse` for ever, 2 s, ease-in-out, keyframes of opacity alone; the radio's dot and `.jp-skel`
  once in under 1 ms; without reduced motion `jp-spin` with keyframes of transform), the demo (both spinners inside a
  `.jp-card` pulse, the results' fade is `none`), the stamps site (a working slot's two spinners pulse, its outline's
  march is `none`). Removing the brand's spinner rule fails three of the brand's tests.
- Address impact: none (no path, key or derivation changed). No user-facing text added or changed.
- **To confirm** (decided while building): (1) the values: 2 s a cycle, 60% at the middle, ease-in-out, for ever; (2)
  the loading placeholders (`.jp-skel`, Home's skeleton lines) stay still, as they are not spinners (they could pulse
  the same way); (3) the stamps site's marching outline on a working slot stays still (its spinner pulses beside it);
  (4) the demo's `.result` fix above.
- Not verified: a real device with its own reduced-motion setting (only Playwright's emulation, in Chromium, Firefox and
  WebKit); how the pulse looks on the partner console's and the stamps site's real buttons (checked by computed styles,
  not by eye); nothing deployed.
- Note 2026-11-25 (D917): to-confirm (1), the values (2 s a cycle, 60% at the middle), and (2), the loading
  placeholders staying still, **confirmed by the Tech Lead**. (3) and (4) were not put: still to confirm.

## Journear Passport inside Sodax's SDK, switched on from Sodax's partner portal (branch `docs/sodax-sdk-integration`), 2026-11-24

Investigated on `docs/sodax-sdk-integration` (from `next`), docs only: no product code changed, nothing deployed. Number
note: D907 and D908 are taken by `feat/payment-account-name`; D909 is the next free number after both. Current state
and plan: `docs/sodax-sdk-integration.md`.

Context: the aim of the investigation is our SDK inside Sodax's SDK, so that a Sodax partner switches Journear
Passport on from Sodax's partner portal. That aim is what was investigated, not a decision.

### D909. One wallet across every Sodax partner site; who vouches for their web addresses is parked; Sodax's other chains are planned, not excluded
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: **the shared wallet decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24**; the long run chain coverage is
  **the Tech Lead's direction 2026-11-24** ("we'll possibly need to cover as many chains that Sodax supports as
  possible in the long run"), with no dates; everything else **investigated, not built** · Built: nothing ·
  Relates to D39, D51, D99, D235, D428, D429, D436, D492, D706, D708, D720, D774, D776
- **Decided** (the Tech Lead, 2026-11-24): Sodax partners get **one wallet across all their sites**: one app per Sodax
  partner, every app in Sodax's organisation and on Sodax's one scope. A user who signs in with the same Google
  account (or email) on two Sodax partner sites gets the same Stellar, EVM and NEAR addresses on both. Test and live
  apps never share a scope (D51), so this is one test scope now and a separate live scope, with different addresses,
  later.
- **Direction** (the Tech Lead, 2026-11-24): cover as many of Sodax's chains as possible in the long run, no dates.
  Every Sodax chain we don't cover is listed as planned, not as an exclusion; order and cost in
  `docs/sodax-sdk-integration.md` ("Chains").
- **Parked:** who vouches for each partner's web address (the allowed origin that lets a site use the shared wallet),
  until it is settled with Sodax.
- **Standing decisions, written down here:** auto-approved Sodax swaps stay deferred (D708). The Tech Lead,
  2026-11-12: NEAR is not planned for the Sodax swap (first written here).
- **Verified on 2026-11-24** (a scratch page with `@sodax/wallet-sdk-react` 2.2.0, `@sodax/sdk` 2.2.0 and our SDK
  from this branch's sources, on the local stack at port base 4930, driven by Playwright in Chromium with the pretend
  Google; every request to a non-loopback host was answered locally or blocked, none was made and nothing was
  broadcast; the harness stays out of the repository because it is a one-off check against a third-party package,
  not a product test). Each point says whether it was tested, read in Sodax's 2.2.0 source, or inferred:
  1. **EVM needs no Sodax-specific code** (tested): once `createHana({ evm })` runs, Sodax's wallet list shows
     "Journear Passport" with its icon, also when the SDK is created 2 s after Sodax's kit mounted (our client
     announces itself when created and on every EIP-6963 request; wagmi keeps listening). Sodax's own connect opens
     our sign-in; Sodax's own `EvmWalletProvider` sends through our provider. A test key on Base (8453) is refused
     with `4100` before any window; a test app with the mainnet demo on shows the approval with the red banner, and a
     reject comes back to Sodax as `4001`.
  2. **Stellar needs code in Sodax's kit.** Read in 2.2.0's source: Sodax's `StellarXService` builds its own Stellar
     Wallets Kit 1.9.5 with `allowAllModules()` and takes no option to add a module; its discovery runs at 0, 100 and
     500 ms. Tested: a connector passed in `config.STELLAR.connectors` is replaced by that discovery; pushing
     `HanaIdModule` into the kit's private module list before discovery made "Journear Passport" appear, and then
     connect and Sodax's `StellarWalletProvider` worked; pushed 2 s later, it never appeared. Tested: in both cases
     tried (a test key's public-network refusal, and the user's Reject in a demo approval) Sodax's Stellar provider
     reported "Failed to sign transaction" and dropped our error code.
  3. **The shared wallet works as decided** (tested): two test apps on one scope, on two origins: the same Google
     account got the same EVM and Stellar addresses on both. Read in our code: nothing in the sign-in or approval
     windows says the wallet is shared with other sites; only Passport Home lists the apps that use a wallet.
  4. **Not on npm** (tested): `@hana-id/core`, `web` and `sodax` answer 404 on the public registry (D706 keeps
     tarballs). Measured: our SDK adds about 114 kB minified (36 kB gzip) for `createHana`, the Stellar Wallets Kit
     module and the Sodax adapters; our test page with Sodax's wallet kit was 11.3 MB minified.
  5. **No service-to-service API exists** (read in our code): apps are created only by Journear staff
     (`AdminRpc.createApp`, the admin CLI); a partner's origin additions need an on-chain owner's fresh Google sign-in
     (the console's step-up).
  6. **The mainnet demo** (read in our code) is a staff switch per test app in a dev testnet env (sandbox-dev is one),
     Base and Stellar's public network only, $9.99 per transaction, no daily cap, never auto-approved. Nothing stops
     staff switching it on for many apps of one scope; on a shared wallet that puts one wallet's real funds within
     reach of every such site.
- **Recommended, for the Tech Lead to decide:** keep the mainnet demo a staff switch per partner app, out of Sodax's
  portal switch (D428 rejected letting partners set it); build the service API only once origin vouching is settled.
- Address impact: none now. The one secret the NEAR MPC gives each user is enough to derive a key on every curve a
  Sodax chain needs (HKDF derives the keys from it, in the browser). Each new chain adds a new (name, curve) pair: no
  existing address moves, but that pair's name, curve and key rule are final from the day it ships (from the address
  freeze if it ships before it). Bitcoin's Taproot rule and whether Injective reuses the EVM key are part of what
  becomes final. To be called out when built (CLAUDE.md).

## A payment's account name in the partner's sentence (branch `feat/payment-account-name`), 2026-11-24

From `next` @ 7ecaae60, with `next` @ adc40e36 (D906) and 9750f25f (D909) merged in; not merged, not deployed. Numbered D907 and D908 when they were built; they sit after D909, which reached `next` first.

### D907. A matching classic payment's sentence ends with Journear's joining word and the address book's name of the destination: "Stamp Rally says: pay the fare to Coffee Club till"
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: the direction **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** ("go with A"); the joining words, the
  forms with and without a phrase, the length rule and the editor's words decided while building, **to confirm** (the
  list at the end) · Amends D896 (after PR 123's review: "No partner 'To' row … the address book's name is not shown
  for a classic payment"), with a row of "Superseded or amended" · Built: `packages/core/src/partner-labels/words.ts`
  (`PAYMENT_DESTINATION_WORDS`, `paymentDestinationWord`), `match.ts` (`destinationParts`, used by `build` for a match
  and by `previewLabelDocument`), `schema.ts` (`sentenceTextFits` for a payment); `packages/web/src/auth/render-labels.ts`
  (`labelBox`'s comment: the window renders the new parts with its existing value styling, no code change);
  `apps/console/web/src/labels/Editor.tsx` (`BOOK_NAME_LABEL`, `BOOK_NAME_HINT`, `PAYMENT_NAME_NOTE`). Tests:
  `packages/core/test/partner-labels-payment-name.test.ts` (new), `partner-labels-match.test.ts`,
  `partner-labels-preview.test.ts`; `packages/web/test/auth/render-labels.test.ts`, `approve-page-labels.test.ts`;
  `apps/console/web/test/labels.test.tsx`; `apps/e2e/tests/partner-labels-window.spec.ts`,
  `partner-labels-console.spec.ts`.
- **Why (found by the Tech Lead in a hand test, 2026-11-24).** The console's "Your accounts" asked for each account's
  "Its name for users", but for a classic payment the name went nowhere: the matcher built `destination`, and the
  window's box, by D896's review decision, has no partner "To" row (one beside Journear's own "To" row could be read as
  Journear's). The editor's preview read "Stamp Rally says: pay" with no name.
- **The Tech Lead's choice (A):** the name goes inside the partner's sentence, in the partner's box, for a matching
  classic payment; "These are {App}'s words, not Journear's." stays under it; Journear's own "To" line with the full
  address stays exactly as it is, above the box; still no partner "To" row.
- **What is built.** For a payment that matches, core appends two parts to the sentence: Journear's joining word for the
  verb (`word`, plain text in the window) and the destination (`value`, path `destination`, source
  `partner_address_book`), so the window sets the name apart as every partner value (its own outlined span, direction
  isolated, `span.partner-value.partner-words`). Only when the destination's base account is an exact address-book
  entry (an M… form of a listed account counts, as before; the destination keeps the request's M… form). Never for the
  amber or red cases (no match carries no parts). The address is never replaced: Journear's "To" row is unchanged, the
  box still holds no account, and the plain form keeps the account whole beside the name.
- **One source.** The window (`labelBox` over `parts`), the console's preview (the window's own `renderApproval`), the
  plain form (`sentencePlainText`, `labelLinePlainText`: "pay the fare to “Coffee Club till” (G…)") and
  `previewLabelDocument` (the API's preview, the staff screen, the partner notice and diff, the console's "Reads:" line
  and Labels tab) all come from `destinationParts`. The preview uses the first listed G… account, as the console's
  example payment does. `partnerAttribution` is unchanged.
- **The joining word, by verb** (as first built; **narrowed after PR 135's review, below**: a payment may now use only
  pay, send, donate, deposit, repay, lend, buy, stake and bid) (`PAYMENT_DESTINATION_WORDS`; the same word with or
  without a phrase): "to" after pay, send, donate, deposit, sell, lend, repay, withdraw, unstake; "from" after buy and
  borrow; "with" after bid, stake and swap. Each says the named account is where the value goes, the seller or lender, or the other side; never that the
  user receives from it. The 17 soft verbs need none: the parser refuses them for a payment (a test holds the table to
  exactly the verbs a payment may use). The exact sentences, with phrase "the fare" and name "Coffee Club till": "pay to
  Coffee Club till" / "pay the fare to Coffee Club till"; likewise "send to", "donate to", "deposit to", "sell to",
  "lend to", "repay to", "withdraw to", "unstake to"; "buy from Coffee Club till" / "buy the fare from Coffee Club
  till", "borrow from …"; "bid with …", "stake with …", "swap with …". The name always ends the sentence, after the
  partner's own parts: "pay the fare for 1042 to Coffee Club till". Rejected: "pay {name}" with no phrase (the proposal
  found it reads wrong; also "buy {name}" would read as buying the account); one "to" for every verb ("buy the ticket to
  Coffee Club till" reads as a ticket to somewhere).
- **The name's rules.** It was already held to every text rule, as the phrase is (`partnerTextProblem`, role
  `addressName`, 32 characters): the Latin allowlist, Journear's names, the reviewed lists' names, claim words, "you" and
  "your", negations, the window's words, number, money, phishing and ownership words, other currency and brand names,
  numbers and address-like runs, jargon; two names equal after folding are refused. No new text rule at first (PR 135's
  review added several, below). **One existing rule
  newly applies:** D892 item 3's 40 partner characters per sentence (the phrase plus its one partner-worded value) now
  counts the longest address-book name for a payment (`sentence_text` at `intent.object`, shown beside the phrase). A
  tightening of the parser: a payment document already over it is refused by the vault and the window (the plain
  window); partner labels are on in no checked-in env.
- **Misleading names, as the rules stood when first built** (tested; PR 135's review tightened them, below): refused: "your own account" and "Your till" (`text_you`), "My
  account", "Own till" (`text_ownership`), "Journear", "Journear fees", "Passport top up", "Hana desk" (`text_brand`),
  "refund", "Refund desk", "Verified till", "Safe account", "Official till" (`text_claim`), "GBX3KQ2MABCDEFGH", "GBX3
  KQ2M", "0xabc" (`text_looks_like_address`), "GD6R...QRSL" (`text_character`), "till 12345" (`text_number`), "USDC
  till" (`text_reviewed_name`), "Coinbase" (`text_other_name`), "Wallet", "Support desk" (`text_phishing`), "Tap here"
  (`text_ui_word`), "Rewards till" (`text_money_word`), "Nobody" (`text_negation`). Allowed, and could still mislead:
  "a friend", "the user", "Escrow", "Return to sender", "GABC" (four characters), the app's own name; another listed
  account's name exactly is refused, but a look-alike spelling ("Coffee Club tiIl" beside "Coffee Club till") passes.
  What bounds them: the name is inside the attributed box, Journear's "To" row shows the real address, and every listed
  account is the partner's own.
- **The editor.** The field is now "Name shown to users", with a hint per kind: payments "Shown at the end of your
  sentence in place of the account’s address, as “pay the fare to Coffee Club till”. Journear’s own To line still shows
  the full address. Up to 32 characters."; NEAR and Soroban "Shown in your sentence in place of the account’s address,
  as “Coffee Club till”. In a row, the full address shows under it. Up to 32 characters." Under a payment's sentence
  parts: "Journear ends the sentence with the name of the account the payment goes to, from your accounts, as “to Coffee
  Club till”."
- **Address impact: none.** Display only: nothing signed, decoded, derived or digested changes; no key or path is
  touched; the approval digest is unchanged.
- **To confirm** (decided while building): (1) the joining word per verb above, the same with or without a phrase, and
  "pay to Coffee Club till" with no phrase; (2) the name counting in the sentence's 40 partner characters (the
  alternative: not counting it, which lets a payment's sentence hold up to 62 partner characters); (3) the plain form
  keeping the account beside the name in the staff screen, the notices and the console's lines ("“Coffee Club till”
  (G…)"); (4) the editor's label, hints and note; (5) borrow, withdraw and unstake with a payment read oddly whatever
  the word ("borrow from Bike Shed till" while paying it): narrowing a payment's verbs is an option, not built; (6)
  whether duplicate names should also be compared on the look-alike skeleton (i/l, rn/m), as app names are: proposed,
  not built.
- Note 2026-11-25 (D917): **confirmed by the Tech Lead**: (2) the name counting in the 40 partner characters; (5)
  the narrowed verbs (pay, send, donate, deposit, repay, lend, buy, stake, bid; sell, borrow, withdraw, unstake and
  swap refused, built after PR 135's review); (6) look-alike names as duplicates (built after the review); the hints
  of (4). Still to confirm: (1) the joining word per verb and "pay to Coffee Club till"; (3) the plain form; the
  field's label and the note of (4).

### D908. The Request labels form: "See an example" for payments, the memo label's hint, and how soon the email goes out
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: the three changes **approved by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** ("yes all"); the wording, the

#### After PR 135's review (2026-11-24): what changed, for D907 and D908, each decided while building, **to confirm**
1. **HIGH: the example's account had a public secret key.** `GBBQI276…SS55TZP` is the account of the seed 32 × 0x1f,
   so anyone can sign for it, and it exists on the public network under a stranger's control. A partner submitting the
   example unchanged would have listed it as its own, and payments to it would have lost the red "not one of the
   accounts listed" line. Now: "See an example" leaves the account empty, so the form's own problem ("Add one of your
   own Stellar accounts here (G…).", a new plain message for an empty account in core's parser) holds Review until the
   developer adds one; the console names no account of its own (`EXAMPLE_ACCOUNT` removed). And core's parser refuses,
   in any Stellar or Soroban address book on any app, the API's and the console's alike (so the advanced text can't list
   one either), every account whose secret key is public as far as Journear knows: the account of each seed made of one
   repeated byte (32 × 0x00 to 32 × 0xff, the usual test and example seeds) and the all-zero public key
   (`packages/core/src/partner-labels/public-accounts.ts` `isPublicSeedAccount`; code `public_account`, "This is a test
   or example account whose secret key is public, so anyone can use it: list one of your own accounts."). Stored as the
   first 4 bytes of each of the 257 public keys (2 KB in the SDK, a test derives them again from the seeds); about one
   chance in 16 million that an unrelated account shares a prefix and is refused too. **The tests:** every fixture
   account an address book lists is now a random public key no one has the secret key of (the labels fixtures' own
   `OTHER` in core, the vault labels test's till, the e2e and console tills, the staff screen's preview), not a
   test-aware exception in the rule; the shared Stellar fixtures, whose accounts only pay or are paid (some feed
   derivations the tests pin), keep their seeds. Not covered: a public seed of another shape (a hash of a
   known word, a published test key elsewhere): the list is a first filter, the real guard is that the console never
   suggests an account.
2. **MEDIUM-HIGH: verbs that say the money comes the other way.** A classic payment (the user sends money) now refuses
   sell, borrow, withdraw, unstake and swap (`PAYMENT_VERBS`; `bad_verb`, "\"sell\" doesn’t fit a payment, where your
   user sends money to your account: use pay, send, donate, deposit, repay, lend, buy, stake or bid."), with every soft
   verb as before. The console's verb list shows them as "(not for a payment)". **The final table**, the same word with
   or without a phrase: pay, send, donate, deposit, repay, lend → "to" ("pay to Coffee Club till", "pay the fare to
   Coffee Club till"); buy → "from" ("buy the fare from Coffee Club till": the user pays the seller); stake, bid →
   "with" ("stake with Coffee Club till", "bid the fare with Coffee Club till"). Reconsidered with the smaller set:
   deposit kept "to" ("deposit with" reads as a bank deposit, less clear about where the money goes); lend kept "to".
   **New text rules** (whole words, compared as the other lists, after "you/your"):
   - `text_self`, in an object phrase and an account's name: me, us, we, our, ours, user, users, this, sender, senders,
     holder, holders, back, return, returns, returned, reversal, reversals, reversed, undo, undone, chargeback,
     chargebacks ("Don’t write “me”, “us”, “user”, “this”, “sender”, “back”, “return”, “undo” or similar: the window says
     who pays whom itself.");
   - `text_says`, in a phrase and a name: says, said, saying ("Don’t write “says”: the window says who is speaking.");
   - `text_outcome`, in a name: the order number's lure words (paid, done, success, complete, approved, claimed,
     winner, …, with plurals) and thanks, thank, welcome, settled, cleared, confirmed ("Don’t name an account with an
     outcome (paid, done, success, complete, approved, …): the window says what happens."). Not in a phrase or an
     enumeration label (the stamps' "Fare paid" is an honest enumeration label);
   - `text_authority`, in a name: police, government, govt, gov, revenue, customs, court, courts, ministry, embassy,
     irs, hmrc, lhdn, and "tax office" and "taxman" (adjacent words joined) ("Don’t name an account as an authority
     (police, government, tax office, customs, court, …): users could think they must pay it."). A bare "Bank" was
     already refused (`bank` is on the other-names list);
   - on the other-names list (every role): Phantom (until now left out on purpose as an everyday word; an honest
     "Phantom of the Opera tickets" is now refused), Bitget, Wend (a whole word: "Wendy’s till" passes).
   - Judged too broad, not added: "treasury" ("Club treasury" is an honest name); "tax" alone ("Sales tax account");
     "this" and "return" were asked for and added, though they refuse honest phrases such as "this ticket" and "the
     return fare".
3. **MEDIUM: only the first account's name was in the preview and the diff.** Now every account of the address book is
   listed with its name and whole address in every preview (core `addressBookLines`: "Account “Coffee Club till”
   (G…)"; the API's preview carries them as `accounts`), shown on the staff screen, in the partner's security email,
   on the console's review page and Labels tab, and under the editor's "Reads:" line (with "The example pays your
   first account; a payment to another ends with that account’s name instead." when there are several). The API's diff
   has one line per account, keyed by its account (`(account) G…`): a rename is "changed", re-pointing a name to
   another account is one "removed" and one "added". Tested in the API (`labels-document.test.ts`), the staff screen,
   the email, the console and the e2e waiting card.
4. **LOW-MEDIUM: stored documents.** A payment document valid before can now fail the 40 characters, a verb or a
   word, and a still-valid one now shows the account's name, which nobody saw when it was reviewed. The rules are not
   weakened. `docs/operations.md` ("Before switching partner labels on in an env") now requires, before
   `partnerLabels.enabled` goes on anywhere, re-parsing every stored version waiting or in force with the build's
   parser, and having any that fails or reads differently proposed again (and the old one blocked with a note). No admin
   command exists to extend, so the check is described by hand. Today there is nothing to check: migration 0025 is
   applied nowhere and labels are on in no env.
5. **LOW: the email's timing on sandbox-dev.** The deployed sandbox-dev admin Worker runs its notices every 30 minutes
   (the triggers set by hand on 2026-11-19) until its next normal deploy. The wording "usually within a few minutes"
   stays; `docs/operations.md` now says the admin Worker must be deployed with this change, which restores the
   five-minute trigger.
6. **LOW: focus after the example's question.** After "Keep what I typed", focus returns to "See an example"; after
   "Replace with the example", to the first account (which now needs filling). Tested in the console unit tests and the
   e2e.
7. **LOW: screen readers hear the name run into the sentence.** Not built: the window sets every partner value (the
   phrase, an enumeration label, an id, an amount) apart only visually, with nothing announced between them; adding
   hidden quotation marks around the name alone would make it announced differently from every other partner value,
   and around all of them would change what is announced today. For the Tech Lead: whether to announce a boundary
   (hidden quotation marks, or "named …") around every partner value in the window's sentence.
8. **LOW: name rules.** Two names that read alike are one name: compared on core's name skeleton (look-alike letters,
   "rn" as "m", spaces dropped) with digits read as letters and i/l and u/v as one (`partnerLookalikeKey`): "Coffee Club
   tiIl", "Coffee Club ti11", "CoffeeClub till" and "Modem till" beside "Modern till" are refused as duplicates. The
   authority words, Phantom, Bitget, Wend and "says" are in item 2.
9. **INFO:** no decision number in the comments added or changed in core (they ship in source maps).
- Address impact: none (display, the parser's refusals and console text; nothing signed, decoded or derived changes).
- Note 2026-11-25 (D917): **confirmed by the Tech Lead**: item 2's verbs and its new text rules (`text_self`,
  `text_says`, `text_outcome`, `text_authority`, with honest phrases such as "this ticket" refused); item 7 left as it
  is (no boundary announced around partner values); item 8's look-alike duplicates. Still to confirm: items 1, 3, 4,
  5, 6 and 9; in item 2, Phantom, Bitget and Wend on the other-names list, the words judged too broad, and the joining
  word per verb.

## The partner platform: the Tech Lead's answers of 2026-11-24 (branch `docs/partner-platform-spec`)

From `next` @ 6f51a033; docs only, not merged, not built, not deployed. Numbered D913: parallel branches may take D910
to D912. Revised after PR 139's security review (same day).

### D913. Real-money demo swaps stay a staff switch per partner app; each app on a shared scope gets its own User ID, with linking for the scope's owner and staff; npm and the licence parked; the small items started; the platform API built on the origin recommendation; the spec's eleven questions answered
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: points 2 to 6 and the eleven answers **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24**; question 8
  **to re-confirm with the Tech Lead before piece P9 is built** (the security review advises against it); the design
  that carries them out **proposed, not built** (`docs/partner-platform-spec.md`, with nine further open questions)
  · Relates to D39, D51, D127, D346, D356, D394, D428, D704, D708, D760, D835, D894, D909 · Built: nothing
- **In the Tech Lead's words** (2026-11-24). Point 1 (one wallet across all of the network's partner sites, one app
  per partner, all on the network's one scope and organisation) is D909, unchanged.
  - **2.** Real-money demo swaps (the mainnet demo, D428) stay a **staff switch per partner app**, for a short pilot
    list, and are never part of the network's portal switch. D428 is unchanged.
  - **3.** Each app on a shared scope gets **its own User ID** in the identity token (today `sub` is per scope, so
    every partner backend gets the same ID for a person). Then the question: "if Sodax wanted to diagnose one user
    across multiple Sodax partner apps, is it still possible? some sort of linking is needed?"
  - **4.** npm publishing and the core package's licence: parked.
  - **5.** Start the small items now (naming the six EVM chains our approval window doesn't name yet; a "this wallet
    is also used on other apps" line in our windows; both on other branches) and build the portal connection on the
    recommendation of point 6, to be adjusted after the Tech Lead has talked to the network.
  - **6.** Who vouches for a partner's web address (parked in D909): build on the recommendation for now, adjust
    later. The recommendation: the network vouches for every partner site it adds (it is the customer and the scope's
    owner); a site added through the network's backend takes effect only after the usual guarded-change delay (at
    least 24 h on a production network; 60 s on the dev testnet env) with the usual announcement to the org's
    security contacts and its cancel link; Journear keeps a per-partner-app off switch and can revoke the network's
    credential at once; every call is audited.
- **The spec's answer to the linking question** (proposed, in plain words): yes. The person's IDs on each of the
  network's apps all come from one ID of the person on the network's scope, which only Journear can compute. So the
  network's owners (in our partner portal) and Journear staff (in the admin portal) can look a person up by any one
  app's User ID or Support ID and see that person's IDs on the network's other apps, each lookup audited, rate limited
  and alerted on in volume; a partner can't turn its IDs into another partner's. **Honestly:** on a shared wallet the
  wallet addresses are the same on every site and are in every identity token, so partners who compare addresses can
  match users anyway. Per-app IDs remove the ready-made join key (the shared `sub` and Support ID) and protect a
  partner that forgets to check `aud`; they are not privacy between partners. Existing apps keep their IDs exactly:
  only apps created on a scope that staff mark for it get per-app IDs.
- **The spec's eleven questions, answered by the Tech Lead** ("yes all" to the recommendations, 2026-11-24):
  1. requests are signed with ECDSA P-256 (ES256) only;
  2. the network's on-chain owners may register a platform key themselves, and it still waits the delay;
  3. platform keys expire after one year;
  4. no user lookup from the network's backend for now: linking is in our partner portal only;
  5. the cross-app view of one person is for the network's owners only, not its viewers;
  6. keep per-app User IDs, knowing partners can still match people by wallet address;
  7. a per-app Support ID as well;
  8. staff may restore, without the 24 h wait, an origin a stolen key removed. **The security review of PR 139 advises
     against it** (finding M1: a restore that skips the delay is the one path by which an origin comes into force
     with no time to object, and a staffer tricked by someone posing as the network could use it). **To re-confirm
     with the Tech Lead before P9 is built**; if built, only in the review's narrowed form: only an origin whose
     removal was by the `platform` actor, on the same app, in force when removed, within 7 days; only once that key
     is revoked or the org's platform switch is off; with a notice to the org's security contacts and owners before
     the origin is back; and with two people (one staff member proposes, a second approves, each with a reason);
  9. report a partner origin with no sign-in for 60 days to the network and staff, as a later piece;
  10. tell users in Passport Home that the network can see which of its sites they use;
  11. staff may **not** expedite a platform-proposed origin.
- **Proposed in the spec, not the Tech Lead's own words** (built on his answers above): per-org request signing
  rather than OAuth client-credentials tokens (follows from answer 1), with the env, method, path, body hash, a
  timestamp and a single-use nonce signed; registration by an owner of each scope or by staff with the owner's
  acceptance or a second staff member; the platform's reach (its own org, its scopes, test only, only apps it
  created) held in the SQL of every read and write; auto-approve refused in code on a shared scope before the
  platform is on for any org; the quotas, data model, endpoints and build plan. PR 139's security review findings
  (H1 to H3, M1 to M9, L1 to L16) are folded in as requirements, each tied to the piece it gates.
- **Open, for the Tech Lead** (the spec's N1 to N9, each with its recommendation): the platform acts only on apps it
  created (no); the same model for the future live scope (yes, with its own review); a platform minimum delay on dev
  envs (24 h everywhere but `local*`); auto-approve refused in code on shared scopes (yes); owner acceptance of a
  staff-registered key (yes); the "also used on other apps" line before the platform is on (yes); the network giving
  one partner another's ID (no); platform test apps in Passport Home on dev envs (yes); key notices to the org's
  owners (yes).
- Address impact: **none.** Nothing touches the contract, a key, a path or an address derivation. The per-app User ID
  is an off-chain pseudonym; its layout becomes final, for the partners that store it, from the day it ships.
- Note 2026-11-25 (D914): question 8 **re-confirmed by the Tech Lead as no**: staff may not restore a removed origin
  without the wait; nothing of the narrowed form above is built. The spec's N1 to N9 ("Open, for the Tech Lead"
  above) are **answered** in D914: all as recommended except N3, where a platform-proposed origin comes into force at
  once when an owner of the organisation confirms it, else after a 24 h platform minimum; platform keys follow a rule
  of their own (four eyes on a real-money setup). Point 6's "60 s on the dev testnet env" no longer holds for a site
  the network's backend adds: it waits at least 24 h unless an owner confirms it.

### D910. The approval window names HyperEVM, LightLink, Redbelly Network, Kaia, Hedera and Robinhood Chain, with their own coins, as real-money networks
- Date 2026-11-24 · Status: **approved by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24** as one of the small Sodax items to start now;
  built · Relates to D39, D44, D428, D853, D909
- **The gap** (`docs/sodax-sdk-integration.md`, "Chains"): our one EVM key works on all 14 EVM chains Sodax's SDK lists
  (`@sodax/types` 2.2.0), but the window named only 8. For the other six it said "A network Journear doesn't know
  (no. 999)" and "of this network's coin".
- **Built:** `KNOWN_EVM_MAINNETS` and the native coin table in `packages/core/src/networks.ts` gain the six. Every
  surface that names a chain reads them through `evmChainInfo`: the approval summary (the network row, the send, the
  value sent with a call, the fee, "None of your … is used", the one-time setup line), the window's amount headline
  (a plain transfer only), the auto-approve consent screen (its chain heading and limits; on Hedera the raw number in
  brackets says "weibars" instead of "wei", and the partner guide says Hedera's limits are in weibars, 18 decimals, not
  tinybars, 8), the demo page's label. The explorer table (`EVM_EXPLORERS`) and the verified Sodax contracts already had all six.

  | Chain id | Name shown | Coin | Window label |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 999 | HyperEVM | HYPE | "HyperEVM (real money)" |
  | 1890 | LightLink | ETH | "LightLink (real money)" |
  | 151 | Redbelly Network | RBNT | "Redbelly Network (real money)" |
  | 8217 | Kaia | KAIA | "Kaia (real money)" |
  | 295 | Hedera | HBAR | "Hedera (real money)" |
  | 4663 | Robinhood Chain | ETH | "Robinhood Chain (real money)" |

- **Verified on 2026-11-24**, each against the chain's own docs and the public registries (ethereum-lists/chains'
  `_data/chains/eip155-<id>.json` and chainlist.org's `rpcs.json`), not only Sodax's package:
  - **999 HyperEVM, HYPE, 18 decimals.** Hyperliquid's docs (hyperliquid.gitbook.io, "HyperEVM"): mainnet chain ID
    999 (testnet 998), "HYPE is the native gas token on the HyperEVM", 18 decimals. chainlist.org: 999 "HyperEVM", HYPE,
    18. **Conflict:** ethereum-lists gives 999 to "Wanchain Testnet" (WAN), and that network is live: its registry RPC
    answered chain ID 999 on 2026-11-24. Named HyperEVM anyway: one chain ID means the same signature is valid on both
    networks, so "real money" is the safe label, and HyperEVM is the chain Sodax and its users mean. For the same
    reason 999 must never be added to `TEST_EVM_CHAINS` (a test app could then sign a transaction good on HyperEVM):
    `packages/core/test/networks.test.ts`, "999 is never a test chain", enforces it.
  - **1890 LightLink, ETH, 18.** LightLink's docs (docs.lightlink.io, "Live Networks"): Phoenix Mainnet, chain ID 1890,
    currency ETH (Pegasus testnet 1891). ethereum-lists and chainlist.org: "Lightlink Phoenix Mainnet", ETH, 18. Shown
    as "LightLink", the plain name; Phoenix is the mainnet's own name and stays out of the label.
  - **151 Redbelly Network, RBNT, 18.** Redbelly's docs (vine.redbelly.network/environments): "Redbelly Network
    Mainnet", chain ID 151, currency RBNT (testnet 153). ethereum-lists and chainlist.org: "Redbelly Network Mainnet",
    RBNT, 18.
  - **8217 Kaia, KAIA, 18.** Kaia's docs (docs.kaia.io, "Connecting MetaMask"): "Kaia Mainnet", chain ID 8217, symbol
    KAIA; "Kaia native coin": 1 KAIA is 10^18 kei. ethereum-lists and chainlist.org: "Kaia Mainnet", KAIA, 18.
  - **295 Hedera, HBAR, 18 in a transaction.** Hedera's docs (docs.hedera.com/evm/development/json-rpc): mainnet 295
    (testnet 296, previewnet 297); the relay "uses 18 decimals (weibars) for HBAR on the wire" for a transaction's value,
    balances and the gas price. docs.hedera.com/evm/differences/hbar-decimals: 1 tinybar is 10^10 weibars; inside a
    program `msg.value` is in tinybars (8 decimals); a nonzero value under one tinybar is refused by the relay.
    ethereum-lists and chainlist.org: "Hedera Mainnet", HBAR, 18. Sodax lists HBAR with 8 decimals: its token amounts
    are in tinybars, as programs see them. The window shows HBAR only from a transaction's value and its fee fields
    (weibars, 18 decimals, as every other named chain), never from an amount inside a program's call, so the 18 is
    right where it is used. Not checked: Hedera's own account and fee rules through its relay (as D909 noted); they are
    the network's behaviour, not its name.
  - **4663 Robinhood Chain, ETH, 18.** Robinhood's docs (docs.robinhood.com/chain/connecting): network name "Robinhood
    Chain", chain ID 4663, currency ETH, explorer robinhoodchain.blockscout.com (testnet 46630). ethereum-lists and
    chainlist.org: "Robinhood Chain", ETH, 18.
  - Every one of the six: `mainnet: true` in `@sodax/types` 2.2.0's `baseChainInfo`, with the same chain ID, and its
    native token's symbol the one above.
- **What naming changes, and what it doesn't.** `KNOWN_EVM_MAINNETS` and the coin table are for display only. Checked
  every reader: the summary, the amount headline, the consent screen, the demo page's label (`evmChainInfo`), and the
  EVM delegate deploy script, which refuses a known mainnet (it now refuses six more, stricter). Nothing else keys off
  a named chain: a test app's rule is `TEST_EVM_CHAINS` (unchanged, 13 chains; none of the six's test networks added),
  gas sponsorship takes only `TEST_EVM_CHAINS` chains (the manifest schema and the vault), the mainnet demo stays Base
  and Stellar's public network (`MAINNET_DEMO_EVM_CHAINS` = [8453], tested), auto-approve policies list their own
  chains, and known tokens and verified contracts have their own tables (no token added). An unknown token, program,
  call or spender on a named chain reads exactly as on an unnamed one (tested). The partner labels' list of coin words
  a label may not use (`NATIVE_COINS` in `partner-labels/text-rules.ts`: NEAR, ETH, XLM, BTC) is not keyed by chain and
  does not hold BNB, POL, S or AVAX either; left as is.
- **Tests:** core (`networks.test.ts`: the six names, coins and labels, each still refused for a test app and named a
  mainnet by `mainnetOfRequest`, their test networks still unnamed, 999 never a test chain; `approval-summary.test.ts`: the send, fee and
  network, and an unknown call, an unlisted token's transfer and an unlimited approve on each, read as on an unnamed
  chain); web (`approval-design.test.ts`: the amount headline and the consent screen's heading and limits, Hedera's in
  weibars); sodax (new
  `networks.test.ts`: every EVM chain in the installed `@sodax/types` is named, as real money, with Sodax's coin symbol,
  Hedera's 8 against our 18 pinned, the mainnet demo still Base only; a `@sodax/types` upgrade that adds an EVM chain
  fails it until the chain is checked and named); e2e (`approval-summary.spec.ts`: each of the six injected into a live
  app's real window, its name, coin and fee, the plain-words check, and an unknown call there still the red line).
- **To confirm (the Tech Lead):** the name "HyperEVM" holds "EVM", a word the plain-wording rule keeps out of what
  users read (D853: "Ethereum-style" instead); it passes the check only because the word is inside the name.
  "Hyperliquid" is the plainer alternative (the project's name users know). Left as "HyperEVM" for now, the chain's
  own name in its docs and in chainlist.org; the Tech Lead decides. Also open: the approval window's folded details
  still write a Hedera value's raw number as "wei" (`render-approval.ts`, the value and fee rows), where the consent
  screen now says "weibars".
- Address impact: none (display only; no key, path or derivation changes).

- Note 2026-11-25 (D917): the name "HyperEVM" **confirmed by the Tech Lead** (it stays). The folded details' "wei"
  for a Hedera value was not put: still open.
