- **The words** (the same everywhere): "This wallet is also used on 2 other apps." ("on 1 other app." for one), then
  "See which". Opened: the other apps' names, one per line, each quoted in the partner-words box (the marks inside
  the box with the name, tight against it: 2026-11-25, below), at most 5, then "and 3 more apps" ("and 1 more app") for the
  rest, then "Any of them can ask you to approve payments from this wallet, so check who is asking each time." Plain
  words only (D853; `auth/shared-wallet.ts` is on the sign-in pages' word scan). "Apps", not "sites": the windows call
  partners apps everywhere else ("Signing in to {App}", "From {App}").
- **Where:** right under who is asking, outside its box: the box holds the partner's own name and web address, and
  this line is Journear's. In the sign-in window: under "Signing in to {App} at {web address}" on the method chooser,
  on the way to Google, and on the email step's own screens (the address, the code, the waits between them, the
  chooser again after a cancelled Google screen); not on the follow-up screens after Google (they can be about another
  wallet or a link) and not in the key window's "Confirm it’s you". In the approval window: under the "From {App}" box,
  before the account line, on a request and on the automatic approvals consent screen; never in the partner's labels
  box. Muted small text like the account line, a native `<details>` (no colour box, no icon), so it comes before every
  warning and doesn't compete with one: the red and amber boxes keep their order and colours (tested: the same alerts
  in the same order, all after the line). Before, the screens had nothing here; screenshots for the Tech Lead at 390 and
  1280 px, light and dark, before and after (`apps/e2e/tests/shared-wallet.spec.ts`, `HANA_SHOTS_DIR`).
- **Who counts** (`readOtherApps`): the other apps of the app's scope (one scope is one wallet) that are not deleted,
  not suspended (any suspension bit, or the legacy status), have had a sign-in (`first_login_at`; after PR 141's
  review, below) and have at least one web address in force now. An app with
  no address in force (none yet, or only one still in its waiting period) can't be used by any site, so it doesn't
  count; it counts from the next read after its first address takes effect. **Test and live apps:** they never share a
  scope (D51), so a test app's line counts test apps only and a live app's live apps only; nothing else to decide. An
  app no one has signed in to yet is neither counted nor named (it counts from the read after its first sign-in), as
  Passport Home doesn't list it to people outside its scope (D462). Names oldest first (`created_at`, then id),
  as stored; the vault and the windows cut each one as Passport Home shows it (`homeAppName`: trimmed, at most 60
  characters then "…", one with a control, direction-changing or invisible character, or over 200, becomes "Unnamed
  app"; the app still counts), and they reach the page only as text nodes.
- **How it reaches the windows:** `GET /v1/app` carries `otherApps: {count, names}` only on the vault's own read
  (`Origin: VAULT_ORIGIN`), from one D1 statement on every read (no cache, as `partnerLabels`; phase `otherApps`); `count`
  0 for an app alone; a failed read leaves the field out (log `other_apps_unavailable`). Its cost: one more statement
  on the vault's read (H9's minute read included, `apps/api/test/home-devices.test.ts` now counts 8 and 9), about 3 rows
  read for an app alone and about 2 more per other app and its addresses (through the `apps_scope_id` index). The vault keeps the latest
  answer that had it (an answer without it, a failed read, keeps what it knew) and passes it, only when `count` is at
  least 1, in `hana:auth-params` (from the login's own read, as the logo) and in each `hana:approve-request` and
  `hana:consent-request`, all posted to the auth origin only. The login popup hands it to the email step in its own
  sessionStorage context. Freshness as the logo's: the vault's latest `GET /v1/app` answer (read when the vault starts
  and kept; read again whenever the vault re-reads the app for something else: the policy, raw signing, the mainnet
  demo, partner labels; a login uses the answer the vault holds). A request that reaches the approval
  queue before the vault's first answer had the field waits for one read, once, at most 3 s (`OTHER_APPS_WAIT_MS`), and
  then goes with the line or without it: never blocked or failed by it (`approvals.ts` `otherAppsWait`). The request's
  first check (`enqueue`) and its send leave the field out rather than lose the request should the popup refuse it.
- **An app alone sees no change at all:** the vault sends no field, the windows draw nothing, and each screen is the
  older one element for element (tested in unit tests and in the stack: no `.shared-wallet`, no new text, the box
  followed by the buttons or the account line as before).
- **The partner page never learns it:** the field is served only to the vault's origin (a partner page's own
  `GET /v1/app`, and the export window's on the auth origin, never carry it); the vault never puts it in anything it
  sends the partner page (its port, events, errors); the windows are cross-origin to the partner page. Proved by
  `packages/web/test/vault/other-apps.test.ts` (no name, nor the field, in any port message or window message to the
  partner) and `apps/e2e/tests/shared-wallet.spec.ts` (the partner page's own `GET /v1/app` and every message it
  received on its window and its MessagePorts, recorded from before its scripts ran, carry neither the field nor the
  other app's name, while both windows show it). Residual, as for `partnerLabels` and the consent status: the Origin
  header is a browser's guarantee, so a client outside a browser that forges `Origin: VAULT_ORIGIN` with the app's
  publishable key (which is public) can read the count and the names of the apps on that key's scope that have had a
  sign-in. (Corrected after PR 141's review: this branch first said they were "names users see in the windows and
  Passport Home anyway", which was wrong for apps no one had signed in to, which Passport Home hides from strangers.)
- **The stack:** every app the specs make is on the `e2e` scope unless it names another, the hosted demo's and the
  stamps site's included; the stack's mocked /v1/login records no first sign-in, so none of them counts and their
  windows show no line (the stamps spec's checks of the line, added first, were taken out again). The new spec uses
  scopes of its own and marks the apps that should count `launched`.
- **Not built:** a Google-only app's sign-in window goes straight to Google, and any app can send it straight there
  too (`hana.login({method: 'google'})`, `login-page.ts`), so the line shows only for the moment before Google's page;
  the chooser is where it stays on screen, and the approval window is the screen relied on; a tab left open keeps the count it read until the
  vault reads the app again (an app added meanwhile shows from then); a consent to automatic approvals given while the
  scope had N apps isn't asked again when another joins (auto-approved Sodax swaps stay deferred, D708).
- **A gate for the partner platform (D913):** `docs/partner-platform-spec.md` makes this line a condition of the
  platform switch (its question N6, answered yes by the Tech Lead 2026-11-24; its build order: "The platform switch
  stays off for every org until P0 is deployed, N3 is decided and, per N6, the "also used on other apps" line has
  shipped"). So this line must be deployed and live in an env before the partner platform is switched on for any
  organisation there; merging this branch alone doesn't meet the gate.
- **Address impact: none** (display and one read of D1; nothing signed, decoded or derived changes).
- **To confirm** (decided while building; (1), (3), (4), (6) and (7) **confirmed by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25**, the
  section at the end): (1) the words, "apps" and "payments" included, and the "may" line below; (2) the placement,
  right under who is asking and outside its box, on the screens listed above; (3) the counting rule: not suspended, not
  deleted, a web address in force, and a sign-in recorded (this last part follows PR 141's review and the main session's
  recommendation; the D462-exact alternative, apps no one has signed in to shown only on a read that carries a valid
  live share of a user of the scope, is not built); (4) the cap, 5 names then "and N more apps"; (5) the names quoted in
  the partner-words box; (6) the kept answer's 24 hours, and 0 never kept; (7) the "may" line's words.

#### After PR 141's security review (2026-11-24): what changed, each decided while building, **to confirm**
1. **MEDIUM (M1): a hostile partner page could hide the line in its own approval window.** `GET /v1/app` counted every
   caller from one IP in one window (`<appId>:config:minute`, the plan's 20 a minute), the partner page's reads and the
   vault's alike; the vault's first read comes after it reports ready, and a request that found no answer went without
   the line. A page that read its config 20 times a minute before creating the SDK made every approval open without
   it. Fixed three ways: (a) a Journear page's own read (the vault's or an auth page's, `caller.page`) counts in a
   window of its own, `<appId>:config:hana:minute`, with the same cap, so the partner page's reads can't use it up; that
   one window serves the vault's policy, raw-signing, consent, share and other-apps reads alike (tested: 20 partner reads
   from one IP, the 21st refused, the vault's and the export window's still answered with the apps); (b) the vault
   keeps its last answer that named other apps in the vault origin's localStorage (`hana.other-apps.<appId>`, the vault
   frame's own storage in the partner site's partition, which the partner page can't read or write), with when it was
   read. **A kept answer never proves "alone"** (corrected the same day after an automated check of the first fix, which
   also kept a count of 0: an app joining the scope later could then be hidden behind an old "alone" while a hostile page
   blocked the reads): a count of 0 is never kept, and a fresh read of 0 deletes the entry. **Staleness rule:** a kept
   count of 1 or more is used only while younger than **24 hours** (`OTHER_APPS_KEPT_MS`, on the vault's
   server-corrected clock: about the longest a vault session lives, the contract's 24 h less 10 min, so it covers one
   sign-in's tabs and the next day's return while an answer that may be stale, an app added or removed since, is never
   shown longer; it can only over-warn or under-count, never hide the line); one older, from the future or unreadable is
   deleted; the next successful read replaces it; one entry per app id (overwritten, never appended), so it can't grow
   without bound. (c) When the vault has no fresh read in this session and nothing kept, a request waits once (3 s) and
   then the windows get `otherAppsUnknown` and say **"This wallet may also be used on other apps."** in the same place
   and style, with no "See which". **Only a fresh successful read saying 0 shows nothing.** So an app alone on its
   wallet shows nothing in the normal case; its users see the "may" line only when the vault's reads failed (refused,
   late or without the field) in that vault session and the 3 s wait ran out (the sign-in window too, when its read had
   no field). The sign-in window takes the vault's knowledge the same way. Reproduced and covered:
   `packages/web/test/vault/other-apps.test.ts` (a fresh 0 shows nothing; every read refused with 429: a new tab shows
   the kept apps and names; a fresh 0 before (nothing kept) or an older kept 0 plus a failed read: the "may" line; a kept
   answer past 24 hours is ignored and deleted), `apps/api/test/other-apps.test.ts` (the exhaustion attempt) and
   `apps/e2e/tests/shared-wallet.spec.ts` (the vault's reads routed to 429 in the browser: the stack doesn't enforce rate
   limits). Residual: a partner page can still load many vault frames to use up the vault's own window from one IP;
   the kept answer and the "may" line cover that, and a kept answer can then be up to 24 hours old.
2. **MEDIUM (M2): apps no one had signed in to were counted and named**, showing an unreleased app's name to anyone who
   opened a window on any site of the scope and undoing D462. Now only apps with `first_login_at` count, in the count and
   the names. The residual above corrected.
3. **LOW (L1):** the "Not built" note now says any app, not only a Google-only one, can send the sign-in window straight
   to Google, so the approval window is the screen relied on.
4. **LOW (L2): a name could read as Journear's words** (an app named "and 40 more apps", or an instruction). Each name
   is now quoted and set in the approval window's partner-words box (`.shared-wallet-apps .partner-words`, the style of
   partner values in the labels box), still text only; "and N more apps" stays Journear's, unboxed.
5. **LOW (L3):** the API test asserts the status of a partner-origin read with the vault's other headers (200, no
   field); the e2e disclosure test now also drives the consent window for automatic approvals and a rejected request's
   error event. Unit-only: the export window's read (it never asks for the field), the email step's screens and the
   follow-up screens' absence of the line, a malformed kept entry, and the API's failed-read path.
6. Screenshots retaken (closed, open, and the "may" line in both windows; 390 and 1280 px, light and dark).

#### Confirmed by the Tech Lead (2026-11-25), and the quotation marks' spacing
- **Confirmed:** the Tech Lead answered "ok for A to E" on 2026-11-25 (in full "ok for A to E except E's 17, what
  does it mean …?"; E's 17 is about D914, not this line; the whole list and answer are in D917). Group A, its items 1
  to 5, was this PR's five points: 1. the main words, "This wallet is also used on 2 other apps." with "See which" and
  its note ("Any of them can ask you to approve payments from this wallet, so check who is asking each time."); 2. the
  neutral fallback "This wallet may also be used on other apps."; 3. only apps someone has signed in to are counted
  and named; 4. at most 5 names, then "and 3 more apps"; 5. the answer remembered for 24 hours (a count of 0 never

  of the review's section, are confirmed. Not among the five, so still decided while building, **to confirm**: (2) the
  placement and (5) the quoted partner-words box.
- **The quotation marks' spacing** (seen in the screenshots: “ Stamp Trail ” read with gaps, because the marks sat
  outside the box and its padding and border came between them and the name): the marks now sit inside the box, in the
  box's one text node with the name (`auth/shared-wallet.ts`), as the consent screen shows a policy's label in its
  quotation marks; a long name that wraps keeps them on its first and last line, and a right-to-left or mixed-script
  name keeps them at the outer ends (the box isolates its direction). What screen readers hear is unchanged (each item
  still reads “Stamp Trail”), the name is still a text node only, and no words changed. Tested:
  `packages/web/test/auth/shared-wallet.test.ts` (each item is the box alone, the box one text node starting and ending
  with a mark) and `apps/e2e/tests/shared-wallet.spec.ts` (`marksHugNames`: both marks drawn inside the box's own line

## The partner platform: the Tech Lead's answers of 2026-11-25 (branch `docs/platform-answers`)

From `next` @ 0b99ec12; docs only, not merged, not built, not deployed. Numbered D914: D912 is held by an open pull
request, D915 and D916 by two branches being built at the same time. Revised the same day with the Tech Lead's rule on
platform keys, their answer on the fresh sign-in, and PR 142's review.

### D914. The partner platform spec's N1 to N9 answered: a platform-proposed web address is in force at once when an owner of the organisation confirms it in the portal, else after 24 h; a new platform key the same way, with four eyes on a real-money setup; staff may not restore a removed web address without the wait
- Date 2026-11-25 · Status: N1, N2 and N4 to N9 **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25** as recommended; N3 **decided
  by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25, differently from the recommendation**; who may confirm (with the fresh sign-in)
  **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25**; how a platform key comes into force **decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25**
  (four eyes on a real-money setup); question 8 of D913 **re-confirmed by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25 as no**; several
  points of the design **proposed while writing the spec, to confirm with the Tech Lead** (listed below); two points
  **open**; the design that carries them out **proposed, not built** (`docs/partner-platform-spec.md`, A3, A14, A15,
  pieces P2 and P10) · Relates to D51, D89, D127, D235, D356, D428, D909, D913 · Built: nothing
- **How the questions were put, and the Tech Lead's words** (2026-11-25), in this order:
  1. The spec's N1 to N9 as a table numbered 1 to 9, plus "The re-check (earlier question 8)" with the recommendation
     no, and the line: Reply "yes all, restore no" to accept everything. The Tech Lead answered **"yes to all except
     for number 3"**: the recommendations accepted for N1, N2 and N4 to N9, the recommendation on the restore being
     no. "Number 3" is N3, not D913's question 3. The reply "Noted: yes to the other eight, and no to staff restoring
     without the wait" drew no objection.
  2. After a discussion of N3 and of the risk that an owner's Google account is taken over: "I think this is too
     pessimistic, if an owner's own Google account is taken over, then more is at risk (other than these stuff), his
     banking etc"; then, to the rule below, "go".
  3. On platform keys: asked whether a 24 h wait would block an urgent key rotation, then "what if we made this also
     use confirmation emails? is it secure enough?", then, to the key rule below, "sounds good, I like this "four
     eyes" rule, please suggest this for future decisions similar to this. also ok with this."
  4. On who may confirm, after it was explained as the owner proving it is them with Google at the moment they press
     Confirm, the same bar as adding a web address by hand today: "ok with fresh sign in when confirming".
- **The Tech Lead's answers:**
  - **N1. No:** the platform sees and changes only apps it created; the network's own site and staff-made apps stay
    outside its reach.
  - **N2. Yes:** the same credential model will serve the network's future live scope, with a separate key and its
    own security review before any live app is opened to it.
  - **N4. Yes:** auto-approve is refused in code for every app on a shared scope (piece P0).
  - **N5. Yes:** a key that staff register works only once the network's owner (or a second staff member) accepts it.
  - **N6. Yes:** the "also used on other apps" line ships before the platform is switched on for any org.
  - **N7. No:** the network may not give one partner another partner's ID for the same person.
  - **N8. Yes:** platform-created test apps are listed in Passport Home on dev envs, like any app a person used.
  - **N9. Yes:** key-registration notices also go to the org's owners.
  - **Question 8 (D913): now no.** Staff may not restore, without the wait, an origin a stolen key removed, as PR
    139's security review advised (M1). The spec's A14 now says only that it was considered and refused, and why;
    piece P9 keeps only the 60-day unused-origin report.
  - **N3, decided differently from the recommendation** (which was a 24 h minimum for platform-proposed origins and
    keys in every env except `local*` test envs). The rule, the same in every env except `local*` test envs:
    1. An origin proposed by the platform starts waiting and is announced as today.
    2. It comes into force **at once** when an owner of the organisation confirms it: signed in to the console,
       pressing Confirm on a page that shows the app and the origin. The email's Confirm link only opens that
       console page; a GET never confirms (mail scanners open links, emails get forwarded). The cancel link stays
       one click from the email with no sign-in, as today.
    3. If nobody confirms it, it comes into force after a platform minimum of 24 h, unless cancelled.
  - **The accepted risk**, in the Tech Lead's words above: one owner's Google account taken over can propose nothing
    through the platform, but it can confirm an origin a stolen platform key proposed, or both can be in one
    attacker's hands, and then an attacker's origin is in force at once.
  - **Who may confirm** (origins and keys alike): a console member whose role is `owner`, who is an on-chain owner
    (`Owner::Oidc`) of the app's scope (for a key: of each scope it names), with a fresh Google sign-in when pressing
    Confirm.
  - **Platform keys:**
    - A newly registered platform key is announced as today (security contacts, owners, the alias) and waits the
      24 h platform minimum, unless confirmed. Revocation stays immediate.
    - **Test setup** (dev envs; not `local*` test envs, which keep their own short delay): any owner who meets the
      confirmation bar may confirm it in the console, including the owner who registered it, and it is in force at
      once. That is "no wait" in practice for an owner-registered key. Accepted there because an owner can already
      add an origin by hand with the 60 s delay, test funds are worthless, and partner testing and an urgent rotation
      need the speed.
    - **Real-money setup** (production envs): **four eyes.** The confirming owner must be a different person from
      the one who registered the key; the registrant's own confirmation is refused; with no second owner's
      confirmation the key waits the 24 h. An org with one owner therefore always waits.
    - The same mechanics as the origin confirmation: the email's link only opens the console page; a GET never
      confirms; the confirmation is a console route the platform key can never reach; the one-click cancel from the
      email stays.
  - **Direction** (the Tech Lead): suggest the "four eyes" rule for future decisions of the same kind.
- **The spec's reading, not the Tech Lead's words:** a stolen platform key alone gets only the slow, cancellable path.
  What still bounds the accepted risk: the approval window names the app and its web address; the "also used on other
  apps" line; staff suspend an app at once; origins can be removed at once; the confirmation's notice to every owner,
  the security contacts and Journear, with its removal link (proposed).
- **Proposed while writing the spec, to confirm with the Tech Lead** (`docs/partner-platform-spec.md`):
  1. **"A different person"** for the four-eyes rule (A3): a different console user (one console user is one Google
     account), a different verified Google `sub`, a different email address (compared without dots and `+tags`), and
     an owner of the org since before the key was registered. The user and `sub` checks are in the database write
     (a CHECK and the commit predicate); the email and owner-since checks in the console's server. What it can't
     catch: one person with two separate Google accounts, both owners long enough; two owners who collude; a
     compromised console server skipping the email and owner-since checks.
  2. **A staff-registered key** (A3, N5): an owner's acceptance counts as its confirmation (on a test setup because
     any owner may confirm; on a real-money setup because a staff registration and one owner's acceptance are two
     people), and the key is in force once its announcement is sent; a key a second staff member approved waits the
     24 h unless an owner confirms it.
  3. **The confirmation's notice carries a one-click removal link** valid 7 days (A15), because the announcement's
     cancel link no longer works once the origin is in force and security contacts need not be console members;
     and the same for a key: a one-click revoke link (A3).
  4. **Waiting key registrations** are cancelled by staff's switch-off of the org and by a freeze (A3).
  5. **Staff proposals on a shared scope**: staff's `addOrigins` on a platform-created app or a flagged scope waits
     the platform minimum, with no waiver and no expedite (A15). If the Tech Lead prefers today's staff path there,
     it is recorded as an accepted risk instead.
  6. **The org's owners on a platform proposal's announcement** (A15, A6), as N9 decided for key notices, since
     only owners can confirm.
  7. **The `local*` guard** (A15): the exemption from the 24 h minimum holds only for a `local*` env on testnet with a
     loopback API, enforced by the manifest schema, the API's start-up check and the deploy wrapper; today only the
     name is tested.
- **Advice to the network** (proposed): keep a second key registered and in force as a standby (the two-credential
  quota exists for this), so an urgent rotation needs no wait at all.
- **Open (not decisions):**
  - To revisit at mainnet preparation: on a production env an origin a member adds by hand in the console still waits
    the full guarded-change delay (at least 24 h), while an owner's confirmation of a platform proposal is in force at
    once. So confirming the platform's proposal is faster than adding one by hand, and an on-chain owner who also
    holds the platform key could use the platform to skip the production delay. Not changed now.
  - With the key rule, on a real-money setup one taken-over owner account alone still can't get a key in force at
    once; on a test setup it can.
- **Proposed in the spec as requirements** (from the design and PR 142's review, not questions for the Tech Lead):
  the confirmation is a console route (`ConsoleRpc.confirmOrigins`, `ConsoleRpc.confirmPlatformKey`, after the
  console's step-up, each nonce with its own label), never a platform route, and refuses every actor but a member;
  only an announced, waiting, unconfirmed platform proposal can be confirmed; a confirmation names 1 to 20 changes of
  one app and one proposing request and writes one `origin.confirmed` row for the set, all or nothing, with the
  proposing key in force, the switch on, the app in the key's reach and not suspended by Journear in the commit
  predicate; each revocation route, expiry, the switch-off and a freeze cancel the key's waiting proposals in the same
  batch; the origins sent with a create are platform proposals; the proposal's email goes to the owners too and
  states the 24 h wait "or sooner if an owner confirms"; the CLI's announce refuses a platform proposal; triggers keep
  a stored earliest in-force time so no writer brings a platform origin or key forward without a confirmation; the
  four-eyes rule held in a `platform_keys` CHECK. The key confirmation is built in **P2** (credentials); the origin
  confirmation in a new piece **P10**, after P2, P4 and P5; each with its required tests and an independent security
  review. The platform switch stays off for every org until P0, P2, the platform minimum (P4) and P10 are built,
  reviewed and deployed, and the "also used on other apps" line has shipped (N6).
- Address impact: **none.** Nothing touches the contract, a key, a path or an address derivation; the confirmations
  and the delays are off-chain records of which web addresses and platform keys may act for an app.
- Note 2026-11-25 (D917): **confirmed by the Tech Lead**: proposals 1 ("a different person"), 2 (a staff key's
  acceptance as its confirmation), 3's removal link for origins, 4 (switch-off and freeze cancel waiting keys) and 6
  (the owners on a proposal's announcement), and the requirement that a revocation cancels the key's waiting
  proposals. Proposal 5 **replaced** by the Tech Lead's "four eyes": a staff proposal on a shared scope is in force at
  once when a second person (another staff member or an owner) confirms it, else after 24 h (D917). Still to confirm:
  proposal 3's revoke link for keys, proposal 7 (the `local*` guard), the standby-key advice.

## Shared-scope rules in code (branch `feat/shared-scope-rules`), 2026-11-25

From `next` @ 0b99ec12, with `next` @ 57e30825 merged in after PR 145's review; not merged, not deployed. Piece P0 of

### D915. Auto-approve is refused in code for every app on a shared scope and every platform-created app; staff mark a scope as shared, one way
- Date 2026-11-25 · Status: **the rule decided by the Tech Lead 2026-11-25** (open question N4 of the spec, answered
  "yes": auto-approve refused in code for every app on a shared scope); built as the spec's P0 row; the points marked
  "to confirm" below were decided while building · Relates to D39, D51, D428, D708, D894, D909, D913 · Built:
  `apps/api/migrations/0026_shared_scope_rules.sql`, `apps/api/src/changes/{admin,apps,settings,drift,views}.ts`,
  `apps/api/src/rpc/admin.ts`, `packages/console-core/src/shared-scope.ts`, `scripts/lib/admin-settings.ts`,
  `apps/console/src/actions.ts`, the console's Signing and Overview tabs, the admin Worker's route and app page
- **Why.** On a scope several partners share (D909), one wallet per person serves every partner's site. A policy one
  partner set would let that partner's site sign, without asking, from the wallet every other partner's site also uses.
  Until now that was a rule kept by hand (`sodax-sdk-integration.md` section 4).
- **Built:**
  - Migration **0026** (API D1; the next free number on `next`): `scopes.app_user_ids` 0/1 (default 0) and
    `apps.created_by_kind` `'hana'`/`'platform'` (default `'hana'`; console-core `APP_CREATOR_KINDS`). Every existing
    row keeps every value (tested). Nothing writes `'platform'` until the platform API (P4); the per-app User IDs that
    will also read the flag are P6.
  - `AdminRpc.setScopeAppUserIds({orgId, scopeId})` → `{changed}`: staff only; one way (no off in the input; already
    marked is no write); `conflict` while any app of the scope has a policy in force, waiting in its columns or proposed
    (an open `policy_set`), in the plan read and the commit predicate; another org's scope `not_found`; one ledger row
    `scope.app_user_ids` ("Scope marked as a shared wallet") listing the scope's apps. The admin Worker's
    `POST /api/scopes/:scope/app-user-ids` calls it from the app page.
  - `proposeChange` in AdminRpc and ConsoleRpc refuses a `policy_set` for an app on a marked scope or created by the
    platform: `policy_invalid`, "Auto-approve is off for apps that share a wallet", before the policy is validated,
    and again in the commit predicate (a scope marked between the read and the write commits nothing:
    `version_conflict`). The console's `policy.set` action refuses it before any sign-in. `admin app:settings` refuses
    a new `--auto-approve` policy in its plan and in its write guard. `--auto-approve off`, `turnOff` and raw signing
    are untouched.
  - The hourly drift check reports any policy, waiting policy or open `policy_set` on such an app (not deleted) as a
    `drift` event `what: 'shared_wallet_policy'` (`source` `policy`, `policy_pending` or `change`), once per finding,
    even when a forged announced change explains it to the other checks.
  - `getApp` answers `sharedScope`, `createdByKind` and `sharedWallet`. The console's Signing tab shows "Auto-approve is
    off for apps that share a wallet. This app uses the same wallet as other apps, so users approve every request
    themselves." instead of the editor, and its Overview stops suggesting a policy; the admin portal's app page shows the
    same words in the policy row with no proposal form, and a "Shared wallet" row (the mark, or "Mark the scope as
    shared" behind a confirmation). "Remove the policy" stays wherever a policy is found.
  - Tests: refused through each of the three paths (AdminRpc, ConsoleRpc with a valid step-up, `app:settings`) for a
    marked scope and for a platform-created app; an unmarked app unchanged on each; the mark refused with a proposed,
    a waiting and an in-force policy, and allowed once removed; both commit predicates (a race injected between the
    read and the batch; the policy predicate of `proposeChange` and the CLI's guard were each removed once to see their tests fail); the drift finding for bare D1 writes
    and for a forged announced change; the migration (defaults, rows unchanged, triggers, CHECK = `APP_CREATOR_KINDS`);
    the console and admin screens hiding the editor; the admin route through the real API.
- **To confirm (the Tech Lead):**
  1. **Database triggers as a backstop**, beyond the spec: migration 0026 refuses un-marking a scope, marking one while
     an app of it has a policy, and any change of `created_by_kind`, whatever writes it. Not added: a trigger refusing
     a policy on a marked app, so a bare D1 write is reported by drift as the spec says rather than blocked.
  2. **A deleted app doesn't hold the mark back**, and drift skips deleted apps as it always has: a deleted app serves
     nothing, can't come back, and can't be turned off (every write on it is `not_found`), so counting its stored
     policy would block the scope for good.
  3. **Raw signing is not refused on a marked scope.** The spec's P0 names auto-approve only. Test scopes already refuse
     raw signing (D39); on a future live shared scope a staff or owner proposal would still go through. Recommend
     refusing it there too when a live shared scope is opened (N2). **After PR 145's review (item 3): only test scopes can
     be marked for now, so this can't arise yet.**
  4. **The vault doesn't refuse to serve a policy found on such an app**: drift reports it within the hour and the kill
     switch removes it. Refusing it in `GET /v1/app` as well would close that hour; not built, as the spec puts the
     bare-write case on drift. **Superseded after PR 145's review (below, item 2): built; no longer to confirm.**
  5. **`admin app:settings` refuses any new policy on a hot D1 without migration 0026** (it can't check the rule
     there); `off` and the other settings still work.
  6. **Where staff mark a scope:** the admin portal has no scope page, so the control is a "Shared wallet" row on each
     app's page (A11 says "on the scope"). ~~It is offered for live scopes too.~~ After PR 145's review: test scopes
     only (item 3).
  7. **The console's scope line of A11** ("Shared wallet: apps here get their own user IDs, and auto-approve is off")
     is not shown: the per-app User ID half isn't true until P6. The console says it on the app's Signing and Overview
     tabs only.
  8. **The drift event's title** stays the kind's "App setting in force without a notice", which reads oddly for a
     policy that did have a notice; a kind of its own needs `security_events` rebuilt, which piece P1 is doing
     anyway. Recommend adding `shared_wallet_policy` as a kind there.
  9. **Operations:** Sodax's scope must be marked before its first partner app; until a scope is marked, only
     platform-created apps are covered.
- **Found in the spec:** A7's SQL puts `apps.partner_bit_by` under a "P0:" comment, but the P0 row and the build plan
  give who holds the partner bit to P4 (L4): left to P4. A11's scope line promises per-app User IDs (P6) and the admin
  portal has no scope page (above). "Refused while a policy is in force or waiting" was read as including a proposed,
  not yet announced policy.
- Address impact: **none.** No key, path or address derivation changes; no contract call. The two columns are
  off-chain settings.
- **After PR 145's review (2026-11-25)**, on the same branch:
  1. **Migration 0027 must re-create `scopes_app_user_ids_no_policy` word for word.** The trigger reads
     `guarded_changes`, which P1's 0027 drops and renames; the P1 builder drops this trigger before its `DROP TABLE` and
     creates it again after the renames, with exactly the SQL in `0026_shared_scope_rules.sql` (unchanged since the
     review; keep it so). P1's migration test should compare the two by `sqlite_schema`.
  2. **The vault never serves a policy for an app that shares a wallet** (`apps/api/src/vault/settings.ts`:
     `getSettingsRow` joins the app's scope, `effectiveSettings` returns no policy when the scope is marked, its row is
     missing or the creator isn't `hana`, with an error line `auto_approve_policy_shared_wallet` naming only the app and
     why). That covers every reader: `GET /v1/app`, the vault page, consent registration (`policy_not_in_force`, nothing
     recorded), the share checks and the identity token (which read only the session settings). One more D1 row per
     `GET /v1/app` (the scope's), so the read's budget in `home-devices.test.ts` is 12 and 15 rows.
  3. **Test scopes only, for now.** `setScopeAppUserIds` refuses a live scope (`env_mismatch`, "Only a test scope can be
     marked as shared for now: a live shared scope needs its own security review first") in its read and its commit
     predicate; the admin route refuses it before calling the API (it reads the org's apps); a trigger refuses it in D1;
     the admin page doesn't offer it and says why. **To confirm (the Tech Lead):** when a live shared scope opens (N2,
     D914), raw signing must be refused for its apps in the same commit check as the policy, and the mark refused while
     raw signing is on or waiting.
  4. **The one-way mark holds against a direct write**: triggers refuse a replacing insert or an upsert that would
     leave a marked scope unmarked, and deleting a marked scope (checked: no code deletes or replaces scope rows:
     `deleteApp` leaves the scope, `d1-move` imports only into an empty database, the e2e harness uses `INSERT OR IGNORE`
     on scopes it never marks). Drift counts a scope as marked also when the append-only ledger has its
     `scope.app_user_ids` row, and reports a scope whose latest mark isn't in its column (`shared_scope_unmarked`); the
     retention purge keeps every such ledger row (D364).
  5. **Drift's shared-wallet finding can't go quiet**: its id is per app, source and `settings_version` (or change id),
     so a policy forged again after the kill switch (which bumps the version) is reported again; findings already
     recorded are left out of the read, in a fixed order, so over 100 standing findings never crowd out a new one.
  6. **A network's scope can be marked before its first partner app**: `createApp`'s `appUserIds` (AdminRpc; the admin
     route takes it too) and `admin app:create --shared-wallet` create the scope marked, in the same write as its first
     row, with the mark's own ledger row (request id `<id>:mark`); test scopes only; on an existing scope it must already
     be marked. The order is in `operations.md`. The admin portal's create form has no checkbox for it yet (the CLI and
     the RPC have it). **To confirm (the Tech Lead):** whether staff want that checkbox.
  7. **Fail closed on unexpected values**: `autoApproveRefused` counts any creator but `hana`, `sharedWallet` and the
     vault any scope flag that isn't 0 (a missing scope row included), drift a missing scope row and any creator but
     `hana`, and the commit predicates and the CLI's guard a missing scope row, as sharing a wallet.
  - Also: a test for an app created on an already-marked scope; the CLI's column check reads `sqlite_master` (as the
    0014 check does) instead of a pragma function, untried against a remote D1 until its first use (`operations.md`
    says how to try it); the mark's confirmation in the admin portal lists the scope's apps.
- **Changed by D916 (2026-11-25, branch `feat/platform-actor`, after this piece merged):** point 1 is done (0027 drops
  and re-creates the trigger; the 0027 test asks `sqlite_schema` for every trigger and view that names the rebuilt
  tables and compares every trigger in the schema by its SQL; 0026's own test checks the trigger still refuses the
  mark after 0027). The two drift findings are security events of their own kinds from 0027 on: `shared_wallet_policy`
  ("Auto-approve found on an app that shares a wallet") and `shared_scope_unmarked` ("A shared wallet’s mark was
  removed by hand"), each with a playbook; before 0027 they stay `drift` events with the same detail.

## The `platform` actor: the ledger rebuilt with its kinds as triggers (branch `feat/platform-actor`), 2026-11-25

From `next` @ 0b99ec12; not merged, not deployed, migration applied nowhere. Piece P1 of `docs/partner-platform-spec.md`
(its A7, finding M9). D916 was given to this piece when it was started; P0, built at the same time, holds migration 0026.

### D916. The ledger can hold and show a `platform` actor: `app_changes` and `guarded_changes` rebuilt once with their kinds as triggers, `security_events` with three more kinds, the views' words, and `ledger-check` for the deploy
- Date 2026-11-25 · Status: **built** (the design is the Tech Lead's D913 and the spec's A7; the points marked "to
  confirm (the Tech Lead)" below were decided while building) · Relates to D90, D704, D894, D913 · Built: migration
  0027, the views, `ledger-check`
- **What it does.** Nothing can act as `platform` yet; after this piece the ledger and the views can hold and show it.
  - **Migration 0027** (`apps/api/migrations/0027_platform_actor.sql`), as A7 orders it: `app_changes_new` and
    `guarded_changes_new` with every column in order, the kind CHECK left off each; a copy with explicit column lists,
    `seq` copied as it is; the old tables dropped (no foreign key or other table's trigger reads them, and a DROP TABLE
    fires no trigger) and the new ones renamed; then every index and trigger of 0006, word for word, and the kind
    triggers: `app_changes_actor_kind` (`member`, `hana`, `system`, `link`, `platform`) and
    `guarded_changes_proposer_kind` (`member`, `hana`, `system`, `platform`). The next kind is a DROP TRIGGER and
    CREATE TRIGGER, never another rebuild. `security_events` gains `platform_quota`, `platform_auth_failures` and
    `link_lookup_volume`, its CHECK widened by a rebuild as 0018 to 0025 did. It reads nothing P0's 0026 adds, so the
    two apply in either order.
  - **console-core**: `ACTOR_KINDS` and `PROPOSER_KINDS` gain `platform`; the three event kinds get titles ("Platform
    key: a limit was reached", "Platform key: many failed requests in a minute", "Many look-ups of one person across
    apps"). The RPC `actor` union is unchanged, so `ConsoleRpc` and `AdminRpc` refuse a `platform` actor at their input
    check until P3 and P4 add it.
  - **Words.** The change notice's "Proposed by": "your platform key (pkc_…)" (since the review: "the organisation's
    platform key (pkc_…)", F7 below). The "Changed by" rows and the feed digests' "By": "a platform key (pkc_…)" (the
    same since the review). The console's Audit: "your platform key pkc_…"; a waiting change: "Requested
    by your platform key pkc_…". The admin SPA: "Platform key". Each list is exhaustive over the kinds, so a later kind
    can't reach a page or an email unnamed; a kind a newer API wrote reads as itself.
  - **`ledger-check`** (`scripts/ledger-check.ts`): the deploy step's before-and-after comparison (A7, M9). Every row of
    the three tables is read in its key's order through `wrangler d1 execute --json` and hashed locally: per table the
    row count, `max(seq)` and a SHA-256 over every row; per row a hash of all columns and of the columns no job writes.
    Indexes and triggers are compared by their SQL. Snapshots hold no row and go to `.secrets/<env>/` (0600). The deploy
    steps are in `docs/operations.md` "Ledger rebuild (hot-DB migration 0027, D916)": not during the monthly retention
    job, the Time Travel bookmark, the snapshot, the migration, the comparison (a rollback to the bookmark on any loss),
    then the API, then the admin and console Workers.
- **Tests.** `apps/api/test/migration-0027.test.ts`: on a database holding every app change kind by every actor of
  before, every guarded change kind, status and proposer, with and without waivers and cancel link hashes, every
  security event kind, a `seq` gap left by a purged row and a `seq` far above the rest: every row back unchanged and in
  order, `max(seq)` kept and the next row after it; every column; every index and trigger by its SQL, only the three
  kind triggers new; each table's SQL the old one less the moved CHECK; the trigger lists equal to `ACTOR_KINDS` and
  `PROPOSER_KINDS`; `platform` taken, unknown kinds (case, spaces, empty, NULL, `link` as a proposer) refused;
  append-only, 60 months, the unique request id, JSON, every `guarded_changes` rule and the event kinds kept. Each of
  six broken copies of the migration (an index dropped, `seq` not copied, the 60-month rule changed, a kind left out,
  the update trigger on another column, a row skipped) fails it. `scripts/test/ledger-check.test.ts`: the real
  migration `identical`; seven broken copies `roll_back`; the jobs' writes in between `kept`; a lifecycle write can't
  hide a fixed column's change; paging changes no hash; no snapshot holds a row's value. Views: the notice, "Changed by"
  and the digests for each kind (`apps/admin/test/email.test.ts`), the console's Audit and waiting change for each
  kind (`apps/console/web/test/ux.test.tsx`), the console's `audit_log` CHECK against its own list.
- **Decided while building, to confirm (the Tech Lead):**
  1. **An update trigger as well.** A7 names only `BEFORE INSERT` triggers, saying an insert is the only write the
     ledger allows. That holds for `app_changes`, not for `guarded_changes`, whose lifecycle columns are updated: its
     old column CHECK also refused an update of `proposed_by_kind`. So 0027 adds
     `guarded_changes_proposer_kind_update` (`BEFORE UPDATE OF proposed_by_kind`, the same list) to keep that refusal.
  2. **`security_events` keeps a CHECK**, widened by a rebuild as 0018 to 0025 did (A7's words for it), not a trigger:
     the table is updated too (`notified_at`), and a CHECK holds updates without a second trigger.
  3. **The console's `audit_log` keeps its own list** (`AUDIT_LOG_ACTOR_KINDS`, the four kinds of before). `ACTOR_KINDS`
     was also the list a test holds that table's CHECK to; the console never records a `platform` row (the platform
     acts only through the API), so its D1 isn't rebuilt. Console rows' views use the console list, app changes' views
     `ACTOR_KINDS`. The staff audit filter keeps `ACTOR_KINDS`, so an export can be filtered to the platform's rows.
  4. **The key's id, not its label, for now.** A6 and A11 name the actor by the key's label ("your platform key
     "{label}" ({pkc_…})"); labels live in `platform_keys`, which P2 adds. Until then every view names the key by its
     `pkc_…` id; P2 or P5 adds the label.
  5. **"Changed by" for an emailed link** now says "an emailed link" (it fell through to "the system" before; no
     notice with that row has a `link` actor today).
  6. **What `ledger-check` calls a rollback.** A7 says any difference is a rollback. The API and the admin Worker keep
     running while the migration applies, so between the two snapshots a notice can be acknowledged (a guarded
     change's lifecycle columns), an event emailed (`notified_at`) and ledger rows added. The check rolls back on a
     row lost, a column no job writes changed (any column of an `app_changes` row), a new ledger row at or below the old
     `max(seq)`, or an index or trigger missing or changed; rows written since and lifecycle-only updates are reported
     (how many, the first keys) as `kept`. The deploy steps keep it away from the monthly retention job, whose
     deletions would read as lost rows.
  7. **Wording** of the three event titles and of "your platform key" / "a platform key" / "Platform key" (plain words,
     to be read again with P5's screens).
- **Found in A7 while building** (the spec's design not changed): (a) point 1 above; (b) point 6 above; (c) `ACTOR_KINDS`
  is also the console's `audit_log` list (point 3); (d) D1 refuses `PRAGMA integrity_check` (`SQLITE_AUTH`), so the
  migration test runs `PRAGMA quick_check` and `foreign_key_check` and checks the kind rules itself; (e) a renamed
  table's SQL in `sqlite_schema` quotes its name (`CREATE TABLE "app_changes"`), so "every table the same SQL" can only
  mean the same SQL less the moved CHECK, which is what the test checks. Not built here, as the P1 row leaves them to
  later pieces: the console's `pending_actions` rebuild (P2), playbooks for the new event kinds (P5), and the change
  notice's waiver sentence, which a platform proposal never qualifies for (P5's one email per request).
- **Merging beside P0**: 0026 must not rebuild `security_events` (0027's copy would refuse a kind 0027 doesn't list);
  the migration tests that list every migration file (0003's, 0006's) gain 0026 and 0027 from the two branches, a
  plain text merge. (It didn't rebuild it; its trigger on `scopes` did need handling: "After P0 merged" below.)
- **After PR 143's review** (2026-11-25; the review found the migration, the code and the views sound, and the
  deploy's safety net not):
  - **F1, `compare` passed a damaged rebuild as "kept".** Any difference in a job-written column passed. Now each
    row's job-written columns are recorded as their state (NULL or a short hash; `status` itself), and only the
    jobs' own moves pass (`lifecycleProblem`, `scripts/lib/ledger-check.ts`: an ack sets `notified_at` with
    `active_from`, and `waiver`, `cancel_token_hash`; expedite changes `active_from` with `expedited_by` and
    `expedite_reason`; activation pending → active with `activated_recorded_at`; an end active or pending → ended with
    `ended_at`; a cancel pending → cancelled with `cancelled_at` and `cancelled_by`; an event's `notified_at` NULL →
    set); anything else is `MOVED WRONG`, a rollback. `active_from` "earlier" can't be checked without its value, so
    the rule is "changed only together with an expedite". And the copy now checks itself inside the migration: before
    each DROP, a `ledger_copy_check` row with `CHECK (ok = 1)` takes "the old table EXCEPT the copy, and the copy EXCEPT
    the old table, are both empty, with equal counts", so a damaged copy aborts the whole file whatever the API does.
    Tests: seven damaged copies abort it with the old tables, rows, triggers and `d1_migrations` untouched; seven
    job-column damages come back `roll_back` from `ledger-check` with that check switched off; every real job move,
    and several in a row, comes back `kept`. A bug found on the way: `hex(NULL)` is '', so a cleared cancel-link hash
    read like an empty one; NULL blobs are now read as NULL.
  - **F2, the deploy steps.** Snapshot, then the bookmark, then the migration at once (the bookmark first made a
    post-restore compare say ROLL BACK again). The rollback now has the export first, the restore, the admin feed's
    cursor at once (`ledger-check <env> feed-cursor --remote --before <snapshot> [--yes]`: lowers `ops.state`
    `feed.app_changes.seq` and its `.init` to the snapshot's `max(seq)`, never above the restored one, never raises
    it; a repeat digest rather than a gap), the check (`not applied`), then "Re-run afterwards". The cursor step is
    also added to "Restoring a D1 database (Time Travel)" for any restore. Time Travel has never been rehearsed (D152),
    so the rehearsal is a required step 1 with a restore drill on the scratch copy.
  - **F3**: the comparison reads the three tables' own SQL and expects exactly the old SQL less the moved CHECK (the
    0027 test's normalisation); a dropped CHECK, `json_valid`, NOT NULL or new kind is a rollback.
  - **F4**: rows are read with `apiPrivateD1Execute` (REST API remotely, a 0600 file and wrangler's log off locally),
    not `d1Execute`, so no row reaches `~/.wrangler/logs`; a test holds the script to it.
  - **F5**: `--d1-name <rehearsal database>` (a name containing "rehearsal", none naming production, remote only); a
    mainnet env refused; the rehearsal step in `docs/operations.md`.
  - **F6**: `app_changes_no_replace` refuses an insert with a request id or `seq` already recorded, so `INSERT OR
    REPLACE` can't rewrite a ledger row (its delete fires no trigger). `guarded_changes` and `security_events` are left
    as they are: no append-only rule applies to them (an UPDATE may already change any column), and every write to
    `security_events` is `INSERT OR IGNORE` on its id (a trigger that aborts would break those; one that ignores would
    turn a plain duplicate insert silent). Nothing writes the ledger with OR REPLACE, OR IGNORE or ON CONFLICT.
  - **F7**: the change notice goes to the security alias and the org's contacts as one message, so it says "the
    organisation's platform key (pkc_…)"; "Changed by" and the digests say the same. The console keeps "your platform
    key" (its readers are the org's members). The admin's audit "Done by" filter offers "Platform key"; the staff
    audit filter's schema takes it (tests).
  - **Noted, not built**: P0 (PR 145) asks for a `shared_wallet_policy` event kind, as its drift finding reuses the
    generic "App setting in force without a notice". The kind list 0027 widens is where it would go, with its title in
    `SECURITY_EVENT_TITLES`; the coordinator will have it added once P0 is on `next` (built then: "After P0 merged"
    below).
  - **To confirm (the Tech Lead)**: the job-move rules above (they are the code's writers as read on 2026-11-25; a new
    writer of a lifecycle column must be added to them); the feed cursor going back to the snapshot (a repeated digest
    after a rollback rather than a missed one).
- **After P0 (PR 145, D915) merged into `next`** (2026-11-25):
  - **0026's trigger re-created.** `scopes_app_user_ids_no_policy` (on `scopes`) reads `guarded_changes`, and SQLite

  - **D915's drift findings get their own kinds**, in the list 0027 widens anyway: `shared_wallet_policy`, titled
    "Auto-approve found on an app that shares a wallet", and `shared_scope_unmarked`, titled "A shared wallet’s mark was
    removed by hand", each with a playbook (`shared-wallet-policy`, `shared-scope-unmarked`) mapped in the admin's
    security screen. The drift check writes them once 0027 is there (it reads `security_events`' SQL once per run that

  "ok for items 20 to 22 as well."; then, on 17, after a four-eyes rule was proposed instead of a flat wait and they
  asked "if we go with four eyes, we no longer make it 24 hrs?" (the answer: correct, 24 h stays only as the fallback
  when nobody confirms): "four eyes".
- **A (1 to 5): the "also used on other apps" line** (PR 141): confirmed; recorded in D912 on that PR's branch.
- **B (6): "HyperEVM"** (the chain's own name) or "Hyperliquid", recommended HyperEVM: **HyperEVM stays** (D910's first
  to-confirm point).
- **C: the Request labels form** (D907, D908 and their "After PR 135's review" list), as put and what each maps to:
  - **7.** A payment's verbs are pay, send, donate, deposit, repay, lend, buy, stake and bid; sell, borrow, withdraw,
    unstake and swap are refused: confirmed (D907 to-confirm 5, the narrowing, built by the review's item 2).
  - **8.** The refused words in phrases and names: me, us, user, this, back, return, undo and similar (`text_self`);
    "says" (`text_says`); outcome words in names (`text_outcome`); authority words in names (`text_authority`); told
    that honest phrases such as "this ticket" and "the return fare" are refused too: confirmed (the review's item 2).
  - **9.** The account's name counts towards the sentence's 40 partner characters: confirmed (D907 to-confirm 2).
  - **10.** Names that look alike are duplicates: confirmed (D907 to-confirm 6, built by the review's item 8).
  - **11.** Screen readers: partner values are not announced differently (not built; recommended to leave it):
    confirmed as **leave as it is** (the review's item 7).
  - **12.** The small wording: the example's text (D908 to-confirm 1, its words and "pay for the order"), the hints
    (D908 to-confirm 4, the memo label's hint; and the hints of D907 to-confirm 4, the "Name shown to users" field's
    hint per kind) and "usually within a few minutes" (D908 to-confirm 5): confirmed.
- **D (13): the spinner** (D906's to-confirm): the pulse's values (2 s a cycle, 60% at the middle; D906 to-confirm 1)
  and the loading placeholders staying still (to-confirm 2): confirmed.
- **E: D914's proposals:**
  - **14.** Revoking a stolen key also cancels everything it proposed that isn't in force yet (with the switch-off and
    a freeze): confirmed.
  - **15.** The one-click removal link in the "address confirmed" email, valid about a week: confirmed (D914 proposal
    3, its origin half). The key's revoke link in a key's confirmation notice was not put separately: **not read as
    covered**, still to confirm.
  - **16.** The org's owners also get the "new address proposed" email: confirmed (D914 proposal 6).
  - **17. Not as proposed** (D914 proposal 5, a flat 24 h wait for staff proposals): **four eyes**, below.
  - **20.** What "a different person" means for four eyes on keys (a different console account, Google account and
    email, and already an owner before the key was registered; told what it can't catch): confirmed (D914 proposal 1).
  - **21.** An owner's acceptance of a staff-registered key counts as its confirmation: confirmed (D914 proposal 2).
  - **22.** Switching the org's platform off or freezing it also cancels waiting keys: confirmed (D914 proposal 4).
- **Item 17, decided** (the Tech Lead: "four eyes"). An origin Journear staff add to a platform-created app, and (the
  reach D914's proposal had) to any app on a flagged shared scope, comes into force **at once when a second person
  confirms it**: a different staff member in the admin portal, or an owner of the org in the console with the same bar
  as for a platform proposal (console `owner`, on-chain owner of the scope, fresh Google sign-in). With no
  confirmation it comes into force after the 24 h platform minimum, unless cancelled; no waiver, no expedite by the
  proposer alone. The staff member who proposed it can never be the one who confirms it. **The catch, told to the
  Tech Lead:** they are the only staff member today, so until a second admin exists a Sodax owner confirms it or it
  waits the day.
- **The Tech Lead's direction**, already in D914 in their words ("sounds good, I like this "four eyes" rule, please
  suggest this for future decisions similar to this."): item 17 is the first decision taken under it.
- **Proposed for item 17, to confirm with the Tech Lead** (`docs/partner-platform-spec.md` A15, A7, P10):
  1. **How the second staff member proves who they are:** the admin portal's existing identity, the Cloudflare Access
     application token on every `/api/*` request (`Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`, verified by `AccessJwtVerifier`,
     `type = 'app'`, a non-empty `sub`, so no service token) and the email on the manifest's staff list

     confirmation's commit predicate.
  3. **The notices:** the proposal's announcement (alias, security contacts, owners, with the cancel and Confirm
     links); the confirmation's notice naming both people, with the removal link, as for other confirmations.
  4. **Built in P10**, with its tests (the proposing staffer's confirm refused; a second staffer's confirm brings it
     into force; an owner's confirm brings it into force; nobody: 24 h; no waiver or expedite path) and an independent
     security review.
- **Still open after this** (not put to the Tech Lead, or put and not answered; each stays as its entry says):

  - D906: the stamps site's marching outline staying still (to-confirm 3); the demo's `.result` fix (to-confirm 4).

  - D914: the `local*` guard (proposal 7); the standby-key advice; the key's revoke link (proposal 3, its key half);
